aboue his ȝerde; forsothe the name of Aaron schal be in the lynage of Leuy, and o ȝerde schal conteyne alle the meynees of hem.
And thou schalt putte tho ȝerdis in the tabernacle of boond of pees, bifor the witnessyng, where Y schal speke to thee; the ȝerde of hym schal buriowne,
whom Y schal chese of hem; and Y schal refreyne fro me the playnyngis of the sones of Israel, bi whiche thei grutchen aȝens ȝou.
And Moyses spak to the sones of Israel; and alle princes ȝauen to hym ȝerdis, bi alle lynagis; and the ȝerdis weren twelue, without the ȝerde of Aaron.
And whanne Moises hadde put tho ȝerdis bifor the Lord, in the tabernacle of witnessyng,
he ȝede aȝen in the day suynge, and founde that the ȝerde of Aaron, in the hows of Leuy, buriounnede; and whanne knoppis weren greet, the blossoms hadden broke out, whiche weren alargid in leeuys, and weren fourmed in to alemaundis.
Therfor Moyses brouȝte forth alle the ȝerdis fro the siȝt of the Lord to al the sones of Israel; and thei sien, and resseyueden ech his ȝerde.
And the Lord seide to Moises, Bere aȝen the ȝerde of Aaron in to the tabernacle of witnessyng, that it be kept there in to the signe of the rebel sones of Israel, and that her playntis reste fro me, lest thei dien.
And Moises dide, as the Lord comaundide.
Forsothe the sones of Israel seiden to Moises, Lo! we ben wastid, alle we perischiden;
who euer neiȝeth to the tabernacle of the Lord, he dieth; whethir we schulen be doon awei alle til to deeth?
And the Lord seide to Aaron, Thou, and thi sones, and the hows of thi fadir with thee, schulen bere the wickidnesse of the seyntuarie; and thou and thi sones togidere schulen suffre the synnes of ȝoure preesthod.
But also take thou with thee thi britheren of the lynage of Leuy, and the power of thi fadir, and be thei redi, that thei mynystre to thee. Forsothe thou and thi sones schulen mynystre in the tabernacle of witnessyng; and the dekenes
schulen wake at thi comaundementis, and at alle werkis of the tabernacle; so oneli that thei neiȝe not to the vessels of seyntuarie, and to the autir, lest bothe thei dien, and ȝe perischen togidere.
Forsothe be thei with thee, and wake thei in the kepyngis of the tabernacle, and in alle the cerymonyes therof. An alien schal not be meddlid with ȝou.
Wake ȝe in the kepyng of the seyntuarie, and in the seruyce of the auter, lest indignacioun rise on the sones of Israel.
Lo! Y haue ȝouun to ȝou ȝoure britheren, dekenes, fro the myddis of the sones of Israel, and Y haue ȝoue a fre ȝifte to the Lord, that thei serue in the seruyces of his tabernacle.
Forsothe thou and thi sones, kepe ȝoure preesthod; and alle thingis that perteynen to the ournyng of the auter, and ben with ynne the veil, schulen be mynystrid bi preestis; if ony straunger neiȝeth, he schal be slayn.
The Lord spak to Aaron, Lo! Y haue ȝoue to thee the kepyng of my firste fruytis; Y haue ȝoue to thee and to thi sones alle thingis, that ben halewid of the sones of Israel, for preestis office euerlastynge lawful thingis.
Therfor thou schalt take these thingis of tho thingis that ben halewid, and ben offrid to the Lord; ech offryng, and sacrifice, and what euer thing is ȝoldun to me for synne and for trespas, and cometh in to hooli of hooli thingis, schal be thin and thi sones.
Thou schalt ete it in the seyntuarie; malis oneli schulen ete therof, for it is halewid to the Lord. Forsothe Y haue
ȝoue to thee, and to thi sones and douȝtris, bi euerlastynge riȝt, the firste fruytis whiche the sones of Israel a vowen and offren; he that is clene in thin hous, schal ete tho.
Y ȝaf to thee al the merowe of oile, and of wyn, and of wheete, what euer thing of the firste fruytis thei schulen offre to the Lord.
Alle the bigynnyngis of fruytis whiche the erthe bryngith forth, and ben brouȝt to the Lord, schulen falle in to thin vsis; he that is cleene in thin hous, schal ete of tho.
Al thing which the sones of Israel ȝelden bi avow, schal be thin.
What euer thing schal breke out first of the wombe of al fleisch, which fleisch thei offren to the Lord, whether it is of men, ethir of beestis, it schal be of thi riȝt; so oneli that thou take prijs for the firste gendrid child of man, and that thou make ech beeste which
is vncleene to be bouȝt aȝen; whos aȝenbiyng schal be aftir o monethe, for fyue siclis of siluer, bi the weiȝte of seyntuarie; a sicle hath xx. halpens.
Forsothe thou schalt not make the firste gendrid of oxe, and of scheep, and of goet, to be aȝen bouȝt, for tho ben halewid to the Lord; oneli thou schalt schede the blood of tho on the auter, and thou schalt brenne the ynnere fatnesse in to swettist odour to the Lord.
Forsothe the fleischis schulen falle in to thin vss, as the brest halewid and the riȝt schuldur, schulen be thine.
Y ȝaf to the and to thi sones and douȝtris, bi euerlastynge riȝt, alle the firste fruytis of seyntuarie, whiche the sones of Israel offren to the Lord; it is euerlastynge couenant of salt bifor the Lord, to thee, and to thi sones.
And the Lord seide to Aaron, Ȝe schulen not welde ony thing in the lond of hem, nether ȝe schulen haue part among hem; Y am thi part and erytage, in the myddis of the sones of Israel.
Forsothe Y ȝaf to the sones of Leuy alle the tithis of Israel in to possessioun, for the seruyce bi whyche thei seruen me in the tabernacle of boond
of pees; that the sones of Israel neiȝe no more to the tabernacle of boond of pees, nether do dedli synne.
To the sones aloone of Leuy, seruynge me in the tabernacle, and berynge the synnes of the puple, it schal be a lawful thing euerlastynge in ȝoure generaciouns.
Thei schulen welde noon other thing, and thei schulen be apeied with the offryng of tithis, whiche Y departide in to vsis and necessaries of hem.
And the Lord spak to Moises and
seide, Comaunde thou, and denounse to the dekenes, Whanne ȝe han take tithis of the sones of Israel, whiche Y ȝaf to ȝou, offre ȝe the firste fruytis of tho to the Lord, that is, the tenthe part of the dyme,
that it be arettid to ȝou in to offryng of the firste fruytis, as wel of corn flooris
as of pressis; and of alle thingis of whiche ȝe taken tithis, offre ȝe the firste fruytis to the Lord, and ȝyue ȝe to Aaron, preest.
Alle thingis whiche ȝe schulen offre of tithis, and schulen departe in to the ȝiftis of the Lord, schulen be the beste, and alle chosun thingis.
And thou schalt seye to hem, If ȝe offren to the Lord alle the clere and betere thingis of tithis, it schal be arettid to ȝou, as if ȝe ȝauen the firste fruitis of the corn floor and presse.
And ȝe schulen ete tho tithis in alle ȝoure placis, as wel ȝe as ȝoure meynees, for it is the prijs for the seruyce, in whiche ȝe seruen in the tabernacle of witnessyng.
And ȝe schulen not do synne on this thing, and resserue noble thingis and fat to ȝou, lest ȝe defoulen the offryngis of the sones of Israel, and ȝe dien.
And the Lord spak to Moises and to
Aaron, and seide, This is the religioun of sacrifice, which the Lord ordeynede. Comaunde thou to the sones of Israel, that thei brynge to thee a reed cow of hool age, in which is no wem, nether sche hath bore ȝok.
And ȝe schulen bitake hir to Eleazar, preest, which schal offre the cow, led out of the tentis, in the siȝt of alle men.
And he schal dippe his fyngur in the blood therof, and schal sprynge seuene sithis aȝens the ȝatis of the tabernacle.
And he schal brenne that cow, while alle men sien; and he schal ȝyue as wel the skyn and fleischis therof as the blood and dung to flawme.
Also the preest schal sende a tre of cedre, and ysope, and reed threed died twies, into the flawme that deuourith the cow.
And thanne at the laste, whanne hise clothis and bodi ben waischun, he schal entre in to the tentis, and he schal be defoulid til to euentid.
But also he that brente the cow, schal waische hise clothis, and bodi, and he schal be vncleene til to euentid.
Forsothe a cleene man schal gadere the aischis of the cow, and schal schede out tho with out the tentis, in a place moost cleene, that tho be to the multitude of the sones of Israel in to keping, and in to watir of spryngyng; for the cow is brent for synne.
And whanne he that bar the aischis of the cow, hath waische hise clothis, he schal be vncleene til to euentid. And the sones of Israel, and comelyngis that dwellen among hem, schulen haue this hooli bi euerlastynge lawe.
He that touchith a deed bodi of man, and is vncleene for this bi seuene
daies, schal be spreynt of this watir in the thridde, and in the seuenthe dai; and so he schal be clensid. If he is not spreynt in the thridde dai, he schal not mow be clensid in the seuenthe dai.
Ech that touchith the deed bodi bi it silf of mannus soule, and is not spreynt with this medlyng, defoulith the tabernacle of the Lord, and he schal perische fro Israel; for he is not spreynt with the wateris of clensyng, he schal be vncleene, and his filthe schal dwelle on hym.
This is the lawe of a man that dieth in the tabernacle; alle that entren in to his tente, and alle vessels that ben there, schulen be defoulid bi seuene daies.
A vessel that hath not an hilyng, nethir a byndyng aboue, schal be vncleene.
If ony man touchith the deed bodi of man slayn in the feeld, ether deed bi hym silf, ether a boon, ether the sepulcre of hym, he schal be vncleene bi seuene daies.
And thei schulen take of the aischis of the brennyng, and of the synne, and thei schulen sende quyk watris in to a vessel
on tho aischis; in whiche whanne a cleene man hath dippid ysope, he schal spreynge therof the tente, and al the purtenaunce of howshold, and men defoulid bi sich defoulyng.
And in this maner a cleene man schal clense an vncleene, in the thridde and in the seuenthe dai; and he schal be clensid in the seuenthe dai. And he schal waische hym silf, and hise clothis, and he schal be vncleene til to euentid.
If ony man is not clensid bi this custom, the soule of hym schal perische fro the myddis of the chirche; for he defoulith the seyntuarie of the Lord, and is not spreynt with the watir of clensyng.
This comaundement schal be a lawful thing euerlastynge. Also he that schal sprenge the watris schal waische his clothis; ech man that touchith the watris of clensyng, schal be vncleene til to euentid.
What euer thing an vncleene man touchith, he schal make it vncleene; and a soule that touchith ony of these thingis defoulid so, schal be vncleene til to euentid.
And the sones of Israel and al the multitude camen in to the deseert of Syn, in the firste monethe. And the puple dwellide in Cades; and Marie was deed there, and biried in the same place.
And whanne the puple hadde nede to watir, thei ȝeden togidere aȝens Moises and Aaron;
and thei weren turned in to dissensioun, and seiden, We wolden that we hadden perischid among oure britheren bifor the Lord.
Whi han ȝe led out the chirche of the Lord in to wildirnesse, that bothe we and oure beestis die?
Whi han ȝe maad vs to stie from Egipt, and han brouȝt vs in to this werste place, which may not be sowun, which nether bryngith forth fige tre, nether vineris, nether pumgranatis, ferthermore and hath not watir to drynke?
And whanne the multitude was left, Moises and Aaron entriden in to the tabernacle of boond of pees, and felden lowe to erthe, and crieden to God, and seiden, Lord God, here the cry of this puple, and opene to hem thi tresour, a welle of quyk watir, that whanne thei ben fillid, the grutchyng of hem ceesse. And the
glorie of the Lord apperide on hem; and
the Lord spak to Moises, and seide, Take the ȝerde, and gadere the puple, thou, and Aaron thi brother; and speke ȝe to the stoon bifore hem, and it schal ȝyue watris. And whanne thou hast led watir out of the stoon, al the multitude schal drynke, and the beestis therof schulden drynke.
Therfor Moises took the ȝerde that was in the siȝt of the Lord, as the
Lord comaundide to hym, whanne the multitude was gaderid bifor the stoon; and he seide to hem, Here ȝe, rebel and vnbileueful; whether we moun brynge out of this stoon watir to ȝou?
And whanne Moises hadde reisid the hond, and hadde smyte the flynt twies with the ȝerde, largeste watris ȝeden out, so that the puple drank, and the beestis drunken.
And the Lord seide to Moises and to Aaron, For ȝe bileueden not to me, that ȝe schulden halewe me bifor the sones of Israel, ȝe schulen not lede these puples in to the lond which Y schal ȝyue to hem.
This is the watir of aȝenseiyng; there the sones of Israel stryueden aȝens the Lord, and he was halewid in hem.
In the meene tyme Moises sente messangeres fro Cades to the kyng of Edom, whiche seiden, Israel thi brother sendith these thinges. Thou knowist
al the trauel that took vs, hou oure fadris ȝeden doun in to Egipt, and we dwelliden there myche tyme, and Egipcians turmentiden vs and oure fadris;
and hou we crieden to the Lord, and he herde vs, and sente an aungel that ledde vs out of Egipt. And lo! we ben set in the citee of Cades, which is in thi laste
coostis, and we bisechen that it be leueful to vs to passe thorou thi lond; we schulen not go bi feeldis, nether bi vyneris, nether we schulen drynke watris of thi pittis; but we schulen go in the comyn weie, and we schulen not bowe to the riȝt side, nether to the left side, til we passen thi termes.
To whom Edom answeride, Ȝe schulen not passe bi me, ellis Y schal be armed, and come aȝens thee.
And the sones of Israel seiden, We schulen go bi the weie comynli vsid, and if we and oure beestis drynken thi watris, we schulen ȝyue that that is iust; noon hardnesse schal be in prijs, onely passe we swiftli.
And he answeride, Ȝe schulen not passe. And anoon he ȝede out aȝens Israel, with a multitude without noumbre, and strong
hond, nether he wolde assente to Israel bisechynge, that he schulde graunte passage bi hise coostis. Wherfor Israel turnede awey fro hym.
And whanne thei hadden moued tentis fro Cades, thei camen in to the hil of Hor, which is in the endis
of the lond of Edom; where the Lord spak
to Moyses and seide, Aaron go to his puples; for he schal not entre in to the lond which Y ȝaf to the sones of Israel, for he was vnbileueful to my mouth, at the watris of aȝenseiyng.
Take thou Aaron, and his sone with hym, and thou schalt lede
hem in to the hil of Hor; and whanne thou hast maad nakid the fadir of his cloth, thou schalt clothe with it Eleazar, his sone, and Aaron schal be gederid, and schal die there.
Moises dide as the Lord comaundide; and thei stieden in to the hil of Hor, bifor al the multitude.
And whanne he hadde maad nakid Aaron of hise clothis, he clothide with tho Eleazar, his sone.
Sotheli whanne Aaron was deed in the cop of the hil, Moises cam doun with Eleazar.
Sotheli al the multitude siȝ that Aaron was deed, and wepte on hym thretti daies, bi alle her meynees.
And whanne Chananei, the kyng of Arad, that dwellide at the south, hadde herd this, that is, that Israel cam bi the weye of aspieris, he fauȝt aȝens hem; and Chananei was ouercomere and ledde pray of Israel.
And Israel bounde hym sylf bi avow to the Lord, and seide, If thou schalt bitake this puple in myn hond, Y schal do awei the citees therof.
And the Lord herde the preieris of Israel, and bitook the Chananey; and Israel killid hym, and distruyede hise citees; and clepide the name of that place Horma, that is, cursyng, ethir hangyng up.
Forsothe thei ȝeden forth also fro the hil of Hor, bi the weie that ledith to the reed see, that thei schulden cumpasse the lond of Edom; and it bigan to anoye the puple, of the weie and trauel.
And the puple spak aȝens the Lord and Moises, and seide, Whi leddist thou vs out of Egipt, that we schulden die in wildirnesse? breed failith, watris ben not; oure soule wlatith now on this meete moost liȝt.
Wherfor the Lord sente firid serpentis in to the puple; at the woundis of whiche serpentis,
and the dethis of ful many men, thei camen to Moyses, and seiden, We synneden, for we spaken aȝens the Lord and thee; preie thou, that he take awey fro vs the serpentis.
And Moises preiede for the puple; and the Lord seide to hym, Make thou a serpent of bras, and sette thou it for a signe; he that is smytun and biholdith it, schal lyue.
Therfor Moyses made a serpent of bras, and settide for a signe; and men smytun and biholdynge it, weren heelid.
And the sones of Israel
ȝeden forth, and settiden tentis in Oboth; fro whennus thei ȝeden forth, and settiden tentis in Neabarym, in the wildirnesse, that biholdith Moab, aȝens the eest coost.
And thei moueden fro thennus, and camen
to the stronde of Zareth; which thei leften, and settiden tentis aȝens Arnon, which is in the deseert, and apperith in the coostis of Amorrei. Forsothe Arnon is the terme of Moab, and departith Moabitis and Ammoreis.
Wherfor it is seid in the book of batels of the Lord, As he dide in the reed see, so he schal do in the strondis of
Arnon; the harde rochis of the strondis weren bowid, that tho schulen reste in Arnon, and schulden ligge in the coostis of Moabitis.
Fro that place the pit apperide, of which the Lord spak to Moyses, Gadere thou the puple, and Y schal ȝyue watir to it.
Thanne Israel soong this
song, The pit stie; thei sungen togidere, The pit which the princes diggiden, and the duykis of the multitude maden redi, in the ȝyuere of the lawe, and in her stauys. And thei ȝeden forth fro the
wildirnesse to Mathana, fro Mathana to
Naaliel, fro Naaliel in to Bamoth; Bamoth is a valey in the cuntrey of Moab, in the cop of Phasga, that biholdith aȝens the deseert.
Forsothe Israel sente messangeris to Seon, kyng of Ammorreis, and
seide, Y biseche that it be leueful to me to passe thorou thi loond; we schulen not bowe in to the feeldis and vyneris; we schulen not drynke watris of pittis; we schulen go in the kyngis weie, til we passen thi termes.
Which nolde graunte that Israel schulde passe thurȝ hise coostis, but rather, whanne the oost was gaderid, he ȝede out aȝens Israel, in to deseert. And he cam in to Yasa, and fauȝt aȝens
Israel; of whom he was smytun in the scharpnesse of swerd, and his lond was weldid fro Arnon til to Jeboth and the sones of Amon; for the termes of Amonytis weren holdun bi strong help.
Therfor Israel took alle the citees of hym, and dwelliden in the citees of Amorrei, that is, in Esebon, and hise townes.
The citee of Esebon was Seons, kyng of Ammorei, which Seon fauȝt aȝens the kyng of Moab, and took al the lond that was of his lordschip, til to Arnon.
Therfor it is seid in prouerbe, Come ȝe in to Esebon, be it bildid, and maad the citee of
Seon; fier ȝede out of Esebon, flawme ȝede out of the citee ethir greet castel of Seon, and deuouryde Ar of Moabitis, and the dwelleris of the hiȝe places of Arnon.
Moab, wo to thee! thou, puple of Chamos, perischidist; it ȝaf the sones therof in to fliȝt, and the douȝtris in to caitifte
to Seon, kyng of Ammoreis; the ȝok of hem perischide, fro Esebon til to Dibon; the wery men camen in to Jophe, and til to Medaba.
And so Israel dwellide in the lond of Ammorrey.
And Moises sente men that schulden aspie Jaser, whos townes thei token, and weldiden the dwelleris.
And thei turniden hem silf, and stieden bi the weie of Basan. And Og, the kyng of Basan, with al his puple cam aȝens hem, to fiȝte in Edray.
And the Lord seide to Moises, Drede thou not hym, for Y haue bitake hym, and al his loond, and puple, in thin hoond; and thou schalt do to hym as thou didist to Seon, kyng of Ammorreis, the dwellere of Esebon.
Therfor thei smytiden bothe hym with hise sones and al his puple, til to deeth; and thei weldiden the lond of hym.
And thei ȝeden forth, and settiden tentis in the feeldi places of Moab, where Jerico is set ouer Jordan.
Forsothe Balach, the sone of Sephor, siȝ alle thingis whiche
Israel hadde do to Ammorrei, and that men of Moab hadden dred Israel, and miȝten not bere the assailing of him.
And he seide to the grettere men in birthe of Madian, So this puple schal do awei alle men that dwellen in oure coostis, as an oxe is wont to do awei an eerbe til to the rootis. Forsothe he, that is, Balaac, was kyng in that tyme in Moab.
Therfor he sente messangeris to Balaam, the sone of Beor, a fals diuynour, that dwellide on the flood of the lond of the sones of Amon, that thei schulden clepe hym, and schulden seie, Lo! a puple ȝede out of Egipt, which puple hilide the face of erthe, and sittith aȝens me.
Therfor come thou, and curse this puple, which is strongere than Y, if in ony maner Y may smyte and dryue hym out of my lond; for Y knowe, that he is blissid whom thou blissist, and he is cursid whom thou hast cursid.
The eldere men of Moab and the grettere men in birthe of Madian ȝeden forth, hauynge in hondis the prijs of fals dyuynyng; and whanne thei hadden come to Balaam, and hadden teld to hym alle the wordis of Balaach,
he answeride, Dwelle ȝe here to nyȝt, and Y schal answere what euer thing the Lord schal seie to me. Sotheli while thei dwelliden at Balaam, God cam, and seide to
hym, What wolen these men at thee to hem silf?
Balaam answeride, Balaach, the sone of Sephor, kyng of Moabitis,
sente to me, and seide, Lo! a puple which is gon out of Egipt hilide the face of erthe; come thou, and curse hem, if in ony maner Y may fiȝte, and dryue hym awey.
And God seide to Balaam, Nyle thou go with hem, nether curse thou the puple, for it is blessid.
Which Balaam roos eerli, and seide to the princes, Go ȝe in to ȝoure lond, for God forbeed me to come with ȝou.
The princes turneden aȝen, and seiden to Balaach, Balaam nolde come with vs.
Eft Balaach sente many mo and noblere men, than he hadde sent
bifore; whiche seiden, whanne thei hadden come to Balaam, Balaach, the sone of Sephor, seith thus, Tarye thou not to come
to me, redi to onoure thee; and what euer thing thou wolt, Y schal ȝyue to thee; come thou, and curse this puple.
Balaam answeride, Thouȝ Balaach schal ȝyue to me his howsful of siluer and of gold, Y schal not mowe chaunge the word of my God, that Y speke ethir more ethir lesse.
Y biseche, that ȝe dwelle here also in this nyȝt, that Y may wite what the Lord schal answere eft to me.
Therfor the Lord cam to Balaam in the nyȝt, and seide to hym, If these men comen to clepe thee, rise thou, and go with hem, so oneli that thou do that that Y schal comaunde to thee.
Balaam roos eerli, and whanne his femal asse was sadelid, he ȝede forth with hem.
And God was wrooth. And the aungel of the Lord stood in the weie aȝens Balam, that sat on the femal asse, and hadde twei children with hym.
The femal asse siȝ the aungel stondynge in the weie, with swerd drawun, and turnede a wei hir silf fro the weie, and ȝede bi the feeld. And whanne Balaam beet hir, and wolde lede
aȝen to the path, the aungel stood in the streitnessis of twei wallis, with whiche the vyneris weren cumpassid.
And the femal asse siȝ the aungel, and ioynede hir silf to the wal, and hurtlide the foot of the sittere; and he beet eft the asse.
And neuer the lesse the aungel ȝede to the streit place, where me myȝte not go out of the weie, nether to the riȝt side nether to the left side, and stood aȝens hym.
And whanne the femal asse siȝ the aungel stondynge, sche felde doun vndir the feet of the sittere, which was wrooth ful greetli, and beet hir sidis with a staaf.
And the Lord openyde the mouth of the femal asse, and sche spak, What have Y doon to thee? whi smytist thou me, lo! now the thridde tyme?
Balaam answeride, For thou hast disserued, and hast scornyd me; Y wolde that Y hadde a swerd to sle thee.
And the femal asse seide, Whether Y am not thi beeste on which thou were wont to sitte euere til in to this present dai? seie thou, what lijk thing Y dide euere to thee? And he seide, Neuere.
Anoon the Lord openyde the iȝen of Balaam, and he siȝ the aungel stondynge in the weie, holdynge a drawun swerd in the hoond; and Balaam worschipide hym lowli in to erthe.
To whom the aungel seide, Whi betist thou thi femal asse the thridde tyme? Y cam to be aduersarie to thee, for thi weie is weiward, and contrarye to me;
and if the femal asse hadde not bowid awey fro the weie, and ȝoue place to aȝenstondere, Y hadde slayn thee, and sche schulde lyue.
Balaam seide, Y synnede, not witynge that thou stodist aȝens me; and now, if it displesith thee that Y go, Y schal turne aȝen.
The aungel seide, Go thou with these men, but be war that thou speke not other thing than Y schal comaunde to thee. Therfor Balaam ȝede with the princes.
And whanne Balaach hadde herde this, he ȝede out in to the comyng of hym, in the citee of Moabitis, whiche is set in the laste coostis of Arnon.
And he seide to Balaam, Y sente messangeris to clepe thee; whi camest thou not anoon to me? whethir for Y may not ȝelde meede to thi comyng?
To whom Balaam answeride, Lo! Y am present, whethir Y schal mow speke other thing than that, that God schal putte in my mouth?
Therfor thei ȝeden forth to gidere, and camen in to a citee, which was in the laste coost of his rewme.
And whanne Balaach hadde slayn scheep and oxun, he sente ȝiftis to Balaam and the princes that weren with hym.
Forsothe whanne the morewtid was maad, Balaach ledde Balaam to the hiȝe placis of Baal, and he bihelde the laste part of the puple, that is, al the oost til to the laste part.
And Balaam seide to Balaach, Bilde thou here to me seuene auteris, and make redi so many caluys, and rammes of the same noumbre.
And whanne he hadde do bi the word of Balaam, thei puttiden a calf and a ram togidere on the auter.
And Balaam seide to Balaach, Stond thou a litil while bisidis thi brent sacrifice, while Y go, if in hap the Lord meete me; and Y schal speke to thee what euer thing he schal comaunde.
And whanne he hadde go swiftli, God cam to hym; and Balaam spak to hym, and seide, Y reiside seuene auteris, and Y puttide a calf and a ram aboue.
Forsothe the Lord puttide a word in his mouth, and seide, Turne aȝen to Balaach, and thou schalt speke these thingis.
He turnede aȝen, and fond Balach stondynge bisidis his brent sacrifice, and alle the princes of Moabitis.
And whanne his parable was takun, he seide, Balaach, the kyng of Moabitis, brouȝte me fro Aran, fro the hillis of the eest; and he seide, Come thou and curse Jacob; haaste thou, and greetli curse thou Israel.
How schal Y curse whom God cursid not? bi what resoun schal Y haue abhomynable whom God hath not abhomynable?
Fro the hiȝeste flyntis Y schal se hym, and fro litle hillis Y schal biholde hym; the puple schal dwelle aloone, and it schal not be arettid among hethene men.
Who may noumbre the dust, that is, kynrede, of Jacob, and knowe the noumbre of the generacioun of Israel? My lijf die in the deeth of iust men, and my laste thingis be maad lijk hem!
And Balaach seide to Balaam, What is this that thou doist? Y clepide thee, that thou schuldist curse myn enemyes, and aȝenward thou blessist hem.
To whom Balaam answeride, Whether Y may speke othir thing no but that that the Lord comaundith?
Therfor Balaach seide to Balaam, Come with me in to anothir place, fro whennus thou se a part of Israel, and mayst not se al; fro thennus curse thou hym.
And whanne he hadde led Balaam in to an hiȝ place, on the cop of the hil of Phasga, he bildide seuene auteris to Balaam, and whanne calues and
rammes weren put aboue, he seide to Balaach, Stonde here bisidis thi brent sacrifice, while Y go.
And whanne the Lord hadde come to him, and hadde put a word in his mouth, he seide, Turne aȝen to Balach, and thou schalt seie these thingis to hym.
He turnyde aȝen, and foond Balach stondynge bisidis his brent sacrifice, and the princis of Moabitis with hym. To whom Balach seide, What spak the Lord?
And whanne his parable was takun, he seide, Stonde, Balach, and herkene; here, thou sone of Sephor. God
is not as a man, that he lye, nethir he is as the sone of a man, that he be chaungid; therfor he seide, and schal he not do? he spak, and schal he not fulfille?
Y am brouȝt to blesse, Y may not forbede blessyng.
Noon idol is in Jacob, nethir symylacre is seyn in Israel; his Lord God is with hym, and the sown of victorie of kyng is in hym.
The Lord God ledde hym out of Egipt, whos strengthe is lijk
an vnicorn; fals tellyng bi chiteryng of bryddis, ethir idolatrie, is not in Jacob, nethir fals dyuynyng is in Israel. In his tymes it schal be seide to Jacob and Israel,
What the Lord hath wrought! Lo! the puple schal rise to gidere as a lionesse, and schal be reisid as a lioun; the lioun schal not reste, til he deuoure prey, and drynke the blood of hem that ben slayn.
And Balach seide to Balaam, Nether curse thou, nether blesse thou hym.
And he seide, Whether Y seide not to thee, that what euer thing that God comaundide to me, Y wolde do this?
And Balach seide to hym, Come, and Y schal lede thee to an other place, if in hap it plesith God that fro thennus thou curse hym.
And whanne Balaach hadde led hym out on the cop of the hil of Phegor, that biholdith
the wildirnesse, Balaam seide to hym, Bilde here seuene auteris to me, and make redi so many caluys, and rammes of the same noumbre.
Balaach dide as Balaam seide, and he puttide caluys and rammes, bi alle auteris.
And whanne Balaam siȝ that it pleside the Lord that he schulde blesse Israel, he ȝede not as he hadde go bifore, that he schulde seke fals dyuynyng bi chiteryng of briddis, but he dresside his face aȝens
the desert, and reiside iȝen, and siȝ Israel dwellynge in tentis bi hise lynagis. And whanne the Spirit of God felde on hym,
and whanne a parable was takun, he seide, Balaam, the sone of Beor, seide, a
man whois iȝe is stoppid seide, the herere of Goddis wordis seide, which bihelde the reuelacioun of almyȝti God, which fallith doun, and hise iȝen ben openyd so,
Hou faire ben thi tabernaclis, Jacob, and
thi tentis, Israel! as valeys ful of woodis, and moiste gardyns bisidis floodis, as tabernaclis whiche the Lord hath set, as cedris
bisidis watris; watir schal flowe of his bokat, and his seed schal be in to many watris, that is, puplis. The kyng of hym schal be takun awei for Agag, and the rewme of hym schal be doon awai.
God ledde hym out of Egipt, whos strengthe is lijk an vnicorn; thei schulen deuoure hethene men, enemyes of hym, that is, of Israel; and thei schulen breke the boonus of hem, and schulen perse with arowis.
He restide and slepte as a lyoun, and as a lionesse, whom no man schal dore reise. He that blessith thee, schal be blessid; he that cursith, schal be arettid in to cursyng
And Balaach was wrooth aȝens Balaam, and seide, whanne the hondis weren wrungun to gidere, I clepide thee to curse myn enemyes, whiche aȝenward thou hast blessid thries.
Turne aȝen to thi place; forsothe Y demede to onoure thee greetli, but the Lord priuyde thee fro onour disposid.
Balaam answeride to Balaach, Whethir Y seide not to thi messangeris, whiche thou
sentist to me, Thouȝ Balaach schal ȝyue to me his hows ful of siluer and of gold, Y schal not mow passe the word of my Lord God, that Y brynge forth of myn herte ony thing, ethir of good ethir of yuel, but what euer thing the Lord schal seie, Y schal speke this?
Netheles Y schal go to my puple, and Y schal ȝyue counsel to thee, what thi puple schal do in the laste tyme to this puple.
Therfor whanne a parable was takun, he seide eft, Balaam, the sone of Beor seide, a man
whos iȝe is stoppid, seide, the herere of Goddis wordis seide, which knowith the doctrine of the hiȝeste, and seeth the reuelacioun of almiȝti God, which fallith
doun and hath opyn iȝen, Y schal se hym, but not now; Y schal biholde hym, but not nyȝ; a sterre schal be borun of Jacob, and a ȝerde schal rise of Israel; and he schal smyte the duykis of Moab, and he schal waste alle the sones of Seth;
and Ydumye schal be hys possessioun, the eritage of Seir schal bifalle to his enemyes; forsothe Israel schal do strongli,
of Jacob schal be he that schal be lord, and schal leese the relikis of the citee.
And whanne he hadde seyn Amalech, he took a parable, and seide, Amalech is the bigynning of hethene men, whos laste thingis schulen be lost.
Also he siȝ Cyney, and whanne a parable was takun, he seide, Forsothe thi dwellyng place is strong, but if thou schalt sette thi nest in
a stoon, and schalt be chosun of the generacioun of Cyn, hou longe schalt thou mow dwelle? forsothe Assur schal take thee.
And whanne a parable was takun, he spak eft, Alas! who schal lyue, whanne the Lord schal make thes thingis?
Thei schulen come in grete schippis fro Ytalie, thei schulen ouercome Assiries, and thei schulen distrie Ebrews, and at the last also thei hem silf schulen perische.
And Balaam roos, and turnide aȝen in to his place; and Balaach ȝede aȝen bi the weye in which he cam.
Forsothe in that tyme Israel dwellide in Sechym; and the puple dide fornycacioun
with the douȝtris of Moab; whiche douȝtris clepiden hem to her sacrifices, and thei eten, and worschipiden the
goddis of tho douȝtris; and Israel made sacrifice to Belphegor. And the Lord was
wrooth, and seide to Moises, Take thou alle the princes of the puple, and hange hem aȝens the sunne in iebatis, that my wodnesse, that is stronge veniaunce, be turned awai fro Israel.
And Moises seide to the iugis of Israel, Ech man sle his neiȝboris, that maden sacrifice to Belphagor.
And, lo! oon of the sones of Israel entride bifor his britheren to an hoore of Madian, in the siȝt of Moises, and al the cumpeny of the sones of Israel, whiche wepten bifor the ȝatis of the tabernacle.
And whanne Phynees, the sone of Eleazar, sone of Aaron, preest, hadde seyn this, he roos fro the myddis of the multitude; and whanne he hadde take a
swerd, he entride aftir the man of Israel in to the hoore hows, and stikide thorou both togidere, that is, the man and the womman, in the places of gendryng. And the veniaunce ceesside fro the sones
of Israel, and foure and twenti thousand of men weren slayn.
And the Lord seide
to Moises, Fynees, the sone of Eleazar, sone of Aaron, preest, turnede away myn yre fro the sones of Israel; for he was stirid aȝens hem bi my feruent loue, that Y my silf schulde not do awai the sones of Israel in my greet hete, ether strong veniaunce.
Therfor speke thou to hym, Lo! Y ȝyue to hym the pees of
my couenaunt, and it schal be an euerlastynge couenaunt of preesthod, as wel to hym silf as to his seed; for he louyde feruentli for his God, and he clenside the greet trespas of the sones of Israel.
Forsothe the name of the man of Israel, that was slayn with the womman of Madian, was Zambri, the sone of Salu, duyk of the kynrede and lynage of Symeon.
Forsothe the womman of Madian that was slayn togidere, was clepid Cobri, the douȝter of Sur, the nobleste prince of Madianytis.
And the Lord spak to Moises
and seide, Madianytis feele ȝou enemyes,
and smyte ȝe hem; for also thei diden enemyliche aȝens ȝou, and disseyueden thorow tresouns, bi the idol of Phegor, and bi the douȝter of Corbri, duyk of Madian, her sister, which douȝter was sleyn in the dai of veniaunce, for the sacrilege of Phegor.
Aftir that the blood of gilti men was sched out, the Lord seide to Moises and
to Eleasar, preest, sone of Aaron, Noumbre ȝe al the summe of the sones of Israel, fro twenti ȝeer and aboue, bi her housis, and kynredis, alle men that mowen go forth to batels.
And so Moises and Eleasar, preest, spaken in the feeldi places of Moab, ouer Jordan, aȝens Jerico, to hem
that weren of twenti ȝeer and aboue, as the Lord comaundide; of whiche this is the noumbre.
Ruben, the firste gendrid of Israel; the sone of hym was Enoch, of whom was the meynee of Enochitis; and Phallu, of whom the meynee of Phalluytis;
and Esrom, of whom the meynee of Esromytis; and Charmy, of whom the meynee of Charmytis.
Thes weren the meynees of the generacioun of Ruben, of whiche meynees the noumbre was foundun thre and fourti thousand seuene hundrid and thretti.
The sone of Phallu was
Heliab; the sones of hym weren Namuel, and Dathan and Abiron. These weren Dathan and Abiron, prynces of the puple, that riseden aȝens Moises and Aaron, in the rebelte of Chore, whanne thei
rebelliden aȝens the Lord; and the erthe openyde his mouth, and deuouride Chore, while ful many men dieden, whanne the fier brente two hundrid men and fifti; and
a greet myracle was maad, that whanne Chore perischide, hise sones perischiden not.
The sones of Symeon bi her kynredis; Namuel, of hym was the meynee of Namuelitis; Jamyn, of hym was the meynee of Jamynytis; Jachin, of hym was
the meynee of Jachynytis; Zare, of hym the meynee of Zarenytis; Saul, of hym the meynee of Saulitis.
These weren the meynees of Symeon, of whiche all the noumbre was two and twenti thousynde and two hundrid.
The sones of Gad bi her kynredis; Sephon, of hym the meynee of Sephonytis; Aggi, of hym the meynee of Aggitis; Sumy, of hym the meynee of
Sumytis; Ozny, of hym the meynee of Oznytis; Heri, of hym the meynee of
Hereytis; Arod, of hym the meynee of Aroditis; Ariel, of hym the meynee of Arielitis.
These weren the meynees of Gad, of whiche al the noumbre was fourti thousynde and fyue hundrid.
The sones of Juda weren Her and Onan, whiche bothe weren deed in the lond of Canaan.
And the sones of Juda weren bi her kynredis; Sela, of whom the meynee of Selaitis; Phares, of whom the meynee of Pharesitis; Zare, of whom the meynee of Zareitis.
Sotheli the sones of Phares weren Esrom, of whom the meynee of Esromytis; and Amul, of whom the meynee of Amulitis.
These weren the meynees of Juda, of whiche al the noumbre was seuenty thousynde and fyue hundrid.
The sones of Isachar bi her kynredis; Thola, of whom the meynee of Tholaitis; Phua, of whom the meynee
of Phuitis; Jasub, of whom the meynee of Jasubitis; Semran, of whom the meynee of Semranytis.
These weren the kynredis of Isachar, of whiche the noumbre was foure and sixti thousynd and three hundrid.
The sones of Zabulon bi her kinredis; Sarad, of whom the meynee of Sareditis; Helon, of whom the meynee of Helonytis; Jalel, of whom the meynee of Jalelitis.
These weren the kynredis of Zabulon, of whiche the noumbre was sixti thousynde and fyue hundrid.
The sones of Joseph bi her kynredis weren Manasses and Effraym.
Of Manasses was borun Machir, of whom the meynee of Machiritis. Machir gendride Galaad, of whom the meynee of Galaditis.
Galaad hadde sones; Hizezer, of whom the meynee of Hizezeritis; and Helech, of whom the
meynee of Helechitis; and Ariel, of whom the meynee of Arielitis; and Sechem, of
whom the meynee of Sechemytis; and Semyda, of whom the meynee of Semydaitis; and Epher, of whom the meynee of Epheritis.
Forsothe Epher was the fadir of Salphath, that hadde not sones, but oneli douȝtris; of whiche these weren the names; Maala, and Noha, and Egla, and Melcha, and Thersa.
These weren the meynees of Manasse, and the noumbre of hem was two and fifty thousynde and seuene hundrid.
Forsothe the sones of Effraym bi her kynredis weren these; Suthala, of whom the meynee of Suthalaitis; Bether, of whom the meynee of Betherytis; Tehen, of whom the meynee of Thehenytis.
Forsothe the sone of Suthala was Heram, of whom the meynee of Heramytis.
These weren the kynredis of the sones of Effraym, of whiche the noumbre was two and thretti thousynde and fyue hundrid.
These weren the sones of Joseph, bi her meynees. The sones of Beniamyn in her kynredis; Bale, of whom the meynee of Baleytis; Azbel, of whom the meynee of Azbelitis; Ahiram,
of whom the meynee of Ahiramitis; Suphan, of whom the meynee of Suphanitis; Huphan, of whom the meynee of Huphanitis.
The sones of Bale, Hered and Noeman; of Hered, the meyne of Hereditis; of Noeman, the meynee of Noemanitis.
Thes weren the sones of Beniamyn bi her kynredis, of whiche the noumbre was fyue and fourti thousynde and sixe hundrid.
The sones of Dan bi her kynredis; Suphan, of whom the meynee of Suphanytis. These weren the kynredis
of Dan bi her meynees; alle weren Suphanytis, of whiche the noumbre was foure and sixti thousynde and foure hundrid.
The sones of Aser bi her kynredis; Jemma, of whom the meynee of Jemmaytis; Jesuy, of whom the meynee of Jesuytis; Brie, of whom the meynee of Brieitis.
The sones of Brie; Haber, of whom the meynee of Haberitis; and Melchiel, of whom the meynee of Melchielitis.
Sotheli the name of the douȝtir of Azer was Zara.
These weren the kynredis of the sones of Aser, and the noumbre of hem was foure and fifti thousynde and foure hundrid.
The sones of Neptalym bi her kynredis; Jesehel, of whom the meynee of Jeselitis; Guny, of whom the meynee
of Gunytis; Jeser, of whom the meynee of Jeserytis; Sellem, of whom the meynee of Sellemytis.
Thes weren the kynredis of the sones of Neptalym bi her meynees, of whiche the noumbre was fyue and fourti thousynde and foure hundrid.
This is the summe of the sones of Israel, that weren noumbrid, sixe hundrid thousynde and a thousynde seuene hundrid and thretti.
And the Lord spak to Moises,
and seide, The lond schal be departid to these, bi the noumbre of names in to her
possessiouns; thou schalt ȝyue the grettere part to mo men, and the lesse part to fewere men; possessioun schal be ȝouun to alle bi hem silf, as thei ben noumbrid
now; so oneli that lot departe the lond to lynagis and meynees.
What euer thing bifallith bi lot, ethir mo ether fewere men take this.
Also this is the noumbre of the sones of Leuy bi her meynees; Gerson, of whom the meynee of Gersonytis; Caath, of whom the meynee of Caathitis; Merary, of whom the meynee of Meraritis.
These weren the meynees of Leuy; the meynee of Lobny, the meynee of Ebron, the meynee of Mooli, the meynee of Musi, the meynee of Chori. And sotheli
Caath gendride Amram, which hadde a wijf, Jocabeth, douȝter of Leuy, which douȝter was borun to hym in Egipt. This Jocabeth gendride to hir hosebonde Amram sones, Aaron, and Moyses, and Marie, the sister of hem.
Nadab, and Abyu, and Eleazar, and Ithamar weren bigetun
of Aaron; of whiche Nadab and Abyu weren deed, whanne thei hadden offrid alien fier bifor the Lord.
And alle that weren noumbrid weren thre and twenti thousynde of male kynde, fro o monethe and aboue, whiche weren not noumbrid among the sones of Israel, nether possessioun was ȝouun to hem with othir men.
This is the noumbre of the sones of Israel, that weren discryued of Moises and Eleasar, preest, in the feeldi places of
Moab, ouer Jordan, aȝen Jerico; among whiche noon of hem was that weren noumbrid bifor of Moises and Aaron, in
the deseert of Synay; for the Lord bifore seide, that alle schulden die in the wildirnesse; and noon of hem dwellide, no but Caleph, the sone of Jephone, and Josue, the sone of Nun.
Forsothe the douȝtris of Salphaat, sone of Epher, sone of Galaad, sone of Machir, sone of Manasses, that was the sone of Joseph, neiȝeden; of whiche douȝtris these ben the names; Maala, and Noha, and Egla, and Melcha, and Thersa.
And thei stoden bifore Moises, and Eleazar, preest, and alle the princes of the puple, at the dore of tabernacle of boond of pees;
and seiden, Oure fadir was deed in the deseert, nether he was in the rebelte, that was reisid aȝens the Lord, vndur Chore, but he was deed in his synne; he hadde no male sones. Whi is the name of hym takun awei fro his meynee, for he hath no sone? Ȝif ȝe possessioun to vs among the kynesmen of oure fadir.
And Moises telde the cause of hem to the doom of
the Lord; which seide to Moyses,
The douȝtris of Salphaath axen a iust thing; ȝyue thou possessioun to hem among the kynnysmen of her fadir, and be thei successouris to hym in to eritage.
Forsothe thou schalt speke these thingis to the
sons of Israel, Whanne a man is deed with out sone, the eritage schal go to his
douȝter; if he hath not a douȝter, he
schal haue eiris his britheren; that and if britheren ben not, ȝe schulen ȝyue the
eritage to the britheren of his fadir; forsothe if he hath no britheren of his fadir, the eritage schal be ȝouun to hem that ben next to hym. And this schal be hooli, that is, stidefast, bi euerlastynge lawe to the sones of Israel, as the Lord comaundide to Moises.
Also the Lord seide to Moises, Stie thou in to this hil of Aberym, and biholde thou fro thennus the lond, which Y schal ȝyue to the sones of Israel.
And whanne thou hast seyn it, also thou schalt go to thi puple, as thi
brother Aaron ȝede; for thou offenddidist me in the deseert of Syn, in the aȝen seiyng of the multitude, nether woldist halewe me bifor it, on the watris. These ben the watris of aȝen seiyng, in Cades, of the deseert of Syn.
To whom Moises
answeryde, The Lord God of spiritis of al fleisch puruey a man, that be on
this multitude, and may go out, and entre bifor hem, and lede hem out, and lede hem yn, lest the puple of the Lord be as scheep with out schepherde.
And the Lord seide to hym, Take thou Josue, the sone of Nun, a man in whom the spyrit of God is, and set thin hond on hym;
and he schal stonde bifore Eleazar, preest, and bifore al the multitude.
And thou schalt ȝyue to hym comaundementis, in the siȝt of alle men, and a part of thi glorie, that al the synagoge of the sones of Israel here hym.
If ony thing schal be worthi to be do for this man, Eleasar, preest, schal counseil the Lord; he schal go out, and schal go yn, at the word of Eleazar; he, and alle the sones of Israel with him, and the tother multitude.
Moises dide as the Lord comaundide, and whanne he hadde take Josue, he settide hym bifore Eleazar, preest, and
bifore al the multitude of the puple; and whanne he hadde set hondis on his heed, he reherside alle thingis whiche the Lord comaundide.
Also the Lord seide to Moises,
Comaunde thou to the sones of Israel, and thou schalt seie to hem, Offre ȝe bi her tymes myn offryng, and looues, and encense of swettist odour.
These ben the sacrificis whiche ȝe owen to offre; twey lambren of o ȝeer, with out wem, ech dai in to euerlastynge brent sacrifice.
Ȝe schulen offre oon eerli, and the tother at euentid.
Ȝe schulen offre the tenthe part of ephi of floure, which be spreynt with pureste oile, and haue the fourthe part of hyn.
It is continuel brent sacrifice, which ȝe offriden in the hil of Synai, in to odour of swettiste encense to the Lord.
And ȝe schulen offre the fourthe part of hyn of wyn, bi ech lomb, in the seyntuarie of the Lord.
And ȝe schulen offre in lijk maner the tother lomb at euentid, bi al the custom of the morewe sacrifice, and of moist sacrifices therof, an offryng of swettist odour to the Lord.
Forsothe in the dai of sabat ȝe schulen offre twey lambren of o ȝeer, without wem, and twei tenthe partis of flour spreynt togidere with oile, in sacrifice, and ȝe schulen offre moiste sacrificis
that ben sched bi custom, bi alle sabatis, in to euerlastynge brent sacrifice.
Forsothe in calendis, that is, in the bigynnyngis of monethis, ȝe schulen offre brent sacrifice to the Lord, tweyne calues of the droue, o ram, seuene lambren of o ȝeer,
without wem, and thre tenthe partis of flour spreynt to gidere with oile, in sacrifice, bi ech calf, and twey tenthe partis of flour spreynt to gidere with oile, bi ech
ram; and the tenthe part of a dyme of flour of oile in sacrifice, bi ech lomb; it is brent sacrifice of swetist odour, and of encense to the Lord.
Forsothe the moiste sacrifices of wyn, that schulen be sched bi alle slayn sacrificis, schulen be these; the half part of hyn bi ech calf, the thridde part bi a ram, the fourthe part bi a lomb; this schal be brent sacrifices bi ech monethe, that comen oon aftir anothir while the ȝeer turneth.
Also a buc of geet schal be offrid to the Lord for synnes, in to euerlastynge brent sacrifice, with his moiste offryngis.
Forsothe in the firste monethe, in the fouretenthe dai of the monethe, schal be phase, that is, pask ethir passyng, of the Lord;
and in the fiftenthe day schal be the solempnyte of the therf looues. Bi seuene
daies ȝe schulen ete therf looues; of whiche the firste dai schal be worschipful and hooli; ȝe schulen not do ony seruyle werk therynne.
And ȝe schulen offre brent sacrifice to the Lord, twey calues, o ram, seuene lambren of o ȝeer,
without wem; and the sacrifices of ech bi itsilf of flour, which be spreynt to gidere with oile, thre tenthe partis bi ech
calf, and twey tenthe partis bi a ram, and the tenthe part of a dyme bi ech lomb, that is, bi seuene lambren.
And ȝe schulen offre o buc of geet for synne, that
clensyng be maad for ȝou, outakun the brent sacrifice of the morewtid, which ȝe schulen offre euere.
So ȝe schulen do bi ech dai of seuene daies, into the nurschyng of fier, and in to swettist odour to the Lord, that schal rise of the brent sacrifice, and of moiste sacrifices of ech.
Also the seuenthe day schal be moost solempne and hooli to ȝou; ȝe schulen not do ony seruyle werk ther ynne.
Also the dai of the firste fruytis, whanne ȝe schulen offre newe fruitis to the Lord, whanne the wokis schulen be fillyd, schal be worschipful and hooli; ȝe schulen not do ony seruyle werk ther ynne.
And ȝe schulen offre brent sacrifice to the Lord, in to swettiste odour; twey calues of the droue, o ram, and seuene lambren of o ȝeer, with out
wem; and in the sacrifices of tho ȝe schulen offre thre tenthe partis of flour spreynt togidere with oile, bi ech calf,
twei tenthe partis bi rammes, the tenthe parte of a dyme bi the lambren, whiche ben to gidere, seuene lambren. And ȝe schulen offre a buc of geet, which is offrid for clensyng, outakun brent sacrifice euerlastynge, and the moiste sacrifices
therof; ȝe schulen offre alle thingis with out wem, with her moyste sacrifices.
Forsothe the firste dai of the seuenthe monethe schal be hooli, and worschipful to ȝou; ȝe schulen not do ony seruyle werk ther ynne, for it is the day of sownyng, and of trumpis.
And ȝe schulen offre brent sacrifice, in to swettest odour to the Lord, o calf of the droue, o ram, and seuene lambren of o ȝeer, with out wem;
and in the sacrificis of tho ȝe schulen offre thre tenthe partis of flour spreynt togidere with oile, bi ech calfe, twey tenthe
partis bi a ram, o tenthe part bi a lomb, whiche togidere ben seuene lambren.
And ȝe schulen offre a buc of geet, which is offrid for synne, in to the clensyng
of the puple, with out the brent sacrifice of kalendis, with hise sacrifices, and without euerlastynge brent sacrifice, with customable fletynge offryngis; and bi the same cerymonyes ȝe schulen offre encense in to swettiste odour to the Lord.
Also the tenthe dai of this seuenthe monethe schal be hooli and worschipful to ȝou, and ȝe schulen turmente ȝoure soulis; ȝe schulen not do ony seruyle werk ther ynne.
And ȝe schulen offre brent sacrifice to the Lord, in to swettiste odour; o calf of the droue, o ram, seuene lambren of o ȝeer with out wem.
And in the sacrifices of tho ȝe schulen offre thre tenthe partis of flour spreynt togidere with oyle, bi ech calf, twey tenthe
partis bi a ram, the tenthe part of a dyme bi each lomb, that ben togidere seuene lambren.
And ȝe schulen offre a buc of geet for synne, with out these thingis that ben wont to be offrid for synne in to clensyng, and ȝe schulen offre euerlastinge brent sacrifice in sacrifice, and fletinge offryngis of tho.
Forsothe in the fiftenthe dai of this seuenthe monethe, that schal be hooli and worschipful to ȝou, ȝe schulen not do ony seruyle werk, but ȝe schulen halewe solempnyte to the Lord in seuene daies;
and ȝe schulen offre brent sacrifice, in to swetiste odour to the Lord, threttene calues of the droue, twey rammes, fouretene lambren of o ȝeer, with out wem.
And in the moiste sacrifices of tho ȝe schulen offre thre tenthe partis of flour spreynt to gidere with oile bi ech calf, that ben togidere threttene calues, and ȝe schulen offre twei tenthe partis to twei rammes to gidere, that is, o tenthe part to o ram,
and ȝe schulen offre the tenthe part of a dyme to ech lomb, whiche ben to gidere fourteene lambren.
And ȝe schulen offre a buc of geet for synne, with out euerlastynge brent sacrifice, and with out the sacrifice and moiste offryng therof.
In the tother dai ȝe schulen offre twelue calues of the droue, twei rammes, fouretene lambren of o ȝeer without wem.
And ȝe schulen halewe riȝtfuli sacrifices, and moiste offryngis of alle, bi calues, and rammes, and lambren.
And ȝe schulen offre a buc of geet for synne, with out euerlastynge brent sacrifice, and with out the sacrifice and moist offryng therof.
In the thridde dai ȝe schulen offre euleuen calues, twei rammes, fourtene lambren of o ȝeer, without wem.
And ȝe schulen halewe riȝtfuli the sacrifices, and moiste offryngis of alle, bi the caluys, and rammes, and lambren.
And ȝe schulen offre a buk of geet for synne, with out euerlastynge brent sacrifice, and with out the sacrifice and moiste offryng therof.
In the fourthe day ȝe schulen offre ten calues, twey rammes, fourtene lambren of o ȝeer with oute wem.
And ȝe schulen halewe riȝtfuli the sacrifices, and moiste offryngis of alle, bi the calues, and rammes, and lambren.
And ȝe schulen offre a buk of geet for synne, with out euerlastynge brent sacrifice, and with out the sacrifice and moiste offryng therof.
In the fyuethe dai ȝe schulen offre nyne calues, twei rammes, fourtene lambren of o ȝeer, with oute wem.
And ȝe schulen halewe riȝtfuli the sacrifices, and moiste offryngis of alle, bi the calues, and rammes, and lambren.
And ȝe schulen offre a buc of geet for synne, with out euerlastynge brent sacrifice, and with out the sacrifice and moiste offryng therof.
In the sixte dai ȝe schulen offre eiȝt calues, and twei rammes, fourtene lambren of o ȝeer with out wem.
And ȝe schulen halewe riȝtfuli the sacrifices, and moiste offryngis of alle, bi the calues, and rammes, and lambren.
And ȝe schulen offre a buk of geet for synne, with out euerlastynge brent sacrifice, and with out the sacrifice and moiste offryng therof.
In the seuenthe dai ȝe schulen offre seuene calues, twei rammes, fourtene lambren of o ȝeer with out wem.
And ȝe schulen halewe riȝtfuli the sacrifices, and moiste offryngis of alle, bi the calues, and rammes, and lambren.
And ȝe schulen offre a buc of geet for synne, with out euerlastynge brent sacrifice, and with out the sacrifice and moiste offryng therof.
In the eiȝthe dai, which is moost solempne ether hooli, ȝe schulen
not do ony seruyle werk, and ȝe schulen offre brent sacrifice in to swettest odour to the Lord, o calf, o ram, seuene lambren of o ȝeer with out wem.
And ȝe schulen halewe riȝtfuli the sacrifices and moiste offryngis of alle, bi the calues, and rammes, and lambren.
And ȝe schulen offre a buc of geet for synne, with out euerlastynge brent sacrifice, and with out the sacrifice, and moiste offryng therof.
Ȝe schulen offre these thingis to the Lord, in ȝoure solempnytees, with out avowis, and wilful offryngis, in brent sacrifice, in sacrifice, in moist offryng, and in peesible sacrifices.
And Moises telde to the sones of Israel alle thingis whiche the Lord comaundide to hym.
And he spak to the princes of the lynagis of the sones of Israel, This is the word, which the Lord comaundide,
If ony of men makith a vowe to the Lord, ethir byndith hym silf bi an ooth, he schal not make voide his word, but he schal fille al thing which he bihiȝte.
If a womman which is in the hows of hir fadir, and is ȝit in the age of a damysel, that is, not ȝit weddid, avowith ony thing, ethir byndith hir silf bi an ooth, if the fadir knowith the avow, which sche bihiȝte, and the ooth bi which sche boond hir soule, and he is stille, sche schal be gilti of the ooth, that is, boundun
bi the ooth; what euer thing sche bihiȝte and swoor, sche schall fille in werk.
Forsothe if the fadir aȝenseide anoon as he herde, bothe the vowis and oothis of hir schulen be voide, and sche schal not be holdun boundun to the biheeste, for the fadir aȝenseide.
If sche hath an hosebonde, and avowith ony thing, and a word goynge out of hir mouth onys
byndith hir soule with an ooth, in what dai the hosebonde herith, and aȝenseith not, sche schal be gilti of avow; sche schal ȝelde, what euer thing sche bihiȝte.
But if the hosebonde herith, and anoon aȝenseith, and makith void alle hir biheestis, and wordis bi whiche sche boond hir soule, the Lord schal be merciful to hir.
A widewe, and a womman forsakun of hir hosebonde, schulen ȝelde, what euer thing thei avowen.
Whanne a wijf in the hous of hir hosebonde byndith hir
silf bi a vow and an ooth, if the hosebonde herith, and is stille and aȝenseith not the biheest, sche schal ȝelde, what euer thing sche bihiȝte.
Sotheli if the hosebonde aȝenseide anoon, sche schal not be holdun gilti of biheest, for the hosebonde aȝenseide, and the Lord schal be merciful to hir.
If sche avowith, and byndith hir silf bi an ooth, that sche turmente hir soule bi fastyng, ethir bi abstynence of othere thingis, it schal be in the doom of the hosebonde, that sche do, ether do not.
That if the hosebonde herith, and is stille, and delaieth the sentence in the tother dai, sche schal ȝelde what euer thing sche avowide and bihiȝte, for he was stille, anoon as he herde.
Forsothe if the hosebonde aȝenseide aftir that he wiste, he schal bere his wickidnesse. These ben the lawis, which the Lord ordeynede to Moyses bitwixe the hosebonde and the wijf, bitwixe the fadir and the douȝtir, which is ȝit in the age of a damysel, that is, not ȝit maried, ether which dwellith in the hows of the fadir.
And the Lord spak to Moyses, and
seide, Venge thou firste the sones of Israel of Madianytis, and so thou schalt be gaderid to thi puple.
And anoon Moises seide, Arme ȝe men of ȝou to batel, that moun take of Madianytis the veniaunce of the Lord.
Of ech lynage be chosun a thousynde men of Israel, that schulen be sent to batel.
And of ech lynage thei ȝauen a thousynde, that is twelue thousynde
of men, redi to batel; whiche Moises sente with Fynees, the sone of Eleazar, preest. And he bitook to hem hooli vesselis, and trumpis to make sown.
And whanne thei hadden fouȝt aȝens Madianytis, and hadden ouercome, thei killiden
alle the malis, and the kyngis of hem, Euy, and Reem, and Sur, and Hur, and Rebe, fyue princes of the folc of hem. Also thei killiden bi swerd Balaam, the sone of Beor.
And thei token the wymmen of hem, and the litle children, and alle beestis, and al purtenaunce of howshold; what euer thei myȝten haue, thei
spuyleden; flawme brente as wel citees, as litle townes and castels.
And they token pray, and alle thingis whiche thei hadden take, as wel of men as of beestis,
and thei brouȝten to Moyses, and to Eleazar, preest, and to al the multitude of the sones of Israel. Forsothe thei baren othere thingis perteynynge to vss, to the castels in the feldi places of Moab bisidis Jordan, aȝens Jericho.
Moises and Eleazar, preest, and alle the princes of the synagoge, ȝeden out in to the comyng of hem, with out the castels, that is, of the tabernacle.
And Moises was wrooth to the princes of the oost, to tribunes, and centuriouns, that camen fro batel;
and he seide, Whi reserueden ȝe wymmen?
whether it be not these that disseyueden the sones of Israel, at the suggestioun of Balaam, and maden ȝou to do trespas aȝens the Lord, on the synne of Phegor, wherfor also the puple was slayn?
And therfor sle ȝe alle men, what euer thing is of male kynde, and litle children; and strangle ȝe the wymmen that
knew men fleischli; forsothe reserue ȝe to ȝou damesels, and alle wymmen virgyns,
and dwelle ȝe with out the castels in seuene daies. He that sleeth a man, ether touchith a slayn man, schal be clensid in the thridde and the seuenthe
dai; and of al the pray, whether it is clooth, ether vessel, and ony thing maad redi in to thingis perteynynge to vss, of the skynnys and heeris of geet, and of tre, it schal be clensid.
And Eleazar, preest, spak thus to the men of the oost that fouȝten, This is the comaundement of the lawe, which the Lord comaundide
to Moises, The gold, and siluer, and bras, and yrun, and tiyn, and leed, and al thing that may passe by flawme, schal be purgid
bi fier; sotheli what euer thing may not suffre fier, schal be halewid bi the watir of clensyng.
And ȝe schulen waische ȝoure clothis in the seuenthe dai, and ȝe schulen be clensid; and aftirward ȝe schulen entre in to the castels of the tabernacle.
And the Lord seide to Moises,
Take ȝe the summe of tho thingis that ben takun, fro man til to beeste, thou, and Eleazar, preest, and alle the princes of the comyn puple.
And thou schalt departe euenli the prey bytwixe hem that fouȝten and ȝeden out to batel, and bitwixe al the multitude.
And thou schalt departe a part to the Lord, of hem that fouȝten, and weren in batel, o soule of fiue hundrid, as wel of men, as of oxun, and of assis, and of scheep.
And thou schalt ȝyue that part to Eleazar, preest, for tho ben the firste fruytis of the Lord.
Also of the myddil part of the sones of Israel, thou schalt take the fiftithe heed of men, and of oxun, and of assis, and of scheep, and of alle lyuynge beestis; and thou schalt ȝyue tho to the dekenes, that waken in the kepyngis of the tabernacle of the Lord.
And Moyses and Eleazar diden, as the Lord comaundide.
Forsothe the prey which the oost hadde take, was sixe hundrid fyue and seuenti thousynde of
scheep, of oxun two and seuenti thousynde,
of assis sixti thousynde and a thousynde;
the soules of persones of femal kynde, that knewen not fleischli men, two and thretti thousynde.
And the myddil part was ȝouun to hem that weren in the batel, of scheep thre hundrid seuene and thretti thousynde and fyue hundrid;
of whiche sixe hundrid fyue and seuenti scheep weren noumbrid in to the part of
the Lord; and of sixe and thretti thousynde
oxun, two and seuenti oxun, and of thretti thousynde assis and fyue hundryd,
oon and sixti assis; of sixtene thousynde persoones of men, twei and thretti persoones bifelden in to the part of the Lord.
And Moises bitook the noumbre of the firste fruytis of the Lord to Eleazar, preest, as it was comaundid
to hym, of the myddil part of the sones of Israel, which he departide to hem that weren in batel.
And of the myddil part that bifelde to the tother multitude, that is, of thre hundrid seuene and thretti thousynde scheep and fyue hundrid,
of sixe and thretti thousynde oxun,
and of thretti thousynde assis and fyue hundrid,
and of sixtene thousynde wymmen,
Moyses took the fyftithe heed, and ȝaf to the dekenes, that wakiden in the tabernacle of the Lord, as the Lord comaundide.
And whanne the princes of the oost, and the tribunes and centuriouns hadden
neiȝed to Moises, thei seiden, We thi seruauntis han teld the noumbre of fiȝters, whiche we hadden vndur oure hoond, and
sotheli not oon failide; for which cause we offren in the fre ȝiftis of the Lord, alle bi vs silf, that that we myȝten fynde of gold in the pray, girdelis for the myddil of wymmen, and bies of the armes, and ryngis, and ournementis of the arm nyȝ the hond, and bies of the neckis of wymmen, that thou preye the Lord for vs.
And Moises and Eleazar, preest, token al
the gold in dyuerse spices, ether kyndis, bi the weiȝte of the seyntuarye, sixtene thousynde seuene hundrid and fifti siclis, of the tribunes, and centuriouns.
For that that ech man rauyschide in the prey,
was his owne; and thei baren the gold taken in to the tabernacle of witnessyng, in to the mynde of the sones of Israel, bifor the Lord.
Forsothe the sones of Ruben and of Gad hadden many beestis, and catel with out noumbre was to hem, in werk beestis. And whanne thei hadden seyn Jazer and Galaad, couenable londis to beestis to be
fed, thei camen to Moyses and Eleazar, preest, and to the princes of the multitude,
and seiden, Astaroth, and Dibon, and Jacer, and Nemra, Esebon, and Eleale,
and Sabam, and Nebo, and Beon, the lond which the Lord smoot in the siȝt of the sones of Israel, is of moost plenteuous cuntrey to the pasture of beestis; and we
thi seruauntis han ful many beestis; and we preyen, if we han founde grace bifor thee, that thou ȝyue to vs thi seruauntis that cuntrey in to possessioun, and make not vs to passe Jordan.
To whiche Moises answeride, Whether ȝoure britheren schulen go to batel, and ȝe schulen sitte here?
Whi peruerten ȝe the soulis of Israel, that thei doren not passe in to the place, which the Lord schal ȝyue to hem?
Whether ȝoure fadris diden not so, whanne Y sente fro Cades Barne to aspie the
lond, and whanne thei camen to the valey of Clustre, whanne al the cuntrey was cumpassid, thei peruertiden the herte of the sones of Israel, that thei entriden not in to the coostis, whiche the Lord ȝaf to
hem. And the Lord was wrooth, and
swoor, seiynge, Thes men that stieden fro Egipt, fro twenti ȝeer and aboue, schulen not se the lond which Y bihiȝte vndur an ooth to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
and nolden sue me, outakun Caleph, Cenezei, the sone of Jephone, and Josue, the sone of Nun; these tweyne filliden my wille.
And the Lord was wrooth aȝens Israel, and ledde hym aboute the deseert bi fourti ȝeer, til al the generacioun was wastid, that hadde do yuel in the siȝt of the Lord.
And Moyses seide, Lo! ȝe encressyngis, and nurreis, ether nurschid children, of synful men, han ryse for ȝoure fadris, that ȝe schulden encreesse the strong veniaunce of the Lord aȝens Israel.
That if ȝe nylen sue the Lord, in the wildirnesse he schal forsake the puple, and ȝe schulen be cause of the deeth of alle men.
And thei neiȝiden nyȝ, and seiden, We schulen make foldis of scheep, and the stablis of beestis, and we schulen make strengthid citees to oure litle children.
Forsothe we vs silf schulen be armed to defence, and schulen be gird with armeris to asailyng, and schulen go to batel bifor the sones of Israel, til we bryngen hem in to her places; oure litle children and what euer thing we moun haue, schulen be in strengthid cytees, for the tresouns of the dwelleris.
We schulen not turne aȝen in to oure housis, til the sones of Israel welden her
eritage; and we schulen not axe ony thing ouer Jordan, for we han now oure possessioun in the eest coost therof.
To whiche Moises seide, If ȝe doen that, that ȝe biheten, be ȝe maad redi, and go ȝe to batel
bifor the Lord; and ech man fiȝtere be armed, and passe Jordan, til the Lord
distrye hise enemyes, and al the lond be maad suget to hym; thanne ȝe schulen be giltles anentis God, and anentis Israel, and ȝe schulen holde the cuntreys, whiche ȝe wolen, bifor the Lord.
But if ȝe doon not that, that ye seien, it is not doute to ony man, that ne ȝe synnen aȝens God; and wite ȝe, that ȝoure synne schal take ȝou.
Therfor bilde ȝe citees to ȝoure litle children, and foldis and stablis to scheep, and to beestis; and fille ȝe that, that ȝe bihiȝten.
And the sones of Gad and of Ruben seiden to Moises, We ben thi seruauntis; we schulen do that, that oure lord comaundith.
We schulen leeue oure litle children, and wymmen, and scheep,
and beestis in the citees of Galaad; forsothe alle we thi seruauntis schulen go redi to batel, as thou, lord, spekist.
Therfor Moyses comaundide to Eleazar, preest, and to Josue, the sone of Nun, and to the princes of meynees, bi the lynagis of Israel,
and seide to hem, If the sones of Gad, and the sones of Ruben goen alle armed with ȝou, to batel bifor the Lord, and the lond be maad suget to ȝou, ȝyue
ȝe to hem Galaad in to possessioun; but if thei nylen passe with ȝou in to the lond of Chanaan, take thei places to dwelle among ȝou.
And the sones of Gad and the sones of Ruben answeriden, As the Lord spak to hise seruauntis, so we
schulen do; we schulen go armed bifor the Lord, in to the lond of Chanaan, and we knowlechen, that we han take now possessioun ouer Jordan.
And so Moises ȝaf to the sones of Gad and of Ruben, and to half the lynage of Manasses, sone of Joseph, the rewme of Seon, kyng of Ammorey, and the rewme of Og, kyng of Basan, and the lond of hem, with her citees, bi cumpas.
Therfor the sones of Gad bildiden Dibon, and Astaroth, and
Aroer, and Roth-Sophan, and Jazer, and
Jebaa, and Beeth-Nemra, and Betharan, strengid citees; and foldis to her beestis.
Forsothe the sones of Ruben bildiden Esebon, and Eleale, and Cariathiarym,
and Nabo, and Balmeon, whanne the names weren turned, and thei bildiden Sabama; and puttiden names to the citees, whiche thei hadden bildid.
Forsothe the sones of Machir, sone of Manasses, ȝeden in to Galaad, and distrieden it, and killiden Ammorei, enhabitere therof.
Therfor Moises ȝaf the lond of Galaad to Machir, sone of Manasses, which Machir dwellide ther ynne.
Forsothe Jair, the sone of Manasses, ȝede, and occupiede the townes therof, whiche he clepide Anochiair, that is, the townes of Jair.
Also Nobe ȝede, and took Canath, with hise townes, and clepide it, bi his name, Nobe.
These ben the dwellyngis of the sones of Israel, that ȝeden out of the lond of Egipt, bi her cumpenyes, in the hond of
Moises and of Aaron; whiche dwellyngis Moises discriuede bi the places of tentis, that weren chaungid bi comaundement of the Lord.
Therfor the sones of Israel ȝeden forth in an hiȝ hond fro Ramesses, in the firste monethe, in the fiftenthe dai of the firste monethe, in the tother dai of pask, while alle Egipcians
sien, and birieden the firste gendrid children, whiche the Lord hadde slayn; for the Lord hadde take veniaunce also on the goddis of hem.
The sones of Israel
settiden tentis in Socoth, and fro Sochoth thei camen into Etham, which is in the laste coostis of the wildirnesse;
fro thennus thei ȝeden out, and camen aȝens Phiayroth, whiche biholdith Beelsephon, and settiden tentis bifor Magdalun.
And thei ȝeden forth fro Phiairoth, and passiden bi the myddil see in to the wildirnesse, and thei ȝeden thre daies bi the deseert of Ethan, and settiden tentis in Mara.
And thei ȝeden forth fro Mara, and camen in to Helym, where weren twelue wellis of watir, and seuenti palm trees; and there thei settiden tentis.
But also thei ȝeden out fro thennus, and settiden tentis on the Reed See. And
thei ȝeden forth fro the Reed See, and settiden
tentis in the deseert of Syn, fro whennus thei ȝeden out, and camen in to Depheca.
And thei ȝeden forth fro Depheca, and settiden tentis in Haluys.
And thei ȝeden forth fro Haluys, and settiden tentis in Raphidyn, where watir failide to the puple to drinke.
And thei ȝeden forth fro Raphidyn, and settiden tentis in the deseert of Synai.
But also thei ȝeden out of the wildirnesse of Synay, and camen to the Sepulcris of Coueitise.
And thei ȝeden forth fro the Sepulcris of Coueytise, and settiden tentis in Asseroth.
And fro Asseroth thei camen in to Rethma.
And thei ȝeden forth fro Rethma, and settiden tentis in Remon
Phares; fro whennus thei ȝeden forth, and camen in to Lemphna.
And fro Lemphna thei settiden tentis in Ressa.
And thei ȝeden out fro Ressa, and camen into Celatha; fro whennus thei ȝeden forth, and settiden tentis in the hil of Sepher.
Thei ȝeden out fro the hil of
Sepher, and camen in to Arada; fro thennus thei ȝeden forth, and settiden tentis in Maceloth.
And thei ȝeden forth fro Maceloth, and camen in to Caath.
Fro Caath thei settiden tentis
in Thare; fro whennus thei ȝeden out, and settiden tentis in Methcha.
And fro Methcha thei settiden tentis in Esmona.
And thei ȝeden forth fro Asmona, and
camen in to Moseroth; and fro Moseroth thei settiden tentis in Benalachan.
And thei ȝeden forth fro Benalachan, and
camen in to the hil of Galgad; fro whennus thei ȝeden forth, and settiden tentis in Jethebacha.
And fro Jethebacha thei camen in to Ebrona.
And thei ȝeden out fro Ebrona, and settiden tentis in
Asiongaber; fro thennus thei ȝeden forth, and camen in to deseert of Syn; this is Cades.
And thei ȝeden fro Cades, and thei settiden tentis in the hil of Hor, in the laste coostis of the lond of Edom.
And Aaron, the preest, stiede in to the hil of Hor, for the Lord comaundide, and there he was deed, in the fourti ȝeer of the goyng out of the sones of Israel fro Egipt, in the fyuethe monethe, in the
firste dai of the monethe; whanne he was of an hundrid and thre and twenti ȝeer.
And Chanaan, kyng of Arad, that dwellide at the south, in the lond of Canaan, herde that the sones of Israel camen.
And thei ȝeden forth fro the hil of Hor,
and settiden tentis in Salmona; fro thennus thei ȝeden forth, and camen in to Phynon.
And thei ȝeden forth fro Phynon, and settiden tentis in Oboth.
And fro Oboth thei camen in to Neabarym, that is, into the wildirnesse of Abarym, which is in the endis of Moabitis.
And thei ȝeden forth fro Neabarym, and thei
settiden tentis in Dibon of Gad; fro whennus thei ȝeden forth, and settiden tentis in Helmon of Deblathaym.
And thei ȝeden out fro Helmon of Deblathaym, and camen to the hillis of Abarym, aȝens Nabo.
And thei ȝeden forth fro the hillis of Abarym, and passiden to the feeldi places of Moab, ouer Jordan, aȝens Jericho.
And there thei settiden tentis, fro Bethsymon til to Belsathym, in the
pleynere places of Moabitis, where the Lord spak to Moises,
Comaunde thou to the sones of Israel, and seie thou to hem, Whanne ȝe han passid Jordan, and han entrid in to the
lond of Canaan, distrie ȝe alle the dwelleris of that cuntrey; breke ȝe the titlis, that is, auteris, and dryue ȝe to poudre the ymagis, and distrie ȝe alle heiȝ
thingis, and clense ȝe the lond, and alle men dwellynge thereynne. For Y ȝaf to
ȝou that lond into possessioun whiche ȝe schulen departe to ȝou bi lot; to mo men ȝe schulen ȝyue largere lond, and to fewere men streytere lond, as lot fallith to alle men, so eritage schal be ȝouun; possessioun schal be departid bi lynagis and meynees.
But if ȝe nylen sle the dwelleris of the lond, thei, that abiden, schulen be to ȝou as nailes in the iȝen, and speris in the sidis, that is, deedli aduersaries; and thei schulen be aduersaries to ȝou in
the lond of ȝoure abitacioun; and what euer thing Y thouȝte to do to hem, Y schal do to ȝou.
And the Lord spak to
Moises, and seide, Comaunde thou to the sones of Israel, and thou schalt seie to hem, Whanne ȝe han entrid in to the lond of Canaan, and it bifelde in to possessioun to ȝou bi lot, it schal be endid bi these endis.
The south part schal bigynne at the wildirnesse of Syn, which is bisidis Edom, and it schal haue termes aȝens
the eest, the saltiste see, whiche termes schulen cumpasse the south coost bi the stiynge of Scorpioun, that is, of an hil clepid Scorpioun, so that tho passe in to Senna, and come to the south, til to Cades Barne; fro whennus the coostis schulen go out to the town, Abdar bi name, and schulen strecche forth til to
Asemona; and the terme schal go bi cumpas fro Assemona til to the stronde of Egipt, and it schal be endid bi the brynke of the grete see.
Forsothe the west coost schal bigynne at the greet see, and schal be closid bi that ende.
Sotheli at the north coost, the termes schulen bigynne at the greet see, and schulen come til to
the hiȝeste hil, fro which tho schulen come in to Emath, til to the termes of
Sedada; and the coostis schulen go til to Ephrona, and the town of Enan. These schulen be the termes in the north part.
Fro thennus thei schulen mete coostis aȝens the eest coost, fro the
town Henan til to Sephama; and fro Sephama termes schulen go doun in to Reblatha, aȝens the welle of Daphnyn; fro thennus tho schulen come aȝens the
eest to the se of Cenereth; and tho schulen strecche forth til to Jordan, and at the laste tho schulen be closid with the salteste see. Ȝe schulen haue this lond bi hise coostis in cumpas.
And Moises comaundide to the sones of Israel, and seide, This schal be the lond which ȝe schulen welde bi lot, and which the Lord comaundide to be ȝouun to nyne lynagis
and to the half lynage; for the lynage of the sones of Ruben, bi her meynees, and the lynage of the sones of Gad, bi kynrede and noumbre, and half the lynage of
Manasses, that is, twey lynagis and an half, han take her part ouer Jordan, aȝens Jerico, at the eest coost.
And the Lord
seide to Moises, These ben the names of men that schulen departe the lond to ȝou, Eleazar, preest, and Josue, the sone of
Nun, and of each lynage, o prynce;
of whiche these ben the names, of the lynage
of Juda, Caleph, the sone of Jephone; of the lynage of Symeon, Samuhel, the sone
of Amyud; of the lynage of Beniamyn,
Heliad, sone of Casselon; of the lynage of the sones of Dan, Bochi, sone of Jogli;
of the sones of Joseph, of the lynage of
Manasses, Hamyel, sone of Ephoth; of the lynage of Effraym, Camuhel, sone of
Septhan; of the lynage of Zabulon, Elisaphan,
sone of Pharnat; of the lynage of Isacar, duyk Phaltiel, the sone of Ozan;
of the lynage of Azer, Abyud, the sone of
Salomy; of the lynage of Neptalym, Fedahel, the sone of Amyud.
These men it ben, to whiche the Lord comaundide, that thei schulden departe to the sones of Israel the lond of Chanaan.
And the Lord spak these thingis to Moises, in the feeldi places of Moab, aboue
Jordan, aȝens Jericho, Comaunde thou to the sones of Israel, that thei ȝyue to dekenes
of her possessiouns, citees to dwelle, and the suburbabis of tho bi cumpas, that thei dwelle in the citees, and the suburbabis be to beestis, and
werk beestis; whiche suburbabis schulen be strecchid forth fro the wallis of citees with outforth bi cumpas, in the
space of a thousynde paacis; aȝens the eest schulen be two thousynde cubitis, and aȝens the south in lijk manere schulen be two thousynde cubitis, and at the see that biholdith to the west schal be the same mesure, and the north coost schal be endid bi euene terme. And the citees schulen be in the myddis, and the suburbabis with outforth.
Forsothe of tho citees whiche ȝe schulen ȝyue to dekenes, sixe schulen be departid in to helpis of fugityues, ether of fleynge men, that he that schedde blood, fle to tho; and outakun these sixe, ȝe schulen ȝyue to
dekenes othere two and fourti citees, that is, to gidere eiȝte and fourti, with her surburbabis.
And tho citees that schulen be ȝouun of the possessiouns of sones of Israel, schulen be takun awey, mo fro hem that han more, and fewere schulen be takun awey fro hem that han lesse, alle bi hem silf schulen ȝyue bi the mesure of her eritage, citees to dekenes.
The Lord
seide to Moises, Spek thou to the sones of Israel, and thou schalt seie to hem, Whanne ȝe han passid Jordan, in the lond
of Canaan, deme ȝe whiche citees owen to be in to the helpis of fugityues, whiche not wilfuli han sched blood.
In whiche whanne the fleere hath fled, the kynesman of hym that is slayn, schal not mow sle hym, til he stonde in the siȝt of the multitude, and the cause of hym be demed.
Forsothe of tho citees that ben departid
to the helpis of fugityues, thre schulen be ouer Jordan, and thre in the lond of
Canaan; as wel to the sones of Israel as to comelyngis and pilgryms; that he fle to tho citees, that schedde blood not wilfuli.
If ony man smytith a man with yrun, and he that is smytun is deed, the smyter schal be gilti of mansleyng, and he schal die.
If he castith a stoon, and a man is deed bi the strook, he schal be punyschid in lijk maner.
If a man smytun with a staf dieth, he schal be vengid bi the blood of the smytere.
The niȝ kynesman of hym that is slayn schal sle the mansleere; anoon as he takith hym, that is, the manquellere, he schal sle hym.
If bi haterede a man hurtlith, ethir schoufith, a man, ethir castith ony
thing in to hym bi aspiyngis, ether whanne he was enemy, smoot with hond, and he is deed, the smytere schal be gilti of mansleyng. The kynesman of him that is slayn, anoon as he findith him, that is, the sleere, schal sle hym.
That if bi sudeyn caas, and without
hatrede and enemytees, he doith ony
thing of these; and this is preued in heryng of the puple, and the questioun of blood is discussid bitwixe the smytere
and the kynesman, the innocent schal be delyuered fro the hond of the vengere, and bi sentence of iugis he schal be led aȝen in to the citee, to which he fledde, and he schal dwelle there, til the grete preest die, which is anoyntid with oile.
If the sleere is foundun with out the coostis of the citees that ben asigned to exilid
men, and is slayn of him that is vengere, he that sleeth him, that is, the exilid man,
schal be with out gilt; for the exilid man ouȝte sitte in the citee til to the deth of the bischop; forsothe aftir that thilke bischop is deed, the mansleere schal turne aȝen in to his lond.
