These schulen be euerlastynge and lawful thingis in alle ȝoure dwellyngis.
A mansleere schal be punyschid vndur witnessis; no man schal be dampned at the witnessyng of o man.
Ȝe schulen not take prijs of him which is gilti of blood, anoon and he schal die.
Men exilid, and fugityues, schulen not mow turne aȝen in ony maner in to her citees, bifore the deeth of the bischop,
lest ȝe defoulen the lond of ȝoure abitacioun, which is defoulid bi the blood of innocent men; and it may not be clensid in other maner, no but bi the blood of hym, that schedde the blood of anothir man.
And so ȝoure possessioun schal be clensid, for Y schal dwelle with ȝou; for Y am the Lord, that dwelle among the sones of Israel.
Forsothe and the princes of the meynees of Galaad sone of Machir, sone of Manasses, of the generacioun of the sones of Joseph, neiȝiden, and spaken to Moises
bifor the princes of Israel, and seiden, The Lord comaundide to thee oure lord, that thou schuldist departe the lond bi lot to the sones of Israel, and that thou schuldist ȝyue to the douȝtris of Salphaat, oure brothir, possessioun due to the fadir.
And if men of anothir lynage schulen take to wyues these douȝtris, her possessioun schal sue, and it schal be translatid to anothir lynage, and schal be decreessid
fro oure eritage; and so it schal be doon, that whanne the iubilee, that is, the fiftithe ȝeer of remyssioun, cometh, the departyng of lottis be schent, and that the possessioun of othere men passe to othere men.
Moises answeride to the sones of Israel, and seide, for the Lord comaundide, The lynage of the sones of Joseph spak riȝtfuli,
and this lawe is denounsid of the Lord on the douȝtris of Salphaat; be thei weddid to whiche men thei wolen,
oneli to the men of her lynage; lest the possessioun of the sones of Joseph be meddlid fro lynage in to lynage. For alle men schulen wedde wyues of her lynage
and kynrede; and alle wymmen schulen take hosebondis of the same lynage, that
the erytage dwelle in meynees, and lynagis be not meddlid to hem silf, but
dwelle so, as tho ben departid of the Lord. And the douȝtris of Salphaat diden, as it was comaundid to hem.
And Maala, and Thersa, and Egla, and Melcha, and Noha, weren weddid to the sones of her
fadris brother, of the meynee of Manaasses, that was the sone of Joseph, and the possessioun that was ȝouun to hem, dwellide in the lynage and meynee of her fadir.
These ben the comaundementis and domes, whiche the Lord comaundide, bi the hond of Moyses, to the sones of Israel, in the feeldi places of Moab, aboue Jordan, aȝens Jericho.
THESE ben the wordis whiche Moyses spak to al Israel ouer Jordan, in the wildirnesse of the feeld, aȝens the reed see, bitwix Pharan and Tophel and Laban and Asseroth, where is ful myche gold,
by enleuene daies fro Oreb bi the weie of the hil of Seir, til to Cades Barne.
In the fortithe ȝeer, in the enleuenth monethe, in the firste dai of the monethe, Moises spak to the sones of Israel alle thingis whiche the Lord commandide to hym that he
schulde seie to hem, after that he smoot Seon, kyng of Ammorreis, that dwellide in Esebon, and Og, the kyng of Basan, that dwelide in Asseroth and in Edray, ouer Jordan, in the lond of Moab.
And Moyses bigan to declare the lawe, and to
seie, Oure Lord God spak to vs in Oreb, and seide, It suffisith to ȝou that ȝe han
dwellid in this hil; turne ȝe aȝen, and come ȝe to the hil of Amorreis, and to othere placis that ben next it; to places of feeldis, and of hillis, and to lowere places aȝens the south, and bisidis the brenke of the see, to the lond of Cananeys, and of Liban, til to the greet
flood Eufrates. Lo, he seith, Y haue ȝoue to ȝou; entre ȝe, and welde ȝe that lond on which the Lord swoor to ȝoure fadrys, Abraham, Ysaac, and Jacob, that he schulde ȝyue it to hem, and to her seed after hem.
And Y seide to ȝou in that time,
Y may not aloone susteyne ȝou, for ȝoure Lord God hath multiplied ȝou, and ȝe ben ful
many to dai, as the sterris of heuene; the Lord God of ȝoure fadris adde to this noumbre many thousyndis, and blesse ȝou, as he spak.
Y may not aloone susteyne ȝoure causis, and birthun, and stryues;
ȝyue ȝe of ȝou men wise in dyuyn thingis, and witti in mennus thingis worthi to be don, whose conuersacioun is preued in ȝoure lynagis, that Y sette hem princes to ȝou.
Thanne ȝe answeriden to me, The thing is good which thou wolt do.
And Y took of ȝoure lynagis men wise and noble, in vertues and kyn; and Y ordeynede hem princis, tribunes, and centuryouns, and quynquagenaries, and denys, whiche schulden teche ȝou all thingis.
And Y comaundide to hem, and seide, Here ȝe hem, and deme ȝe that that is iust, whether he be a citeseyn, whether a pilgrym.
No difference schal be of persones; ȝe schulen here so a litil man, that is, pore, as a greet man, nether ȝe schulen take the persoone of ony man, for it is the doom of God. That if ony thing semeth hard to ȝou, telle ȝe to me, and Y schal here.
And Y comaundide alle thingis whiche ȝe ouȝten to do.
Forsothe we ȝeden forth fro Oreb, and passiden bi a feerdful deseert, and grettiste wildirnesse, which ȝe sien, bi the weye of the hil of Ammorrey, as oure Lord God comaundide to vs. And whanne we hadden
come in to Cades Barne, Y seide to ȝou, Ȝe ben comen to the hil of Ammorrey, which ȝoure Lord God schal ȝyue to ȝou; se thou the lond which thi
Lord God schal ȝyue to thee; stie thou, and welde it, as oure Lord God spak to thi fadris; nyle thou drede, nether drede thou in herte ony thing.
And alle ȝe neiȝiden to me, and ȝe seiden, Sende we men, that schulen biholde the lond, and telle to vs bi what weye we owen stie, and to whiche citees we owen to go.
And whanne the word pleside to me, Y sente of ȝou twelue men, of ech lynage oon.
And whanne thei hadden go, and hadden stied in to the hilli places, thei camen til to the valei of Clustre; and whanne thei
hadden biholde the lond, thei token of the fruytis therof, to schewe the plentee, and brouȝten to vs, and seiden, The lond is good which oure Lord God schal ȝyue to vs.
And ȝe nolden stie, but ȝe weren vnbileueful to the word of oure Lord God.
And ȝe grutchiden in ȝoure tabernaclis, and ȝe seiden, The Lord hatith vs, and herfor he ledde vs out of the lond of Egipt, that he schulde bitake vs in the hond of Ammorey, and schulde do awei vs.
Whidur schulen we stie? the messangeris maden aferd oure herte, and seiden, A grettiste multitude is, and largere in stature than we; the citees ben greete, and wallid til to the heuene; we sien there the sones of Enachym, that is, giauntis.
And Y seide to ȝou, Nyle ȝe drede with ynne, nether drede withoutforth;
the Lord God hym silf, which is ȝoure ledere, schal fiȝte for ȝou, as he dide in Egipt, while alle men sien.
And ȝe sien in the wildirnesse, thi Lord God bar thee, as a man is wont to bere his litil sone, in al the weie bi which ȝe ȝeden til ȝe camen to this place.
And sotheli nether so ȝe bileueden to ȝoure Lord God,
that ȝede bifor ȝou in the weie, and mesuride the place in which ȝe ouȝten to sette tentis, and schewide in nyȝt the weie to ȝou bi fier, and in dai bi a piler of cloude.
And whanne the Lord hadde herd the vois of ȝoure wordis, he was
wrooth, and swoor, and seide, Noon of the men of this werste generacioun schal se the good lond, which Y bihiȝte vndur
an ooth to ȝoure fadris, outakun Caleph, the sone of Jephone; for he schal se it, and Y schal ȝyue to hym the lond on which he trad, and to hise sones, for he suede the Lord.
Nether the indignacioun aȝens the puple is wondirful, sithen the Lord was wrooth also to me for ȝou, and
seide, Nether thou schalt entre thidur, but Josue, the sone of Nun, thi mynystre, he schal entre for thee; excyte and strengthe thou him, and he schal departe the lond bi lot to Israel.
Ȝoure litle children, of whiche ȝe seiden, that thei schulden be led prisoneris, and the sones that kunnen not to dai the diuersite of good and of yuel, thei schulen entre; and Y schal ȝyue to hem the lond, and thei schulen welde it.
Sotheli turne ȝe aȝen, and go ȝe in to the wildirnesse, bi the weie of the Reed See.
And ȝe answeriden to me, We synneden to the Lord; we schulen stie, and we schulen fiȝte, as oure Lord God comaundide. And whanne ȝe weren arayed with armeris, and ȝeden
into the hil, the Lord seide to me, Seie thou to hem, Nyle ȝe stye, nether fiȝte ȝe, for Y am not with ȝou, lest ȝe fallen bifor ȝoure enemyes.
Y spak, and ȝe herden not; but ȝe weren aduersaries to the comaundement of the Lord, and bolnden with prijde, and stieden in to the hil.
Therfor Ammorrey ȝede out, that dwellide in the hillis, and he cam aȝens ȝou, and pursuede ȝou, as bees ben wont to pursue, and killide fro Seir til Horma.
And whanne ȝe turneden aȝen, and wepten bifor the Lord, he herde not ȝou, nether
wolde asente to ȝoure vois; therfor ȝe saten in Cades Barne bi myche tyme.
And we ȝeden forth fro thennus, and camen in to the wildirnesse that ledith to the Reed See, as the Lord seide to me; and we cumpassiden the hil of Seir in long tyme.
And the Lord seide to me,
It sufficith to ȝou to cumpasse this hil; go ȝe aȝens the north.
And comaunde thou to the puple, and seie, Ȝe schulen passe bi the termes of ȝoure britheren, the sones of Esau, that dwellen in Seir, and thei schulen drede ȝou.
Therfor se ȝe diligentli, that ȝe be not moued aȝens hem; for Y schal not ȝyue to ȝou of the land of hem as myche as the steppe of o foot may trede, for Y ȝaf the hil of Seir in to the possessioun of Esau.
Ȝe schulden bie of hem metis for money, and ȝe schulen ete; ȝe schulden drawe, and drynke watir bouȝt.
Thi Lord God blesside thee in al the werk of thin hondis; he knewe thi weye, hou thou passidist this moste wildirnesse, bi fourti ȝeer; and thi Lord God dwellide with thee, and no thing failide to thee.
And whanne we hadden passid bi oure britheren, the sones of Esau, that dwelliden in Seir, bi the weie of the feeld of Elath, and of Asiongaber, we camen to the weie that ledith in to deseert of Moab.
And the Lord seide to me, Fiȝte thou not aȝens Moabitis, nether bigyn thou batel aȝens hem, for Y schal not ȝyue to thee ony thing of the lond of hem, for Y ȝaf Ar in to possessioun to the sones of Loth.
Emyn, that is, griseful men, weren first dwelleris therof, a greet puple, and strong, and so hiȝ, that thei weren
bileued as giantis, of the generacioun of Enachym, and thei weren lijk the sones of Enachym; forsothe Moabitis clepen hem Emyn.
Forsothe Horreis dwelliden bifore in Seir, and whanne thei weren put out, and weren doon awey, the sones of Esau dwelliden there, as Israel dide in the lond of his possessioun, which the Lord ȝaf to hym.
Therfor we riseden, that we schulden passe the stronde of Zared, and camen to it.
Sotheli the tyme in whiche we ȝeden fro Cades Barne til to the passynge of the stronde of Zared, was of eiȝte and thretti ȝeer, til al the generacioun of men fiȝteris was wastid fro the castels, as the Lord hadde swore;
whos hond was aȝens hem, that thei schulden perische fro the myddis of the castels.
Forsothe after that alle the fiȝteris felden
doun, the Lord spak to me, and seide,
Thou schalt passe to dai the termes of
Moab, the cytee, Ar bi name, and thou schalt neiȝ in the nyȝ coost of the sones of Amon; be thou war that thou fiȝte not aȝens hem, nether be moued to batel; for Y schal not ȝyue to thee of the lond of the sones of Amon, for Y ȝaf it to the sones of Loth in to possessioun.
It is arettid the lond of giauntis, and giauntis enhabitiden therynne sumtyme, whiche giauntis
Amonytis clepen Zonym; a myche puple and greet, and of noble lengthe, as Enachym, whiche the Lord dide awey fro the
face of hem, and made hem to dwelle for tho giauntis, as he dide to the sones of Esau, that dwellen in Seire, and dide awai Horreis, and ȝaf to hem the lond of Horreis, which the sones of Esau welden til in to present tyme.
Also men of Capadocie puttiden out Eueys, that dwelliden in Asseryn, til to Gaza; which ȝeden out fro Capadocie, and diden awey Eueis, and dwelliden for hem.
Rise ȝe, and passe ȝe the stronde of Arnon; lo! Y haue bitake in thin hond Seon, king of Esebon, of Amorreis; and his lond bigynne thou to welde, and smyte thou batel aȝens him.
To dai Y schal bigynne to sende thi drede and strengthe in to puplis that dwellen vndir al heuene, that whanne thi name is herd, thei drede, and tremble bi the maner of wymmen trauelynge of child, and be holdun with sorewe.
Therfor Y sente messangeris fro the wildirnesse of Cademoch to Seon, kyng of Esebon; and Y
seide with pesible wordis, We schulen passe thorou thi lond, we schulen go in the comyn weie; we schulen not bowe nether to the riȝt side, nether to the left side.
Sille thow metis to vs for prijs, that we ete; ȝif thow watir for money, and so we schulen drynke. Oneli it is
that thou graunte passage to vs, as the sones of Esau diden, that dwellen in Seir, and as Moabitis diden, that dwellen in Ar, til we comen to Jordan, and passen to the lond which oure Lord God schal ȝyue to vs.
And Seon, kyng of Esebon, nolde ȝyue passage to vs; for thi Lord God made hard his spirit, and made sad in yuel the herte of hym, that he schulde be bitakun in to thin hondis, as thou seest now.
And the Lord seide to me, Lo, Y bigan to bitake to thee Seon, and his lond; bigynne thou to welde it.
And Seon ȝede out aȝens vs with al his puple to batel in Jasa.
And oure Lord God bitook hym to vs, and we han smyte hym with hise sones, and al his puple.
And we token in that tyme alle the citees, whanne the dwelleris of tho citees, men, and wymmen, and children weren slayn;
we leften not in hem ony thing, outakun beestis that camen in to the part of men takynge prey, and outakun spuylis of the cytees whiche we tokun.
Fro Aroer, which is on the brenke of the stronde of Arnon, fro the toun which is set in the valey, til to Galaad, no town was ether citee, that ascapide oure hondis.
Oure Lord God bitook alle to vs; outakun the lond of the sones of Amon, to which lond we neiȝiden not, and outakun alle thingis that liggen to the stronde of Jeboth, and outakun the citees of the munteyns, and alle places fro whiche oure Lord God forbeed vs.
And so we turneden, and stieden bi the weie of Basan; and Og, the kyng of Basan, ȝede out aȝens vs with his puple, to fiȝte in Edrai.
And the Lord seide to me, Drede thou not hym, for he is bitakun in thin hond, with al his puple, and his lond; and thou schalt do to hym, as thou didist to Seon, kyng of Ammoreis, that dwellide in Esebon.
Therfor oure Lord God bitook in oure hondis also Og, kyng of Basan, and al his puple; and we han
smyte hym til to deeth, and wastiden alle the citees of him in o tyme; no town was that ascapide vs; we destrieden sixti citees, al the cuntrei of Argob, of the rewme of Og in Basan.
Alle the citees weren strengthid with hiȝest wallis, and with ȝatis and barris; with out townes vnnoumbrable, that hadden not wallis.
And we diden awey thilke men, as we diden to Seon, kyng of Esebon; and we losten ech citee, and men, and wymmen, and
litle children; forsothe we token bi prey beestis, and the spuylis of citees.
And we token in that tyme the lond fro the hond of twey kyngis of Ammorreis, that weren biȝonde Jordan, fro the stronde of
Arnon til to the hil of Hermon, which hil Sidonyes clepen Sarion, and Ammorreis clepen Sanyr.
We tooken alle the citees that weren set in the pleyn, and al the lond of Galaad, and of Basan, til to Selcha and Edray, citees of the rewme of Og, in Basan.
For Og aloone, kyng of Basan, was left of the generacioun of giauntis; and his yrun bed is schewid, which is in Rabath, of the sones of Amon, and hath nyne cubitis of lengthe, and foure cubitis of breede, at the mesure of a cubit of mannus hond.
And we weldiden in that tyme the lond, fro Aroer, which is on the brynke of the stronde of Arnon, til to the myddil paart of the hil of Galaad; and Y ȝaf the citees of hym to Ruben and Gad.
Forsothe Y ȝaf the tother part of Galaad, and al Basan, of the rewme of Og, to the half lynage of Manasses, and al the cuntrei of Argob. Al Basan was clepid the lond of giauntis.
Jair, sone of Manasses, weldide al the cuntrey of Argob, til to the lond of Gesuri and of Machati; and he clepide bi his name Basan Anothiair, that is, the townes of Jair, til in to present dai.
Also Y ȝaf Galaad to Machir;
and to the lynagis of Ruben and of Gad Y ȝaf the lond of Galaad, til to the strond of Arnon, the myddil of the stronde, and of the endis til to the stronde of Jeboth, which is the terme of the sones of Amon.
And Y ȝaf the pleyn of the wildernesse til to Jordan, and the termes of Cenereth til to the see of deseert, which see is moost salt, at the rotis of the hil of Phasga, aȝens the eest.
And Y comaundide to ȝou in that tyme, and seide, Ȝoure Lord God ȝyueth to ȝou this lond
in to erytage; alle ȝe stronge men, without wyues and litle children and beestis, be maad redi, and go ȝe bifor ȝoure brithren, the sones of Israel. For Y knowe that ȝe han many beestis, and tho schulen
dwelle in citees whiche Y ȝaf to ȝou, til the Lord ȝyue reste to ȝoure brithren, as he ȝaf to ȝou, and til thei also welden the lond which the Lord schal ȝyue to hem biȝonde Jordan; thanne ech man schal turne aȝen in to his possessioun which Y ȝaf to ȝou.
Also Y comaundid to Josue in that tyme, and seide, Thin iȝen sien what thingis ȝoure Lord God dide to these twei kyngis; so he schal do to alle rewmes, to whiche thou schalt go; drede thou not hem.
And Y preiede the
Lord in that tyme, and seide,
Lord God, thou hast bigunne to schewe to thi seruaunt thi greetnesse, and strongeste hond, for noon other God is ether in heuene, ether in erthe, that mai do thi werkis, and may be comparisound to thi strengthe.
Therfor Y schal passe, and schal se this beeste lond biȝende Jordan, and this noble hil and Liban.
And the Lord was wrooth to me for ȝou, nethir he herde me, but seide to me, It suffisith to thee; speke thou no more of this thing to me.
Stye thou in to the hiȝnesse of Phasga, and caste aboute thin iȝen to the west, and north, and south, and eest, and biholde, for thou schalt not passe this Jordan.
Comaunde thou to Josue, and strengthe thou and coumforte hym; for he schal go bifore this puple, and he schal departe to hem the lond, which thou schalt se.
And we dwelliden in the valey aȝens the temple of Phegor.
And now, thou Israel, here the comaundementis and domes whiche Y teche thee, that thou do tho, and lyue, and that thow entre and welde the lond which the Lord God of ȝoure fadris schal ȝyue to ȝou.
Ȝe schulen not adde to the word which Y speke to ȝou, nether ȝe schulen take awei fro it; kepe ȝe the comaundementis of ȝoure Lord God, which Y comaunde to ȝou.
Ȝoure iȝen sien alle thingis whiche the Lord dide aȝens Belphegor; how he alto brak alle the worschiperis of hym fro the myddis of ȝou.
Forsothe ȝe that cleuen to ȝoure Lord God lyuen alle til in to present day.
Ȝe witen that Y tauȝte ȝou the comaundementis and riȝtfulnessis, as my Lord God comaundide to me; so ȝe schulen do tho
in the lond whiche ȝe schulen welde, and ȝe schulen kepe, and schulen fille in werk. For this is ȝoure wisdom and vndurstondyng bifor puplis, that alle men here these comaundementis, and seie, Lo! a wise puple and vnderstondynge! a greet folk!
Noon other nacioun is so greet, not in noumbre ether in bodili quantite, but in dignite, that hath Goddis neiȝynge to it silf, as oure God is redi to alle oure bisechyngis.
For whi what other folk is so noble, that it hath cerymonyes and iust domes, and al the lawe which Y schal sette forth to dai bifor ȝoure iȝen?
Therfor kepe thi silf, and thi soule bisili; forȝete thou not the wordis whiche thin iȝen sien, and falle tho not doun fro thin herte, in alle the daies of thi lijf. Thou schalt teche tho thi sones and thi sones sones.
Telle thou the day in which thou stodist bifor thi Lord God in Oreb, whanne the Lord spak to me, and seide, Gadere thou the puple to me, that it here my wordis, and lerne for to drede me in al tyme in which it lyueth in erthe, and teche hise sones.
And ȝe neiȝiden to the roote of the hille, that brente til to heuene; and derknessis, and cloude, and myist weren therynne.
And the Lord spak to ȝou fro the myddis of fier; ȝe herden the vois of hise wordis, and outirli ȝe sien no fourme.
And he schewide to ȝou his couenaunt, which he comaundide, that ȝe schulden do, and he schewide ten wordis, whiche he wroot in two tablis of stoon.
And he comaundide to me in that tyme, that Y schulde teche ȝou cerymonyes and domes, whiche ȝe owen to do in the lond whiche ȝe schulen welde.
Therfor kepe ȝe bisili ȝoure soulis; ȝe sien not ony licnesse in the dai in which the Lord spak to ȝou in Oreb, fro the
myddis of the fier; lest perauenture ȝe be disseyued and make to ȝou a grauun licnesse, ether an ymage of male, ether
of female; a licnesse of alle beestis that ben on erthe, ether of bridis fleynge
vndur heuene, and of crepynge beestis that ben moued in erthe, ether of fischis that dwellen vndur the erthe in watris;
lest perauenture, whanne thin iȝen ben reisid to heuene, thou se the sonne, and moone, and alle the sterris of heuene, and be disseyued bi errour, and worschipe tho, bi outermer reuerence, and onour, bi ynner reuerence, tho thingis whiche thi Lord God made of nouȝt, in to seruyce to alle folkis that ben vndur heuene.
Forsothe the Lord took ȝou, and ledde out of the yrun furneys of Egipt, that he schulde haue a puple of eritage, as it is in present dai.
And the Lord was wrooth aȝens me for ȝoure wordis, and swoor that Y schulde not passe Jordan, and schulde not entre in to the beeste lond, which he schal ȝyue to ȝou.
Lo! Y die in this erthe; Y schal not passe Jordan; ȝe schulen passe, and schulen welde the noble lond.
Be thou war, lest ony tyme thou forȝete the couenaunt of thi Lord God, which he made with thee, and lest thou make to thee a grauun licness of tho thingis whiche the Lord forbeed to make.
For thi Lord God is fier wastynge; God, a feruent louyere.
If ȝe gendren sones, and sones of sones, and ȝe dwellen in the lond, and ȝe be disceyued, and make to ȝou ony licnesse, and doen yuel bifor ȝoure Lord God, that ȝe terren
hym to greet wrathe, Y clepe witnesses to dai heuene and erthe, that is, ech resonable creature beynge in heuene and in erthe, that ȝe schulen perische soone fro the lond, which ȝe schulen welde, whanne ȝe han passid Jordan; ȝe schulen not dwelle long tyme therynne, but the
Lord schal do awey ȝou, and schal scatere in to alle hethen men, and ȝe schulen leeue fewe among naciouns, to whiche the Lord schal lede ȝou.
And there ȝe schulen serue to goddis, that ben maad bi the hond of men, to a tre and a stoon, that seen not, nether heren, nether eten, nether smellen.
And whanne thou hast souȝt there thi Lord God, thou schalt fynde hym; if netheles thou sekist with al the herte, and with al the tribulacioun of thi soule.
Aftir that alle thingis han founde thee, that ben biforseid, forsothe in the laste tyme, thou schalt turne aȝen to thi Lord God, and thou schalt here his vois.
For thi Lord God is merciful God; he schal not forsake thee, nethir he schal do awey outirli, nethir he schal forȝete the couenaunt, in which he swoor to thi fadris.
Axe thou of elde daies that weren bifor thee, fro the day in which thi Lord God made of nouȝt man on erthe, axe thou fro that oon ende of heuene til to the tother ende therof, if sich a thing was doon ony tyme, ether if it was
euere knowun, that a puple herde the vois of God spekynge fro the myddis of
the fier, as thou herdist, and siest; if God dide, that he entride, and took to him silf a folc fro the middis of naciouns, bi temptaciouns, myraclis, and grete wondris, bi batel, and strong hond, and arm holdun forth, and orrible siȝtis, bi alle thingis whiche ȝoure Lord God dide for ȝou in Egipt, while thin iȝen
sien; that thou schuldist wite, that the Lord hym silf is God, and noon other is, outakun oon.
Fro heuene he made thee to here his vois, that he schulde teche thee; and in erthe he schewide to thee his grettiste fier, and thou herdist the wordis
of hym fro the myddis of the fier; for he louyde thi fadris, and chees her seed aftir hem. And he ledde thee out of Egipt,
and ȝede bifore in his greet vertu, that he schulde do awei grettiste naciouns, and strongere than thou, in thin entryng, and that he schulde lede thee ynne, and schulde ȝyue to thee the lond of hem in to possessioun, as thou seest in present day. Therfor wite thou to dai, and thenke in
thin herte, that the Lord him silfe is God in heuene aboue, and in erthe bynethe, and noon other is.
Kepe thou hise heestis, and comaundementis, whiche Y comaunde to thee, that it be wel to thee, and to thi sones after thee, and that thou dwelle mych tyme on the lond, which thi Lord God schal ȝyue to thee.
Thanne Moises departide thre citees biȝende Jordan
at the eest coost, that he fle to tho, that sleeth his neighbore not wilfuli, and was not enemy bifore oon and the tother dai, and that he mai fle to summe
of these citees; Bosor in the wildirnesse, which is set in the feeldi lond, of the lynage of Ruben; and Ramoth in Galaad, which is in the lynage of Gad; and Golan in Basan, which is in the lynage of Manasses.
This is the lawe which Moises settide forth bifor the sones of
Israel, and these ben the witnessyngis, and cerymonyes, and domes, whiche he spak to the sones of Israel, whanne thei
ȝeden out of Egipt, biȝende Jordan, in the valey aȝens the temple of Phegor, in the lond of Seon, kyng of Ammorreis, that dwellide in Esebon, whom Moises killide. And the sones of Israel ȝeden out of Egipt,
and weldiden the lond of him, and the lond of Og, kyng of Basan, twei kyngis of Ammoreis, that weren biȝende
Jordan, at the rysyng of the sunne; fro Aroer which is set on the brenke of the stronde of Arnon, til to the hil of Seon,
which is Hermon; thei weldiden al the pleyn biȝende Jordan, at the eest coost, til to the see of wildirnesse, and til to the rootis of the hil of Phasga.
And Moises clepide al Israel, and seide to hym, Here, thou Israel, the cerymonyes and domes, whiche Y speke to dai in ȝoure eeris; lerne ȝe tho, and fille ȝe in werk.
Oure Lord God made a boond of pees with
vs in Oreb; he made not couenaunt, that is, of lawe writun, with oure fadris, but with vs that ben present, and lyuen.
Face to face he spak to vs in the hil, fro the myddis of the fier.
Y was recouncelere and mediatour bitwixe God and ȝou in that tyme, that Y schulde telle to ȝou the wordis of hym, for ȝe dredden the fier, and stieden not in to the hil. And the
Lord seide, Y am thi Lord God, that ladde thee out of the lond of Egipt, fro the hows of seruage.
Thou schalt not haue alien Goddis in my siȝt.
Thou schalt not make to thee a grauun ymage, nether a licnesse of alle thingis that ben in heuene aboue, and that ben in erthe bynethe, and that lyuen in watris vndur
erthe; thou schalt not herie tho, and thou schalt not worschipe tho; for Y am thi Lord God, God a feruent louyer; and Y ȝelde the wickidnesse of fadris, in to sones in to the thridde and the fourthe
generacioun to hem that haten me, and Y do mersy in to many thousyndis to hem that louen me, and kepen myn heestis.
Thou schalt not mystake the name of thi Lord God in veyn, for he schal not be vnpunyschid, that takith the name of God on a veyn thing.
Kepe thou the day of sabat that thou halewe it, as thi Lord God comaundide to thee.
In sixe daies thou schalt worche, and thou schalt do
alle thi werkis; the seventhe day is of sabat, that is the reste of thi Lord God. Thou schalt not do therynne ony thing of werk; thou, and thi sone, and douȝter , seruaunt, and handmaide, and oxe, and asse, and al thi werk beeste, and the pilgrym which is with ynne thi ȝatis; that thi seruaunt reste and thin handmaide, as also thou.
Bithenke thou, that also thou seruedist in Egipt, and thi Lord God ledde thee out fro thennus, in a strong hond, and arm holdun forth; therfor he comaundide to thee, that thou schuldist kepe the dai of sabat.
Onoure thi fadir and thi modir, as thi Lord God comaundide to thee, that thou lyue in long tyme, and that it be wel to thee, in the lond which thi Lord God schal ȝyue to thee.
Thou schalt not sle.
Thou schalt not do letcherie.
And thou schalt not do thefte.
Thou schalt not speke fals witnessyng aȝens thi neiȝbore.
Thou schalt not coueite the wijf of thi neiȝbore, not hows, not feeld, not seruaunt, not handmayde, not oxe, not asse, and alle thingis that ben hise.
The Lord spak these wordis to al ȝoure multitude, in the hil, fro the myddis of fier and of cloude and of myist, with greet vois, and addide no thing more; and he wroot tho wordis in two tablis of stoon, whiche he ȝaf to me.
Forsothe after that ȝe herden the vois fro the myddis of the derknessis, and sien the hil brenne, alle ȝe princis of lynagis, and the grettere men in birthe, neiȝiden
to me, and seiden, Lo! oure Lord God schewide to vs his maieste and greetnesse; we herden his vois fro the myddis of fier, and we preueden to day that a man lyuede, while God spak with man.
Whi therfor schulen we die, and schal this gretteste fier deuoure vs? For if we heren more the vois of oure Lord God, we schulen die.
What is ech man, that he here the vois of God lyuynge, that spekith fro the myddis of fier, as we herden, and that he may lyue?
Rathere neiȝe thou, and here thou alle thingis whiche oure Lord God schal seie to thee; and thou schalt speke to vs, and we schulen here, and schulen do tho wordis.
And whanne the Lord hadde herd this, he seide to me, Y herde the vois of the wordis of this puple, whiche thei spaken to thee; thei spaken wel alle thingis.
Who schal ȝyue that thei haue siche soule, that thei drede me, and kepe alle my comaundementis in al tyme, that it be wel to hem and to the sones of hem, with outen ende?
Go thou, and seye to hem, Turne ȝe aȝen in to ȝoure tentis.
Sotheli stonde thou here with me, and Y schal speke to thee alle comaundementis, and cerymonyes, and domes, whiche thou schalt teche hem, that thei do tho in the lond which Y schal ȝyue to hem in to possessioun.
Therfor kepe ȝe, and do ȝe tho thingis, whiche the Lord God comaundide to ȝou; ȝe schulen not bowe awey, nether to the riȝt side nether to
the left side, but ȝe schulen go bi the weie whiche ȝoure Lord God comaundide, that ȝe lyue, and that it be wel to ȝou, and that ȝoure daies be lengthid in the lond of ȝoure possessioun.
These ben the comaundementis, and cerymonyes, and domes, whiche ȝoure Lord God comaundide that Y schulde teche ȝou, and that ȝe do tho in the lond
to which ȝe passen ouer to welde; that thou drede thi Lord God, and kepe alle hise comaundementis, and heestis, whiche Y comaunde to thee, and to thi sones, and sones of sones, in alle the daies of thi lijf, that thi daies be lengthid.
Thou Israel, here, and kepe, that thou do tho thingis whiche the Lord comaundide to thee, and that it be wel to thee, and thou be multiplied more, as the Lord God of thi fadris bihiȝte, to ȝyue to thee a lond flowynge with mylk and hony.
Thou Israel, here, thi Lord God is o God.
Thou schalt loue thi Lord God of al thin herte, and of al thi soule, and of al thi strengthe.
And these wordis whiche Y comaunde to
thee to dai, schulen be in thin herte; and thou schalt telle tho to thi sones, and thou schalt thenke on tho, sittynge in thin hows, and goynge in the weie, slepynge, and rysinge.
And thou schalt bynde tho as a signe in thin hond; and tho schulen be, and schulen be moued bifor thin iȝen;
and thou schalt write tho in the lyntel, and in the doris of thin hows.
And whanne thi Lord God hath brouȝt thee in to the lond, for which he swoor to thi fadris, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and hath ȝoue to thee grete citees, and beeste,
whiche thou bildidist not, housis fulle of alle richessis, whiche thou madist not, and cisternes, which thou diggedist not, places of vynes, and places of olyues, whiche
thou plauntidist not, and thou hast ete,
and art fillid, be war diligentli, lest thou forȝete the Lord, that ladde thee out of the lond of Egipt, fro the hows of seruage. Thou schalt drede thi Lord God, and thou schalt serue hym aloone, bi seruyce due to God onely, and thou schalt swere bi his name.
Ȝe schulen not go aftir alien goddis, of alle hethen men that ben in
ȝoure cumpas; for God is a feruent louyere, thi Lord God is in the myddis of thee, lest ony tyme the strong veniaunce of thi Lord God be wrooth aȝens thee, and do awei thee fro the face of the erthe.
Thou schalt not tempte thi Lord God, as thou temptidist in the place of temptyng.
Kepe thou the comaundementis of thi Lord God, and the witnessyngis, and cerymonyes, whiche he comaundide
to thee; and do thou that that is plesaunt and good in the siȝt of the Lord, that it be wel to thee, and that thou entre, and welde the beste lond, of which
the Lord swoor to thi fadris, that he schulde do awey alle thin enemyes bifor thee, as he spak.
And whanne thi sone schal axe thee to morewe, that is, in tyme comyng, and schal seie, What wolen these witnessyngis, and cerymonyes, and domes to hem silf, whiche oure Lord God comaundide
to vs? thou schalt seie to hym, We weren seruauntis of Farao in Egipt, and the Lord ledde vs out of Egipt,
in strong hond; and he dide myraclis, and grete wondris, and werste, that is, moost peyneful veniaunces, in Egipt, aȝens Farao and al his hows, in oure siȝt.
And he ledde vs out therof, that he schulde ȝyue to vs led yn, the lond of which he swoor to oure fadris.
And the Lord comaundide to vs, that we do alle these lawful thingis, and drede oure Lord God, that it be wel to vs in alle the daies of oure lijf, as it is to dai.
And he schal be merciful to vs, if we schulen do and kepe alle hise heestis, bifor oure Lord God, as he comaundide to vs.
Whanne thi Lord God hath lad thee in to the lond, in to which thou schalt entre to welde, and hath do awey many folkis bifor thee, Ethei, and Gergesei, and Ammorrey, Canenei, and Pherezei, Euey, and Jebusei; seuene folkis, of myche gretter noumbre than thou art, and strengere than
thou; and thi Lord God hath bitake hem to thee, thou schalt smyte hem til to deeth, thou schalt not make with hem a boond of pees, nether thou schalt haue
merci on hem, nether thou schalt felowschipe mariagis with him; thou schalt not ȝyue thi douȝter to the sone of hym, nether thou schalt take his douȝtir to thi
sone; for sche schal disceyue thi sone, that he sue not me, and that he serue more alien goddis; and the strong veniaunce of the Lord schal be wrooth, and schal do awei thee soone.
But rather thou schalt do these thingis to hem; destrie ȝe the auteris of hem, and breke ȝe ymagis of metal, and kitte ȝe doun wodis, and brenne ȝe grauun ymagis.
For thou art an hooli puple to thi Lord God; thi Lord God chees thee, that thou be a special puple to hym, of alle puplis that ben on erthe.
Not for ȝe ouercamen in noumbre alle folkis, the Lord is ioyned to ȝou, and chees ȝow, sithen ȝe ben
fewere than alle puplis; but for the Lord louede ȝou, and kepte the ooth which he swoor to ȝoure fadris; and he ledde ȝou out in strong hond, and aȝen bouȝte ȝou fro the hows of seruage, fro the hows of Farao, kyng of Egipt.
And thou schalt wite, that thi Lord God hym silf is a strong God, and feithful, and kepith couenaunt and mersi to hem that louen hym, and to hem that kepen hise comaundementis, in to a thousynde generaciouns;
and ȝeldith anoon to hem that haten hym, so that he destrie hem, and differr no lengere; restorynge anoon to hem that that thei disseruen.
Therfor kepe thou the comaundementis, and cerymonyes, and domes, whiche Y comaunde to thee to dai, that thou do.
If aftir that thou herist these domes, thou kepist, and doist tho, thi Lord God schal kepe to thee couenaunt, and mersi, which he swoor to thi fadris.
And he schal loue thee, and schal multiplie thee, and he schal blesse the fruyt of thi wombe, and the fruyt of thi lond, thi wheete, and vindage, oile, and droues of beestis, and the flockis of thi scheep, on the lond for which he swoor to thi fadris, that he schulde ȝyue it to thee.
Thou schalt be blessid among alle puplis; noon bareyn of euer eithir kynde schal be at thee, as well in men, as in thi flockis.
The Lord schal do awei fro thee all ache, ether sorewe; and he schal not brynge to thee the worste siknessis of Egipt, whiche thou knewist, but to alle thin enemyes.
And thou schalt deuoure, that is, distrie, alle puplis, whiche thi Lord God schal ȝyue to thee; thin iȝe schal not spare hem, nethir thou schalt serue the goddis of hem, lest thei ben in to the fallyng of thee.
If thou seist in thin herte, These folkis ben
mo than Y, hou may Y do awei hem? nyle thou drede, but haue thou mynde, what thingis thi Lord God dide to Farao, and
alle Egipcians; he dide the gretteste veniaunces, whiche thin iȝen sien, and miraclis and grete wondris, and the strong hond, and arm holdun forth, that thi Lord God schulde lede thee out; so he schal do to alle puplis whiche thou dredist.
Ferthermore and thi Lord God schal sende venemouse flies in to hem, til he do awei, and destrye alle men, that fledden thee, and thei schulen not mowe be hid.
Thou schalt not drede hem, for thi Lord is in the myddis of thee, grete God, and ferdful.
He hym silf schal waste these naciouns in thi siȝt, litil and litil, and bi partis; thou schalt not mow do awey tho naciouns togidere, lest peraventure beestis
of erthe be multiplied aȝens thee; and thi Lord God schal ȝyue hem in thi siȝt, and he schal sle hem, til thei be doon awey outerly.
And he schal bitake the kyngis of hem in to thin hondis, and thou schalt destrie the names of hem vndur heuene; noon schal mow aȝenstonde thee, til thou al to-breke hem.
Thou schalt brenne in fier the grauun ymagis of hem; thou schalt not coueite the siluer and gold, of whiche tho ymagis ben maad, nether thou schalt take of tho ony thing to thee, lest thou offende therfor, for it is abhominacioun of thi Lord God.
Nether thou schalt brynge ony thing of the idol in to thin hous, lest thou be maad cursid, as also that idol is; thou schalt wlate it as filthe, and thou schalt haue it as defoulyng, and filthis of abhomynacioun, for it is cursid.
Be thou war diligentli, that thou do ech comaundement which Y comaunde to thee to dai, that ȝe moun lyue, and be multiplied, and that ȝe entre, and welde the lond, for which the Lord swoor to ȝoure fadris.
And thou schalt haue mynde of al the weie, bi which thi Lord God ledde thee by fourti ȝeer, bi deseert, that he schulde turmente, and schulde tempte thee; and that tho thingis that weren tretid in thi soule schulden be knowun, whether thou woldist kepe hise comaundementis, ethir nay.
And he turmentide thee with nedynesse, and he ȝaf to thee meete, manna which thou knewist not, and thi fadris knewen not, that he schulde schewe to thee, that a man lyueth not in breed aloone, but in ech word that cometh out of the Lordis mouth, that is, bi manna, that cam down at the heest of the Lord.
Thi cloth, bi which thou were hilid, failide not for eldnesse, and thi foot was not brokun undernethe,
lo! the fourtith ȝeer is; that thou thenke in thin herte, for as a man techith
his sone, so thi Lord God tauȝte thee, that thou kepe the comaundementis of thi Lord God, and go in hise weies, and drede hym.
For thi Lord God schal lede thee in to a good lond, in to the lond of ryueris, and of stondynge watris, and of wellis, in whos feeldis and mounteyns the depthis
of floodis breken out; in to the lond of wheete, of barli, and of vyneris, in which lond fige trees, and pumgranadis, and olyue trees comen forth; in to the lond
of oile, and of hony; where thow schalt ete thi breed with out nedynesse, and schalt vse the aboundaunce of alle thingis; of which lond the stonys ben yrun, and metals of tyn ben diggid of the
hillis therof; that whanne thou hast ete, and art fillid, thou blesse thi Lord God for the beste lond which he ȝaf to thee.
Therfor kepe thou, and be war, lest ony tyme thou forȝete thi Lord God, and dispise hise comaundementis, and domes, and cerymonyes, whiche Y comaunde to
thee to dai; lest aftir that thou hast ete, and art fillid, hast bildid faire housis, and
hast dwellid in tho, and hast droues of oxun, and flockis of scheep, and plente of siluer, and of gold, and of alle thingis,
thine herte be reisid, and thenke not on thi Lord God, that ledde thee out of the lond of Egipt, and fro the hous of seruage,
and was thi ledere in the greet wildirnesse and ferdful, in which was a serpent brenninge with blast, and scorpioun, and dipsas, and outirli no watris; which Lord ledde out stremes of
the hardeste stoon, and fedde thee with manna in the wildirnesse, which manna thi fadris knewen not. And after that the Lord turmentid thee, and preuede, at
the last he hadd mersi on thee, lest thou woldist seie in thin herte, My strengthe, and the myȝt of myn hond ȝaf alle these thingis to me.
But thenke thou on thi Lord God, that he ȝaf strengthis to thee, that he schulde fille his couenaunt, of whiche he swoor to thi fadris, as present dai schewith.
Forsothe if thou forȝetist thi Lord God, and suest aliene goddis, and worschipist hem in herte, and onourist with outforth, lo! now Y biforseie to
thee, that thou schalt perische outerli; as hethen men perischiden, whiche the Lord dide awei in thin entryng, so and ȝe schulen perische, if ȝe schulen be vnobedient to the vois of ȝoure Lord God.
Here thou, Israel; thou schalt passe Jordan to dai, that thou welde mooste naciouns, and strengere than thou; grete
citees, and wallid til to heuene; a greet puple, and hiȝ; the sones of Enachym, whiche thi silf siest, and herdist, whiche no man may aȝenstonde in the contrarie part.
Therfor thou schalt wite to dai, that thi Lord God hym silf schal passe bifor thee; he is a fier deuourynge and wastynge, that schal al to breke hem, and schal do awei, and destrie bifor thi face swiftli, as he spak to thee.
Seie thou not in thin herte, whanne thi Lord God hath do hem awey in thi siȝt, For my riȝtfulnesse the Lord brouȝte me yn, that Y schulde welde this lond; sithen these naciouns ben doon awey for her wickidnessis.
For not for thi riȝtfulnessis, and equyte of thin herte thou schalt entre that thou welde the lond of hem; but for thei diden wickidli, thei weren doon awey, whanne thou entridist, and that the Lord schulde fille his word which he bihiȝte vndur an ooth to thi fadris, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Therfor wite thou that not for thi riȝtfulnesses thi Lord God ȝaf to thee this beste lond in to possessioun, sithen thou art a puple of hardeste nol.
Haue thou mynde, and forȝete not, hou in the wildirnesse thou terridist thi Lord God to greet wraththe; fro that dai in which thou ȝedist out of Egipt til to this place, thou striuedist euere aȝens the Lord.
For whi also in Oreb thou terridist hym, and he was wrooth, and wolde do thee awei,
whanne Y stiede in to the hil, that Y schulde take two tablis of stoon, the tablis of couenaunt which the Lord made with ȝou, and Y continuede in the hil fourti daies and nyȝtis, and Y eet not breed, and Y drank not watir.
And the Lord ȝaf to me, twey tablis of stoon, euer either wrytun with Goddis fyngur, and conteynynge alle the wordis whiche he spak to ȝou in the hil, fro the myddis of the fier, whanne the cumpany of puple was gaderid togidere.
And whanne fourti daies and so many nyȝtis hadden passid, the Lord ȝaf to me twei tablis of stoon, tablis
of boond of pees; and he seide to me, Rise thou, and go doun fro hennys soone, for thi puple, which thou leddist out of Egipt, han forsake swiftli the weie which thou schewidist to hem, and thei han maad to hem a ȝotun calf.
And eft the Lord seide to me, Y se that this puple is
of hard nol; suffre thou me, that I alto breke hym, and do awey the name of hym fro vndur heuene; and Y schal ordeyne thee on a folk which is grettere and strongere than this folk.
And whanne Y cam doun fro the hil brennynge, and helde with euer either hond twei tablis
of boond of pees, and Y seiȝ, that ȝe hadde synned to ȝoure Lord God, and hadden maad to ȝou a ȝotun calf, and hadden forsake swiftli the weie of God which he
schewide to ȝou, Y castide doun the tablis fro myn hondis, and brak tho tablis in ȝoure siȝt.
And Y felde doun bifor the Lord as biforto, in fourti daies and fourti nyȝtis, and Y eet not breed, and drank not watir, for alle ȝoure synnes whiche ȝe diden aȝens the Lord, and terriden hym
to greet wraththe; for Y dredde the indignacioun and yre of hym, by which he was stirid aȝens ȝou, and wolde do ȝou awey. And the Lord herde me also in this tyme.
Also the Lord was wrooth greteli aȝens Aaron, and wolde alto breke hym, and Y preiede in lijk maner for hym.
Forsothe Y took ȝoure synne which ȝe maden, that is, the calf, and brente it in fier, and Y alto brak in gobetis, and droof outerli in to dust, and castide forth in to the stronde, that cam doun fro the hil.
Also in the brennyng, and in the temptacioun at the watris of aȝenseiyng, and in the Sepulcris of Coueytise, ȝe
terriden the Lord; and whanne Y sente ȝou fro Cades Barne, and seide, Stye ȝe, and welde the lond which Y ȝaf to ȝou, and ȝe dispisiden the comaundement of ȝoure Lord God, and ȝe bileueden not to
him, nether ȝe wolden here his vois; but euere ȝe weren rebel, fro the day in which Y bigan to knowe ȝou.
And Y lay byfore the Lord fourti daies and fourti nyȝtis, in whiche Y bisouȝte hym mekeli, that he schulde not do awey ȝou, as he manaasside.
And Y preiede, and seide, Lord God, distrye not thi puple, and thin eritage, which thou aȝen bouȝtist in thi greetnesse, which thou leddist out of Egipt in strong hond.
Haue thou mynde of thi seruauntis, of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; biholde thou not the hardnesse of this puple, and the wickidnesse, and the
synne therof, lest perauenture the dwelleris of the lond, out of which thou leddist vs, seien, The Lord myȝte not bryng hem in to the lond which he bihiȝte to hem, and he hatide hem; therfor he ledde hem out that he schulde sle hem in wildirnesse;
and thei ben thi puple and thin eritage, which thou leddist out in thi greet strengthe, and in thin arm holdun forth.
In that tyme the Lord seide to me, Hewe thou twei tablis of stoon to thee, as the formere weren; and stie thou to me in to the hil. And thou schalt make an
arke, ether a cofere, of tree, and Y schal write in the tablis, the wordis that weren in these tablis whiche thou brakist bifore; and thou schalt putte tho tablis in to the arke.
Therfor Y made an ark of the trees of Sechim, and whanne Y hadde hewe twei tablis of stoon, at the licnesse of the formere tablis, Y stiede in to the hil, and hadde the tablis in the hondis.
And he wroot in the tablis, bi that that he hadde writun bifore, ten wordis, whiche the Lord spak to ȝou in the hil, fro the myddis of the fyer, whanne the puple was gaderid, and he ȝaf the tablis to me.
And Y turnide aȝen fro the hil, and cam doun, and puttide the tablis in to the arke which Y hadde maad, whiche tablis ben there hidur to, as the Lord comaundide to me.
Forsothe the sones of Israel moueden tentis fro Beroth of the sones of Jachan in to Mosera, where Aaron was deed, and biried, for whom his sone Eleazar was set in preesthod.
Fro thennus thei camen in to Galgad; fro which place thei ȝeden forth, and settiden tentis in Jehabatha, in the lond of watris and of strondis.
In that tyme Y departide the lynage of Leuy, that it schulde bere the arke of boond of pees of the Lord, and schulde stonde bifor hym in seruyce, and schulde blesse in his name til in to present dai.
For which thing Leuy hadde not part, nether possession with hise brithren, for the Lord hym silf is his possessioun, as thi Lord God bihiȝte to hym.
Forsothe Y stood in the hil as bifore, fourti daies and fourti niȝtis, and the Lord herde me also in this tyme, and nolde leese thee.
And he seide to me, Go thou, and go bifor this puple, that it entre, and welde the lond which Y swoor to her fadris, that Y schulde ȝeue to hem.
And now, Israel, what axith thi Lord God of thee, no but that thou drede thi Lord, and go in hise weies, and that thou loue hym, and serue thi Lord God in al
thin herte, and in al thi soule; and that thou kepe the comaundementis of thi Lord God, and the cerymonyes of hym, whiche Y comaunde to thee to dai, that it be wel to thee.
Lo! heuene is of thi Lord God, and heuene of heuene; the erthe and alle thingis that ben ther ynne ben
hise; and netheles the Lord was glued to thi fadris, and louede hem, and he chees her seed after hem, and ȝou of alle folkis, as it is preued to dai.
Therfor circumcide ȝe the prepucie, ethir vnclennesse, of ȝoure herte, and no more make ȝe harde ȝoure nol.
For ȝoure Lord God hym silf is God of goddis, and Lord of lordis, God greet, and miȝti, and feerdful, which takith not persoone, nether ȝiftis.
He makith doom to the fadirles, and modirles, and to the widewe; he loueth a pilgrym, and ȝyueth to hym lyiflode and clothing.
And therfor loue ȝe pilgryms, for also ȝe weren comelyngis in the lond of Egipt.
Thou schalt drede thi Lord God, and thou schalt serue hym aloone, and thou schalt cleue to hym, and thou schalt swere in his name.
He is thi preisyng, and thi God, that made to thee these grete dedis, and ferdful, whiche thin iȝen siȝen.
In seuenti men thi fadris ȝeden doun in to Egipt, and lo! now thi Lord God hath multiplied thee as the sterris of heuene.
Therfor loue thi Lord God, and kepe thou hise comaundementis and cerymonyes, domes and heestis, in al tyme.
Knowe ȝe to day tho thingis whiche ȝoure sones knowen not, whiche sones sien not the doctryn of ȝoure Lord God, hise grete dedis, and strong hond, and
arm holdun forth, myraclis and werkis, whiche he dide in the myddis of Egipt to Farao, kyng, and to al the lond of hym,
and to al the oost of Egipcians, and to horsis, and carris; hou the watris of the reed see hiliden hem, whanne thei pursueden ȝou, and the Lord dide awei hem
til in to present dai; and whiche thingis the Lord dide to ȝou in wildernesse,
til ȝe camen to this place; and to Dathan and Abiron, the sones of Heliab, that was the sone of Ruben, whiche the erthe swolewide, whanne his mouth was openyd, with the housis and tabernaclis, and al the catel of hem which thei hadden, in the myddis of Israel.
Ȝoure iȝen sien alle the grete werkis of the
Lord, whiche he dide, that ȝe kepe alle hise heestis whiche Y comaunde to dai to ȝou, and that ȝe moun entre, and welde
the lond, to which ȝe schulen entre, and ȝe lyue therynne in myche time; which lond, flowynge with mylk and hony, the Lord bihiȝte vndur an ooth to ȝoure fadris and to the seed of hem.
For the lond, to which thou schalt entre to welde, is not as the lond of Egipt, out of which thou ȝedist, where whanne the seed is cast in the maner of gardyns, moist waters
ben led; but it is hilli, and feldi,
and abidith reynes fro heuene, which lond thi Lord God biholdith, and hise iȝen ben therynne, fro the bigynnyng of the ȝeer til to the ende therof.
Therfor if ȝe schulen obeie to myn heestis whiche Y comaunde to dai to ȝou, that ȝe loue ȝoure Lord God, and serue hym in
al ȝoure herte, and in al ȝoure soule; he schal ȝyue to ȝoure lond reyn tymeful and late, that ȝe gadere wheete, and wyn,
and oile, hey of the feeldis to feede beestis, that ȝe bothe ete and be fillid.
Be ȝe war, lest perauenture ȝoure herte be disseyued, and ȝe go awei fro the Lord, and serue alien goddis, and worschipe
hem; and the Lord be wrooth, and close heuene, and reynes come not doun, nether the erthe ȝyue his fruyt, and ȝe perische swiftli fro the beste lond which the Lord schal ȝyue to ȝou.
Putte ȝe thes wordis in ȝoure hertes and soules, and honge ȝe tho wordis for a signe in the hondis, and sette ȝe bitwixe ȝoure iȝen.
Teche ȝoure sones, that thei thenke on tho wordis, whanne thou sittist in thin hows, and goist in the weie, and lyggist doun, and risist.
Thou schalt write tho wordis on the postis, and ȝatis of thin
hous, that the daies of thee and of thi sones be multiplied in the lond which the Lord swoor to thi fadris, that he schulde ȝyue to hem, as long as heuene is a boue erthe.
For if ȝe kepen the heestis whiche Y comaunde to ȝou, and ȝe do tho, that ȝe loue ȝoure Lord God, and go in alle
hise weies, and cleue to hym, the Lord schal destrie alle these hethen men bifor ȝoure face, and ȝe schulen welde tho folkis that ben grettere and strongere than ȝe.
Ech place which ȝoure foot schal trede, schal be ȝoure; fro the deseert, and fro the Liban, and fro the greet flood Eufrates til to the west see, schulen be ȝoure termes.
Noon schal stonde aȝens ȝou; ȝoure Lord God schal ȝiue ȝoure outward drede and inward drede on ech lond which ȝe schulen trede, as he spak to ȝou.
Lo! Y sette forth in ȝoure siȝt to
day blissyng and cursyng; blessyng, if ȝe obeien to the heestis of ȝoure Lord God,
whiche Y comaunde to ȝou to dai; cursyng, if ȝe heren not the heestis of ȝoure Lord God, but goen awei fro the weie which Y schewe now to ȝou, and goen after alien goddis whiche ȝe knowen not.
Sotheli whanne thi Lord God hath brouȝt thee in to the lond, to which to enhabite thou goist, thou schalt sette blessyng on the hil Garisym, cursyng on the hil Hebal,
whiche hillis ben biȝende Jordan, aftir the weie that goith to the goyng doun of the sunne, in the lond of Cananey, that dwellith in the feeldi places aȝens Galgala, which is bisidis the valey goynge and entrynge fer.
For ȝe schulen passe Jordan, that ȝe welde the lond which ȝoure Lord God schal ȝyue to ȝou, and that ȝe haue and welde that lond.
Therfor se ȝe, that ȝe fille the cerymonyes and domes, whiche I schal sette to dai in ȝoure siȝt.
These ben the heestis and domes, whiche ȝe owen to do, in the lond which the Lord God of thi fadrys schal ȝyue to thee, that thou welde it, in alle daies in whiche thou schalt go on erthe.
Distrie ȝe alle the places wherynne hethen men whiche ȝe schulen welde, worschipiden her goddis, on hiȝ mounteyns, and litle hillis, and vndur ech tre ful of bowis.
Distrie ȝe the auteris of hem, and breke ȝe the ymagis; brenne ȝe the wodis with fier, and al to breke ȝe the idolis; destrie ȝe the names of hem fro the places.
Ȝe schulen not
do so to ȝoure Lord God; but ȝe schulen come to the place which ȝoure Lord God chees of alle ȝoure lynagis, that he putte
his name there, and dwelle therynne; and ȝe schulen come, and schulen offre in that place ȝoure brent sacrifices, and slayn sacrifices, the dymes, and firste fruytis of ȝoure hondis, and a vowis and ȝiftis, the firste gendrid thingis of oxun, and of scheep.
And ȝe and ȝoure housis schulen ete there in the siȝt of ȝoure Lord God; and ȝe schulen be glad in alle thingis to whiche ȝe putten hond, in whiche ȝoure Lord God blesside ȝou.
Ȝe schulen not do there tho thingis whiche we don here to dai, ech man that semeth riȝtful to hym silf.
For til in to present tyme ȝe camen not to reste and possessioun, which the Lord God schal ȝyue to ȝou.
Ȝe schulen passe Jordan, and ȝe schulen dwelle in the lond which ȝoure Lord God schal ȝyue to ȝou, that ȝe reste fro alle enemyes bi cumpas, and dwelle without ony drede.
In the place which ȝoure Lord God chees that his name be therynne. Thidur ȝe schulen bere alle thingis, whiche Y comaunde, brent sacrifices, and sacrifices, and the dymes, and firste fruytis of ȝoure hondis, and what euere is the beste in ȝiftis, whiche ȝe auowiden to the Lord.
Ther ȝe schulen ete bifor ȝoure Lord God, ȝe, and ȝoure sones, and douȝtris, ȝoure seruauntis, and seruauntessis, and the dekenes, that dwellen in ȝoure citees; for thei han not other part and possessioun among ȝou.
Be thou war lest thou offre thi brent sacrifices
in ech place which thou seest, but in that place which the Lord chees in oon of thi lynagis thou schalt offre sacrifices, and schalt do what euer thingis Y comaunde to thee.
Forsothe if thou wolt ete, and the etyng of fleischis delitith thee, sle thou, and ete, bi the blessyng of thi Lord God, which he ȝaf to thee in thi citees, whether it is vnclene, that is, spottid ether wemmed and feble, ether clene, that is, hool in membris and with out wem, which is leueful to be offrid, thou schalt ete as a capret and hert;
oneli without etyng of blood, which thou schalt schede out as watir on the erthe.
Thou schalt not mowe ete in thi citees the tithis of thi wheete, wyn, and oile, the firste gendrid thingis of droues, and of scheep, and alle thingis whiche thou hast avowid and wolt offre bi fre wille,
and the firste fruytis of thin hondis; but thou schalt ete tho bifor thi Lord God, in the place which thi Lord God chees, thou, and thi sone, and douȝter, seruaunt, and seruauntesse, and the dekene that dwellith in thi citees; and thou schalt be glad, and schalt be fillid bifor thi Lord God in alle thingis to whiche thou holdist forth thin hond.
Be thou war lest thou forsake the dekene in al tyme, in which thou lyuest in erthe.
Whanne thi Lord God hath alargid thi termes, as he spak to thee, and thou wolt ete fleischis,
whiche thi soule desirith, forsothe if the place is fer, which thi Lord God chees, that his name be there, thou schalt sle of thin oxun, and scheep, whiche thou hast, as the Lord comaundide to thee; and thou schalt ete in thi citees as it plesith thee.
As a capret and hert is etun, so thou schalt ete tho; bothe a cleene man and vncleene schulen ete therof in comyn.
Oneli eschewe thou this, that thou ete not blood; for the blood of tho beestis is for the lijf, and therfor thou
owist not ete the lijf with fleischis, but thou schalt schede as watir the blood
on the erthe, that it be wel to thee, and to thi sones after thee, whanne thou hast do that, that plesith in the siȝt of the Lord.
Sotheli thou schalt take that that thou auowidist, and halewidist to the Lord, and thou schalt come to the place
which the Lord chees; and thou schalt offre thin offryngis, fleischis, and blood, on the auter of thi Lord God; thou schalt schede in the auter the blood of sacrifices; forsothe thou schalt ete the fleischis.
Kepe thou and here alle thingis whiche Y comaunde to thee, that it be wel to thee, and to thi sones after thee, with outen ende, whanne thou hast do that, that is good and plesaunt in the siȝt of thi Lord God.
Whanne thi Lord God hath distryed bifor thi face folkis, to whiche thou schalt entre to welde, and thou hast weldid tho folkis, and hast
dwellid in the lond of hem, be thou war lest thou sue hem, aftir that thei ben distried, whanne thou entrist, and thou seke the cerymonyes of hem, and seie, As these folkis worschipyden her goddis, so and Y schal worschipe.
Thou schalt not do in lijk manere to thi Lord God; for thei diden to her goddis alle abhomynaciouns whiche the Lord wlatith, and offriden her sones and douȝtris, and brenten with fier.
Do thou to the Lord this thing oneli which Y comaunde to thee, nethir adde thou ony thing, nether abate.
If a prophete risith in the myddis of thee, ethir he that seith hym silf to haue seyn a dreem, and he biforseith a signe
and a wondur to comynge aftir, and this that he spak bifallith, and he seith to thee, Go we, and sue alien goddis, whiche thou knowist not, and serue we
hem, thou schalt not here the wordis of that prophete, ether of dremere; for ȝoure Lord God assaieth ȝou, that he wite opynli whether ȝe louen hym ether nay, in al ȝoure herte, and in al ȝoure soule.
Sue ȝe ȝoure Lord, and drede ȝe hym; kepe ȝe his comaundementis, and here ȝe the vois of hym; ȝe schulen serue hym, and ȝe schulen cleue to hym.
Forsothe thilke prophete, ether the feynere of dremes, schal be slayn; for he spak that he schulde turne ȝou awei fro ȝoure Lord God, that ladde ȝou out of the lond of Egipt, and aȝenbouȝte ȝou fro the hous of seruage, that thilke prophete schulde make thee to erre fro the weie which thi Lord God comaundide to thee; and thou schalt do awey yuel fro the myddis of thee.
If thi brothir, the sone of thi modir, ether thi sone, ethir thi douȝter, ether the wijf which is in thi bosum, ethir thi freend whom thou louest as thi soule, wole counsele thee, and seith priueli, Go we and serue alien goddis, whiche
thou knowist not, and thi fadris, of alle the folkis in cumpas, that ben niȝ ether fer, fro the bigynnyng til to the ende of
the lond, assente thou not to hym, nether here thou, nether thin iȝen spare hym,
that thou haue mercy, and hide hym, but anoon thou schalt sle hym Thin hond be fyrst on him and aftir thee al the puple putte to hond.
He schal be oppressid with stoonus, and schal be slayn; for he wolde drawe thee awei fro thi Lord God, that ledde thee out of the lond of Egipt,
fro the hous of seruage, that al Israel here and drede, and do no more ony thing lijk this thing.
If thou herist ony men seiynge in oon of thi citees, whiche thi Lord God schal ȝyue to thee to enhabite,
The sones of Belial ȝeden out fro the myddis of thee, and turneden awei the dwelleris of the citee, and seiden, Go we, and serue alien goddis whiche ȝe knowen
not, enquere thou bisili, and whanne the treuthe of the thing is biholdun diligentli, if thou fyndist that this thing is certeyn, which is seid, and that this abhominacioun
is doon in werk, anoon thou schalt smyte the dwelleris of that citee bi the scharpnesse of swerd, and thou schalt do it awey, and alle thingis that ben ther ynne, til to beestis.
Also what euer thing of purtenaunce of houshold is, thou schalt gadere in the myddis of the stretis therof, and thou schalt brenne with that citee, so that thou waste alle thingis to thi Lord God, and it be a biriel euerlastynge; it schal no more be bildid.
And no thing of that cursyng schal cleue in thin hond, that the Lord be turned awei fro the yre of his strong veniaunce, and haue mercy on thee, and multiplie thee, as he swoor to thi fadris.
Whanne thou hast herd the vois of thi Lord God, thou schalt kepe alle hise heestis whiche Y comaunde to thee to day, that thou do that that is plesaunt in the siȝt of thi Lord God.
Be ȝe the sones of ȝoure Lord God; ȝe schulen not kitte ȝou, nether ȝe schulen
make ballidnesse, on a deed man, for thou art an hooli puple to thi Lord God, and he chees thee that thou be to hym in to a special puple, of alle folkis that ben on erthe.
Ete ȝe not tho thingis that ben vncleene.
This is a beeste which ȝe schulen ete; an oxe, and a scheep, and a goet,
an hert, a capret, a wielde oxe, tregelafun, that is, a beeste in parti lijk a buk of geet, and in parti liik an hert, a figarde, an ostrich, a camelioun, that is, a beeste lijk in the heed to a camel, and hath white spottis in the bodi as a parde, and is lijk an hors in the necke, and in the feet is lijc a wilde oxe, and a parde.
Ȝe schulen ete ech beeste that departith the clee in to twei partis, and chewith code.
Sotheli ȝe schulen not ete these beestis, of these that chewen code, and departen not the clee; a camel, an hare, and a cirogrille, that is, a beeste ful of prickis, and is more than an irchoun; for tho chewen code, and departen not the clee, tho schulen be vncleene
to ȝou; also a swyn, for it departith the clee, and chewith not code, schal be vncleene; ȝe schulen not ete the fleischis of tho, and ȝe schulen not touche the deed bodies.
Ȝe schulen ete these thingis, of alle that dwellen in watris; ete ȝe tho thingis that han fynnes and scalis;
ete ȝe not tho thingis that ben with out fynnes and scalis, for tho ben vncleene.
Ete ȝe alle clene briddis;
ete ȝe not vncleene briddis, that is, an egle, and a
gripe, and an aliete, ixon, that is, a whijt brid lesse than a vultur, and is of the kynde of vultris, and a vultur, and a
kite bi his kynde, and al thing of rauenys
kynde, and a strucioun, and a nyȝt crowe,
and a lare, and an hauk bi his kynde, a
fawcun, and a swan, and a siconye, and a dippere, a pursirioun, and a reremous,
a cormeraunt, and a caladrie, alle in her kynde; also a lapwynke and a backe.
And al thing that crepith, and hath fynnes, schal be vncleene, and schal not be etun.
Ete ȝe al thing that is cleene;
sotheli what euer thing is deed bi it silf, ete ȝe not therof. Ȝyue thou to the pilgrym which is with ynne thi ȝatis, that he ete, ether sille thou to hym, for thou art the hooli puple of thi Lord God. Thou schalt not sethe a kyde in the mylk of his modir.
Thou schalt departe the tenthe part of alle thi fruytis that comen forth in the
lond bi ech ȝeer; and thou schal ete in the siȝt of thi Lord God, in the place which he chees, that his name be clepid therynne; thou schalt offre the tithe of thi wheete, wyn, and oile, and the firste gendryd thingis of thi droues, and scheep, that thou lerne to drede thi Lord God in al tyme.
Sotheli whanne the wei is lengere, and the place which thi Lord God chees is fer, and he hath blessid thee, and thou maist not bere alle these thingis
to that place, thou schalt sille alle thingis, and schalt turne in to prijs, and thou schalt bere in thin hond, and thou schalt go to the place which thi Lord God
chees; and thou schalt bie of the same money what euer thing plesith to thee, ethir of droues, ether of scheep; also thou schalt bie wyn, and sidur, and al thing that thi soule desirith; and thou schalt ete bifor thi Lord God, and thou schalt
make feeste, thou, and thin hows, and the dekene which is with ynne thi ȝatis; be thou war lest thou forsake hym, for he hath not other part in possessioun.
In the thridde ȝeer thou schalt departe another dyme of alle thingis that growen to thee in that ȝeer, and thou schalt kepe with ynne thi ȝatis.
And the dekene schal come, whych hath noon other part nether possessioun with thee, and the pilgrym, and the fadirles, ether modirles child, and widue, that ben with ynne thi ȝatis, schulen come, and schulen ete, and be fillid, that thi Lord God blesse thee, in alle werkis of thin hondis whiche thou schalt do.
In the seuenthe ȝeer thou schalt make
remyssioun, that schal be fillid bi this ordre. To whom ony thing is dettid, ethir owid of his freend, ether neiȝbore, and brother, he schal not mowe axe, for it is the ȝeer of remyssioun of the Lord.
Thou schalt axe of a pilgrym and comelyng; thou hast not power to axe of a citeseyn
and neiȝbore; and outerli a nedi man and begger schal not be among ȝou, that thi Lord God blesse thee, in the lond which he schal ȝyue to thee in to the possessioun.
If netheles thou schalt here the vois of thi Lord God, and schalt kepe alle thingis whiche he comaundide, and whiche Y comaunde to dai to thee, he schal blesse thee, as he bihiȝte.
Thou schalt leene to many folkis, and thou schalt not take borewyng of ony man; thou schalt be lord of ful many naciouns, and no man schal be lord of thee.
If oon of thi britheren that dwellen with ynne the ȝatis of thi citee, in the lond which thi Lord God schal ȝyue to thee, cometh to pouert, thou schalt not make hard thin herte, nether thou schalt drawe to gydere
the hond, but thou schalt opene it to the pore man, and thou schalt ȝyue loone to which thou siest hym haue nede.
Be thou war lest perauenture wickid thouȝt crepe priueli to thee, and thou seie in thin herte, The seuenthe ȝeer of remyssioun neiȝeth; and thou turne awey the iȝen fro thi pore brother, and thou nyle ȝyue to hym the loone that he axith; lest he crie aȝens thee to the Lord, and it be maad to thee in to synne.
But thou schalt ȝyue to hym, and thou schalt not do ony thing falsly in releuynge hise nedis, that thi Lord God blesse thee in al tyme, and in alle thingis to whiche thou schalt sette to hond.
Pore men schulen not faile in the lond of thin habitacioun; therfor Y comaunde to thee, that thou opene the hond to thi brother nedi and pore, that lyuen with thee in the lond.
Whanne thi brothir an Ebrew man, ethir an Ebrew womman, is seeld to thee, and hath serued thee sixe ȝeer, in the seuenthe ȝeer thou schalt delyuere hym fre.
And thou schalt not suffre hym go awey voide,
to whom thou hast ȝyue fredom; but thou schalt ȝyue lijflode in the weye, of flockis, and of cornfloor, and of thi pressour, in whiche thi Lord God hath blessid thee.
Haue thou mynde that also thou seruedist in the lond of Egipt, and thi Lord God delyurede thee, ether made thee free, and therfor Y comaunde now to thee.
Forsothe if the seruaunt seith, Y nyle go out, for he loueth thee, and thin hows, and feelith that it is wel to hym at thee,
thou schalt take a nal, and thou schalt peerse his eere in the ȝate of thin hous, and he schal serue thee til in to the world, that is til to the iubilee, ethir fiftithe ȝeer ; also thou schalt do in lijk maner to the handmayde.
Thou schalt not turne awei fro hem thin iȝen, whanne thou schalt delyure hem fre, for bi the hire of an hirid man thei serueden thee bi sixe ȝeer; that thi Lord God blesse thee, in alle the werkis whiche thou doist.
Of the first gendrid thingis that ben borun in thi droues, and scheep, what euer is of male kynde, thou schalt halewe to thi Lord God. Thou schalt not worche in the firste gendrid thing of oxe, and thou schalt not clippe the firste gendrid thinges of scheep.
Thou schalt ete tho bi alle ȝeeris in the siȝt of thi Lord God, thou, and thin hows, in the place which the Lord chees.
Sotheli if it hath a wem, ethir is crokid, ethir is blynd, ethir is foul, ethir feble in ony part, it schal not
be offrid to thi Lord God; but thou schalt ete it with ynne the ȝatis of thi citee, bothe a cleene man and vncleene schulen ete tho in lijk maner, as a capret and an hert.
Onely thou schalt kepe this, that thou ete not the blood of tho, but schede out as watir in to erthe.
Kepe thou the monethe of newe fruytis, and of the bigynnyng of somer, that thou make pask to thi Lord God; for in this monethe thi Lord God ledde thee out of Egipt in the nyȝt.
And thou schalt offre pask to thi Lord God, of scheep and of oxun, in the place which thi Lord God chees, that his name dwelle there.
Thou schalt not ete ther ynne breed diȝt with sourdouȝ; in seuene daies thou schalt ete breed of affliccioun, with out sourdouȝ, for in drede thou ȝedist out of Egipt, that thou haue mynde of the dai of thi goyng out of Egipt, in alle the daies of thi lijf.
No thing diȝt with sourdouȝ schal appere in alle thi termes by seuene daies, and of the fleischis of that that is offrid in the euentid, schal not dwelle in the firste dai in the morewtid.
Thou schalt not mow offre pask in ech of thi citees whiche thi Lord God schal ȝyue to thee,
but in the place which thi Lord God chees, that his name dwelle there; thou schalt offre pask in the euentid, at the goyng doun of the sunne, whanne thou ȝedist out of Egipt.
And thou schalt sethe, and ete, in the place which thi Lord God hath chose, and thou schalt rise in the morewtid of the secunde dai, and thou schalt go in to thi tabernaclis.
Bi sixe daies thou schalt ete therf breed; and in the seuenthe dai, for it is the gaderyng of thi Lord God, thou schalt not do werk.
Thou schalt noumbre to thee seuene woukis, fro that dai in which thou settidist a sikil
in to the corn; and thou schalt halewe the feeste dai of woukis to thi Lord God, a wilful offryng of thyn hond, which thou schalt offre by the blessing of thi Lord God.
And thou schalt ete bifore thi Lord God, thou, and thi sone, and thi douȝtir, and thi seruaunt, and thin handmayde, and the dekene which is with ynne thi ȝatis, and the comelynge, and the fadirles ethir modirles child, and the widue, that dwellen with ȝou, in the place which thi Lord God chees that his name dwelle there.
And thou schalt haue mynde for thou were seruaunt in Egipt, and thou schalt kepe and do tho thingis that ben comaundid.
And thou schalt halewe the solempnytee of tabernaclis bi seuene daies, whanne thou hast gaderid thi fruytis of the cornfloor, and pressour.
And thou schalt ete in thi feeste dai, thou, and thi sone, and douȝtir, and thi seruaunt, and handmayde, also the dekene, and comelyng, and the fadirles ether modirles child, and the widewe, that ben with ynne thi ȝatis, schulen ete.
Bi seuene daies thou schalt halewe feestis to thi Lord God, in the place which the Lord chees; and thi Lord God schal blesse thee, in alle thi fruytis, and in al the werk of thin hondis, and thou schalt be in gladnesse.
In thre tymes bi the ȝeer al thi male kynde schal appere in the siȝt of thi Lord, in the place which he chees, in the solempnyte of therf looues, and in the solempnyte of woukis, and in the solempnyte of tabernaclis. A man schal not appere voide bifor the
Lord; but ech man schal offre vpe this that he hath, bi the blessyng of his Lord God, which he ȝaf to that man.
Thou schalt ordeyne iugis, and maystris, in alle thi ȝatis whiche thi Lord God schal ȝyue to thee, bi ech of thi lynagis, that
thei deme the puple bi iust doom, and bowe not in to the tother part for fauour, ethir ȝifte aȝens equete. Thou schalt not take persoone nether ȝiftis, for whi ȝiftis blynden the iȝen of wise men, and chaungen the wordis of iust men.
Thou schalt pursue iustli that that is iust, that thou lyue and welde the lond which thi Lord God schal ȝyue to thee.
Thou schalt not plaunte a wode, and ech tre bi
the auter of thi Lord God; nether thou schalt make to thee, and ordeyne an ymage; whiche thingis thi Lord God hatith.
Thou schalt not offre to thi Lord God an oxe and a scheep in which is a wem, ether ony thing of vice, for it is abhominacioun to thi Lord God.
And whanne a man ether a womman, that doon yuel in the siȝte of thi Lord God, ben foundun at thee, with ynne oon of thi ȝatis whiche thi Lord God schal ȝyue to thee, and thei breken the couenaunt
of God, that thei go and serue alien goddis, and worschipe hem, the sunne, and moone, and al the knyȝthod of heuene,
whiche thingis Y comaundide not; and this is teld to thee, and thou herist, and enquerist diligentli, and fyndist that it is soth, and abhomynacioun is doon in
Israel; thou schalt lede out the man and the womman, that diden a moost cursid thing, to the ȝatis of thy citee, and thei schulen be oppressid with stoonus.
He that schal be slayn, schal perische in the mouth of tweyne, ethir of thre witnessis; no man be slayn, for o man seith witnessyng aȝens hym.
The hond of witnessis schal first sle hym, and the last hond of the tothir puple schal be sent, that thou do a wei yuel fro the myddis of thee.
If thou perseyuest, that hard and douteful doom is at thee, bitwixe blood and blood, cause and cause, lepre and not lepre, and thou seest that the wordis of iugis with ynne thi ȝatis ben dyuerse; rise thou, and stie to the place which thi
Lord God hath choose; and thou schalt come to the preestis of the kyn of Leuy, and to the iuge which is in that tyme, and thou schalt axe of hem, whiche schulen schewe to thee the treuthe of doom.
And thou schalt do, what euer thing thei seien, that ben souereyns in the place which the Lord chees, and techen
thee bi the lawe of the Lord; thou schalt sue the sentence of hem; thou schalt not bowe to the riȝt side, ether to the lefte.
Forsothe that man schal die, which is proud, and nyle obeie to the comaundement of the preest, that mynystrith in that tyme to thi Lord God, and to the sentence of iuge, and thou schalt do
awei yuel fro the myddis of Israel; and al the puple schal here, and drede, that no man fro thennus forth bolne with pride.
Whanne thou hast entrid in to the lond, which thi Lord God schal ȝyue to thee, and weldist it, and dwellist therynne, and seist, Y schal ordeyne a kyng on me, as
alle naciouns bi cumpas han; thou schalt ordeyne hym, whom thi Lord God chesith of the noumbre of thi brethren. Thou schalt not mow make king a man of anothir folk, which man is not thi brother.
And whanne the king is ordeyned, he schal not multiplie horsis to hym, nethir he schal lede aȝen the puple in to Egipt, nethir he schal be reisid bi the noumbre of knyȝtis, moost sithen the Lord comaundide to ȝou, that ȝe turne no more aȝen bi the same weie.
The kyng schal not haue ful many wyues, that drawen his soule to ouer myche fleischlynesse, nether he schal haue grete burthuns of siluer and of gold.
Forsothe after that he hath sete in the trone of his rewme, he schal write to himsilf the deuteronomy of this lawe in a volym ether book, and he schal take a saumpler at preestis
of the kyn of Leuy; and he schal haue it with hym, and he schal rede it in alle the daies of his lijf, that he lerne to drede his Lord God, and to kepe hise wordis and cerymonyes, that ben comaundid in
the lawe; nether his herte be reisid in to pride on hise brithren, nether bowe he in to the riȝt side, ether left side, that he regne long tyme, he and hise sones on Israel.
Preestis and dekenes, and alle men that ben of the same lynage, schulen not haue part and eritage with the tother puple of Israel, for thei schulen ete the sacrifices of
the Lord, and the offryngis of hym; and thei schulen not take ony othir thing of the possessioun of her britheren; for the Lord hym silf is the eritage of hem, as he spak to hem.
This schal be the doom of preestis of the puple, and of hem that offren sacrifices; whether thei offren an oxe, ether a scheep, thei schulen ȝyue to the preest the schuldre, and the paunche,
the firste fruytis of wheete, and of wyn, and of oile, and a part of wollis of the scheryng of scheep.
For thi Lord God chees hym of alle thi lynagis, that he stonde and mynystre to the name of the Lord, he and hise sones, with outen ende.
If a dekene goith out of oon of thi citees of al Israel, in which he dwellith, and wole come and desirith the place which the
Lord chees, he schal mynystre in the name of his Lord God as alle hise britheren dekenes, that schulen stonde in that tyme byfore the Lord.
He schal take the same part of meetis, which and othere dekenes schulen take; outakun that that is due to hym in his citee, bi successioun ethir eritage of fadir.
Whanne thou hast entrid in to the lond which thi Lord God schal ȝyue to thee, be thou war lest thou wole sue abhomynaciouns of tho
folkis; noon be foundun in thee that clensith his sone, ether his douȝtir, and ledith bi the fier, ethir that axith questiouns of dyuynouris that dyuynen aboute the auteris, and that taketh hede to dremes and chiteryng of bryddis; nethir
ony wicche be, nethir an enchauntere, that is, that disseyueth mennus iȝen that a thing seme that is not; nether a man take counsel at hem that han a feend spekynge in the wombe, nether take counsel at false dyuynouris nethir seke of deed men the treuthe.
For the Lord hath abhomynacioun of alle these thingis, and for siche wickidnessis he schal do awei hem in thin entryng.
Thou schalt be perfit and without filthe, with thi Lord God.
These hethen men, the lond of whiche thou schalt welde, heren hem that worchen bi chiteryng of briddis, and false dyuynouris; forsothe thou art tauȝt in other maner of thi Lord God.
Thi Lord God schal reise a prophete of thi folk and of thi britheren as me, thou
schalt here hym; as thou axidist of thi Lord God in Oreb, whanne the cumpany was gaderid, and thou seidist, Y schal no more here the vois of my Lord God, and Y schal no more se this grettiste fier, lest Y die.
And the Lord seide to me, Thei spaken wel alle thingis.
Y schal reise to hem a prophete, lijk thee, of the myddis of her britheren, and Y schal putte my wordis in his mouth, and he schal speke to hem alle thingis, whiche I schal comaunde to him.
Forsothe Y schal be vengere of that man, that nyle here the wordis of hym, whiche he schal speke in my name.
Sotheli a prophete schal be slayn, which is bischrewid with pride, and wole speke in my name tho thingis, whiche Y comaundide not to hym, that he schulde seie, ethir bi the name of alien goddis.
That if thou answerist bi pryuy thouȝt, Hou may Y vndirstonde the word, which the Lord spak not?
thou schalt haue this signe, The Lord spak not this thing which thilke prophete biforseid in the name of the Lord, and it bifallith not, but the prophete feynede bi the pride of his soule, and therfor thou schalt not drede hym.
Whanne thi Lord God hath distried the folkis, whose lond he schal ȝyue to thee, and thou hast weldid it, and hast dwellid
