that alle the puplis of londis lurne the strongeste hond of the Lord, that also ȝe drede ȝoure Lord God in al tyme.
Therfor aftir that alle kyngis of Ammorreys herden, that dwelliden ouer Jordan at the west coost, and alle the kyngis of Canaan, that weldiden nyȝ places of the greet see, that the Lord hadden dried the flowyngis of Jordan bifor the sones of Israel, til thei passiden, the herte of hem was failid, and spirit dwellide not in hem, dredynge the entring of the sones of Israel.
In that tyme the Lord seide to Josue, Make to thee knyues of stoon, and circumside thou the sones of Israel, in the secunde tyme.
Josue dide tho thingis whiche the Lord comaundide, and he circumside the sones of Israel in the hil of prepucies.
Sotheli this is the cause of the secunde circumcisioun; al the puple of male kynde, that ȝede out of Egipt, alle men fiȝteris, weren deed in deseert bi the
lengeste cumpassis of weie, whiche alle weren circumsidid. Sotheli the puple
that was borun in deseert bi fourti ȝeer, in the weie of broddeste wildirnesse, was vncircumsidid til thei weren waastid, that herden not the vois of the Lord, and to whiche he swoor bifore, that he schulde schewe to hem the lond flowynge with mylk and hony.
The sones of hem camen aftirward in to the place of fadris, and thei weren circumsidid of Josue; whiche, as thei weren borun, weren in prepucie, nether ony man hadde circumsidid hem in the weie.
Forsothe aftir that alle weren circumsidid, thei dwelliden in the same place of tentis, til thei weren heelid.
And the Lord seide to Josue, To dai Y haue take awei fro ȝou the schenschip of Egipt. And the name of that place was clepid Galgala, til in to present dai.
And the sones of Israel dwelliden in Galgalis, and maden pask in the fourtenthe dai of the monethe at euentide, in the feeldi places of
Jerico; and thei eten of the fruytis of the lond in the tothir day, therf looues, and potage of the same ȝeer, ether cornys seengid and frotid in the hond.
And manna failide aftir that thei eten of the fruytis of the lond; and the sones of Israel vsiden no more that mete, but thei eten of the fruytis of present ȝeer of the lond of Canaan.
Sothely whanne Josue was in the feeld of the cite of Jerico, he reiside the iȝen, and siȝ a man stondynge aȝens hym, and holdynge a drawun swerd; and Josue ȝede out to hym, and seide, Art thou oure, ethir of aduersaries?
To whom he answeride, Nay, but Y am prince of the hoost of the Lord, and now Y come.
Josue felde lowe to erthe, and worschipide, and seide, What spekith my Lord to his seruaunt?
He seide, Vnlace thi schoo fro thi feet, for the place, in which thou stondist, is hooli. And Josue dide, as it was comaundid to hym.
Forsothe Jerico was closid and wardid, for the drede of the sones of Israel, and no man durste entre, ethir go out.
And the Lord seide to Josue, Lo! Y ȝaf in to thin hondis Jerico, and the king therof, and alle strong men.
Alle ȝe fiȝteris, cumpasse the citee onys bi the day; so ȝe schulen do in sixe daies.
Forsothe in the seuenthe dai the preestis schulen take seuene clariouns, of whiche the vss is in iubile; and thei schulen go bifor the arke of boond of pees; and seuen sithes ȝe schulen cumpasse the citee, and the preestis schulen trumpe with clariouns.
And whanne the vois of the trumpe schal sowne lengere, and more bi whiles, and schal sowne in ȝoure eeris, al the puple schal crie togidere with gretteste cry; and the wallis of the citee schulen falle alle doun, and alle men schulen entre bi the place, aȝens which thei stonden.
Therfor Josue, the sone of Nun, clepide preestis, and seide to hem, Take ȝe the ark of boond of pees, and seuene othere preestis take seuene clariouns of iubile ȝeeris, and go thei bifor the arke of the Lord.
Also Josue seide to the puple, Go ȝe, and cumpasse ȝe the citee, and go ȝe armed bifor the arke of the Lord.
And whanne Josue hadde endid the wordis, and seuene preestis trumpiden with seuen clariouns bifor the arke of boond of pees of
the Lord, and al the puple armed ȝede bifore, the tothir comyn puple of fiȝteris suede the arke, and alle thingis sowneden with clariouns.
Sotheli Josue comaundide to the puple, and seide, Ȝe schulen not crye, nethir ȝoure vois schal be herd, nethir ony word schal go out of ȝoure mouth, til the dai come, in which Y schal seie to ȝou, Crye ȝe, and make ȝe noyse.
Therfor the arke of the Lord cumpasside the citee onys bi day, and turnede aȝen in to the castels, and dwellide there.
Therfor while Josue roos bi nyȝt, preestis tooken
the arke of the Lord; and seuene of the preestis token seuen clariouns, of whiche the vss is in iubilee, and ȝeden bifor the arke of the Lord, and ȝeden, and trumpiden; and the puple ȝede armed bifor hem. Sotheli the tother comyn puple suede the arke, and sownede with clariouns.
And thei cumpassiden the citee in the secunde dai onys, and turneden aȝen in to the castels; so thei dyden in sixe daies.
Sotheli in the seuenthe dai thei risiden eerli, and cumpassiden the citee, as it was disposid, seuen sithis.
And whanne in the seuenthe cumpas preestis sowneden with clariouns, Josue seide to al Israel, Crie ȝe, for the Lord hath bitake
the citee to vs; and this citee be cursid, ethir distried, and alle thingis that ben therynne be halewid to the Lord. Raab the hoor aloone lyue, with alle men that ben with hir in the hows; for sche hidde the messangeris whiche we senten.
Forsothe be ȝe war, lest ȝe touchen ony thing of these that ben comaundid to ȝou, and ȝe ben gilti of trespassyng; and alle the castels of Israel be vndur synne, and be troblid.
Sotheli what euer thing is of gold, and of siluer, and of brasun vessels, and of yrun, be halewid to the Lord, and be kept in hise tresoris.
Therfor while al the puple criede, and the trumpis sowneden, aftir that the sowne sownede in the eeris of the multitude, the walles felden doun anoon; and ech man stiede bi the place that was aȝens hym. And thei token
the citee, and killiden alle thingis that weren therynne, fro man til to womman, fro ȝong child til to eld man; also thei smytiden bi the scharpnesse of swerd, oxun, and scheep, and assis.
Forsothe Josue seide to twei men, that weren sent aspieris, Entre ȝe in to the hows of the womman hoore, and brynge ȝe forth hir, and alle thingis that ben herne, as ȝe maden stedfast to hir bi an ooth.
And the ȝonge men entriden, and ledden out Raab, and her fadir, and modir, and britheren, and al the purtenaunce of houshold, and the kynrede of hir; and maden to dwelle without the castels of Israel.
Sotheli thei brenten the citee, and alle thingis that weren foundun therynne, without gold, and siluer, and brasun vesselis, and yrun, which thei halewiden in to the treserie of the Lord.
Sotheli Josue made Raab the hoore to lyue, and the hows of hir fadir, and alle thingis that sche hadde; and thei dwelliden in the myddis of Israel, til in to present dai; for sche hidde the messangeris, whiche he sente to asspie Jerico. In that tyme Josue
preiede hertli, and seide, Cursid bifor the Lord be the man, that reisith and bildith the citee of Jerico! Leie he the foundementis therof in his firste gendrid sone, and putte he the ȝatis therof in the laste of fre children.
Therfor the Lord was with Josue, and his name was pupplischid in ech lond.
Forsothe the sones of Israel braken the comaundement, and mystoken of the halewid thing; for Achar, the son of Charmy, sone of Zabdi, sone of Zare, of the lynage of Juda, toke sum thing of the halewid thing; and the Lord was wrooth aȝens the sones of Israel.
And whanne Josue sente men fro Jerico aȝens Hai, which is bisidis Bethauen, at the eest coost of the citee Bethel, he seide to hem, Stie ȝe, and aspie ȝe the lond. Whiche filliden the comaundementis,
and aspieden Hay; and thei turneden aȝen, and seiden to hym, Not al the puple stie, but twey ether thre thousynde of men go, and do awei the citee; whi schal al the puple be trauelid in veyn aȝens feweste enemyes?
Therfor thre thousynde of fiȝteris stieden, whiche
turneden the backis anoon, and weren smytun of the men of Hay; and sixe and thretti men of hem felden doun; and aduersaries pursueden hem fro the ȝate til to Saberym; and thei felden doun fleynge bi lowe places. And the herte of the puple dredde, and was maad vnstidefast at the licnesse of watir.
Sotheli Josue torente hise clothis, and felde lowe to the erthe bifor the arke of the Lord, til to euentid, as wel he, as alle the elde men of Israel; and thei castiden powdir on her heedis.
And Josue seide, Alas! alas! Lord God, what woldist thou lede this puple ouer the flood Jordan, that thou schuldist bitake vs in the hond of Ammorrey, and schulde leese vs ? Y wolde, that as we bygunnen, we hadden dwellid biȝondis Jordan.
My Lord God, what schal Y seie, seynge Israel turnynge the backis to hise enemyes?
Cananeys, and alle dwelleris of the lond schulen here, and thei schulen be gaderid togidere, and schulen cumpas vs, and schulen do awei oure name fro erthe; and what schalt thou do to thi grete name?
And the Lord seide to Josue, Rise thou; whi liggist thou low in the erthe?
Israel synnede, and brak my couenaunt; and thei token of the halewid thing, and thei han stole, and lieden, and hidden among her vessels.
And Israel may not stonde bifore hise enemyes, and Israel schal fle hem, for it is defoulid with cursyng; Y schal no more be with ȝou, til ȝe al to breke hym which is gilti of this trespas.
Rise thou, halewe the puple, and seie thou to hem, Be ȝe halewid aȝens to morewe; for the Lord God of Israel seith these thingis, A! Israel! cursyng is in the myddis of thee; thou schalt not mowe stonde bifor thin enemyes, til he that is defoulyd bi this trespas, be doon awei fro thee.
And ȝe schulen come eerli, alle men bi ȝoure lynagis; and whateuer lynage the lot schal fynde, it schal come bi hise meynees; and the meynee schal come bi housis, and the hous schal come bi men.
And whoeuer schal be takun with this trespas, he schal be brent bi fier with al his catel, for he brak the couenaunt of the Lord, and dide vnleueful thing in Israel.
Therfor Josue roos eerly, and settide in ordre Israel, bi hise lynagis; and the lynage of Juda was
foundun; and whanne that lynage was brouȝt forth bi hise meynees, the meyne of Zare was foundun. And Josue brouȝte forth it bi men, ethir housis, and foond
Zabdi; whos hows he departide in to alle men bi hemsilf; and he foond Achar, the sone of Charmy, sone of Zabdi, sone of Zare, of the lynage of Juda.
And he seide to Achar, My sone, ȝyue thou glorie to the Lord God of Israel, and knowleche thou, and schew to me what thou hast do; hide thou not.
And Achar answeryde to Josue, and seide to hym, Verily, Y synnede bifor the Lord God of Israel, and
Y dide so and so; for among the spuylis Y siȝ a reed mentil ful good, and two hundrid siclis of siluer, and a goldun reule of fifti siclis; and Y coueytide, and took awei, and hidde in the erthe, aȝens the myddis of my tabernacle; and Y hilide the siluer with erthe doluun.
Therfor Josue sente mynystris, whyche runnen to his tabernacle, and foundun alle thingis hid in the same place, and the siluer togidere;
and thei token awei fro the tente, and brouȝten tho thingis to Josue, and to alle the sones of Israel; and thei castiden forth bifor the Lord.
Therfor Josue took Achar, the sone of Zare, and the siluer, and the mentil, and the goldun reule, and hise sones, and douȝtris, oxun, assis, and scheep, and the tabernacle it silf, and al the purtenaunce of household, and al Israel with Josue; and thei ledden
hem to the valei of Achar; where Josue seide, For thou disturblidist vs, the Lord schal disturble thee in this dai. And al Israel stonyde hym; and alle thingis that weren hise, weren wastid bi fier.
And thei gaderiden on hym a greet heep of stoonys, whiche dwellen til in to present day. And the strong veniaunce of the Lord was turned awei fro hem; and the name of that place was clepid the valey of Achar til to day.
Forsothe the Lord seide to Josue, Nether drede thou withoutforth, nether drede thou withynne; take with thee al the multitude of fiȝteris, and rise thou, and stie in to the citee of Hay; lo, Y haue bitake in thin hond the king therof, and the puple, and the citee, and the lond.
And thou schalt do to the citee of Hay, and to the king therof, as thou didist to Gerico, and to the king therof; sotheli ȝe schulen take to ȝou the prey, and alle lyuynge beestis; sette thou aspies, ethir buyschementis, to the citee bihynde it.
And Josue roos, and al the oost of fiȝteris with hym, to stie in to Hay; and bi nyȝte he sente thretti chosen thousynde of stronge
men; and comaundide to hem, and seide, Sette ȝe buyschementis bihynde the citee, and go ȝe not ferthere; and alle ȝe schulen
be redi; forsothe Y, and the tothir multitude which is with me, schulen come on the contrarie side aȝens the citee; and whanne thei schulen go out aȝens vs, as we diden bifore, we schulen fle, and turne
the backis, til thei pursuen, and ben drawun away ferthir fro the citee; for thei schulen gesse, that we schulen fle as
bifore. Therfor while we schulen fle, and thei pursue, ȝe schulen ryse fro the buyschementis, and schulen waste the citee; and ȝoure Lord God schal bitake it in to ȝoure hondis.
And whanne ȝe han take it, brenne ȝe it; so ȝe schulen do alle thingis, as Y comaundide.
And Josue lefte hem, and thei ȝeden to the place of buyschementis, and saten bitwixe Bethel and Hay, at the west coost of the citee of Hay. Forsothe Josue dwellide in that nyȝt in the myddis of the puple.
And he roos eerli, and noumbride felowis, and stiede with the eldere in the frount of the oost, and was cumpassid with the helpe of fiȝteris.
And whanne thei hadden come, and hadden stied aȝens the citee, thei stoden at the north coost of the citee, bitwixe which citee and hem the valei was in the myddis.
Sotheli he hadde chose fyue thousynde men, and hadde sette in buyschementis bitwixe Bethauen and Hay, in the west part of the same citee.
Sotheli al the tothir oost dresside scheltroun to the north, so that the laste men of the multitude touchiden the west coost of the citee. Therfor Josue ȝede in that nyȝt, and stood in the myddis
of the valei; and whanne the kyng of Hai had seyn that, he hastide eerli, and ȝede out with al the oost of the citee, and he dresside scheltrun aȝens the deseert; and wiste not that buyschementis weren hid bihinde the bak.
Forsothe Josue and al the multitude of Israel ȝauen place, feynynge drede, and fleynge bi the weie of wildirnesse;
and thei crieden to gidere, and excitiden hem silf to gidere, and pursueden hem. And whanne thei hadden go
awey fro the citee, and sothely not oon hadde left in the citee of Hai and Bethauen, that pursuede not Israel, and thei leften the citees opyn, as thei hadden
broke out, the Lord seide to Josue, Reise thou the scheeld which is in thin hond, aȝens the citee of Hay; for Y schal ȝyue it to thee.
And whanne he hadde reisid the scheld aȝens the citee, buyschementis, that weren hid, riseden anoon; and thei ȝeden to the citee, and token, and brenten it.
Forsothe the men of the citee, that pursueden Josue, bihelden, and siȝen the smoke of the citee stie til to heuene; and thei myȝten no more fle hidur and thidur; most sithen thei that hadden feyned fliȝt, and ȝeden to wildirnesse, withstoden stronglieste aȝens the pursueris.
And Josue siȝ, and al Israel, that the citee was takun, and the smoke of the citee stiede; and he turnede aȝen, and smoot the men of Hay.
Sotheli also thei that hadden take and brent the citee, ȝeden out of the cytee aȝens her men, and bigunnen to smyte the myddil men of enemyes; and whanne aduersaries weren slayn on euer ethir part, so that no man of so greet
multitude was sauyd, thei tokun also the kyng of Hay lyuynge, and brouȝten to Josue.
Therfor, whanne alle men weren slayn, that pursueden Israel goynge to deseert, and felden bi swerd in the same place, the sones of Israel turneden aȝen, and smytiden the citee.
Forsothe thei that felden doun in the same dai, fro man til to womman, weren twelue thousynde of men, alle men of the citee of Hay.
Sotheli Josue withdrow not the hond, which he hadde dressid an hiȝ holdynge the scheld, til alle the dwelleris of Hay weren slayn.
Forsothe the sones of Israel departiden to hem silf the werk beestis, and the preye of the citee, as the Lord
comaundide to Josue; which brente the citee, and made it an euerlastynge biriel.
And he hangide the king therof in a iebat, til to the euentid and the goynge doun of the sunne. And Josue comaundide, and thei puttiden doun his deed bodi fro the cros; and thei castiden forth him in thilke entryng of the citee, and gaderiden on hym a greet heep of stoonus, which heep dwellith til in to present dai.
Thanne Josue bildide an auter to the Lord God of
Israel in the hil of Hebal, as Moises, the seruaunt of the Lord, comaundide to the sones of Israel, and it is writun in the book of Moises lawe, an auter of stoonys vnpolischid, whiche yrun touchide not. And he offride theron brent sacrifice to the Lord, and he offride pesible
sacrifices; and he wroot on the stoonys the Deutronomye of Moises lawe, which he hadde declarid bifor the sones of Israel. Sotheli al the puple, and the grettere
men in birthe, and the duykis, and iugis stoden on euer either side of the arke, in the siȝt of preestis and dekenes, that baren the arke of boond of pees of the Lord; as a comeling, so and a man borun in the lond; the mydil part of hem stood bisidis the hil Garasym, and the myddil part stood bisidis the hil Hebal, as Moises, the seruaunt of the Lord, comaundide. And first sotheli he blesside the puple of Israel.
Aftir these thingis he redde alle the wordis of blessyng and of cursyng, and alle thingis that weren writun in the book of lawe.
He lefte no thing vntouchid of these thingis that Moises comaundide; but he declaride alle thingis bifor al the multitude of Israel, to wymmen, and litle children, and to comelyngis that dwelliden among hem.
And whanne these thingis weren herd, alle the kyngis biȝende Jordan, that lyueden in the hilly places, and in the feeldi places, in the coostis of the see, and in the brynke of the greet see, and thei that dwellen bisidis Liban, Ethei, and Ammorrei, Cananei, and Feresey, Euey, and Jebusey,
weren gaderid togidere to fiȝte aȝens Josue and Israel, with o wille, and the same sentence.
And thei that dwelten in Gabaon, herden alle thingis whiche Josue hadde do to Jerico, and to Hay;
and thei thouȝten felli, and token to hem silf metis, and puttyden elde sackis on assis, and wyn botels brokun and sewid,
and ful elde schoon, whiche weren sewid togidere with patchis, to the schewyng of eldenesse; and thei weren clothid with elde clothis; also looues, whiche thei baren for lijflode in the weie, weren harde and brokun in to gobetis.
And thei ȝeden to Josue, that dwellide thanne in tentis in Galgala; and thei seiden to hym, and to al Israel togidere, We comen fro a fer lond, and coueyten to make pees with ȝou. And the men of Israel answeriden
to hem, and seiden, Lest perauenture ȝe dwellen in the lond, which is due to vs bi eritage, and we moun not make bond of pees with ȝou.
And thei seiden to Josue, We ben thi seruauntis. To whiche Josue seide, What men ben ȝe, and fro whennus camen ȝe?
Thei answeriden, Thi seruauntis camen fro a ful fer lond in the name of thi Lord God, for we herden the fame of his power, alle thingis whiche
he dide in Egipt, and to twei kyngis of Ammorreis biȝendis Jordan; to Seon king of Esebon, and to Og kyng of Basan, that weren in Astroth.
And the eldere men and alle the dwelleris of oure lond seiden to vs, Take ȝe metis in ȝoure hondis, for lengeste weie; and go ȝe to hem, and seie ȝe, We ben ȝoure seruauntis; make ȝe boond of pees with vs.
And we token hoote looues, whanne we ȝeden out of oure housis to come to ȝou; now tho ben maad
drye and brokun, for greet eldenesse; we filliden newe botels of wyn; now tho ben brokun and vndoon; the clothis and schoon, with whiche we ben clothid, and whiche we han in the feet, ben brokun and almost wastid, fro the lengthe of lengere weie.
Therfor the sones of Israel token of the metis of hem, and thei axiden not the mouth of the Lord.
And Josue made pees with hem. And whanne the boond of pees was maad, he bihiȝte, that thei schulden not be slayn; and the princes of the multitude sworen to hem.
Forsothe aftir thre daies of the boond of pees maad, thei herden, that thei dwelliden in nyȝ place, and that thei schulden be among hem.
And the sones of Israel mouyden tentis, and camen in the thridde dai in to the citees of hem, of whiche citees these ben the names; Gabaon, and Caphira, and Beroth, and Cariathiarym.
And thei smytiden not hem, for the princis of the multitude hadden swore to hem in the name of the Lord God of Israel. Therfor al the comyn puple grutchide
aȝens the princis of Israel; whiche answeriden to hem, We sworen to hem in the name of the Lord God of Israel, and
therfor we moun not touche hem; but we schulen do this thing to hem, sotheli be thei reserued that thei lyue, lest the ire of the Lord be stirid aȝens vs, if we forsweren
to hem; but so lyue thei, that thei hewe trees, and bere watris, in to the vsis of al the multitude. And while thei
spaken these thingis, Josue clepide Gabonytis, and seide to hem, Whi wolden ȝe disseyue vs bi fraude, that ȝe seiden, We dwellen ful fer fro ȝou, sithen ȝe ben in the myddis of vs?
Therfor ȝe schulen be vndur cursyng, and noon schal faile of ȝoure generacioun, hewynge trees and berynge watris, in to the hows of my God.
Whiche answeryden, It was told to vs thi seruauntis, that thi Lord God bihiȝte to Moises, his seruaunt, that he schulde bitake to ȝou al the lond, and schulde leese alle the dwelleris therof; therfor we dredden greetli, and purueiden to oure lyues, and weren compellid bi ȝoure drede, and we token this counsel.
Now forsothe we ben in thin hond; do thou to vs that, that semeth riȝtful and good to thee.
Therfor Josue dide, as he seide, and delyuerede hem fro the hondis of the sones of Israel, that thei schulden not be slayn.
And in that dai Josue demyde hem to be in to the seruyce of al the puple, and of the auter of the Lord, and to hewe trees, and to bere watris, til in to present tyme, in the place which the Lord hadde chose.
And whanne Adonysedech, kyng of Jerusalem, hadde herde these thingis, that is, that Josue hadde take Hai, and hadde destried it; for as Josue hadde do to Jerico and to the kyng therof, so he dide to Hay, and to the kyng therof; and that Gabaonytis hadden fled to Israel, and weren
boundun in pees with hem, Adonysedech dredde greetli; for Gabaon was a greet citee, and oon of the kyngis citees, and grettere than the citee of Hai, and alle the fiȝteris therof weren most stronge.
Therfor Adonysedech, kyng of Jerusalem, sente to Ocham, kyng of Ebron, and to Pharam, kyng of Herymoth, and to Japhie, kyng of Lachis, and to Dabir, kyng of Eglon, and
seide, Stie ȝe to me, and helpe ȝe, that we fiȝte aȝens Gabaon, for it was ȝoldun to Josue, and to the sones of Israel.
Therfor fyue kyngis of Ammorreis, the kyng of Jerusalem, the kyng of Ebron, the kyng of Herymoth, the kyng of Lachis, the kyng of Eglon, weren gaderid, and stieden togidere with her oostis; and settiden tentis aȝens Gabaon, and fouȝten aȝens it.
Sotheli the dwelleris of the citee of Gabaon, that weren bisegid, senten to Josue, that dwellide than in tentis at Galgala, and seide to hym, Withdrawe not thin hondis fro the help of thi seruauntis; stie thou soone, and delyuere vs, and helpe thou; for alle the kyngis of Amorreis, that dwelliden in the hilli places, camen togidere aȝens vs.
And Josue stiede fro Galgala, and al the oost of fiȝters, the strengeste men, with hym.
And the Lord seide to Josue, Drede thou not hem, for Y ȝaf hem in to thin hondis; noon of hem schal mow aȝenstonde thee.
Therfor Josue felde sodenli on hem, and
stiede in al the nyȝt fro Galgala; and the Lord disturblide hem fro the face of Israel, and al to-brak with greet veniaunce in Gabaon. And Josue pursuede hem bi the weie of the stiyng of Betheron, and smoot til to Azecha and Maceda.
And whanne thei fledden the sones of Israel, and weren in the goyng doun of Betheron, the Lord sente grete stoonus on hem fro heuene, til to Azecha; and many mo weren deed bi the stoonys of hail, than thei whiche the sones of Israel smytiden bi swerd.
Thanne Josue spak to the Lord, in the dai in which he bitook Amorrey in the siȝt of the sones of Israel; and Josue seide bifore hem, Sunne, be thou not mouyd aȝens Gabaon, and the moone aȝens the valei of Hailon.
And the sunne and the moone stoden, til the folc of God vengide it silf of hise enemyes. Whether this is not writun in the book of iust men? And so the sunne stood in the myddis of heuene, and hastide not to go doun in the space of o dai;
so long a dai was not bifore and aftirward; for the Lord obeiede to the vois of man, and fauȝt for Israel.
And Josue turnede aȝen, with al Israel, in to the tentis of Galgala.
Forsothe fyue kyngis fledden, and hidden hem silf in the denne of the citee of Maceda.
And it was teld to Josue, that fyue kyngis weren foundun hid in the denne of the citee of Maceda.
Which Josue comaundide to felowis, and seide, Walewe ȝe grete stoonus to the mouth of the denne, and putte ȝe witti men, that schulen kepe the closid kyngis;
sotheli nyle ȝe stonde, but pursue ȝe the enemyes, and slee ȝe alle the laste of fleeris; and suffre ȝe not hem entre in to the strengthis of her citees, whiche enemyes ȝoure Lord God bitook in to ȝoure hondis.
Therfor whanne the aduersaries weren betun with greet veniaunce, and weren almost wastid til to deeth, thei that myȝten fle Israel, entriden in to the strengthid citees.
And al the oost turnede aȝen hoole, and in hoole noumbre to Josue, in to Maceda, where the tentis weren thanne; and no man was hardi to grutche, ether to make priuy noise, aȝens the sones of Israel
And Josue comaundide, and seide, Opene ȝe the mouth of the denne, and brynge forth to me the fyue kyngis that ben hid therynne.
And the mynystris diden, as it was comaundid to hem; and thei brouȝten forth to Josue fyue kyngis fro the denne; the kyng of Jerusalem, the kyng of Ebron, the kyng of Herymoth, the kyng of Lachis, the kyng of Eglon.
And whanne thei weren led out to Josue, he clepide alle the men of Israel, and seide to the princes of the oost, that weren with hym, Go ȝe, and sette ȝoure feet on the neckis of these kyngis. And whanne thei hadden go, and trediden the neckis of the kyngis suget
to her feet, eft Josue seide to hem, Nyle ȝe drede, nethir drede ȝe with ynne, be ȝe coumfortid, and be ȝe stronge; for the Lord schal do so to alle ȝoure enemyes, aȝens whiche ȝe schulen fiȝte.
And Josue smoot, and killide hem, and hangide on fyue trees; and thei weren hangid til to euentid.
And whanne the sunne ȝede doun, he comaundide to felowis, that thei schulden put hem doun fro the iebatis; and whanne thei weren put doun, thei castiden forth hem in to the denne, in which thei weren hid; and thei puttiden grete stoonus on the mouth therof, whiche stoonus dwellen til to present tyme.
In the same dai Josue took also Maceda, and smoot bi the scharpnesse of swerd, and killide the kyng therof, and alle the dwelleris therof; he lefte not therynne, nameli, litle relikis; and he dide to the kyng of Maceda as he hadde do to the kyng of Jerico.
Forsothe Josue passide with al Israel fro Maceda in to Lempna,
and fauȝt aȝens it, which the Lord bitook, with the kyng therof, in the hond of Israel; and thei smytiden the citee bi the scharpnesse of swerd, and alle the dwelleris therof, and leften not ony relikis therynne; and thei diden to the kyng of Lempna as thei hadden do to the kyng of Jerico.
Fro Lempna he passide with al Israel in to Lachis; and whanne the oost was disposid bi cumpas, he fauȝt aȝens it.
And the Lord bitook Lachis in the hond of the sones of Israel; and he took it in the tothir dai, and smoot bi the scharpnesse of swerd, and ech man, that was therynne, as he hadde do to Lempna.
In that time Yram, kyng of Gazar, stiede to helpe Lachis; whom Josue smoot, with al his puple, til to deeth.
And he passide fro Lachis in to
Eglon, and cumpasside, and ouercam it in the same dai; and he smoot bi the scharpnesse of swerd alle men that weren therynne, bi alle thingis whiche he hadde do to Lachis.
Also he stiede with al Israel fro Eglon in to Ebron, and fauȝt
aȝens it, and took, and smoot bi the scharpnesse of swerd; and the kyng therof, and alle citees of that cuntrey, and alle men that dwelliden therynne; he lefte not ony relikis therynne; as he hadde do to Eglon so he dide also to Ebron, and wastide bi swerd alle thingis that weren therynne.
Fro thennus he turnyde in to
Dabir, and took it, and wastide; and he smoot bi the scharpnesse of swerd the kyng therof, and alle tounnes bi cumpas; he lefte not ony relikis therynne; as he hadde do to Ebron, and to Lempna, and to the kyngis of tho, so he dide to Dabir, and to the kyng therof.
And so Josue smoot al the lond of the hillis, and of the south, and of the feeld, and Asedoch with her kyngis; he lefte not therynne ony relikis, but he killide al thing that myȝte brethe, as the Lord God of Israel
comaundide to hym; fro Cades Barne til to Gazan, and al the lond of Jesson, til
to Gabaon Josue took, and wastide with o fersnesse alle the kyngis, and cuntreis of hem; for the Lord God of Israel fauȝt for hym.
And he turnede aȝen with al Israel to the place of tentis in Galgala.
And whanne Jabyn, kyng of Asor, hadde herd these thingis, he sente to Jobab, kyng of Madian, and to the kyng of Semeron, and to the kyng of Acsaph;
forsothe to the kyngis of the north, that dwelliden in the hilli places, and in the pleyn aȝens the south of Seneroth, and in the feeldi places, and cuntreis of Dor, bisidis
the see, and to Cananei fro the eest and west, and to Ammorrey, and Ethei, and Feresei, and Jebusei, in the hilli places, and to Euey, that dwellide at the rootis of Hermon, in the lond of Maspha.
And alle ȝeden out with her cumpanyes, a ful myche puple, as the grauel which is in the brynk of the see, and horsis, and charis, of greet multitude.
And alle these kyngis camen togidere at the watris of Meron, to fiȝte aȝens Israel.
And the Lord seyde to Josue, Drede thou not hem, for to morewe, in this same our, Y schal bitake alle these men to be woundid in the siȝt of Israel; thou schalt hoxe the horsis of hem, and thou schalt brenne the charis bi fier.
And Josue cam, and al his oost with hym, aȝens hem sodenli, at the watris of Meron, and felden on hem.
And the Lord bitook hem in to the hondis of Israel; whiche smytiden hem, that is, the hethen kyngis and her oostes, and pursueden til to grete Sidon, and the watris of Maserophoth, and to the feeld of Maspha, which is at the eest part therof. Josue smoot so alle men, that
he lefte no relikis of hem; and he dide as the Lord comaundide to hym; he hoxide the horsis of hem, and brente the charis.
And he turnede aȝen anoon, and took Asor, and smoot bi swerd the kyng therof; for Asor helde bi eld tyme the prinsehed among alle these rewmes.
And he smoot alle persoones that dwelliden there, he lefte not ony relikys therynne, but he wastide alle thingis til to deeth; also he distriede thilke citee bi brennyng.
And he took alle citees bi cumpas, and the kyngis of hem, and smoot, and dide awei, as Moises, the seruaunt of the
Lord, comaundide to hym, without citees that weren set in the grete hillis, and in litle hillis; and Israel brente the othere citees; flawme wastide oneli o citee, Asor, the strongeste.
And the sones of Israel departiden to hem silf al the prei, and werk beestis of these citees, whanne alle men weren slayn.
As the Lord comaundide to his seruaunt Moises, so Moises comaundide to Josue, and he fillide alle thingis; he passide not of alle comaundementis, nether o word sotheli, which the Lord comaundide to Moises.
And so Josue took al the lond of the hillis, and of the south, the lond of Gosen, and the pleyn, and the west coost, and the hil of
Israel, and the feeldi places therof; and the part of the hil that stieth to Seir til to Baalgath, bi the pleyn of Liban vndur the hil of Hermon; Josue took, and smoot, and killide alle the kyngis of the places.
Josue fauȝt myche tyme aȝens
these kyngis; no citee was, which bitook not it silf to the sones of Israel, out takun Euey that dwellide in Gabaon; he took alle bi batel.
For it was the sentence of the Lord, that the hertis of hem schulde be maad hard, and that thei schulden fiȝte aȝens Israel, and schulden falle, and schulden not disserue ony mercy, and schulden perische, as the Lord comaundide to Moises.
Josue cam in that tyme, and killide Enachym, that is, giauntis, fro the hilli placis of Ebron, and of Dabir, and of Anab, and fro al the hil of Juda, and of Israel, and dide awei the citees of hem.
He lefte not ony man of the generacioun of Enachim in the lond of the sones of Israel, without the citees of Gasa, and Geth, and Azotus, in whiche aloone thei weren left.
Therfor Josue took al the lond, as the Lord spak to Moyses, and he ȝaf it in to possessioun to the sones of Israel, bi her partis and lynagis; and the lond restide fro batels.
These ben the kyngis whiche the sones of Israel han smyte, and weldiden the lond of hem, biȝende Jordan, at the risyng of the sunne, fro the stronde of Arnon til to the hil of Hermon, and al the eest coost that biholdith the wildirnesse.
Seon, the kyng of Amorreis, that dwellide in Esebon, was lord fro Aroer, which is set on the brenke of the stronde of Arnon, and of the myddil part in the valey, and of half Galaad, til to the stronde of Jaboth, which is the terme of the sones of Amon, and fro the wildirnesse til to the
see of Ceneroth, aȝens the eest, and til to the see of deseert, which is the saltist see at the eest coost, bi the weie that ledith to Bethessymoth, and fro the south part that liggith vndur Assedoch, til to Phasga.
The terme of Og, kyng of Basan, of the relikis of Raphaym, that is, giauntis, that dwelliden in Astoroth and in Edraym, and he was lord in the hil of Hermon, and in Salacha, and in al Basan,
til to the termes of Gessuri and Machati, and of the half part of Galaad, and to the terme of Seon, kyng of Esebon.
Moyses, the seruaunt of the Lord, and the sones of Israel smytiden hem; and Moises ȝaf the lond of hem in to possessioun to Rubenytis and to Gadditis and to half the lynage of Manaasses.
These ben the kyngis of the lond, whiche Josue and the sones of Israel smytiden biȝende Jordan, at the west coost, fro Algad in the feeld of Liban, til to the hil whos part stieth in to Seir; and Josue ȝaf it in to possessioun to the lynagis of Israel, to ech his owne
part, as wel in hilli placis as in pleyn and feeldi placis; in Asseroth, and in wildirnesse, and in the south was Ethei, and Ammorrei, Cananei, and Pheresei, Euey, and Jebusei.

Josue was eld and of greet age; and the Lord seide to him, Thou hast woxe eld, and art of long tyme; and largeste lond is left, which is not ȝit departid bi
lot; that is, al Galile, Filistiym, and al
Gessuri, fro the troblid flood that moistith Egipt, til to the termes of Acaron aȝenus the north; the lond of Chanaan, which is departid in to fyue litle kyngis of Filistym, of Gaza, and of Azotus, of Ascolon, of Geth, and of Accaron.
Forsothe at the south ben Eueis, al the lond of Canaan, and Maara of Sidonyes, til to Affetha, and to the termes of Amorrei,
and the coostis of hym; and the cuntrei of Liban aȝens the eest, fro Baalgath, vndur the hil of Hermon, til thou entrist
into Emath, of alle men that dwelliden in the hil, fro the Liban til to the watris of Masserephoth, and alle men of Sidon; Y am, that schal do awei hem fro the face of the sones of Israel; therfor come it in to the part of eritage of Israel, as Y comaundide to thee.
And thou now departe the lond in to possessioun to the nyne lynagis, and to the half lynage of
Manasses, with which lynage Ruben and Gad weldiden the lond, which lond Moises, the seruaunt of the Lord, ȝaf to hem biȝende the flowyngis of Jordan, at the eest
coost; fro Aroer, which is set in the brynke of the stronde of Arnon, in the middis of the valei, and alle the feeldi
places of Medaba, til to Dibon, and alle the citees of Seon, kyng of Amorreis, that regnyde in Esebon, til to the termes of

til to Salecha; al the rewme of Og in Basan, that regnede in Astoroth, and in Edraym; he was of the relikis of Rafaym, that is, of giauntis; and Moises smoot hem and dide awey hem.
And the sones of Israel nolden destrye Gessurri and Machati; and thei dwelliden in the myddis of Israel, til in to present dai.
Sotheli he ȝaf not possessioun to the lynage of Leuy, but sacrifices, and slayn sacrifices of the Lord God of Israel; that is his eritage, as God spak to hym.
Therfor Moises ȝaf possessioun to the lynage of the sones of Ruben, bi her kynredis;
and the term of hem was fro Aroer, which is set in the brenke of the stronde of Arnon, and in the myddil valei of the same stronde, al the pleyn that

the citee of Baal Meon, and Gesa, and Sedymoth,
and Mephe, and Cariathaym, and Sabana, and Sarathaphar, in the hil of
the valey of Betheroeth, and of Asedoch,
Phasca, and Bethaissymoth; alle the feeldi citees, and alle the rewmes of Seon, kyng of Amorrey, that regnede in Esebon, whom Moyses smoot, with hise princes, Madian, Euey and Recten, and Sur, and Hur, and Rebee, duykis of Seon, enhabiters of the lond.
And the sones of Israel killiden bi swerd Balaam, the fals diuynour, the sone of Beor, with othere men slayn.
And the terme of the sones of Ruben was maad the flood of Jordan; this is the possessioun of Rubenytis bi her kynredis of
citees and of townes. And Moises ȝaf to the lynage of Gad, and to the sones therof, bi her kynredis, possessioun, of
which this is departyng; he ȝaf the termes of Jazer, and alle the citees of Galaad, and the half part of the lond of the sones of Amon, til to Aroer which is
aȝens Tabba; and fro Esebon til to Ramoth of Masphe, and Bethamyn, and Manayn,
til to the termes of Dabir; and in the valei he ȝaf Betharan, and Bethneuar, and Socoth, and Saphan, the tother part of the rewme of Seon, kyng of Esebon; and the ende of this is Jordan, til to the laste part of the see of Cenereth ouer Jordan, at the eest coost.
This is the possessioun of the sones of Gad, bi her meynees, the citees and townes of tho.
He ȝaf also possessioun to the half lynage of Manasses, and to hise sones, bi her
kynredis, of which possessioun this is the bigynnyng; he ȝaf Ammaym, and al Basan, and alle the rewmes of Og, kyng of Basan, and alle the townes of Jair, that
ben in Basan, sixti citees; and half the part of Galaad, and Astoroth, and Edray, the citees of the rewme of Og, kyng of Basan; to the sones of Machir, sones of Manasses, and to half the part of the sones of Machir, bi her kynredis.
Moises departide this possessioun in the feeldi placis of Moab ouer Jordan, aȝens Jericho, at the eest coost.
Forsothe he ȝaf not possessioun to the lynage of Leuy; for the Lord God himself of Israel is the possessioun of Leuy, as the Lord spak to hym.
This thing it is, which the sones of Israel weldiden in the lond of Canaan, which lond Eleazar the preest, and Josue, the sone of Nun, and the princes of meynees bi the lynagis of Israel ȝauen
to hem, and departiden alle thingis bi lot, as the Lord comaundide in the hond of Moises, to nyne lynagis and the half lynage.
For Moises hadde ȝoue to the twey lynagis and to the half lynage possessioun ouer Jordan; without the Leuytis, that token no thing of the lond
among her britheren; but the sones of Joseph weren departid in to twei lynagis, of Manasses and of Effraym, and weren eiris in to the place of hem. And the Leuytis token noon other part in the lond, no but citees to dwelle, and the subarbis of tho to werke beestis and her scheep to be fed.
As the Lord comaundide to Moises, so the sones of Israel diden, and departiden the lond.
And so the sones of Juda neiȝiden to Josue in Galgalis; and Caleph, the sone of Jephone, of Ceneth, spak to him, Thou knowist, what the Lord spak to Moises, the man of God, of me and of thee in Cades Barne.
Y was of fourti ȝeer, whanne Moises, seruaunt of the Lord, sente me fro Cades Barne, that Y schulde biholde the lond, and Y teelde to hym that, that semyde soth to me.
Forsothe my britheren, thats tieden with me, discoumfortiden the herte of the puple, and neuertheles Y suede my Lord God.
And Moises swoor in that dai, and seide, The lond, which thi foot trad, schal be thi possessioun, and of thi sones withouten ende; for thou suedist thi Lord God.
Sotheli the Lord grauntide lijf to me, as he bihiȝte, til in to present dai. Fourti ȝeer and fyue ben, sithen the Lord spak this word to Moises, whanne Israel ȝede bi the wildirnesse. To dai Y am
of foure scoor ȝeer and fyue, and Y am as myȝti, as Y was myȝti in that time, whanne Y was sent to aspie; the strengthe of that tyme dwellith stabli in me til to dai, as wel to fiȝte, as to go.
Therfor ȝyue thou to me this hil, which the Lord bihiȝte to me, while also thou herdist, in which hil ben Enachym, and grete citees, and strengthid; if in hap the Lord is with me, and Y mai do hem awei, as he bihiȝte to me.
And Josue blesside hym, and ȝaf to hym Ebron in to possessioun.
And fro that tyme Ebron was to Caleph, sone of Jephone, of Cenez, til in to present dai; for he suede the Lord God of Israel.
The name of Ebron was clepid bifore Cariatharbe. Adam, the gretteste, was set there in the lond of Enachym; and the lond ceesside fro batels.
Therfor this was the part of the sones of Juda, bi her kynredis; fro the terme of Edom til to deseert of Syn aȝens the south, and til to the laste part of the
south coost, the bigynnyng therof fro the hiȝnesse of the saltist see, and fro the arm therof, that biholdith to the south.
And it goith out aȝens the stiyng of Scorpioun, and passith in to Syna; and it stieth in to Cades Barne, and cometh in to Ephron, and it stieth to Daran, and
cumpassith Cariacaa; and fro thennus it passith in to Asemona, and cometh to the stronde of Egipt; and the termes therof schulen be the greet see; this schal be the ende of the south coost.
Sotheli fro the eest the bigynnyng schal be the saltiste see, til to the laste partis of Jordan, and tho partis, that biholden the north, fro the arm of the see til to the same flood of Jordan.
And the terme stieth in to Bethaegla, and passith fro the north in to Betharaba; and it stieth
to the stoon of Boen, sone of Ruben, and goith til to the termes of Debera, fro the valei of Achar aȝens the north; and it biholdith Galgala, which is on the contrarie part of the stiyng of Adomyn, fro the south part of the stronde; and it passith the watris, that ben clepid the welle of the sunne; and the outgoyngis therof schulen be to the welle of Rogel.
And it stieth bi the valei of the sone of Ennon, bi the side of Jebusei, at the south; this is Jerusalem; and fro thennus it reisith it silf to the cop of the hil, which is aȝens Jehennon at the west, in the hiȝnesse of the valei of Raphaym,
aȝens the north; and it passith fro the cop of the hil til to the wel of the watir Nepthoa, and cometh til to the tounes of the hil of Ephron; and it is bowid in to Baala, which is Cariathiarym, that is,
the citee of woodis; and it cumpassith fro Baala aȝens the west, til to the hil of Seir, and it passith bi the side of the hil Jarym to the north in Selbon, and goith doun in to Bethsamys; and it passith in
to Thanna, and cometh aȝens the partis of the north bi the side of Accaron; and it is bowid to Secrona, and passith the hil of Baala; and it cometh in to Gebneel, and it is closid with the ende of the grete see, aȝens the west.
These ben the termes of the sones of Juda, bi cumpas in her meynees.
Sotheli Josue ȝaf to Caleph, sone of Jephone, part in the myddis of the sones of Juda, as the Lord comaundide to hym, Cariatharbe, of the fadir of Enach; thilke is Ebron.
And Caleph dide awei fro it thre sones of Enach, Sisai, and Achyman, and Tholmai, of the generacioun of Enach.
And Caleph stiede fro thennus, and cam to the dwelleris of Dabir, that was clepid bifore Cariathsepher, that is, the citee of lettris.
And Caleph seide, Y schal ȝyue Axa, my douȝter, wijf to hym that schal smyte Cariathsepher, and schal take it.
And Othynyel, sone of Ceneth, the ȝongere brother of Caleph, took that citee; and Caleph ȝaf Axa, his douȝtir, wijf to hym.
And whanne sche ȝede togidere, hir hosebonde counseilide hir, that sche schulde axe of hir fadir a feeld; and sche siȝȝide, as sche sat on the
asse; to whom Caleph seide, What hast thou? And sche answeride, Ȝyue thou blessyng to me; thou hast ȝoue to me the south lond and drye; ioyne thou also the moist lond. And Caleph ȝaf to hir the moist lond, aboue and bynethe.
This is the possessioun of the lynage of the sones of Juda, bi her meynees.

Sotheli the sones of Juda myȝten not do awei Jebusei, the dwellere of Jerusalem; and Jebusei dwellide with the sones of Juda in Jerusalem til in to present day.
And the lot, ethir part, of the sones of Joseph felde fro Jordan aȝens Jerico, and at the watris therof, fro the eest; is the wildirnesse, that stieth fro Jerico to
the hil of Bethel, and it goith out fro Bethel in to Luzan, and passith the
terme of Architaroth, and it goith doun to the west, bisidis the terme of Jefleti, til to the termes of the lowere Bethoron, and of Gazer; and the cuntrees therof
ben endid with the greet see, whiche cuntreis Manasses and Effraym, the sones of Joseph, weldiden.
And the terme of the sones of Effraym, bi her meynees, and the possessioun of hem was maad aȝens the eest, Accarothaddar til to the hiȝere Bethoron.
And the coostis goon out in to the see; sotheli Mathmetath biholdith the north, and cumpassith the termes aȝens
the eest in Tharnarselo, and passith fro the stronde of Janee; and it goith doun fro Janee in to Atharoth and Noathara, and cometh in to Jerico; and it goith out
to Jordan fro Taphua, and passith aȝens the see in to the valey of the place of rehedis; and the goyngis out therof ben to the salteste see. This is the possessioun of the sones of Effraym, bi her
meynees; and citees and the townes of tho ben departid to the sones of Effraym, in the myddis of the possessioun of the sones of Manasses.
And the sones of Effraym killiden not Cananey, that dwellide in Gazer; and Cananey dwellide tributarie in the myddis of Effraym til in to this day.
Forsothe lot felde in to the lynage of Manasse, for he is the firste gendrid sone of Joseph; lot felde to Machir, the firste gendrid sone of Manasses, to the fadir of Galaad, that was a werriour, and he hadde possessioun Galaad and Basan.
And lot felde to the othere of the sones of Manasses, bi her meynees; to the sones of Abiezer, and to the sones of Heleth, and to the sones of Hesriel, and to the sones of Sichen, and to the sones of Epher, and to the sones of Semyda; these ben the sones of Manasse, sone of Joseph, the male children, bi her meynees.
Sotheli to Salphaat, the sone of Epher, sone of Galaad, sone of Machir, sone of Manasses, weren not sones, but douȝtris aloone; of whiche these ben the names, Maala, and Noa, and Eegla, and Melcha, and Thersa.
And thei camen in the siȝt of Eleazar, preest, and of Josue, sone of Nun, and of the princes, and seiden, The Lord comaundide bi the hond of Moises, that possessioun should be ȝouun to vs in the myddis of oure britheren. And Josue ȝaf to hem possessioun, bi comaundement of the Lord, in the myddis of the britheren of her fadir.
And ten cordis, that is, londis mesurid bi ten cordis, felden to Manasses, without the lond of Galaad and
of Basan biȝende Jordan; for the douȝtris of Manasses weldiden eritage in the myddis of the sones of hym. Sotheli the lond of Galaad felde in to the part of the sones of Manasses, that weren residue.
And the terme of Manasses was fro Azer Machynathath, that biholdeth Sichem, and goith out to the riȝt side, bisidis the
dwelleris of the welle Taphue; for the lond of Thaphue, which is bisidis the terme of Manasses, and of the sones of Effraym, felde in the lot of Manasses.
And the terme of the valey of place of rehedis goith doun in the south of the stronde of the citees of Effraym, that ben in the myddis of the citees of Manasses. The terme of Manasses is fro the north of the stronde, and the goyng out therof
goith to the see; so that the possessioun of Effraym is fro the south, and the possessioun of Manasses fro the north, and the see closith euer either; and tho ben ioyned to hem silf in the linage of Aser fro the north, and in the lynage of Isachar fro the eest.
And the eritage of Manasses was in Isachar and in Aser, Bersan, and the townes therof, and Jeblaan, with hise townes, and the dwellers of Dor, with her citees; and the dwelleris of Endor, with her townes, and also the dwelleris of Thanath, with her townes, and the dwelleris of Maiedo, with her townes, and the thridde part of the citee Nophet.
And the sones of Manasses miȝten not distrie these citees, but Cananei bigan to dwelle in this lond.
Sotheli aftir that the sones of Israel weren stronge, thei maden suget Cananeis, and maden tributaries to hem silf, and killiden not Cananeis.
And the sones of Joseph spaken to Josue, and seiden, Whi hast thou ȝoue to me lond in to possessioun of o lot and part, sithen Y am of so greet multitude, and the Lord hath blesside me, that is, hath alargid me in children ?
To whiche Josue seide, If thou art myche puple, stie thou into the wode, and kitte doun to thee spaces in the lond of Feresei, and of Raphaym, for the possessioun of the hil of Effraym is streiȝt to thee.
To whom the sones of Joseph answerden, We moun not stie to the hilli places, sithen Cananeis, that dwellen in the lond of the feeld, vsen ironne charis; in which lond Bersan, with hise townes, and Jesrael, weldynge the myddil valey, ben set.
And Josue seide to the hows of Joseph, and of Effraym, and of Manasses, Thou art myche puple, and of greet strengthe; thou
schalt not haue o lot, but thou schalt passe to the hil, and thou schalt kitte doun to thee; and thou schalt clense spaces to dwelle. And thou schalt mow go forth ferthere, whanne thou hast distried Cananei, whom thou seist to haue irone charis, and to be moost strong.
And alle the sones of Israel weren gaderid in Silo, and there thei settiden faste the tabernacle of witnessing; and the lond was suget to hem.
Sotheli seuene linagis of the sones of Israel dwelliden, that hadden not ȝit takun her possessiouns.
To whiche Josue seide, Hou longe faden ȝe bi cowardise, ethir slouthe, and entren not to welde the lond, which the Lord God of ȝoure fadris ȝaf to ȝou?
Chese ȝe of ech lynage thre men, that Y sende hem, and thei go, and cumpasse the lond; and that thei discryue the lond bi the noumbre of ech multitude, and brynge to me that, that ȝe han discriued.
Departe ȝe the lond to ȝou in to seuene partis; Judas be in hise termes at the south coost, and the hows of Joseph at the north;
discryue ȝe the myddil lond bitwixe hem in to seuene partis; and thanne ȝe schulen come to me, that Y sende lot to ȝou here
bifor ȝoure Lord God; for the part of Leuytis is not among ȝou, but the preesthod of the Lord, this is the eritage of hem. Forsothe Gad, and Ruben, and the half lynage of Manasses hadden take now her possessiouns ouer Jordan, at the eest coost, whiche possessiouns Moises, the seruaunt of the Lord, ȝaf to hem.
And whanne the men hadden rise to go, to discryue the lond, Josue comaundide to hem, and seide, Cumpasse ȝe the lond, and discryue it, and turne aȝen to me, that Y sende lot to ȝou here in Silo, bifore ȝoure Lord God.
And so thei ȝeden, and cumpassiden that lond, and departiden in to seuene partis, writynge in a book; and thei turneden aȝen to Josue, in to the castels in Silo.
Which Josue sente lottis bifor the Lord God in Silo, and departide the lond to the sones of Israel, in to seuene partis.
And the firste lot of the sones of Beniamyn, bi her meynees, stiede, that thei schulden welde the lond bitwixe the sones of Juda and the sones of Joseph.
And the terme of hem was aȝens the north fro Jordan, and passide bi the side of Jerico of the north coost; and it stiede fro thennus aȝens the west to the hilli places, and it cam to the wildirnesse of
Bethauen; and it passide bisidis Luza to the south; thilke is Bethel; and it goith doun in to Astoroth Adar, in to the hil which is at the south of lowere Betheron;
and is bowid, and cumpassith aȝens the see, at the south of the hil that biholdith Betheron aȝens the north; and the outgoyngis therof ben in to Cariathbaal, which is clepid also Cariathiarym, the citee of the sones of Juda; this is the greet coost aȝens the see, at the west.
Sotheli fro the south, bi the part of Cariathiarym, the terme goith out aȝens the see, and cometh til to the wel of watris
of Nepthoa; and it goith doun in to the part of the hil that biholdith the valei of the sones of Ennon, and is aȝens the north coost, in the laste part of the valey of Raphaym; and Jehennon, that is, the valei of Ennon, goith doun bi the side of Jebusei, at the south, and cometh to the welle
of Rogel, and passith to the north, and goith out to Emsemes, that is, the welle
of the sunne, and passith to the litle hillis that ben aȝens the stiyng of Adomyn; and it goith doun to Taben Boen, that is, the stoon of Boen, sone of Ruben, and passide bi the side of the north to the feeldi places; and it goith doun in to
the pleyn, and passith forth aȝens the north to Bethagala; and the outgoyngis therof ben aȝens the arm of the salteste see, fro the north, in the ende of Jordan
at the south coost, which is the terme therof fro the eest. This is the possessioun of the sones of Beniamyn, bi her termes
in cumpas, and bi her meynees; and the citees therof weren Jerico, and Bethagla,

This is the possessioun of the lynage of Dan, bi her meynees, the citees, and townes of tho.
And whanne thei hadden fillid to departe the lond bi lot to alle men bi her lynagis, the sones of Israel ȝauen possessioun to Josue, sone
of Nun, in the myddis of hem, bi the comaundement of the Lord, the citee which he axide, Thannath Sara, in the hil of Effraym; and he bildide the citee, and dwellide therynne.
These ben the possessiouns whiche Eleazar, preest, and Josue, sone of Nun, and the princis of meynees, and of the lynagis of the sones of Israel, departiden bi lot in Silo, bifor the Lord, at the dore of tabernacle of witnessing, and departiden the lond.
And the Lord spak to Josue, and seide, Spek thou to the sones of Israel, and seie
thou to hem, Departe ȝe the citees of fugytyues, ether of men exilid for vnwilful schedyng of blood, of whiche citees
Y spak to ȝou bi the hond of Moises, that whoeuer sleeth vnwytyngli a man, fle to
tho citees; that whanne he hath fled to oon of these citees, he may ascape the ire of the neiȝbore, which is veniere of blood. And he schal stonde bifor the ȝatis of the citee, and he schal speke to the eldre men of that citee tho thingis that schulen preue hym innocent; and so thei schulen resseyue hym, and schulen ȝyue to hym place to dwelle.
And whanne the vengere of blood pursueth hym, thei schulen not bitake hym in to the hondis of the vengere; for vnwityngli he killide his neiȝbore, and is not preued his enemy bifor the secounde dai ethir the thridde dai.
And he schal dwelle in that citee, til he stonde bifor the doom, and ȝelde cause of his dede. And he that killide a man, dwelle in that citee, til the grete preest die, which is in that tyme; thanne the mansleere schal turne aȝen, and he schal entre in to his citee and hows, fro which he fledde.
And thei ordeyneden Cedes in Galilee, of the hil of Neptalym, and Sichem in the hil of Effraym, and Cariatharbe, thilke is Ebron, in the hil of Juda.
And biȝende Jordan, aȝens the eest coost of Jerico, thei ordeyneden Bosor, which is set in the feeldi wildirnesse of the lynage of Ruben, and Ramoth in Galaad, of the lynage of Gad, and Gaulon in Basan, of the lynage of Manasses.
These citees weren ordeyned to alle the sones of Israel, and to comelyngis that dwellen among hem, that he that killide vnwityngli a man, schulde fle to tho citees; and he schulde not die in the hond of neiȝbore, coueitynge to venge the blood sched out, til he stood bifor the puple, to declare his cause.
And the princes of meynees of Leuy neiȝiden to Eleazar, preest, and to Josue, sone of Nun, and to the duykis of kynredis, bi alle the lynagis of the sones of
Israel; and the Leuytis spaken to hem in Sylo, of the lond of Canaan, and seiden, The Lord comaundide bi the honde of Moises, that citees schulden be ȝouun to vs to dwelle ynne, and the subarbis of tho to werk beestis to be fed.
And the sones of Israel ȝauen of her possessiouns, bi comaundement of the Lord, citees and the subarbis of tho.
And the lot ȝede out in to the meynee of Caath, of the sones of Aaron, preest, of the lynages of Juda, and of Symeon, and of Beniamyn, threttene
citees; and to the othere of the sones of Caath, that is, to dekenes that weren left, of the lynagis of Effraym, and of Dan, and of the half lynage of Manasse, ten citees.
Sotheli lot ȝede out to the sones of Gerson, that thei schulden take of the lynagis of Isachar, and of Aser, and of Neptalym, and of the half lynage of Manasses in Basan, threttene citees
in noumbre; and to the sones of Merari, bi her meynees, of the lynagis of Ruben, and of Gad, and of Zabulon, twelue citees.
And the sones of Israel ȝauen to dekenes cytees, and the subarbis of tho, as the Lord comaundide bi the hond of Moises; and alle ȝauen bi lot.
Of the lynagis of the sones of Juda, and of Symeon,
Josue ȝaf citees; to the sones of Aaron, bi the meynees of Caath, of the kyn of Leuy, of whiche citees these ben the names;
for the firste lot ȝede out to hem; Cariatharbe, of the fadir of Enach, which is clepid Ebron, in the hil of Juda, and
the subarbis therof bi cumpas; sotheli he hadde ȝoue the feeldis and townes therof to Caleph, sone of Jephone, to haue in possessioun.
Therfor Josue ȝaf to the sones of Aaron, preest, Ebron, a citee of refuyt, and the subarbis of it, and Lebnam
with hise subarbis, and Jether, and
Yschymon, and Elon, and Dabir, and Ayn, and Lethan, and Bethsames, with her subarbis;
nyne citees, of twei lynagis, as it is seid.
Sotheli of the lynage of the sones of Beniamyn, he ȝaf Gabaon, and Gabee,
and Anatoth, and Almon, with her subarbis; foure citees.
Alle the citees togidere of the sones of Aaron, preest, weren threttene, with her subarbis.
Forsothe to the othere, bi the meynees of the sones of Caath, of the kyn of Leuy, this possessioun
was ȝouun; of the lynage of Effraym, the citee of refuyt, Sichen, with hise subarbis, in the hil of Effraym, and
Gazer, and Sebsam, and Bethoron, with
her subarbis; foure citees; also of the lynage of Dan, Helthece, and Gebethon,
and Haialon, and Gethremmon, with her
subarbis; foure citees; sotheli of the half lynage of Manasses, Thanach, and Gethremon, with her subarbis; twei citees.
Alle the citees ten, and the subarbis of tho weren ȝouun to the sones of Caath, of the lowere degree.
Also to the sones of Gerson, of the kyn of Leuy, Josue ȝaf of the half lynage of Manasses, citees of refuyt, Gaulon in Basan, and Bosra, with her subarbis, twei citees.
Forsothe of the lynage of Isachar, he ȝaf Cesion,
and Daberath, and Jerimoth, and Engannym, with her subarbis; foure citees.
Of the lynage of Aser, he ȝaf Masal, and
Abdon, and Elecath, and Roob, with her subarbis; foure citees.
Also of the lynage of Neptalym, he ȝaf the citee of refuyt, Cedes in Galile, and Amodor, and Carthan, with her subarbis; thre citees.
Alle the citees of the meynees of Gerson weren threttene, with her subarbis.
Sotheli to the sones of Merary, dekenes of the lowere degree, bi her meynees, was ȝouun Getheran, of the linage of Zabulon,
and Charcha, and Demna, and Nalol; foure citees, with her subarbis.
And of the lynage of Gad, he ȝaf the citee of refuyt, Ramoth in Galaad, and Manaym, and Esebon, and Jaser; foure citees, with her subarbis.
And of the lynage of Ruben, biȝende Jordan, aȝens Jerico, he ȝaf the citee of refuyt, Bosor in the wildirnesse of Mysor, and Jazer, and Jecson, and Maspha; foure citees, with her subarbis.
Alle the citees of Merary, bi her meynees and kynredis, weren twelue.
And so alle the citees of Leuytis, in the myddis of possessioun of the sones of Israel,
weren eiȝte and fourti, with her subarbis; and alle citees weren departid by meynees.
And the Lord ȝaf to Israel al the lond which he swoor hym silf to ȝyue to the fadris of hem, and thei hadden it in possessioun, and dwelliden therynne.
And pees was ȝouun of hym in to alle naciouns by cumpas; and noon of enemyes was hardi to withstonde hem, but alle weren dryuen in to the lordschip of hem.
Forsothe nether o word, which he bihiȝte him silf to ȝyue to hem, was voide, but alle wordis weren fillid in werkis.
In the same tyme Josue clepide men of Ruben, and men of Gad, and half the
lynage of Manasses, and seide to hem, Ȝe han do alle thingis whiche Moises, seruaunt of the Lord, comaundide to ȝou,
also ȝe obeieden to me in alle thingis; nether ȝe han lefte ȝoure britheren in mych tyme til in to present dai, and ȝe kepten the comaundement of ȝoure Lord God.
Therfor for ȝoure Lord God ȝaf reste and pees to ȝoure britheren, as he bihiȝte, turne ȝe aȝen, and go ȝe in to ȝoure tabernaclis, and in to the loond of ȝoure possessioun, which lond Moyses, the seruaunt of the Lord, ȝaf to ȝou biȝende
Jordan; so onely that ȝe kepe bisili, and fille in werk the comaundement and lawe, which lawe Moises, the seruaunt of the Lord, comaundide to ȝou; that ȝe loue ȝoure Lord God, and go in alle hise weies, and kepe hise heestis, and cleue to hym and serue him in al ȝoure herte, and in al ȝoure soule.
And Josue blesside hem, and lefte hem, whiche turneden aȝen in to her tabernaclis.
Sotheli Moyses hadde ȝoue possessioun in Basan to the half lynage of Manasses; and therfor to the half lynage that lefte Josue ȝaf part among her othere britheren biȝendis Jordan, at the west coost therof. And whanne Josue leet hem go in to her tabernaclis, and hadde blessid
hem, he seyde to hem, With myche catel and richessis turne ȝe aȝen to ȝoure seetis; with siluer and gold, and bras, and yrun, and myche clothing; departe ȝe the prey of enemyes with ȝoure britheren.
And the sones of Ruben, and the sones of Gad, and half the lynage of Manasses turneden aȝen, and ȝeden fro the sones of Israel fro Silo, which is set in the lond of Canaan, that thei schulden entre in to Galaad, the lond of her possessioun, which thei gaten bi comaundement of the Lord in the hond of Moises.
And whanne thei hadden come to the litle hillis of Jordan, in to the lond of Canaan, thei bildiden bisidis Jordan an auter of greetnesse ouer comyn mesure.
And whanne the sones of Israel hadden herd this, and certeyn messangeris hadden teld to hem, that the sones of Ruben, and of Gad, and the half lynage of Manasses hadden bildid an auter in the lond of Canaan, on the heepis of Jordan, aȝens the
sones of Israel, alle camen togidir in Silo, that thei schulden stie, and fiȝte aȝens hem.
And in the meene tyme thei senten to hem in to the lond of Galaad, Fynees,
preest, the sone of Eleazar, and ten princes with hym; of ech lynage o prince.
Whiche camen to the sones of Ruben, and of Gad, and of the half lynage of Manasses, in to the lond of Galaad, and
seiden to hem, Al the puple of the Lord sendith these thingis; What is this trespassyng? Whi han ȝe forsake the Lord God of Israel, and han bildid a cursid auter, and han go awei fro the worschiping of hym?
Whether it is litil to ȝou that ȝe synneden in Belfegor, and the wem of this trespas dwellith in ȝou til in to present dai, and many of the puple felden doun?
And to day ȝe han forsake the Lord, and to morewe, that is, in tyme to comynge, the ire of hym schal be feers aȝens al Israel.
That if ȝe gessen, that the lond of ȝoure possessioun is vncleene, passe to the lond, in which the tabernacle of the Lord is, and dwelle ȝe among vs, oneli that ȝe go not awei fro the Lord, and fro oure felouschipe, bi an auter bildid outakun the auter of oure Lord God.
Whether not Achar, the sone of Zare, passide the comaundement of the Lord, and his ire felde on al the puple of Israel? And he was o man; and we wolden that he aloone hadde perischid in his trespas.
And the sones of Ruben, and of Gad, and of half the lynage of Manasses, answeriden to the princes of the
message of Israel, The strongeste Lord God hym silf of Israel knowith, and Israel schal vndirstonde togidere; if we bildiden this auter for entent of trespassyng, that is, of ydolatrye, he kepe not vs, but
punysche in present time; and if we diden bi that mynde, that we schulden putte theronne brent sacrifice, and sacrifice, and pesible sacrifices, he seke, and deme;
and not more bi that thouȝt and tretyng that we seiden, Ȝoure sones schulen seie to morew to oure sones, What is to ȝou and to the Lord God of Israel? Ȝe
sones of Ruben, and ȝe sones of Gad, the Lord hath set a terme, the flood Jordan, bitwixe vs and ȝou; and therfor ȝe han not part in the Lord; and bi this occasioun ȝoure sones schulen turne awei oure sones fro the drede of the Lord. Therfor
we gessiden betere, and seiden, Bilde we an auter to vs, not in to brent sacrifices,
nethir to sacrifices to be offrid, but in to witnessyng bitwixe vs and ȝou, and bitwixe oure children and ȝoure generacioun, that we serue the Lord, and that it be of oure riȝt to offre brent sacrifices, and sacrifices, and pesible sacrifices; and that ȝoure sones seie not to morewe to oure sones, No part in the
Lord is to ȝou. And if ȝoure sones wolen seie this, oure sones schulen answere hem, Lo! the auter of the Lord, which oure fadris maden, not in to brent sacrifices, nether in to sacrifice, but in to oure and ȝour witnessing euerlastinge.
Fer be this trespas fro vs, that we go awei fro the Lord, and forsake hise steppis, bi an auter bildid to brent sacrifices, and sacrifices, and sacrifices of preisyng to be offrid, outakun the auter of oure Lord God, which is bildid bifore his tabernacle.
And whanne these thingis weren herd, Fynees, preest, and the princes of message of Israel, that weren with hym, weren plesyd; and thei resseyueden gladli the wordis of the sones of Ruben, and of Gad, and of the half lynage of Manasses.
And Finees, preest, the sone of Eleazar, seide to hem, Now we wyten, that the Lord is with ȝou; for ȝe ben alien fro this trespassyng, and ȝe han delyuered the sones of Israel fro the hond, that is, punyschyng, of the Lord.
And Fynees turnede aȝen with the princes fro the sones of Ruben and of Gad, fro the lond of Galaad to the coost of Canaan, to the sones of Israel; and he telde to hem.
And the word pleside to alle men herynge; and the sones of Israel preisiden God, and seiden, that no more thei schulden stie aȝens hem, and fiȝte, and do awei the lond of her possessioun.
And the sones of Ruben and the sones of Gad clepiden the auter, which thei hadden bildid, Oure Witnessyng, that the Lord hym silf is God.
Forsothe whanne myche tyme was passid after that the Lord had ȝoue pees to Israel, for alle naciouns in cumpas weren suget; and whanne Josue was thanne of long lijf, and of ful eld age,
Josue clepide al Israel, and the grettere men in birthe, and the princes, and dukis, and maistris, and seide to hem, Y wexide
elde, and Y am of grettere age; and ȝe seen alle thingis whiche ȝoure Lord God hath do to alle naciouns bi cumpas, hou he fauȝt for ȝou.
And now for he departide to ȝou bi lot al the lond, fro the eest part of Jordan til to the grete see,
and many naciouns ben left ȝit, ȝoure Lord God schal distrie hem, and schal take awei fro ȝoure face; and ȝe schulen welde the lond, as he bihiȝte to ȝou.
Oneli be ȝe coumfortid, and be ȝe bisy, that ȝe kepe alle thingis that ben writun in the book of Moises lawe, and bowe not awei fro tho, nether to the riȝt side nether to
the left side, lest aftir that ȝe han entrid to the hethene men, that schulen be among ȝou, ȝe swere in the name of the goddis of hem, and ȝe serue tho goddis, and worschipe hem.
But cleue ȝe to ȝoure Lord God, which thing ȝe han do til in to
this dai; and thanne the Lord God schal do awei in ȝoure siȝt grete folkis, and strongeste; and noon schal mow aȝenstonde ȝou.
Oon of ȝou schal pursue a thousynde men of enemyes, for ȝoure Lord God schal fiȝte for ȝou, as he bihiȝte.
Be ȝe war bifore moost diligentli of this thing oneli, that ȝe loue ȝoure Lord God.
That if ȝe wolen cleue to the errouris of these folkis that dwellen among ȝou, and wolen medle mariagis with hem, and couple
frenschipis, wite ȝe riȝt now, that ȝoure Lord God schal not do awei hem bifor ȝoure face, but thei schulen be to ȝou in to a dich, and a snare, and in to hirtyng of ȝoure side, and in to stakis in ȝoure iȝen, til ȝoure Lord God take awei ȝou, and distrie fro this beste loond, which he ȝaf to ȝou.
Lo! Y entre to dai in to the weye of al erthe; and ȝe schulen knowe with al soule, that of al wordis whiche the Lord bihiȝte hym silf to ȝyue to ȝou, not oon passide in veyn.
Therfor as he fillide in werk that, that he bihiȝte, and alle thingis bifelden bi prosperite, so he schal brynge on ȝou whateuer thing of yuelis he manaasside, til he take awei ȝou, and distrie fro this beste lond, which he ȝaf to ȝou.
For ȝe braken the couenaunt of ȝoure Lord God, which he made with ȝou, and serueden alien goddis, and worschipeden hem, sone and swiftli the strong veniaunce of the Lord schal rise on to ȝou; and ȝe schulen be takun awei fro this beste lond, which he ȝaf to ȝou.
And Josue gaderide alle the lynagis of Israel in to Sechem; and he clepide the grettere men in birthe, and the princes, and iugis, and maistris; and thei stoden in the siȝt of the Lord.
And he spak thus to the puple, The Lord God of Israel seith these thingis, Ȝoure fadris dwelliden at the bigynnyng biȝende the flood Eufrates, Thare, the fadir of Abraham, and Nachor, and thei serueden alien goddis.
Therfor Y took ȝoure fadir Abraham fro the coostis of Mesopotanye, and Y brouȝte hym in to the lond of Canaan; and Y
multipliede the seed of hym, and Y ȝaf Isaac to hym; and eft Y ȝaf to Isaac, Jacob, and Esau, of whiche Y ȝaf to Esau the hil of Seir, to haue in possessioun; forsothe Jacob and hise sones ȝeden doun in to Egipt.
And Y sente Moises and Aaron, and Y smoot Egipt
with many signes and wondris, and Y ledde ȝou and ȝoure fadris out of Egipt. And ȝe camen to the see, and Egipcians pursueden ȝoure fadris with charis, and multitude of knyȝtis, til to the Reed See.
Forsothe the sones of Israel crieden to the Lord, and he settide derknessis bitwixe ȝou and Egipcians; and he brouȝte the see on hem, and hilide hem. Ȝoure iȝen sien alle thingis, whiche Y dide in Egipt. And ȝe dwelliden in wildirnesse in myche tyme.
And Y brouȝte ȝou in to the lond of Ammorrei, that dwellide biȝende Jordan; and whanne thei fouȝten aȝens ȝou, Y bitook hem in to ȝoure hondis, and ȝe hadden in possessioun the lond of hem, and ȝe killiden hem.
Sotheli Balach, the sone of Sephor, the king of Moab, roos, and fauȝt aȝens Israel; and he sente, and clepide Balaam, the sone of Beor, that he schulde curse ȝou.
And Y nolde here hym, but aȝenward bi hym Y blesside ȝou, and delyuerede ȝou fro hise hondis.
And ȝe passiden Jordan, and camen to Jerico; and men of that citee fouȝten aȝens ȝou, Ammorrei, and Feresei, and Cananei, Ethei, and Gergesei, and Euei, and Jebusei; and Y bitook hem in to ȝoure hondis.
And Y sente flies with venemouse tongis bifor ȝou, and Y castide hem out of her places; Y kyllide twei kyngis of Ammorreis, not in thi swerd and bowe.
And Y ȝaf to ȝou the lond in which ȝe traueiliden not, and citees whiche ȝe bildiden not, that ȝe schulden dwelle in tho, and vyneris, and places of olyue trees, whiche ȝe plauntiden not.
Now therfor drede ȝe the Lord, and serue ȝe hym with perfite herte and moost trewe; and do ȝe awei the goddis, to whiche ȝoure fadris seruyden in Mesopotanye, and in Egipt; and serue ȝe the Lord.
But if it semeth yuel to ȝou, that ȝe serue the Lord, chesyng is ȝouun to ȝou; chese ȝe to ȝou to dai that, that plesith, whom ȝe owen most to serue; whether to goddis, whiche ȝoure fadris serueden in Mesopotanye, whether to the goddis of Ammorreis, in whose lond ȝe dwellen; forsothe Y, and myn hows schulen serue the Lord.
And al the puple answeride and seide, Fer be it fro vs that we forsake the Lord, and serue alien goddis.
Oure Lord God hym silf ledde vs and oure fadris out of the lond of Egipt, fro the hows of seruage, and dide grete signes in oure siȝt; and he kepte vs in al the weie, bi which we ȝeden, and in alle puplis, bi whiche we passiden;
and he castide out alle folkis, Ammorrei, the dwellere of the lond, in to which we entriden. Therfor we schulen serue the Lord, for he is oure Lord God.
And Josue seide to the puple, Ȝe moun not serue the Lord; for God is hooli, and a strong feruent louyere, and he forȝyueth not ȝoure trespassis and synnes.
If ȝe forsaken the Lord, and seruen alien goddis, the Lord schal turne hym silf, and schal turment ȝou, and schal distrie, after that he hath ȝoue goodis to ȝou.
And the puple seide to Josue, It schal not be so, as thou spekist, but we schulen serue the Lord.
And Josue seide to the puple, Ȝe ben witnessis, that ȝe han chose the Lord to ȝou, that ȝe serue him. And thei answeriden, We ben witnessis.
Therfor, he seide, Now do ȝe awei alien goddis fro the myddis of ȝou, and bowe ȝe ȝoure hertis to the Lord God of Israel.
And the puple seide to Josue, We schulen serue oure Lord God, and we schulen be obedient to hise heestis.
Therfor Josue smoot a boond of pees in that dai, and settide forth to the puple comaundementis and domes in Sichen.
And he wroot alle these wordis in the book of Goddis lawe. And he took a greet stoon, and puttide it vndur an ook, that was in the seyntuarie of the Lord.
And he seide to al the puple, Lo! this stoon schal be to ȝou in to witnessing, that ȝe herden alle the wordis of the Lord, whiche he spak to ȝou, lest perauenture ȝe wolden denye aftirward, and lye to ȝoure Lord God.
And he lefte the puple, ech man in to his possessioun.
And after these thingis Josue, the sone of Nun, the seruaunt of the Lord, diede, an hundride ȝeer eld and ten.
And thei birieden hym in the costis of his possessioun, in Thannath of Sare, which is set in the hil of Effraym, fro the north part of the hil Gaas.
And Israel seruede the Lord in alle the daies of Josue, and of the eldre men, that lyueden in long tyme aftir Josue, and whiche eldre men knewen alle the werkis of the Lord, whiche he hadde do in Israel.
Also the sones of Israel birieden the boonys of Joseph, whiche thei baren fro Egipt in Sichen, in the part of the feeld, which feeld Jacob bouȝte of the sones of Emor, fadir of Sichen, for an hundrid ȝonge scheep; and it was in to possessioun of the sones of Joseph.
Also Eliazar, sone of Aaron, preest, diede; and Fynees and hise sones biryden hym in Gabaa, which was ȝouun to hym in the hil of Efraym.
AFTIR the deeth of Josue the sones of Israel counseliden the Lord, and seiden, Who schal stie bifor vs aȝens Cananei, and schal be duik of the batel?
And the Lord seide, Judas schal stie; lo! Y haue ȝoue the lond in to hise hondis.
And Judas seide to Symeon, his brother, Stie thou with me in my lot, and fiȝte thou aȝens Cananei, that Y go with thee in thi lot.
And Symeon ȝede with hym; and Judas stiede. And the Lord bitook Cananey and Feresei in to the hondis of hem, and thei killiden in Besech ten thousynde of men.
And thei founden Adonybozech in Besech, and thei fouȝten aȝens hym, and smytiden Cananei, and Feresey.
Forsothe Adonybozech fledde, whom thei pursueden, and token, and kittiden the endis of hise hondis and feet.
And Adonybozech seide, Seuenti kyngis, whanne the endis of hondis and feet weren kit awey, gaderiden relifs of metis vndur my bord; as Y dide, so God hath ȝolde to me. And thei brouȝten hym in to Jerusalem, and there he diede.
Therfor the sones of Juda fouȝten aȝens Jerusalem, and token it, and smytiden bi the scharpnesse of swerd, and bitoken al the cytee to brennyng.
And aftirward thei ȝeden doun, and fouȝten aȝens Cananey, that dwellide in the hilli places, and at the south, in feeldi places.
And Judas ȝede aȝens Cananei, that dwellide in Ebron, whos name was bi eld tyme Cariatharbe; and Judas killide Sisay, and Achyman, and Tholmai.
And fro thennus he ȝede forth, and ȝede to the dwelleris of Dabir, whos eld name was Cariathsepher, that is, the citee of lettris.
And Caleph seide, Y schal ȝyue Axa, my douȝter, wijf to hym that schal smyte Cariathsepher, and schal waste it.
And whanne Othonyel, sone of Seneth, the lesse brother of Caleph, hadde take it, Caleph ȝaf Axa, his douȝter, wijf to hym.
And hir hosebonde stiride hir, goynge in the weie, that sche schulde axe of hir fadir a feeld; and whanne sche hadde siȝid, sittynge on the asse, Caleph seide to hir, What hast thou?
And sche answeride, Ȝiue thou blessyng to me, for thou hast ȝoue a drye lond to me; ȝyue thou also a moyst lond with watris. And Caleph ȝaf to hir the moist lond aboue, and the moist lond bynethe.
Forsothe the sones of Cyney, alye of Moyses, stieden fro the citee of palmes with the sones of Juda, in to the desert of his lot, which desert is at the south of Arath; and dwelliden with hym.
Sotheli Judas ȝede with Symeon, his brother; and thei smytiden togidere Cananei, that dwellide in Sephar, and killiden hym; and the name of that citee was clepid Horma, that is, cursyng, ether perfit distriyng, for thilke citee was distried outerly.
And Judas took Gaza with hise coostis, and Ascolon, and Accaron with hise termes.
And the Lord was with Judas, and he hadde in possessioun the hilli places; and he myȝte not do awey the dwelleris of the valei, for thei weren plenteuouse in yrun charis, scharpe as sithis.
And the sones of Israel ȝauen Ebron to Caleph, as Moises hadde seid, which Caleph dide awei fro it thre sones of Enach.
Forsothe the sones of Beniamyn diden not awei Jebusei, the dwellere of Jerusalem; and Jebusei dwellide with the sones of Beniamyn in Jerusalem til in to present dai.
Also the hows of Joseph stiede in to Bethel, and the Lord was with hem.
For whanne thei bisegiden the citee, that
was clepid Lusa bifore, thei sien a man goynge out of the citee, and thei seiden to hym, Schewe thou to vs the entrynge of the cytee, and we schulen do mercy with thee.
And whanne he hadde schewid to hem, thei smytiden the citee bi scharpnes of swerd; sotheli thei delyueriden that man and al his kynrede.
And he was delyuerede, and ȝede in to the lond of Sethym, and bildide there a citee, and clepid it Luzam; which is clepid so til in to present dai.
Also Manasses dide not awei Bethsan and Thanael with her townes, and the dwelleris of Endor, and Geblaam and Magedo with her townes; and Cananei bigan to dwelle with hem.
Sotheli after that Israel was coumfortid, he made hem tributaries, ethir to paye tribute, and nolde do awey hem.
Sotheli Effraym killide not Cananei that dwellyde in Gaser, but dwellide with hym.
Zabulon dide not awey the dwelleris of Cethron, and of Naalon; but Cananei dwellide in the myddis of hym, and was maad tributarie to him.
Also Aser dide not awey the dwelleris of Acho, and of Sidon, of Alab, and of Azazib, and of Alba, and Aphech, and of Aloa, and of Pha, and of Roob;
and he dwellide in the myddis of Cananey, dwellere of that lond, and killide not hym.
Neptalym dide not awei the dwelleris of Bethsames, and of Bethanach; and he dwellide among Cananey, dwellere of the lond; and Bethsamytis and Bethanytis weren tributarie to hym.
And Ammorrey helde streit the sones of Dan in the hil, and ȝaf not place to hem to go
