And now thei weren bisidis Jebus, and the day was chaungid in to nyȝt. And the child seide to his lord, Come thou, Y biseche, bowe we to the citee of Jebus, and dwelle we therynne.
To whom the lord answeride, Y schal not entre in to the citee of an alien folc, which is not of the sones of Israel, but Y schal
passe til to Gabaa; and whanne Y schal come thidur, we schulen dwelle therynne, ether certis in the citee of Rama.
Therfor thei passiden Jebus, and token the weie bigunnun. And the sunne ȝede doun to hem bisidis Gabaa, which is in the
lynage of Beniamyn; and thei turneden to it, that thei schulden dwelle there. Whidur whanne thei hadden entrid, thei saten in the street of the citee, and no man wolde resseyue hem to herbore.
And lo! an eld man turnede aȝen fro the feeld, and fro his werk in the euentid, and apperide to hem, which also hym silf was of the hil of Effraym, and he dwellide a pilgrym in Gabaa. Therfor men of that cuntrey weren the sones of Gemyny.
And whanne the eld man reiside his iȝen, he siȝ a man sittynge with hise fardels in the street of the citee; and he seide to that man, Fro whennus comest thou? and whidur goist thou?
Which answeride to hym, We ȝeden forth fro Bethleem of Juda, and we gon to oure place, which is in the side of the hil of Effraym, fro whennus we ȝeden to Bethleem; and now we gon to the hows of God, and no man
wole resseyue vs vndur his roof, and we han prouendre and hey in to mete of assis, and breed and wyn in to myn vsis, and of thin handmayde, and of the child which is with me; we han no nede to ony thing, no but to herbore.
To whom the eld man answeride, Pees be with thee; Y schal ȝyue alle thingis, that ben nedeful; oneli, Y biseche, dwelle thou not in the street.
And he brouȝte hym in to his hows, and ȝaf mete to the assis; and after that thei waischiden her feet, he resseyuede hem in to feeste.
While thei eeten, and refreischiden the bodies with mete and drynk after the trauel of weie, men of that citee camen, the sones of Belial, that is, with out ȝok, and thei cumpassiden the hows of the elde man, and bigunnun to knocke the doris; and thei crieden to the lord of the hows, and seiden, Lede out the man that entride in to thin hows, that we mysuse him.
And the elde man ȝede out to hem, and seide, Nyle ȝe, britheren, nyle ȝe do this yuel; for the man entride in to myn herbore; and ceesse ȝe of this foli.
Y haue a douȝter virgyn, and this man hath a wijf; Y schal lede out hem to ȝou, that ȝe make lowe hem, and fille ȝoure lust; oneli, Y biseche, that ȝe worche not this cursidnesse aȝens kynde aȝens the man.
Thei nolden assente to hise wordis; which thing the man siȝ, and ledde out his wijf to hem, and bitook to hem hir to be defoulid. And whanne thei hadden misusid hir al niȝt, thei leften hir in the morewtid.
And whanne the derknessis departiden, the womman cam to the dore of the hows, where hir lord dwellide, and there sche felde doun.
Whanne the morewtid was maad, the man roos, and openyde the dore, that he schulde fille the weie bigunnun; and lo! his wijf lay bifor the dore, with hondis spred in the threischfold.
And he gesside hir to reste, and spak to hir, Rise thou, and go we. And whanne sche answeride no thing, he vndirstode that sche was deed; and he took hir, and puttide on the asse, and turnede aȝen in to his hows.
And whanne he entride in to that hows, he took a swerd, and departide in to twelue partis and gobetis the deed body of the wijf, and sente in to alle the termes of Israel.
And whanne alle men hadden herde this, thei crieden, Neuere siche a thing was don in Israel, fro that dai in which oure fadris stieden fro Egipt til in to present tyme; seie ȝe sentence, and deme ȝe in comyn, what is nede to be doon.
Therfor alle the sones of Israel ȝeden, and weren gaderid togidere as o man, fro Dan til to Bersabee, and fro the lond of Galaad to the Lord in Maspha; and
alle the corneris of puplis; and alle the lynagis of Israel camen to gidere in to the chirche of the puple of God, foure hundrid thousynde of foot men fiȝters.
And it was not hid fro the sones of Beniamyn, that the sones of Israel hadden stied in to Maspha. And the dekene, hosebonde of the wijf that was slayn, was axid,
how so greet felonye was doon; and he answeride, Y cam with my wijf in to Gabaa of Beniamyn, and Y turnede thidur.
And lo! men of that citee cumpassiden in nyȝt the hows, in which Y dwellide, and thei wolden sle me, and thei bitraueliden my wijf with vnbileueful woodnesse of letcherie; at the last sche was deed.
And Y took, and Y kittide hir in to gobetis, and Y sente partis in to alle the termes of ȝoure possessioun; for so greet felonye and so greuouse synne was neuere doon in Israel.
Alle ȝe sones of Israel ben present; deme ȝe, what ȝe owen do.
And al the puple stood, and answeride as bi word of o man, that is acordyngli, with out aȝenseiyng and with out delay, We schulen not go awei in to oure tabernaclis, nethir ony man schal
entre in to his hows; but we schulen do this in comyn aȝens Gabaa.
Ten men be chosun of an hundrid, of alle the lynagis of Israel, and an hundrid of a thousynde, and a thousynde of ten thousynde, that thei bere metis to the oost, and that we, fiȝtynge aȝens Gabaa of Beniamyn, moun ȝelde to it for the trespas that that it deserueth.
And al the puple, as o man, cam togidere to the citee bi the same thouȝt and o counsel.
And thei senten messangeris to al the lynage of Beniamyn, whiche messangeris seiden, Whi so greet felony is foundun in ȝou?
Bitake ȝe the men of Gabaa, that diden this wickidnesse, that thei die, and yuel be doon awey fro Israel. Whiche nolden here the comaundement of her britheren,
the sones of Israel, but of alle the citees, that weren of her part, thei camen togidere in to Gabaa, to helpe hem, and to fiȝte aȝens al the puple of Israel.
And fyue and twenti thousynde weren foundun of Beniamyn, of men drawynge out swerd,
outakun the dwelleris of Gabaa, whiche weren seuen hundrid strongeste men, fiȝtynge so with the lefthond as with the riȝthond, and castynge so stoonus with slyngis at a certeyn thing, that thei myȝten smyte also an heer, and the strook of the stoon schulde not be borun in to the tother part.
Also of the men of Israel, with out the sones of Beniamin, weren foundun foure hundrid thousynd of men drawynge swerd and redi to batel.
Whiche riseden and camen in to the hows of God, that is in Silo; and thei counceliden God, and seiden, Who schal be prince in oure oost of the batel aȝens the sones of Beniamyn? To whiche the Lord answeride, Judas be ȝoure duyk.
And anoon the sones of Israel risiden eerli, and settiden tentis aȝens Gabaa.
And fro thennus thei ȝeden forth to batel aȝens Beniamyn, and bigunnen to fiȝte aȝens the citee.
And the sones of Beniamyn ȝeden out of Gabaa, and killiden of the sones of Israel in that dai two and twenti thousynde of men.
And eft the sones ofIsrael tristiden in strengthe and noumbre, and dressiden schiltrun, in the same place in which
thei fouȝten bifore; so netheles that thei stieden bifore, and wepten bifor the Lord til to nyȝt, and counseliden hym, and seiden, Owe Y go forth more to fiȝte aȝens the sones of Beniamyn, my britheren, ether nay? To whiche he answeride, Stie ȝe to hem, and bigynne ȝe batel.
And whanne the sones of Israel hadden go forth to batel in the tother dai aȝens
Beniamyn, the sones of Beniamyn braken out of the ȝates of Gabaa, and camen to hem; and the sones of Beniamyn weren wood aȝens hem bi so greet sleyng, that thei castiden doun eiȝtene thousynde of men drawynge swerd.
Wherfor alle the sones of Israel camen in to the hows of God, and saten, and wepten bifore the Lord, and thei fastiden in that dai til to euentid; and thei offeriden to the Lord
brent sacrifices and pesible sacrifices, and axiden of her staat. In that tyme the arke of boond of pees of God was there
in Silo; and Fynees, the sone of Eleazar, sone of Aaron, was souereyn of the hows. Therfor thei counseliden the Lord, and seiden, Owen we go out more to batel aȝens the sones of Beniamyn, oure britheren, ethir reste? To whiche the Lord seide, Stie ȝe, for to morewe Y schal bytake hem in to ȝoure hondis.
And the sones of Israel settiden buyschementis bi
the cumpas of the citee of Gabaa; and the thridde tyme as onys and tweis thei brouȝten forth oost aȝens Beniamyn.
But also the sones of Beniamyn braken out of the citee booldli, and pursueden ferthere the aduersaryes fleynge, so that thei woundiden of hem, as in the firste dai and the secounde, and killiden bi twey paththis the aduersaries turnynge backis; of whiche paththis oon was borun in to Bethel, the tother in to Gabaa. And thei
castiden doun aboute thretti men; for thei gessiden to sle hem bi customable maner; whiche feyneden fliȝt bi craft, and token counsel, that thei schulden drawe hem fro the citee, and that thei as fleynge schulden brynge to the forseid paththis.
Therfor alle the sones of Israel risiden of her seetis, and settiden schiltrun in the place which is clepid Baalthamar. And the buschementis, that weren aboute the citee, bigunnen to opene
hem silf litil and litil, and to go forth fro the west part of the citee. But also othere ten thousynde of men of al Israel excitiden the dwelleris of the cite to batels; and the batel was maad greuous aȝens the sones of Beniamyn, and thei vndurstoden not, that perisching neiȝede to hem on eche part.
And the Lord smoot hem in the siȝt of the sones of Israel, and thei killiden of hem in that dai fyue and twenti thousynde and an hundrid men, alle the werryours and drawynge swerd.
Sotheli the sones of Beniamyn bigunnen to fle, whanne thei sien, that thei weren the lowere. And the sones of Israel sien this, and ȝauen to hem place to fle, that thei schulden come to the buyschementis maad redi, whiche thei hadden set bisidis the citee.
And whanne thei hadden rise sudenli fro hid places, and Beniamyn ȝaf backis to the sleeris, thei entriden in to the citee, and smytiden it by the scharpnesse of swerd.
Sotheli the sones of Israel hadden ȝoue a signe to hem whiche thei hadden set in buyschementis, that aftir that thei hadden take the citee, thei schulden kyndle fier, and that bi smook stiynge an hiȝ, thei schulden schewe the citee takun.
And whanne the sones of Israel set in thilke batel sien this; for the sones of Beniamyn gessiden hem to fle, and thei sueden bisiliere, whanne thretti men of her oost
weren slayn; and the sones of Israel sien as a piler of smoke stie fro the citee; also Beniamyn bihelde bihynde, whanne he siȝ the citee takun, and
flawmes borun an hiȝe, thei that feyneden fliȝt bifore, aȝenstoden strongliere with face turned. And whanne the sones of Beniamyn hadden seyn this, thei weren
turned in to fliȝt, and thei bigunnen to go to the weie of deseert; while also aduersaries pursueden hem there, but also thei, that hadden brent the citee, camen aȝens hem.
And so it was doon, that thei weren slayn of enemyes on ech part, nether ony reste of men diynge was; and thei felden, and weren cast doun at the eest coost of the citee of Gabaa.
Forsothe thei, that weren slayn in the same place, weren eiȝtene thousynde of men, alle strongeste fiȝteris.
And whanne thei that leften of Beniamyn hadden seyn this, thei fledden in to wildirnesse, and thei ȝeden to the stoon, whos name is Remmon. And in that fliȝt the sones of Israel ȝeden opynli, and ȝeden in to dyuerse places, and killiden fyue thousynde men; and whanne thei ȝeden ferther, thei pursueden hem, and killiden also othere twei thousynde.
And so it was doon, that alle that felden doun of Beniamyn in diuerse places, weren fyue and twenti thousynde, fiȝterys moost redi to batels.
And so sixe hundrid men leften of al the noumbre of Beniamyn, that myȝten ascape, and fle in to wildirnesse; and thei saten in the stoon of Remmon foure monethis.
Forsothe the sones of Israel ȝeden out, and smytiden with swerd alle the remenauntis of the citee, fro men til to werk beestis; and deuourynge flawme wastide alle the citees and townes of Beniamyn.
Also the sones of Israel sworen in Maspha, and seiden, Noon of vs schal ȝyue to the sones of Beniamyn a wijf of his douȝtris.
And alle camen to the hows of God in Silo, and thei saten in the siȝt of hym til to euentid, and thei reisiden the vois, and bigunnen to wepe with greet
ȝellyng, and seiden, Lord God of Israel, whi is this yuel don in thi puple, that to dai o lynage be takun awey of vs?
Sotheli in the tother day thei risiden eerli, and bildyden an auter, and offriden there brent sacrifices and pesible sacrifices,
and seiden, Who of alle the lynagis of Israel stiede not in to the oost of the Lord? For whanne thei weren in Maspha, thei hadden bounde hem silf with a greuouse ooth, that thei that failiden schulden be slayn.
And the sones of Israel weren led bi penaunce on her brother Beniamyn, and bigunnen to seie, O lynage of
Israel is takun awey; wherof schulen thei take wyues? for alle we sworen in comyn, that we schulen not ȝyue oure douȝtris to hem.
Therfor thei seiden, Who is of alle the lynagis of Israel, that stiede not to the Lord in Maspha? And lo! the dwelleris of Jabes of Galaad weren foundun, that thei weren not in the oost.
Also in that tyme, whanne thei weren in Silo, noon of hem was foundun there.
Therfor thei senten ten thousynde strongeste men, and comaundiden to hem, Go ȝe, and smyte the dwelleris of Jabes of Galaad bi the scharpnesse of swerd, as wel the wyues as the litle children of hem.
And this thing schal be, which ȝe owen to kepe, sle ȝe alle of male kynde, and the wymmen, that knewen men fleischli; reserue ȝe the virgyns.
And foure hundrid virgyns, that knewen not the bed of man, weren foundun of Jabes of Galaad; and thei brouȝten hem to the castels in Silo, in to the lond of Chanaan.
And thei senten messangeris to the sones of Beniamyn, that weren in the stoon of Remmon; and thei comaundiden to hem, that thei schulden resseyue tho wymmen in pees.
And the sones of Beniamyn camen in that tyme, and the douȝtris of Jabes of Galaad weren ȝouun to hem to wyues; forsothe thei founden not othere wymmen, whiche thei schulden ȝyue in lijk maner.
And al Israel sorewide greetly, and dide penaunce on the sleyng of o lynage of Israel.
And the grettere men in birthe seiden, What schulen we do to the othere men, that han not take wyues? Alle the wymmen in Beniamyn
felden doun, and it is to vs to puruey with greet cure and greet studie, that o lynage be not don awey fro Israel.
We moun not ȝyue oure douȝtris to hem, for we ben boundun with an ooth and cursyng, bi which we seiden, Be he cursid that ȝyueth of hise douȝtris a wijf to Beniamyn.
And thei token a counsel, and seiden, Lo! annyuersarie solempnyte of the Lord is in Silo, whych is set at the north of the citee of Bethel, and at the eest coost of the weie that goith from Bethel to Siccyma, and at the south of the citee of Lebona.
And thei comaundiden to the sones of Beniamyn, and seiden, Go ȝe, be ȝe hid in the vyneris;
and whanne ȝe seen douȝtris of Silo go forth bi custom to lede daunsis, go ȝe out of the vyneris sudeynli, and rauysche ȝe hem, eche man o wijf, and go ȝe in to the lond of Beniamyn.
And whanne the fadris and britheren of hem schulen come, and bigynne to pleyne and plete aȝens ȝou, we schulen seie to hem, Haue ȝe mercy of hem; for thei rauyschiden not hem bi riȝt of fiȝteris and ouercomeris, but ȝe ȝauen not to hem preiynge that thei schulden take; and the synne is of ȝoure part.
And the sones of Beniamyn diden as it was comaundid to hem, and bi her noumbre thei rauyschiden wyues to hem, ech man o wijf, of hem that ledden daunsis. And thei ȝeden in to her possessioun, and bildiden citees, and dwelliden in tho.
And the sones of Israel turneden aȝen, bi lynagis and meynees, in to her tabernaclis. In tho dayes was no kyng in Israel, but ech man dide this, that semyde ryȝtful to hym silf.
IN the daies of o iuge, whanne iugis weren souereynes, hungur was maad in the lond; and a man of Bethleem of Juda ȝede to be a pylgrym in the cuntrei of Moab, with his wijf and twey fre sones.
He was clepid Elymelech, and his wijf Noemy, and the twey sones, the oon was clepid Maalon, and the tother Chelion, Effrateis of Bethleem of Juda; and thei entriden in to the cuntrey of Moab, and dwelliden there.
And Elymelech, the hosebonde of Noemy, diede, and sche
lefte with the sones; and thei token wyues of Moab, of whiche wyues oon was clepid Orpha, the tother Ruth. And
the sones dwelliden there ten ȝeer, and bothe dieden, that is, Maalon and Chelion; and the womman lefte, and was maad bare of twey fre sones, and hosebonde.
And sche roos to go with euer eithir wijf of hir sones in to hir cuntrey fro the cuntrey of Moab; for sche hadde herd, that the Lord hadde biholde his puple, and hadde ȝoue metis to hem.
Therfor sche ȝede out of the place of hir pilgrymage with euer either wijf of hir sones; and now sche was set in the weie of turnyng aȝen in to the lond of
Juda, and sche seide to hem, Go ȝe in to the hows of ȝoure modir; the Lord do mercy with ȝou, as ȝe diden with the
deed men, and with me; the Lord ȝyue to ȝou to fynde reste in the howsis of hosebondis, whiche ȝe schulen take. And sche kiste hem. Whiche bigunnen to wepe
with vois reisid, and to seie, We schulen go with thee to thi puple.
To whiche sche answeride, My douȝtris, turne ȝe aȝen, whi comen ȝe with me? Y haue no more sones in my wombe, that ȝe moun hope hosebondis of me; my douȝtris of
Moab, turne ȝe aȝen, and go; for now Y am maad eeld, and Y am not able to boond of mariage; ȝhe, thouȝ Y myȝte
conseyue in this nyȝt, and bere sones, if ȝe wolen abide til thei wexen, and fillen the ȝeris of mariage, ȝe schulen sunner be eld wymmen than ȝe schulen be weddid; I biseche, nyle ȝe, my douȝtris, for ȝoure angwische oppressith me more, and the hond of the Lord ȝede out aȝens me.
Therfor, whanne the vois was reisid, eft thei bigunnen to wepe. Orpha kisside the modir of hir hosebonde, and turnede aȝen, and Ruth cleuyde to the modir of hir hosebonde.
To whom Noemy seide, Lo! thi kyneswomman turnede aȝen to hir puple, and to hir goddis; go thou with hir.
And sche answeride, Be thou not aduersarye to me, that Y forsake thee, and go awei; whidur euer thou schalt go, Y schal go, and where thou schalt dwelle, and Y schal dwelle togidere; thi puple is my puple, and thi God is my
God; what lond schal resseyue thee diynge, Y schal die ther ynne, and there Y schal take place of biriyng; God do to me these thingis, and adde these thingis, if deeth aloone schal not departe me and thee.
Therfor Noemy siȝ, that Ruth hadde demyde with stidefast soule to go with hir, and sche nolde be aȝens hir, nether counseile ferthere turnynge aȝen to her cuntrei men.
And thei ȝeden forth togidere, and camen in to Bethleem; and whanne thei entriden in to the citee, swift fame roos anentis alle men, and wymmen seiden, This is thilke Noemy.
To whiche sche seide, Clepe ȝe not me Noemy, that is, fair, but clepe ȝe me Mara, that is, bittere; for Almyȝti God hath fillid me greetli with bitternesse.
Y ȝede out ful, and the Lord ledde me aȝen voide; whi therfor clepen ȝe me Noemy, whom the Lord hath maad low, and Almyȝti God hath turmentid?
Therfor Noemy cam with Ruth of Moab, the wijf of hir sone, fro the lond of hir pilgrimage, and turnede aȝen in to Bethleem, whanne barli was ropun first.
Forsothe a myȝti man and a man of grete richessis, Booz bi name, was kynysman of Elymelech.
And Ruth of Moab seide to hir modir in lawe, If thou comaundist, Y schal go in to the feeld, and Y schal gadere eeris of corn that fleen the hondis of reperis, where euer Y schal fynde grace of an hosebonde man merciful in me. To whom sche answeride, Go, my douȝter.
Therfor sche ȝede, and gaderide eeris of corn after the backis of reperis. Forsothe it bifelde, that thilke feeld hadde a lord, Booz bi name, that was of the kynrede of Elymelech.
And lo! he cam fro Bethleem. And he seide to the reperis, The Lord be with ȝou. Whiche answeriden to hym, The Lord blesse thee.
And Booz seide to the ȝong man that was souereyn to the reperis, Who is this damysel?
Whiche answeride, This is the womman of Moab, that cam with Noemy fro the cuntrey of Moab;
and sche preiede, that sche schulde gedere eeris of corn leeuynge bihynde, and sue the steppis of reperis; and fro the morewtid til now sche stondith in the feeld, and sotheli nethir at a moment sche turnede aȝen hoom.
And Booz seide to Ruth, Douȝtir, here thou; go thou not in to anothir feelde to gadere, nether go awei fro this place, but be thou ioyned to
my dameselis, and sue thou where thei repen; for Y comaundide to my children, that no man be diseseful to thee; but also if thou thirstist, go to the fardels, and drynke watris, of whiche my children drynken.
And sche felde on hir face, and worschipide on the erthe; and seide to hym, Wherof is this to me, that Y schulde fynde grace bifor thin iȝen, that thou woldist knowe me a straunge womman?
To whom he answeride, Alle thingis ben teld to me, whiche thou didist to thi modir in lawe after the deeth of thin hosebonde, and that thou hast forsake thi fadir and modir, and the lond in which thou were borun, and hast come to a puple, whom thou knowist not bifore.
The Lord ȝelde to thee for thi werk, and resseyue thou ful mede of the Lord God of Israel, to whom thou camest, and vndir whose wengis thou fleddist.
And sche seide, My lord, Y haue founde grace bifor thin iȝen, which hast coumfortid me, and hast spoke to the herte of thin handmaide, which am not lijk oon of thi damesels
And Booz seide to hir, Whanne the our of etyng is, come thou hidur, and ete breed, and wete thi mussel in vynegre. Therfor sche sat at the side of reperis; and he dresside to hir potage, and sche eet, and was fillid; and sche took the relifs.
And sche roos fro thennus to gadere eeris of corn bi custom. Forsothe Booz comaundide to hise children, and seide, Also if sche wole repe
with ȝou, forbede ȝe not hir, and also of ȝoure handfuls caste ȝe forth of purpos, and suffre ȝe to abide, that sche gadere with out schame; and no man repreue hir gaderynge.
Therfor sche gaderide in the feeld til to euentid; and sche beet with a ȝerde, and schook out tho thingis that sche hadde gaderid; and sche foond of barly as the mesure of ephi, that is, thre buschels
Which sche bar, and turnede aȝen in to the citee, and schewide to hir modir in lawe; ferthermore sche brouȝte forth, and ȝaf to hir the relifs of hir mete, with which mete sche was fillid.
And the modir in lawe seide to hir, Where gaderidist thou to dai, and where didist thou werk? Blessid be he, that hadde mercy on thee. And sche telde to hir, at whom sche wrouȝte; and sche seide the name of the man, that he was clepid Booz.
To whom Noemy answeride, Blessid be he of the Lord, for he kepte also to deed men the same grace, which he ȝaf to the quike. And eft sche seide, He is oure kynysman.
And Ruth seide, Also he comaundide this to me, that so longe Y schulde be ioyned to hise reperis, til alle the cornes weren repid.
To whom hir modir in lawe seide, My douȝter, it is betere that thou go out to repe with hise damysels, lest in another feeld ony man aȝenstonde thee.
Therfor sche was ioyned to the damesels of Booz; and so longe sche rap with hem, til bothe barli and wheete weren closid in the bernys.
Forsothe aftir that Ruth turnede aȝen to hir modir in lawe, Ruth herde of hir, My douȝtir, Y schal seke reste to thee, and Y schal purueye that it be wel to thee.
This Booz, to whose damesels thou were ioyned in the feeld, is oure kynesman, and in this niȝt he wyndewith the corn floor of barli.
Therfor be thou waischun, and anoyntid, and be thou clothid with onestere clothis, and go doun in to the corn floor; the man, that is, Booz, se not thee, til he haue endid the mete and drynke.
Forsothe whanne he goth to slepe, marke thou the place in which he slepith; and thou schalt come and vnhile the cloth, with which he is hilid, fro the part of the feet, and thou schalt caste thee doun, and thou schalt ly there. Forsothe he schal seie to thee, what thou owist to do.
Which answeride, What euer thing thou comaundist, Y schal do.
And sche ȝede doun in to the corn floor, and dide alle thingis whiche hir modir in lawe comaundide to hir.
And whanne Booz hadde ete and drunke, and was maad gladere, and hadde go to slepe bisidis the heep of handfuls, sche cam, and hidde hir silf; and whanne the cloth was vnhilid fro hise feet, sche castide doun hir silf.
And lo! now at mydnyȝt the man dredde, and was troblid; and he siȝ a womman
lyggynge at hise feet; and he seide to hir, Who art thou? Sche answeride, Y am Ruth, thin handmayde; stretche forth thi cloth on thi seruauntesse, for thou art nyȝ of kyn.
And he seide, Douȝtir, thou art blessid of the Lord, and thou hast ouercome the formere mercy with the lattere; for thou suedist not ȝonge men, pore ethir riche.
Therfor nyle thou drede, but what euer thing thou schalt seie to me, Y schal do to thee; for al the puple that dwellith with ynne the ȝatis of my cytee woot, that thou art a womman of vertu.
And Y forsake not, that Y am of nyȝ kyn, but another man
is neer than Y; reste thou in this nyȝt, and whanne the morewtid is maad, if he wole holde thee bi riȝt of nyȝ kyn, the thing is wel doon; forsothe if he nyle, Y schal take thee with outen ony doute, the Lord lyueth, that is, bi the Lord lyuynge; slepe thou til the morewtid.
Therfore sche slepte at hise feet til to the goyng awey of nyȝt, and so sche roos bifor that men knewen hem silf togidere. And Booz seide to hir, Be thou war lest ony man knowe, that thou camest hidir.
And eft he seide, Stretche forth thi mentil with which thou art hilid, and holde thou with euer either hond. And while sche stretchide forth and helde, he mete sixe buyschels of barly, and puttide on hir; and sche bar,
and entride in to the citee, and cam to hir modir in lawe. Which seide to Ruth, What hast thou do, douȝter? And Ruth telde to hir alle thingis, whyche the man hadde do to hir.
And Ruth seide, Lo! he ȝaf to me sixe buyschels of barly; and he seide, Y nyle that thou turne aȝen voide to thi modir in lawe.
And Noemy seide, Abide, douȝtir, til we sien what issu the thing schal haue; for the man schal not ceesse, no but he fille tho thingis whiche he spak.
Therfor Booz stiede to the ȝate, and sat there; and whanne he hadde seyn the kynesman passe forth, of whom the word was had, Booz seide to hym, Bowe thou a litil, and sitte here; and he clepide hym bi his name. And he turnede, and sat.
Forsothe Booz took ten men of the eldere men of the citee, and seide to hem, Sitte ȝe here.
And while thei saten, Booz spak to the kynesman, Noemy, that turnede aȝen fro the cuntrey of Moab, seelde the part of the feeld of oure brother
Elymelech, which thing Y wolde that thou here; and Y wolde seie to thee bifor alle men syttynge and grettere in birthe of my puple. If thou wolt haue in possessioun the feeld bi riȝt of nyȝ kyn, bye thou, and haue thou in possessioun; sotheli if it displesith thee, schewe thou this same thing to me, that Y wyte what Y owe to do; for noon is niȝ in kyn, outakun thee which art the formere, and outakun me which am the secunde. And he answeride, Y schal bie the feeld.
To whom Booz seide, Whanne thou hast bouȝte the feeld of the hond of the womman, thou owist to take also Ruth of Moab, that was the wijf of the deed man, that thou reise the name of thi kynesman in his eritage.
Which answeride, Y forsake the ryȝt of nyȝ kyn; for Y owe not to do awei the eritage of my meynee; vse thou my priuelegie, which priuelegie Y knowleche me to wante gladli.
Forsothe this was the custom bi eld tyme in Israel among kynesmen, that if a man ȝaf his riȝt to anothir man, that the grauntyng were stidefast, the man vnlaase his scho, and ȝaf to his kynesman; this was the witnessyng of the ȝift in Israel.
Therfor Booz seide to his kynesman, Take the scho fro thee; which scho he vnlaside anoon fro his foot.
And Booz seide to the grettere men in birthe and to al the puple, Ȝe ben witnessis to dai, that Y haue take in possessioun alle thingis that weren of Elymelech, and of Chelion, and of Maalon,
bi the ȝifte of Noemy; and that Y haue take in to wedlok Ruth of Moab, the wijf of Maalon, that Y reise the name of the deed man in his erytage; lest his name be doon awey fro his meynee and britheren and puple. Ȝe, he seide, ben witnessis of this thing.
Al the puple, that was in the ȝate, answeride, and the grettere men in birthe answeriden, We ben witnessis; the Lord make this womman, that entrith in to thin hows, as Rachel and Lia, that bildiden the hows of Israel, that sche be ensaumple of vertu in Effrata, and haue a solempne name in Bethleem;
and thin hows be maad as the hows of Fares, whom Thamar childide to Judas, of the seed which the Lord schal ȝyue to thee of this damesel.
Therfor Booz took Ruth, and took hir to wijf; and he entride to hir, and the Lord ȝaf to hir, that sche conseyuede, and childide a sone.
And wymmen seiden to Noemy, Blessid be the Lord, which suffride not, that an eir failide to thi meynee, and his name
were clepid in Israel; and that thou haue a man, that schal coumforte thi soule, and nursche elde age. For a child is borun of thi douȝtir in lawe, which child schal loue thee, and he is myche betere to thee, than if thou haddist seuene sones.
And Noemy puttide the child resseyued in hir bosum; and sche dide the office of a nurische, and of a berere.
Forsothe wymmen neiȝboris thankiden hir, and seiden, A sone is borun to Noemy, and clepide his name Obeth. This is the fadir of Ysay, fadir of Dauid.
These ben the generaciouns of Fares; Fares gendride
Esrom; Esrom gendride Aram; Aram
gendride Amynadab; Amynadab gendride Naason; Naason gendride Salmon;
Salmon gendride Booz; Booz gendride
Obeth; Obeth gendride Isay; Isay gendride Dauid the kyng.
A man was of Ramathym of Sophym, of the hil of Effraym, and his name was Elchana, the sone of Jeroboam, sone of Elyud, sone of Thau, sone of Suph, of Effraym.
And Helchana hadde twei wyues; the name to oon was Anna, and the name of the secounde was Fenenna; and sones weren to Feuenna; forsothe fre children weren not to Anna.
And thilke man styede fro his citee in daies ordeyned, to worschipe and offre sacrifice to the Lord of oostis in Silo. Forsothe twei sones of Heli weren there, Ophym and Fynees, preestis of the Lord.
Therfor the dai cam, and Helcana offride, and ȝaf partis to Fenenna, his wijf, and
to alle hise sones and douȝtris; forsothe he ȝaf soreufuly o part to Anna, for he louyde Anna; forsothe the Lord hadde closid hir wombe.
And hir enemy turmentide hir, and angwischide greetly, in so myche that sche vpbreidide, that the Lord hadde closid hir wombe.
And so sche dide bi alle ȝeeris, whanne in tyme comynge aȝen, thei stieden in to the hows of the Lord; and so sche terride Anna. Forsothe Anna wepte, and took not mete.
Therfor Helcana, hir hosebonde, seide to hir, Anna, whi wepist thou, and whi etist thou not, and whi is thin herte turmentid? Whether Y am not betere to thee than ben ten sones?
Sotheli Anna roos, aftir that sche hadde ete and drunke in Silo. And the while Hely was on his greet seete, bifor the
postis of the hows of the Lord, whanne Anna was in bittere soule, sche preyede
the Lord, and wepte largeli; and made a vow, and seide, Lord God of oostis, if thou biholdist, and seest the turment of thi seruauntesse, and hast mynde of me, and forȝetist not thin handmayde, and ȝyuest to thi seruauntesse a male kynde, Y schal ȝyue hym to the Lord in alle daies of his lijf, and a rasour schal not stie on his heed.
Forsothe it was doon, whanne sche multipliede preieris bifor the Lord, that Ely aspiede hir mouth.
Forsothe Anna spak in hir herte, and oneli hir lippis weren mouyd, and outerly hir vois was not herd. Therfor Hely
gesside hir drunkun, and he seide to hyr, Hou longe schalt thou be drunkun? Difye thou a litil the wyn, bi which thou art moist.
Anna answeride, and seide, Nay, my lord, for Y am a wretchid womman greetli; Y drank not wyn and al thing that may make drunkun, but Y schedde out my soule in the siȝt of the Lord;
gesse thou not thin handmaide as oon of the douȝtris of Belyal, for of the multitude of my sorewe and morenyng Y spak til in to present tyme.
Thanne Hely seide to hir, Go thou in pees, and God of Israel ȝyue to thee the axyng which thou preiedist hym.
And sche seide, Y wolde that thin hondmayde fynde grace in thin iȝen. And the womman ȝede in to hir weie, and eet; and hir cheris weren no more chaungid dyuersly.
And thei ryseden eerly, and worschipiden bifore the Lord; and thei turneden aȝen, and camen in to hir hows in Ramatha. Forsothe Helchana knew fleischli Anna, his wijf; and the Lord thouȝte on hir.
And it was doon after the cumpas of daies, Anna conseyuede, and childide a sone, and sche clepide his name Samuel; for sche hadde axid hym of the Lord.
Forsothe hir hosebonde Helcana stiede, and al his hows, to offre a solempne sacrifice, and his avow to the Lord.
And Anna stiede not, for sche hadde seid to hir hosebonde, Y schal not go, til the ȝonge child be wenyd, and til Y lede hym, and he appere bifor the siȝt of the Lord, and dwelle there contynueli.
And Helcana, hir hosebonde, seide to hir, Do thou that that semeth good to thee, and dwelle thou til thou wene hym; and Y biseche, that the Lord fille his word. Therfor the womman dwellide, and ȝaf mylk to hir sone, til sche remouyde hym fro mylk.
And sche brouȝte hym with hir, aftir that sche hadde wened hym, with thre caluys, and thre buyschelis of mele, and amfore, ether a pot, of wyn; and sche brouȝte hym to the hows of the Lord in Silo. Forsothe the child was ȝit ful ȝonge.
And thei sacrifieden a calf, and thei offriden the child to Hely.
And Anna seide, My lord, Y biseche, that is, that this child be thi disciple and seruaunt, thi soule lyueth; Y am that womman, that stood bifor
thee here, and preiede the Lord; for this child Y preiede, and the Lord ȝaf to me myn axyng which Y axide hym;
therfor Y haue ȝoue hym to the Lord in alle daies, in whiche he is ȝouun to the Lord. And thei worschypiden there the Lord.
And Anna worschipide, and seide, Myn herte fulli ioiede in the Lord, and myn horn is reisid in my God; my mouth is alargid on myn enemyes, for Y was glad in thin helthe.
Noon is hooli as the Lord is; for noon other is, outakun thee, and noon is strong as oure God.
Nyle ȝe multiplie to speke hiȝe thingis, and haue glorie; elde thingis go awey fro ȝoure mouth; for God is Lord of kunnyngis, and thouȝtis ben maad redi to hym.
The bouwe of strong men is ouercomun, and sijk men ben gird with strengthe.
Men fillid bifore settiden hem silf to hire for looues, and hungri men ben fillid; while the bareyn womman childide ful manye, and sche that hadde many sones, was sijke.
The Lord sleeth, and quikeneth; he ledith forth to hellis, and bryngith aȝen.
The Lord makith pore, and makith riche; he makith low, and reisith.
He reisith a nedi man fro poudur, and he reisith a pore man fro dryt, that he sitte with princes, and holde the seete of glorie; for the endis of erthe ben of the Lord, and he hath set the world on tho.
He schal kepe the feet of hise seyntis, and wickid men schulen be stille to gidere in derknessis; for a man schal not be maad strong in his owne strengthe.
Aduersaries of the Lord schulen drede hym, and in heuenes he schal thundre on hem; the Lord schal deme the endis of erthe, and he schal ȝyue lordschip to his kyng, and he schal enhaunse the horn, that is, power, of his Crist.
And Helcana ȝede in to Ramatha, in to his hows; forsothe the child was seruant in the siȝt of the Lord bifor the face of Ely the preest.
Forsothe the sones of Hely weren sones
of Belial, and knewen not the Lord, nether the office of preestis to the puple; but who euer hadde offrid sacrifice, the child of the preest cam, while the fleischis weren in sething, and he hadde a fleischhook with
thre teeth in his hond; and he sente it in to the grete vessel of stoon, ethir in to the caudrun, ethir in to the pot, ethir in to the panne; and what euer thing the fleischhook reiside, the preest took to hym silf; so thei diden to al Israel of men comynge in to Silo.
Ȝhe bifor that the sones of Hely brenten the ynnere fatnesse, the child of the preest cam, and seyde to the offerere, Ȝyue thou fleisch to me, that Y sethe to the preest; for Y schal not take of thee sodun fleisch, but raw.
And the offrere seide to hym, The ynnere fatnesse be brent first to day bi the custom, and take thou to thee hou myche euer thi soule desirith. Whiche answeride, and seide to hym, Nay, for thou schalt ȝyue now; ellis Y schal take bi violence.
Therfor the synne of the children was ful greuouse bifor the Lord; for thei withdrowen men fro the sacrifice of the Lord.
Forsothe Samuel, a child gird with a lynnun clooth, mynystride bifor the face of the Lord.
And his moder made to hym a litil coote, which sche brouȝte in daies ordeyned, and stiede with hir hosebonde, that he schulde offre a solempne offryng, and his auow.
And Heli blesside Helcana and his wijf; and Heli seide to hym, The Lord ȝelde to thee seed of this womman, for the ȝifte which thou hast ȝoue to the Lord. And thei ȝeden in to her place.
Therfor the Lord visitide Anna, and sche conseyuede, and childide thre sones and twei douȝtris. And the child Samuel was magnyfied at the Lord.
Forsothe Hely was ful eld, and he herde alle thingis whiche hise sones diden in al Israel, and hou thei slepten with wymmen, that awaitiden at the dore of the tabernacle.
And he seide to hem, Whi doen ȝe siche thingis, the worste thingis whiche Y here of al the puple?
Nyle ȝe, my sones; it is not good fame, which Y here, that ȝe make the puple of the Lord to do trespas.
If a man synneth aȝens a man, God may be plesid to him; forsothe if a man synneth aȝens the Lord, who schal preye for hym? And thei herden not the vois of her fadir, for God wolde sle hem.
Forsothe the child Samuel profitide, and encreessyde, and pleside bothe God and men.
Sotheli a man of God cam to Hely, and seide to hym, The Lord seith these thingis, Whether Y was not schewid apertli to the hows of thi fadir, whanne he was in Egipt, in the hows of Farao?
And Y chees hym of alle lynagis of Israel in to preest to me, that he schulde stie to myn auter, and schulde brenne encense to me, and that he schulde bere bifor me preestis cloth; and Y ȝaf to the hows of thi fadir alle thingis of the sacrifices of the sones of Israel.
Whi hast thou cast awey with the heele my sacrifice, and my ȝiftis, whiche Y comaundide to be offrid in the temple; and thou onouridst more thi sones than me, that ȝe eeten the principal partis of ech sacrifice of Israel, my puple?
Therfor the Lord God of Israel seith these thingis, Y spekynge spak, that thin hows and the hows of thi fadir schulde mynystre in my siȝt til in to with outen ende; now forsothe the Lord seith, Fer be this fro me; but who euere onourith me, Y schal glorifie hym; forsothe thei that dispisen me, schulen be vnnoble.
Lo! daies comen, and Y schal kitte awei thin arm, and the arm of the hows of thi fadir, that an eld man be not in thin hows.
And thou schalt se thin enemy in the temple, in alle prosperitees of Israel; and an eld man schal not be in thin hows in alle daies.
Netheles Y schal not outerli take awei of thee a man fro myn auter, but that thin iȝen faile, and thi soule faile; and greet part of thin hows schal die, whanne it schal come to mannus age.
Forsothe this schal be signe, that schal come to thi twei sones Ophym and Fynees, bothe schulen die in o dai.
And Y schal reise to me a feithful preest, that schal do bi myn herte and my soule; and Y schal bilde to hym a feithful hows, and he schal go bifore my Crist in alle daies.
Forsothe it schal come, that who euer dwellith in thin hows, he come that me preie for him, and that he offre a peny of siluer, and a cake of breed, and seie, Y biseche, suffre thou me to o part of the preest, that Y ete a mussel of breed.
Forsothe the child Samuel mynystride to the Lord bifor Heli, and the word of the Lord was preciouse; in tho daies was noon opyn reuelacioun.
Therfor it was doon in a dai, Heli lay in his bed, and hise iȝen dasewiden, and he myȝte not se the lanterne of God, bifor that it was quenchid.
Forsothe Samuel slepte in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was.
And the Lord clepide Samuel; and he answeride and seide, Lo! Y.
And he ran to Hely, and seide to hym, Lo! Y; for thou clepidist me. Which Hely seide, Y clepide not thee; turne thou aȝen and slepe. And he ȝede and slepte.
And the Lord addide eft to clepe Samuel; and Samuel roos, and ȝede to Hely, and seide, Lo! Y; for thou clepidist me. And Heli answeride, Y clepide not thee, my sone; turne thou aȝen and slepe.
Forsothe Samuel knew not ȝit the Lord, nether the word of the Lord was shewid to hym.
And the Lord addide, and clepide ȝit Samuel the thridde tyme; which Samuel
roos and ȝede to Heli, and seide, Lo! Y; for thou clepidist me. Therfor Heli vndirstood, that the Lord clepide the child; and Heli seide to Samuel, Go and slepe; and if he clepith thee aftirward, thou schalt seie, Speke thou, Lord, for thi seruaunt herith. Therfor Samuel ȝede and slepte in his place.
And the Lord cam, and stood, and clepide as he hadde clepid the secunde tyme, Samuel, Samuel. And Samuel seide, Speke thou, Lord, for thi seruaunt herith.
And the Lord seide to Samuel, Lo! Y make a word in Israel, which word who euer schal here, bothe hise eeris schulen rynge
In that dai Y schal reise aȝens Heli alle thingis, whiche Y spak on his hows; Y schal bigynne, and Y schal ende.
For Y biforseide to hym, that Y schulde deme his hows with outen ende for wickidnesse; for he knew, that hise sones diden vnworthili, and he chastiside not hem.
Therfor Y swoor to the hows of Heli, that the wickidnesse of his hows schal not be clensid bi sacrifices and ȝiftis til in to with outen ende.
Forsothe Samuel slepte til the morewtid, and he openyde the doris of the hows of the Lord; and Samuel dredde to schewe the reuelacioun to Heli.
Therfor Heli clepide Samuel, and seide, Samuel, my sone. And he answeride and seide, Y am redi.
And Heli axide hym, What is the word which the Lord spak to thee? Y preye thee, hide thou not fro me; God do to thee these thingis, and encreesse these thingis, if thou hidist fro me a word of alle wordis that ben seid to thee.
And Samuel schewide to hym alle the wordis, and hidde not fro hym. And Heli answeride, He is the Lord; do he that, that is good in hise iȝen.
Forsothe Samuel encreeside, and the Lord was with hym, and noon of alle hise wordis felde in to erthe
And al Israel fro Dan to Bersabee knew, that feithful Samuel was a profete of the Lord.
And the Lord addide that he schulde appere in Silo, for the Lord was schewid to Samuel in Silo bi the word of the Lord; and the word of Samuel cam to al Israel.
And it was doon in tho daies Filisteis camen to gidere in to batel; for Israel ȝede out aȝens Filisteis in to batel, and settiden tentis bisidis the stoon of help. Forsothe Filisteis camen in to Aphet,
and maden redi scheltrun aȝens Israel. Sotheli whanne the batel was bigunnun, Israel turned backis to Filisteis; and as foure thousynde of men weren slayn in that batel euery where bi feeldis; and the puple of Israel turnede aȝen to tentis. And the grettere men in birthe of Israel seiden, Whi hath the Lord smyte vs to dai bifore Filisteis? Brynge we to vs fro Silo the arke of boond of pees of the Lord, and come it in to the myddis of vs, that it saue vs fro the hond of oure enemyes.
Therfor the puple sente in to Silo, and thei token fro thennus the arke of boond of pees of the Lord of oostis, that sat on cherubyn. And Ophym and Fynees, twei sones of Heli, weren with the arke of boond of pees of the Lord.
And whanne the arke of boond of pees of the Lord hadde come in to the castels, al Israel criede with grete cry, and the erthe sownede.
And Filisteis herden the vois of cry, and seiden, What is this vois of greet cry in the castels of Ebrews? And thei knewen, that the arke of boond of pees of the Lord hadde come in to castels.
And Filisteis dredden, and seiden, God is come in to the castels; and thei
weiliden, and seiden, Wo to vs! for so greet ful ioiyng was not ȝistirdai, and the thridde day passid; wo to vs! who schal kepe vs fro the hond of these hiȝe goddis? these ben the goddis, that smytiden Egipt with al veniaunce in deseert.
Filisteis, be ȝe coumfortid, and be ȝe men, serue ȝe not Ebrews, as thei serueden vs; be ȝe coumfortid, and fiȝte ȝe.
Therfor Filisteis fouȝten, and Israel was slayn, and ech man flei in to his tabernacle; and a ful greet veniaunce was maad, and thretti thousynde of foot men of Israel felden doun.
And the arke of God was takun; and, twei sones of Heli, Ophym and Fynees, weren deed.
Sotheli a man of Beniamyn ran fro the scheltrun, and cam in to Silo in that dai, with his cloth torent and his heed bispreynt with dust;
and whanne he was comen, Heli sat on an hiȝe seete, and bihelde aȝens the weie; for his herte was dredyng for the arke of the Lord. Sotheli aftir that thilke man entride, he telde to the citee, and al the citee ȝellide.
And Heli herde the soun of cry, and seide, What is this sown of this noise? And he hastide, and cam, and telde to Heli.
Forsothe Heli was of foure score ȝeer and eiȝtene, and hise iȝen dasiwiden, and he myȝte not se.
And he seide to Heli, Y am that cam fro batel, and Y am that flei to dai fro the scheltrun. To whom Ely seide, My sone, what is doon?
Forsothe he that telde answeride, and seide, Israel flei bifor Filisteis, and a greet fal is maad in the puple; ferthermore and thi twey sones, Ophym and Fynees, ben deed, and the arke of God is takun.
And whanne he hadde nemyd the arke of God, Hely felde fro the hiȝe seete bacward bisidis the dore, and was deed; for the nollis weren brokun. For he was an eld man, and of greet age; and he demyde Israel bi fourti ȝeer.
Forsothe his douȝter in lawe, the wijf of Finees, was with childe, and niȝ the child bering; and whanne the message was herd that the arke of God was takun, and that hir fadir in lawe was deed, and hir hosebonde, sche bowide hir silf, and childide; for sodeyn sorewis felden in to hir.
Sotheli in that moment of hir deeth, wymmen that stoden aboute hir, seiden to hir, Drede thou not, for thou hast childid a sone. And sche answeride not to hem, for nether sche perseyuede.
And sche clepide the child Ichaboth, and seide, The glorie of the Lord is translatid fro Israel, for the arke of God is takun; and for hir fadir in lawe and for hir hosebonde
sche seide, The glorie of God is translatid fro Israel, for the arke of God is takun.
Forsothe Filisteis token the arke of God, and baren awey it fro the stoon of help in to Azotus.
And Filisteis tokun the arke of God, and brouȝten it to the temple of Dagon, and settiden it bisidis Dagon.
And whanne men of Azotus hadden rise eerli in the todir dai, lo! Dagon lay low in the erthe bifor the arke of the Lord. And thei token Dagon, and restoriden hym in his place.
And eft thei risiden eerli in the tothir day, and founden Dagon liggynge on his face on the erthe bifor the arke of the Lord. Forsothe the heed of Dagon, and twei pawmes of his hondis weren kit of on
the threisfold; certis the stok aloone of Dagon lefte in his place. For this cause the preestis of Dagon, and alle that entren in to his temple, treden not on the threisfold of Dagon in Azotus til in to this dai.
Forsothe the hond of the Lord was maad greuouse on men of Azotus, and he distriede hem, and he smoot Azotus and the coostis therof in the priuyere part of buttokis; and townes and feeldis in the myddis of that cuntrey buyliden out, and myis camen forth; and greet confusioun of deth was maad in the citee.
Sotheli men of Azotus sien siche a veniaunce, and seiden, The arke of God of Israel dwelle not at vs; for his hond is hard on vs, and on Dagon oure god.
And thei senten, and gaderiden alle the wise men, ether princes, of Filisteis to hem, and seiden, What schulen we do of the arke of God of Israel? And men of Geth answeriden, The arke of God of Israel be led aboute; and thei ledden aboute the arke of God of Israel.
Forsothe while thei ledden it aboute, the hond of the Lord of ful greet sleyng was maad on alle citees; and he smoot men of ech citee fro a litil man til to the more, and the lowere entraylis of hem wexiden rotun, and camen forth; and men of Geth token counsel, and maden to hem seetis of skynnes, ethir cuyschuns.
Therfor thei senten the arke of the Lord in to Accoron. And whanne the arke of the Lord hadde come in to Accoron, men of Accoron crieden, and seiden, Thei han brought to vs the arke of God of Israel, that he sle vs and oure puple.
Therfor thei senten, and gaderiden alle the wise men, ethir princes, of Filisteis; whiche seiden, Delyuere ȝe the arke of God of Israel, and turne it aȝen in to his place, and sle not vs with oure puple.
For dreed of deeth was maad in alle citees, and the hond of the Lord was greuouse greetli. Also the men, that weren not deed, weren smytun in the priuy part of buttokis, and the ȝelling of ech citee stiede in to heuene.
Therfor the arke of the Lord was in the cuntrei of Filisteis bi seuene monethis;
and aftir these thingis Filisteis clepiden preestis and false dyuynours, and seiden, What schulen we do of the arke of God? Shewe ȝe to vs, hou we schulen sende it in to his place.
Whiche seiden, If ȝe senden aȝen the arke of God of Israel, nyle ȝe delyuere it voide, but ȝelde ȝe to hym that, that ȝe owen for synne; and thanne ȝe schulen be heelid, and ȝe schulen wite, whi his hond goith not awei fro ȝou.
And thei seiden, What is it, that we owen to ȝelde to hym for trespas?
And thei answeriden to hem, Bi the noumbre of prouynces of Filisteis ȝe schulen make fyue goldun ersis, and fyue goldun myis; for o veniaunce was to alle ȝou and to ȝoure wise men, ether princes. And ȝe schulen make the licnesse of ȝoure ersis, and the licnesse of myis that distriede ȝoure lond; and ȝe schulen ȝyue glorie to God of Israel, if in hap he withdrawe his hond fro ȝou, and fro ȝoure goddis, and fro youre lond.
Whi maken ȝe heuy ȝoure hertis, as Egipt, and Farao made heuy his herte? Whether not after that he was smytun, thanne he delyuerede hem, and thei ȝeden forth?
Now therfor take ȝe, and make o newe wayn, and ioyne ȝe twei kien hauynge caluys, on whiche kyen no ȝok was put; and close ȝe her calues at hoome.
And ȝe schulen take the arke of the Lord, and ȝe schulen sette in the wayn; and ȝe schulen put in a panyere at the side therof the goldun vessels, whiche ȝe payeden to hym for trespas; and delyuere ȝe the arke, that it go.
And ȝe schulen biholde, and sotheli if it stieth aȝens Bethsames bi the weie of hise coostis, he dide to ȝou this greet yuel; but if nay, we schulen wite for his hond touchide not vs, but if it bifelde bi hap.
Therfor thei diden in this manere; and thei token twei kien that ȝauen mylk to caluys, and ioyneden to the wayn; and thei closiden her caluys at hoome.
And thei puttiden the arke of God on the wayn, and thei puttiden the panyere, that hadde the goldun myis, and the licnesse of ersis on the wayn.
Sotheli the kien ȝeden streiȝtli bi the weie that ledith to Bethsames; and tho ȝeden in o weie goynge and lowynge, and bowiden not nether to the riȝt side nether to the left side; but also the wise men of Filisteis sueden til to the termes of Bethsames.
Forsothe men of Bethsames repiden whete in the valey, and thei reisiden the iȝen, and sien the arke, and thei weren ioyful, whanne thei hadden sien the arke.
And the wayn cam in to the feelde of Josue of Bethsames, and stood there. Forsothe a greet stoon was there; and thei kittiden the trees of the wayn, and puttiden the kien on tho trees, a brent sacrifice to the Lord.
Sotheli dekenes token doun the arke of God, and the panyere, that was bisidis it, where ynne the goldun vessels weren; and thei settiden on the greet stoon. Forsothe the men of Bethsames offriden brent sacrifices, and offriden slayn sacrifices in that dai to the Lord.
And fyue princes of Filisteis sien, and turneden aȝen in to Accoron in that dai.
Sotheli these ben the goldun ersis, whiche the Filisteis ȝeldiden to the Lord for trespas; Azotus ȝeldide oon; Gaza ȝeldide oon; Ascolon ȝeldide oon; Geth ȝeldide oon; Accaron
ȝeldide oon; and Filisteis ȝeldiden golden myis bi the noumbre of citees of Filisteis of fyue prouynces, fro a wallid citee til to a town that was with out wal, and til to the greet Abel, on which thei puttiden the arke of the Lord, that was there til in that dai in the feeld of Josue of Bethsames.
Forsothe the Lord smoot of the men of Bethsames, for thei hadden seyn the arke of the Lord, and he smoot of the puple seuenti men, and fifty thousynde of the porail. And the puple morenyde, for the Lord hadde smyte the puple with greet veniaunce.
And men of Bethsames seiden, Who schal now stonde in the siȝt of the Lord God of this hooli thing, and to whom schal it stie fro vs?
And thei senten messangeris to the dwelleris of Cariathiarym, and seiden, Filisteis han brouȝt aȝen the arke of the Lord; come ȝe doun, and lede it aȝen to ȝou.
Therfor men of Cariathiarym camen, and ledden aȝen the arke of the Lord, and brouȝten it in to the hows of Amynadab in Gabaa. Sotheli thei halewiden Eleazar his sone, that he schulde kepe the ark of the Lord.
And it was doon, fro which dai the arke of the Lord dwellide in Caryathiarym, daies weren multiplied; for the twentithe ȝeer was now, after that Samuel bigan to teche the puple; and al Israel restide aftir the Lord.
Forsothe Samuel spak to al the hows of Israel, and seide, If in al ȝoure herte ȝe turnen aȝen to the Lord, do ȝe awei alien goddis, Balym and Astaroth, fro the myddis of ȝou; and make ȝe redi ȝoure hertis to the Lord, and serue ȝe hym aloone; and he schal delyuere ȝou fro the hond of Filisteis.
Therfor the sones of Israel diden awey Baalym and Astoroth, and serueden the Lord aloone.
Forsothe Samuel seide, Gadere ȝe al Israel in to Masphat, that Y preie the Lord for ȝou.
And thei camen togidere in to Masphat, and thei drowen watir, and shedden out in the siȝt of the Lord; and thei fastiden in that day, and seiden, Lord, we synneden to thee. And Samuel demyde the sones of Israel in Masphat.
And Filisteis herden that the sones of Israel weren gaderid in Masphat; and the princes of Filisteis stieden to Israel. And whanne the sones of Israel hadden herd this, thei dredden of the face of Filisteis.
And thei seiden to Samuel, Ceesse thou not to crye for vs to oure Lord God, that he saue vs fro the hoond of Filisteis.
Forsothe Samuel took o soukynge lomb, and offride that hool in to brent sacrifice to the Lord. And Samuel criede to the Lord for Israel; and the Lord herde hym.
Forsothe it was doon, whanne Samuel offryde brent sacrifice, that Filisteis bigunnen batel aȝens Israel. Sotheli the Lord thundride with greet thundur in that dai on Filisteis, and made hem aferd; and thei weren slayn of the sones of Israel.
And the sones of Israel ȝeden out of Masphat, and pursueden Filisteis, and smytiden hem til to the place that was vndur Bethachar.
Forsothe Samuel took o stoon, and puttide it bitwixe Masphat, and bitwixe Sen; and he clepide the name of that place The stoon of help. And he seide, Hidir to the Lord helpide vs.
And Filisteis weren maad low, and addiden no more to come in to the termes of Israel. And so the hond of the Lord was maad on Filisteis in alle the daies of Samuel.
And the citees whiche the Filisteis token fro Israel, weren ȝoldun to Israel, fro Accaron til to Geth and hise termes; and the Lord delyuerede Israel fro the hond of Filisteis; and pees was bitwixe Israel and Ammorrey.
Also Samuel demyde Israel in alle the daies of his lijf, that is, til to the ordeynyng
and confermyng of Saul; and he ȝede bi alle ȝeeris, and cumpasside Bethel, and Galgal, and Masphat, and he demyde Israel in the forseid places.
And he turnede aȝen in to Ramatha, for his hows was there; and he demyde Israel there, and he bildide there also an auter to the Lord.
Forsothe it was don, whanne Samuel hadde wexide eld, he settide hise sones iugis on Israel.
And the name of his firste gendrid sone was Johel, and the name of the secounde was Abia, iugis in Bersabee.
And hise sones ȝeden not in the weies of hym, but thei bowiden after aueryce, and thei token ȝiftis, and peruertiden doom.
Therfor alle the grettere men in birthe of Israel weren gaderid, and camen to Samuel in to Ramatha.
And thei seiden to hym, Lo! thou hast wexid eld, and thi sones goen not in thi weies; ordeyne thou a kyng to vs, that he deme vs, as also alle naciouns han.
And the word displeside in the iȝen of Samuel, for thei hadden seid, Ȝyue thou to vs a kyng, that he deme vs. And Samuel preiede to the Lord.
Forsothe the Lord seide to Samuel, Here thou the vois of the puple in alle thingis whiche thei speken to thee; for thei han not caste awey thee, but me, that Y regne not on hem.
Bi alle her werkis whiche thei diden, fro the day in whiche Y ledde hem out of Egipt til to this dai, as thei forsoken me, and seruyden alien goddis, so thei doon also to thee.
Now therfor here thou her vois; netheles witnesse thou to hem; biforseie thou to hem the riȝt of the kyng, that schal regne on hem.
Therfor Samuel seide alle the wordis of the Lord to the puple, that hadde axid of him a king;
and he seide, This schal be the riȝt of the kyng, that schal comaunde to ȝou; he schal take ȝoure sones, and schal sette
in hise charis; and he schal make hem to hym silf rideris, and biforegoeris of hise cartis; and he schal ordeyne to hym tribunes, that is, souereyns of a thousynd, and centuriouns, that is, souereyns of an hundrid, and eereris of hise feeldis, and reperis of cornes, and smythis of hise armeris, and charis.
Also he schal make ȝoure douȝtris makeris of oynementis to hym silf, and fueris, and bakeris.
And he schal take ȝoure feeldis and vyneris and the beste places of olyues, and schal ȝyue to hise seruauntis.
But also he schal take the tenthe part of ȝoure cornes, and rentis of vyneris, that he ȝyue to his chaumberleyns and seruauntis.
Sotheli he schal take awey ȝoure seruauntis and handmaydes, and beste ȝong men, and assis, and schal sette in his werk.
Also he schal take the tenthe part of ȝoure flockis, and ȝe schulen be seruauntis to hym.
And ȝe schulen crye in that dai fro the face of ȝoure kyng, whom ȝe han chose to ȝou; and the Lord schal not here ȝou in that dai; for ȝe axiden a kyng to ȝou.
Sotheli the puple nolde here the vois of Samuel, but thei seiden, Nay, for a kyng
schal be on vs; and we also schulen be as alle folkis, and oure kyng schal deme vs, and he schal go out bifor vs, and he schal fiȝte oure batel for vs.
And Samuel herde alle the wordis of the puple, and spak tho in the eeris of the Lord.
Forsothe the Lord seide to Samuel, Here thou the vois of hem, and ordeyne thou a kyng on hem. And Samuel seide to the men of Israel, Ech man go in to his citee.
And a man was of Beniamyn, Cys bi name, the sone of Abiel, sone of Seor, sone of Bethor, sone of Aphia, sone of the man Gemyny, strong in bodili myȝt.
And to hym was a sone, Saul bi name, chosun and good; and no man of the sones of Israel was betere than he; fro the schuldur and aboue he apperide ouer al the puple.
Sotheli the femal assis of Cys, the fadir of Saul, perischyden. And Cys seide to Saul his sone, Take with thee oon of the children, and rise thou, and go, and seke the femal assis. And whanne
thei hadden go bi the hil of Effraym, and bi the lond of Salisa, and hadden not foundun, thei passiden also bi the lond of Salym, and tho weren not there; but also thei passiden bi the lond of Gemyny, and founden not.
Sotheli whanne thei hadden come in to the lond of Suph, and hadden not founde, Saul seide to his child that was with hym, Come thou, and turne we aȝen; lest perauenture my fadir hath lefte the femal assis, and is bisy for vs.
Which child seide to hym, Lo! the man of God is in this citee, a noble man; al thing that he spekith, cometh with out doute. Now therfor go we thidir, if perauenture he schewe to vs of oure weie, for which we camen.
And Saul seide to his child, Lo! we schulen go; what schulen we bere to the man of God? Breede failide in oure scrippis, and we han no present, that we ȝyue to the man of God, nether ony othir thing.
Eft the child answeride to Saul, and seide, Lo! the fourthe part of a stater, that is, a cicle, of siluer is foundun in myn hond; ȝyue we to the man of God, that he schewe to vs oure weie.
Sumtyme in Israel ech man goynge to counsel God spak thus, Come ȝe, and go we to the seere; for he, that is seid to dai a profete, was clepid sumtyme a seere.
And Saul seide to his child, Thi word is the beste; come thou, go we. And thei ȝeden in to the citee, in which the man of God was.
And whanne thei stieden in to the hiȝnesse of the citee, thei founden damesels goynge out to drawe watir, and thei seiden to the dameselis, Whether the seere is here?
Whiche dameselis answeriden, and seiden to hem, He is here; lo! he is bifor thee; haste thou now, for to day he cam in to the citee; for to dai is sacrifice of the puple in the hiȝ place.
Ȝe schulen entre in to the citee, and anoon ȝe schulen fynde hym, bifor that he stie in to the hiȝ place to ete; for the puple schal not ete til he come, for he schal blesse the sacrifice, and afterward thei schulen ete that ben clepid. Now therfor stie ȝe, for to day ȝe schulen fynde hym.
And thei stieden in to the citee. And whanne thei ȝeden in the myddis of the citee, Samuel apperide goynge out aȝens hem, that he schulde stie in to the hiȝ place.
Forsothe the Lord hadde maad reuelacioun in the eere of Samuel bifor o dai, that Saul cam,
and seide, In this same our which is now to morewe, Y schal sende to thee a man of the lond of Beniamyn, and thou schalt anoynte hym duyk on my puple Israel, and he schal saue my puple fro the hond of Filisteis; for Y haue biholde my puple, for the cry of hem cam to me.
And whanne Samuel hadde biholde Saul, the Lord seide to Samuel, Lo! the man, whom Y seide to thee; this man schal be lord of my puple.
Forsothe Saul neiȝede to Samuel in the myddis of the ȝate, and seide, Y preye, schewe thou to me, where is the hows of the seere?
And Samuel answeride to Saul, and seide, Y am the seere; stie thou bifor me in to the hiȝ place, that thou ete with me to dai, and Y schal delyuere thee in the morewtid, and Y schal schewe to thee alle thingis that ben in thin herte.
And be thou not bisy of the femal assis, whiche thou lostist the thridde dai agoon, for tho ben foundun; and whose schulen be alle the beste thingis of Israel, whether not to thee, and to al the hows of thi fader? Sotheli Saul answeride, and seide,
Whether Y am not a sone of Gemyny, of the leeste lynage of Israel, and my kynrede is the laste among alle the meynees of the lynage of Beniamyn? Whi therfor hast thou spoke to me this word?
Therfor Samuel took Saul, and his child, and ledde hem in to the chaumbur of thre ordris, and he ȝaf to hem a place in the bigynnyng of hem that weren clepid; for thei weren as thretti men.
And Samuel seide to the cook, Ȝyue thou the part, which Y ȝaf to thee, and comaundide, that thou schuldist kepe bi it silf anentis thee.
Sotheli the cook reiside the schuldir, and settide bifor Saul. And Samuel seide, Lo! that, that lefte, sette thou bifor thee, and ete; for of purpos it was kept to thee, whanne Y clepide the puple. And Saul eet with Samuel in that dai.
And thei camen doun fro the hiȝ place in to the citee; and Samuel spak with Saul in the soler, and Saul araiede a bed in the soler, and slepte.
And whanne thei hadden rise eerli, and now it bigan to be cleer, Samuel clepide Saul in to the soler, and seide, Rise thou, that Y delyuere thee. And Saul roos, and bothe ȝeden out, that is, he, and Samuel.
And whanne thei ȝeden doun in the laste part of the citee, Samuel seide to Saul, Seie thou to the child, that he go bifor vs, and passe; forsothe stonde thou a litil, that Y schewe to thee the word of the Lord.
Forsothe Samuel took a vessel of oyle, and schedde out on the heed of Saul, and kisside hym, and seide, Lo! the Lord hath anoyntid thee in to prince on hys eritage; and thou schalt delyuere his puple fro the hond of his enemyes, that ben in his cumpas. And this a tokene to thee, that the Lord hath anoyntid thee in to
prince; whanne thou schalt go fro me to day, thou schalt fynde twei men bisidis the sepulcre of Rachel, in the endis of Beniamyn, in myddai, clensynge grete dichis; and thei schulen seie to thee, The femel assis ben foundun, whiche thou ȝedist to seke; and while the assis ben lefte, thi fadir is bisy for ȝou, and seith, What schal Y do of my sone?
And whanne thou hast go fro thennus, and hast passid ferthere, and hast come to the ook of Tabor, thre men, stiynge to God in to Bethel, schulen fynde thee there, o man berynge thre kydis, and another man berynge thre kakis of breed, and an other man berynge a galoun of wyn.
And whanne thei han gret thee, thei schulen ȝyue to thee twei loues, and thou schalt take of the hond of hem.
After these thingis thou schalt come in to the hil of the Lord, where is the stondyng, that is, forselet, of Filisteis; and whanne thou schalt entre in to the citee, there thou schalt haue metynge thee the flok of prophetis comynge doun fro the hiȝ place, and a sautree, and tympane, and pipe, and harpe bifor hem, and hem prophesiynge.
And the Spirit of the Lord schal skippe in to thee, and thou schalt prophecie with hem, and thou schalt be chaungid in to another man.
Therfor whanne alle thesse signes bifallen to thee, do thou, what euer thingis thin hond fyndith, that is, dispose thee to regne comelili and myȝtily, for the Lord is with thee.
And thou schalt go doun bifor me in to Galgala; for Y schal come doun to thee, that thou offre an offryng, and offre pesible sacrifices; bi seuene daies thou schalt abide, til I come to thee, and shewe to thee what thou schal do.
Therfor whanne Saul hadde turnede awei his schuldre to go fro Samuel, God chaungide another herte to Saul, and alle these signes camen in that dai.
And thei camen to the forseid hil, and lo! a cumpeny of prophetis metynge hym; and the Spirit of the Lord scippide on hym, and he propheciede in the myddis of hem.
Sotheli alle men, that knewen hym ȝisterdai and the thrid dai ago, sien that he was with the prophetis, and that he prophesiede, and thei seiden togidere, What thing bifelde to the sone of Cys? Whether also Saul is among prophetis?
And o man answeride to another man, and seide, And who is his fadir? Therfor it was turned in to a prouerbe, Whether also Saul is among prophetis?
Forsothe Saul ceside to prophesie, and he cam to an hiȝ place.
And the brothir of the fadir of Saul seide to hym, and to his child, Whidur ȝeden ȝe? And thei answeriden, To seke the femal assis; and whanne we founden not thoo, we camen to Samuel.
And the brother of his fadir seide to hym, Schewe thou to me what Samuel seide to thee.
And Saul seide to the brother of hys fadir, He schewide to vs, that the femal assis weren foundun. Sotheli Saul schewide not to hym of the word of rewme, which word Samuel spak to hym.
And Samuel clepide togidere the puple to the Lord in
Masphat; and he seide to the sones of Israel, The Lord God of Israel seith these thingis, Y ledde Israel out of the lond of Egipt, and Y delyuerede ȝou fro the hond of Egipcians, and fro the hond of alle kyngis that turmentiden ȝou.
Forsothe to day ȝe han caste awei ȝoure Lord God, which aloone sauyde ȝou fro alle ȝoure yuelis and tribulaciouns; and ȝe seiden, Nay, but ordeyne thou a kyng on vs. Now therfor stonde ȝe bifor the Lord bi ȝoure lynagis, and bi meynees.
And Samuel settide to gidere alle the lynages of Israel, and lot felde on the lynage of Beniamyn.
And he settide togidere the lynage of Beniamyn, and the meynees therof; and lot felde on the meynees of Mathri, and it cam til to Saul, the son of Cys. Therfor thei souȝten hym, and he was not foundun there.
And aftir these thingis thei counseliden the Lord, whether Saul schulde come thidur. And the Lord answeride, Lo! he is hid at hoom.
Therfor thei runnen, and token hym fro thennus; and he stood in the myddil of the puple, and was hiȝere than al the puple fro the schulder and aboue.
And Samuel seide to al the puple, Certis ȝe seen whom the Lord hath chose; for noon in al the puple is lijk hym. And al the puple cryede, and seide, Lyue the kyng!
Forsothe Samuel spak to the puple the lawe of rewme, and wroot in a book, and puttide vp bifor the Lord. And Samuel dilyuerede al the puple, ech man in
to his hows; but also Saul ȝede in to his hous in to Gabaath; and the part of the oost ȝede with hym, whose hertis God hadde touchid.
Forsothe the sones of Belyal seiden, Whether this man may saue vs? And thei dispisiden hym, and brouȝten not ȝiftis, that is, preisyngis, to him; forsothe he dissymelide hym to here.
And it was don as aftir a monethe, Naas of Amon stiede, and bigan to fiȝte aȝens Jabes of Galaad. And alle the men of Jabes seiden to Naas, Haue thou vs boundun in pees, and we schulen serue thee.
And Naas of Amon answeride to hem, In this Y schal smyte boond of pees with ȝou, that Y putte out the riȝt iȝen of alle ȝou, and that Y sette ȝou schenschip in al Israel.
And the eldere men of Jabes seiden to him, Graunte thou to vs seuene daies, that we senden messangeris to alle the termes of Israel; and if noon be that defende vs, we schulen go out to thee.
Therfor messangeris camen in to Gabaad of Saul, and spaken these wordis, while the puple herde; and al the puple reiside her vois, and wepte.
And lo! Saul cam, and suede oxis fro the feeld; and he seide, What hath the puple, for it wepith? And thei telden to hym the wordis of men of Jabes.
And the Spirit of the Lord skippide in to Saul, whanne he hadde herd these wordis, and his woodnesse was wrooth greetli
And he took euer either oxe, and kittide in to gobetis, and sente in to alle the termes of Israel, bi the hondis of messangeris; and seide, Who euer goith not out, and sueth not Saul and Samuel, so it schal be don to hise oxun. Therfor the drede of the Lord asailide the puple, and thei ȝeden out as o man.
And he noumbride hem in Besech; and thre hundrid thousynd weren of the sones of Israel; forsothe of the men of Juda weren thretti thousynde.
And thei seiden to the messangeris that camen, Thus ȝe schulen seie to the men that ben in Jabes of Galaad, To morew schal be helthe to ȝou, whanne the sunne is hoot. Therfor the messangeris camen, and telden to the men of Jabes; whiche
weren glad, and seiden, Eerli we schulen go out to ȝou, and ȝe schulen do to vs al that plesith ȝou.
And it was don, whanne the morewe dai cam, Saul ordeynede the puple in to thre partis; and he entride in to the myddil tentis in the wakyng of the morewtid, and he smoot Amon til the dai was hoot; forsothe the residues weren scaterid, so that tweyne togidere weren not left in hem.
And the puple seide to Samuel, Who is this, that seide, Saul schal not regne on vs? Ȝyue ȝe the men, and we schulen sle hem.
And Saul seide, No man schal be slayn in this dai, for to dai the Lord made helthe in Israel.
Forsothe Samuel seide to the puple, Come ȝe, and go we in to Galgala, and renule we there the rewme.
And al the puple ȝede in to Galgala, and there thei maden Saul kyng bifor the Lord in Galgala; and thei offriden pesible sacrifices bifor the Lord. And Saul was glad there, and alle the men of Israel greetli.
Forsothe Samuel seide to al Israel, Lo! Y herde ȝoure vois bi alle thingis whiche ȝe spaken to me, and Y ordeynede a kyng
on ȝou; and now the king goith bifor ȝou. Sotheli Y wexide eld and hoor; forsothe my sones ben with ȝou; therfor Y lyuyde bifor ȝou fro my ȝong wexynge age til to this dai.
And lo! Y am redi; speke ȝe to me bifor the Lord, and bifor the crist of hym; whether Y took the oxe of ony man, ether the asse; if Y falsly chalengide ony mon; yf Y oppresside ony man; if Y took ȝifte of the hond of ony man; and Y schal dispise it to dai, and Y schal restore to ȝou.
And thei seiden, Thou hast not falsly chalengid vs, nether hast oppressid vs, nether hast take ony thing of the hond of ony man.
And he seide to hem, The Lord is witnesse aȝens ȝou, and his crist is witnesse in this day; for ȝe han not founde ony thing in myn hond. And thei seiden, Witnesse.
And Samuel seide to the puple, The Lord, that made Moises and Aaron, and ledde ȝoure fadris out of the
lond of Egipt, is present; now therfor stonde ȝe, that Y stryue bi doom aȝens ȝou bifor the Lord, of alle the mercyes of the Lord, whiche he dide with ȝou, and with ȝoure fadris.
Hou Jacob entride in to Egipt, and ȝoure fadris crieden to the Lord; and the Lord sente Moises and Aaron, and ledde ȝoure fadris out of Egipt, and settide hem in this place.
Whiche forȝaten her Lord God; and he bitook hem in the hond of Sisara, maystir of the chyualrie of Asor, and in the hond of Filisteis, and in the hond of the kyng of Moab; and thei fouȝten aȝens hem.
Sotheli afterward thei crieden to the Lord, and seiden, We synneden, for we forsoken the Lord, and seruyden Baalym and Astroth; now therfor delyuere thou vs fro the hond of oure enemyes, and we schulen serue thee.
And the Lord sente Gerobaal, and Bedan, that is, Sampson, and Barach, and Jepte, and Samuel, and delyuerede ȝou fro the hond of ȝoure enemyes bi cumpass; and ȝe dwelliden tristili.
Forsothe ȝe sien, that Naas, kyng of the sones of Amon, cam aȝens ȝou; and ȝe seiden to me, counseilynge to axe noon other kyng than God, Nay, but a kyng schal comaunde to vs; whanne ȝoure Lord God regnede in ȝou.
Now therfor ȝoure kyng is redi, whom ȝe han chose and axid; lo! the Lord ȝaf to ȝou a kyng.
If ȝe dreden the Lord, and seruen hym, and heren his vois, and wraththen not the mouth of the Lord; ȝe and ȝoure kyng, that comaundith to ȝou, schulen sue ȝoure Lord God.
Forsothe if ȝe heren not the vois of the Lord, but wraththen his word, the hond of the Lord schal be on ȝou, and on ȝoure fadris.
But also now stonde ȝe, and se this gret thing which the Lord schal make in ȝoure siȝt.
Whether heruest of whete is not to dai? I schal inwardli clepe the Lord, and he schal ȝyue voices, that is, thundris, and reynes; and ȝe schulen wite, and schulen se, for ȝe axynge a kyng on ȝou han do greuouse yuel to ȝou in the siȝt of the Lord.
And Samuel criede to the Lord, and the Lord ȝaf voices and reynes in that dai.
And al the puple dredde greetli the Lord and Samuel; and al the puple seide to Samuel, Preye thou for thi seruauntis to thi Lord God, that we die not; for we addiden yuel to alle oure synnes, that we axiden a kyng to vs.
Forsothe Samuel seide to the puple, Nyle ȝe drede; ȝe han do al this yuel; netheles nyle ȝe go awey fro the bak of the Lord, but
serue ȝe the Lord in al ȝoure herte; and nyle ȝe bowe aftir veyn thingis, that schulen not profite to ȝou, nether schulen delyuere ȝou; for tho ben veyn thingis.
And the Lord schal not forsake his puple for his grete name; for the Lord swoor to make ȝou a puple to hym silf.
Forsothe this synne be fer fro me in the Lord, that Y ceesse to preye for ȝou; and Y schal teche ȝou a riȝtful weie and good.
Therfor drede ȝe the Lord, and serue ȝe hym in treuthe, and of al ȝoure herte; for ȝe sien tho grete thingis, whiche he dide
in ȝou; that if ȝe contynuen in malice, bothe ȝe and ȝoure kyng schulen perische to gidere.
Saul was a child of o ȝeer whanne he bigan to regne; forsothe he regnede on Israel twei ȝeer
And Saul chees to hym thre thousynde of Israel, and twei thousynde weren with Saul in Machynas, in the hil of Bethel; forsothe a thousynde weren with Jonathas in Gabaath of Beniamyn; sotheli he sente aȝen the tother puple ech man in to hise tabernaclis.
And Jonathas smoot the stacioun of Filisteis, that was in Gabaa. And whanne Filisteis hadden herd this, Saul sownede with a clarioun in al the lond, and seide, Ebreys here.
And al Israel herde siche a fame, Saul smoot the stacioun of Filisteis; and Israel reiside hym silf aȝens Filisteis; therfor the puple criede after Saul in Galgala.
And Filisteis weren gaderid to fiȝte aȝens Israel; of Filisteis weren thretti thousynde of charis, and sixe thousynde of knyȝtis, and the tother comyn puple, as grauel which is ful myche in the brynke of the see; and thei stieden, and settiden tentis in Machynas, at the eest of Bethauen.
And whanne men of Israel hadden seyn this, that thei weren set in streiȝtnesse, for the puple was turmentid, thei hidden hem silf in dennes, and in priuey places, and in stonys, and in dychis, and in cisternes.
Sotheli Ebreis passiden Jordan in to the lond of Gad and of Galaad. And whanne Saul was ȝit in Galgala, al the puple was aferd that suede hym.
And seuene daies he abood Samuel bi couenaunt, and Samuel cam not in to Galgala; and the puple ȝede a wei fro Saul.
Therfor Saul seide, Brynge ȝe to me brent sacrifice, and pesible sacrifices; and he offride brent sacrifice.
And whanne he hadde endid offrynge brent sacrifice, lo! Samuel cam; and Saul ȝede out aȝens hym, to greete Samuel.
And Samuel spak to hym, What hast thou do? Saul answeride, For Y siȝ that the puple ȝede awei fro me, and thou camest not bi the daies of couenaunt; certis Filisteis weren
gaderid in Machynas; Y seide, Now Filisteis schulen come doun to me in to Galgala, and Y haue not plesyd the face of the Lord; Y was compellid bi nede, and Y offryde brent sacrifice to the Lord.
And Samuel seide to Saul, Thou hast do folili, and thou keptist not the heestis of thi Lord God, whiche he comaundide to thee; and if thou haddist not do this thing, riȝt now the Lord hadde maad redi thi rewme
on Israel with outen ende; but thi rewme schal not rise ferthere. The Lord hath souȝt a man to hym silf after his herte; and the Lord comaundide to hym, that he schulde be duyk on his puple, for thou keptist not tho thingis whiche the Lord comaundide.
Forsothe Samuel roos, and stiede fro Galgala in to Gabaa of Beniamyn; and the residue puplis stieden after Saul aȝens the puple which fouȝten aȝens hem; and thei camen fro Galgala in to Gabaa, in the hil of Beniamyn. And Saul noumbride the puple, that weren foundun with hym as sixe hundrid men.
And Saul, and Jonathas his sone, and the puple that was foundun with hem, was in Gabaa of Beniamyn; forsothe Filisteis saten togidere in Machynas.
And thre cumpanyes ȝeden out of the castels of Filisteis to take prey; o cumpany ȝede aȝens the weie of Effraym
to the lond of Saul; sothely an other cumpeny entride bi the weie of Bethoron; forsothe the thridde cumpenye turnede it silf to the weie of the terme in the lond of Sabaa; and that terme neiȝeth to the valey of Seboym aȝens the deseert.
Forsothe no smyȝth of yrun was foundun in al the lond of Israel; for Filisteis weren war, ether eschewiden, lest perauenture Ebreis maden a swerd ether a spere.
Therfor al Israel ȝede doun to Filisteis, that ech man schulde scharpe his schar, and picoise, and ax, and sarpe;
and so alle egis weren bluntid of scharris, and of picoisis, and of forkis of thre teeth, and of axis, til to a pricke to be amendid.
And whanne the dai of batel cam, no swerd and spere was foundun in the hond of al the puple that was with Saul and Jonathas, outakun Saul, and Jonathas his sone.
Forsothe the stacioun of Filisteis ȝede out, that it schulde passe in to Machynas.
And it bifelde in a day, that Jonathas, the sone of Saul, seide to his squyer, a ȝong man, Come thou, and passe we to the staciouns of the Filisteis, which is biȝende that place; sotheli he schewide not this same thing to his fadir.
Sotheli Saul dwellide in the laste part of Gabaa, vndur a pumgarnarde tre, that was in the feeld of Gabaa; and the puple as of sixe hundrid men was with hym.
