weren led prisoneris, Dauid and the puple that was with hym reisiden her voices, and weiliden, til teeris failiden in hem.
Forsothe also twei wyues of Dauid weren led prisoneris, Achynoem of Jezrael, and Abigail, the wijf of Nabal of Carmele.
And Dauid was ful sori; forsothe al the puple wold stone hym, for the soule of ech man was bittir on her sones and douȝtris. Forsothe Dauid was coumfortid in his Lord God.
And he seide to Abiathar, preest, the sone of Achymelech, Bringe thou ephoth to me. And Abiathar brouȝte ephoth to Dauid;
and Dauid councelide the Lord, and seide, Schal Y pursue, ether nay, these theues? and schal Y take hem? And the Lord seide to hym, Pursue thou; for with out doute thou schalt take hem, and thou schalt take awey the prey.
Therfor Dauid ȝede, he and sixe hundrid men that weren with hym, and thei camen til to the stronde of Besor; and sotheli the wery men abididen.
Forsothe Dauid pursuede, he and foure hundrid men; for twei hundrid abididen, that weren weeri, and myȝten not passe the stronde of Besor.
And thei founden a man of Egipte in the feeld, and thei brouȝten hym to Dauid; and thei ȝauen breed to hym, that he schulde ete, and schulde drynke watir;
but also thei ȝauen to hym a gobet of a bundel of drye figis, and twei byndyngis of dried grapis. And whanne he hadde ete tho, his spirit turnede aȝen, and he was coumfortid; for he hadde not ete breed, nether hadde drunk watir in thre daies and thre nyȝtis.
Therfor Dauid seide to hym, Whos man art thou, ethir fro whennus and whidur goist thou? And he seide, Y am a child of Egipt, the seruaunt of a man of Amalech; forsothe my lord forsook me, for Y bigan to be sijk the thridde dai ago.
Sotheli we braken out to the south coost of Cerethi, and aȝens Juda, and to the south of Caleb, and we brenten Sichelech bi fier.
And Dauid seide to hym, Maist thou lede me to this cumpeny? Which seide, Swere thou to me bi God, that thou schalt not sle me, and schalt not bitake me in to the hondis of my lord; and Y schal lede thee to this cumpeny. And Dauid swoor to hym.
And whanne the child hadde ledde hym, lo! thei saten at the mete, on the face of al the erthe, etynge and drynkynge, and as halewynge a feeste, for al the prey and spuylis whiche thei hadden take of the lond of Filisteis, and of the lond of Juda.
And Dauid smoot hem fro euentid til to euentid of the tothir dai, and not ony of hem escapide, no but foure hundrid ȝonge men, that stieden on camels, and fledden.
Forsothe Dauid delyuerede alle thingis whiche the men of Amalech token, and he delyuerede hise twei wyues;
nether ony of hem failide fro litil til to greet, as wel of sones as of douȝtris, and of spuylis; and what euer thingis thei hadden rauyschid, Dauid ledde aȝen alle
thingis; and he took alle flockis and grete beestis, and droof bifor his face. And thei seiden, This is the prey of Dauid.
Forsothe Dauid cam to twei hundrid men, that weren weeri, and abididen, and myȝten not sue Dauid; and he hadde comaundid hem to sitte in the stronde of Besor; whiche ȝeden out aȝens Dauid, and the puple that was with hym. Forsothe Dauid neiȝede to the puple, and grette it pesibli.
And o man, the werste and vniust of the men that weren with Dauid, answeride, and seide, For thei camen not with vs, we schulen not ȝyue to hem ony thing of the prey, which we rauyschiden, but his wijf and children suffice to ech man; and whanne thei han take hem, go thei awei.
Forsothe Dauid seide, My britheren, ȝe schulen not do so of these thingis, whiche the Lord ȝaf to vs, and kepte vs, and ȝaf the theues, that braken out aȝens vs, in to oure
hondis; nether ony man schal here vs on this word. For euene part schal be of him that goith doun to batel, and of hym that dwellith at the fardelis; and in lijk maner thei schulen departe.
And this was maad a constitucioun and doom fro that dai and afterward, and as a lawe in Israel til in to this dai.
Therfor Dauid cam in to Sichelech, and sente ȝiftis of the prey to the eldere men of Juda, hise neiȝboris, and seide, Take ȝe blessyng of the prey of
enemyes of the Lord; to hem that weren in Bethel, and that weren in Ramoth, at
the south, and that weren in Jether, and that weren in Aroer, and that weren in Sephamoth, and that weren in Escama,
and that weren in Rethala, and that weren in the citees of Jeramel, and that weren in
the citees of Ceny, and that weren in Arama, and that weren in Lautuasam, and
that weren in Athec, and that weren in Ebron, and to othere men, that weren in these places, in whiche Dauid dwellide and hise men.
Forsothe Filisteis fouȝten aȝens Israel, and the men of Israel fledden bifor the face of Filisteis, and felden slayn in the hil of Gelboe.
And Filisteis hurliden on Saul, and on hise sones, and smytiden Jonathas, and Amynadab, and Melchisua, sones of Saul.
And al the weiȝte of batel was turned in to Saul; and men archeris pursueden hym, and he was woundid greetli of the archeris.
And Saul seide to his squyer, Drawe out thi swerd, and sle me, lest perauenture these vncircumcidid men come, and sle me, and scorne me. And his squyer nolde, for he was aferd bi ful grete drede; therfor Saul took his swerd, and felde theronne.
And whanne his squyer hadde seyn this, that is, that Saul was deed, also he felde on his swerd and was deed with hym.
Therfor Saul was deed, and hise thre sones, and his squyer, and alle his men in that dai togidere.
Forsothe the sones of Israel, that weren biȝendis the valei, and biȝendis Jordan, sien that the men of Israel hadden fled, and that Saul was deed, and hise sones, and thei leften her citees and fledden; and Filisteis camen, and dwelliden there.
Forsothe in the tother dai maad, Filisteis camen, that thei schulden dispuyle the slayn men, and thei founden Saul, and hise thre sones, liggynge in the hil of Gelboe;
and thei kittiden awei the heed of Saul, and dispuyliden hym of armeris; and senten in to the lond of Filisteis bi cumpas, that it schulde be teld in the temple of idols, and in the puplis.
And thei puttiden hise armeris in the temple of Astoroth; sotheli thei hangiden his bodi in the wal of Bethsan.
And whanne the dwellers of Jabes of Galaad hadden herd this, what euer thingis Filisteis hadden
do to Saul, alle the strongeste men risiden, and ȝeden in al that nyȝt, and token the deed bodi of Saul, and the deed bodies of hise sones fro the wal of Bethsan; and the men of Jabes of Galaad camen, and brenten tho deed bodies bi fier.
And thei token the boonus of hem, and birieden in the wode of Jabes, and fastiden bi seuene daies.
Forsothe it was doon, after that Saul was deed, that Dauid turnede aȝen fro the sleyng of Amalech, and dwellide twei daies in Sichelech.
Forsothe in the thridde dai a man apperide, comynge fro the castels of Saul with the cloth to-rent, and his heed spreynt with dust; and as he cam to Dauid, he felde on his face, and worschipide.
And Dauid seide to hym, Fro whennus comest thou? Which seide to Dauid, Y fledde fro the castels of Israel.
And Dauid seide to hym, What is the word which is doon; schewe thou to me. And he seide, The puple fledde fro the batel, and many of the puple felden, and ben deed; but also Saul, and Jonathas, his sonne, perischyden.
And Dauid seide to the ȝong man, that telde to hym, Wherof woost thou, that Saul is deed, and Jonathas, his sonne?
And the ȝong man seide, that telde to hym, Bi hap Y cam in to the hil of Gelboe, and Saul lenyde on his spere; forsothe charis and knyȝtis
neiȝiden to hym; and he turnede bihynde his bak, and siȝ me, and clepide. To whom whanne Y hadde answeride, Y am present; he seide to me, Who art thou?
And Y seide to hym, Y am a man of Amalech.
And he spak to me, Stonde thou on me, and sle me; for angwischis holden me, and ȝit al my lijf is in me.
And Y stood on hym, and Y killide hym; for Y wiste that he myȝte not lyue aftir the fallyng; and Y took the diademe, that was in his heed, and the bye fro his arm, and Y brouȝte hidur to thee, my lord.
Forsothe Dauid took and to-rente hise clothis, and the men
that weren with hym; and thei weiliden, and wepten, and fastiden til to euentid, on Saul, and Jonathas, his sone, and on the puple of the Lord, and on the hows of Israel, for thei hadden feld bi swerd.
And Dauid seide to the ȝong man, that telde to him, Of whennus art thou? And he answeride, Y am the sone of a man comelyng, of a man of Amalech.
And Dauid seide to him, Whi dreddist thou not to sende thine hond, that thou schuldist sle the crist of the Lord?
And Dauid clepide oon of hise children, and seide, Go thou, and falle on hym. Which smoot that ȝong man, and he was deed.
And Dauid seide to hym, Thi blood be on thin heed; for thi mouth spak aȝens thee, and seide, Y killide the crist of the Lord.
Forsooth Dauid biweilide sych a weilyng on
Saul, and on Jonathas, his sone; and comaundide, that thei schulden teche the sones of Juda weilyng, as it is writun in the Book of Just Men. And Dauid seyde, Israel, biholde thou, for these men that ben deed, woundid on thin hiȝe
placis; the noble men of Israel ben slayn on thin hillis.
Hou felden stronge men? nyle ȝe telle in Geth, nether telle ȝe in the weilottis of Ascolon; lest perauenture the douȝtris of Filisteis be glad, lest the douȝtris of vncircumcidid men be glad.
Hillis of Gelboe, neither dew nethir reyn come on you, nether the feeldis of firste fruytis be; for the scheeld of stronge men was cast awey there, the scheeld of Saul, as if he were not anoyntid with oile.
Of the blood of slayn men, of the fatnesse of strong men, the arewe of Jonathas ȝede neuer abak, and the swerd of Saul turnede not aȝen void.
Saul and Jonathas amyable, and fair in her lijf, weren not departid also in deeth; thei weren swiftere than eglis, strongere than liouns.
Douȝtris of Israel, wepe ȝe on Saul, that clothide ȝou with fyn reed colourid in delicis, that ȝaf goldun ournementis to ȝoure atyre.
Hou felden doun stronge men in batel? Jonathas was slayn in the hiȝe places.
Y make sorewe on thee, my brother Jonathas, ful fair, and amyable more than the loue of wymmen; as a modir loueth oon aloone sone, so Y louyde thee.
Hou therfor felden doun stronge men, and armeris of batel perischide?
Therfor aftir these thingis Dauid counseilide the Lord, and seide, Whether Y schal stie in to oon of the citees of Juda? And the Lord seide to hym, Stie thou. And Dauid seide to the Lord, Whidur schal Y stie? And the Lord answeride to hym, In to Ebron.
Therfor Dauid stiede, and hise twei wyues, Achynoem of Jezrael, and Abigail, the wijf of Nabal of Carmele.
But also Dauid ledde the men that weren with hym, ech man with his hows; and thei dwelliden in the townes of Ebron.
And the men of Juda camen, and anoyntiden there Dauid, that he schulde regne on the hows of Juda. And it was teld to Dauid, that men of Jabes of Galaad hadden biried Saul.
Therfor Dauid sente messangeris to the men of Jabes of Galaad, and seide to hem, Blessid be ȝe of the Lord, that diden this mercy with ȝour lord Saul, and birieden hym.
And now sotheli the Lord schal ȝelde to ȝou merci and treuthe, but also Y schal ȝelde thankyng, for ȝe diden this word.
Ȝoure hondis be coumfortid, and be ȝe sones of strengthe; for thouȝ ȝoure lord Saul is deed, netheles the hows of Juda anoyntide me kyng to hym silf.
Forsothe Abner, the sone of Ner, prince of the oost of Saul, took Isbosech, the sone of Saul, and ledde hym
aboute bi the castels, and made him kyng on Galaad, and on Gethsury, and on Jezrael, and on Effraym, and on Beniamyn, and on al Israel. Isbosech, the sone of Saul, was of fourti ȝeer, whanne he began to regne on Israel; and he regnede twei ȝeer. Sotheli the hous aloone of Juda suede Dauid.
And the noumbre of daies, bi whiche Dauid dwellide regnynge in Ebron on the hows of Juda, was of seuene ȝeer and sixe monethis.
And Abner, the sone of Ner, ȝede out, and the children of Isbosech, sone of Saul, fro the castels in Gabaon.
Forsothe Joab, the sone of Saruye, and the children of Dauid ȝeden out, and camen to hem bisidis the cisterne in Gabaon. And whanne thei hadden come togidere in to o place euene aȝens, these saten on o part of the cisterne, and thei on the tother.
And Abner seide to Joab, The children rise, and plei befor us. And Joab answeride, Rise thei.
Therfor thei risiden, and passiden twelue in noumbre of Beniamyn, of the part of Isbosech, sone of Saul; and twelue of the children of Dauid.
And ech man, whanne the heed of his felowe was takun, fastnede the swerde in to the side of the contrarye; and thei felden doun togidere. And the name of that place was clepid The Feeld of stronge men in Gabaon.
And batel hard ynow roos in that dai; and Abner and the sones of Israel weren dryuun of the children of Dauid.
Forsothe thre sones of Saruye weren there, Joab, and Abisai, and Asahel; forsothe Asahel was a rennere moost swift, as oon of the capretis that dwellen in woodis.
Forsothe Asahel pursuede Abner, and bowide not, nether to the riȝt side nether to the left side, ceessynge to pursue Abner.
Therfor Abner bihelde bihynde his bac, and seide, Whether thou art Asahel? Which answeride, Y am.
And Abner seide to hym, Go to the riȝtside, ether to the lefte side; and take oon of the ȝonge men, and take to thee hise spuylis. Sotheli Asahel nolde ceesse, that ne he pursuede hym.
And eft Abner spak to Asahel, Go thou awei; nyle thou pursue me, lest Y be compellid to peerse thee in to erthe, and Y schal not mowe reise my face to Joab, thi brother.
And Asahel dispiside to here, and nolde bowe awey. Therfor Abner smoot him with the spere turned awei in the schar, and roof thorouȝ, and he was deed in the same place; and alle men that passiden bi the place, in which place Asahel felde doun, and was deed, stoden stille.
Forsothe while Joab and Abisai pursueden Abner fleynge, the sunne ȝede doun; and thei camen til to the litil hil of the water cundiyt, which is euene aȝens the valey, and the weie of deseert in Gabaon.
And the sones of Beniamyn weren gaderid to Abner, and thei weren gaderid togidere in to o cumpeny, and stoden in the hiȝnesse of oon heep of erthe.
And Abner criede to Joab, and seide, Whether thi swerd schal be feers til to sleyng? Whether thou knowist not, that dispeir is perelouse? Hou longe seist thou not to the puple, that it ceesse to pursue hise britheren?
And Joab seyde, The Lord lyueth, for if thou haddist spoke eerli, the puple pursuynge his brother hadde go awey.
And Joab sownede with a clarioun, and al the oost stood; and thei pursueden no ferthere Israel, nether bigunnen batel.
Forsothe Abner and hise men ȝeden by the feeldi places of Moab in al that nyȝt, and passiden Jordan; and whanne al Bethoron was compassid, thei camen to the castels.
Sotheli whanne Abner was left, Joab turnede aȝen, and gaderide togidere al the puple; and ten men and nyne, outakun Asahel, failiden of the children of Dauid.
Forsothe the seruauntis of Dauid smytiden of Beniamyn, and of the men that weren with Abner, thre hundrid men and sixti, whiche also weren deed.
And thei token Asahel, and birieden hym in the sepulcre of his fadir in Bethleem. And Joab, and the men that weren with hym, ȝeden in al that nyȝt, and in thilke morewtid thei camen in to Ebron.
Therfor long strijf was maad bitwixe the hows of Dauid and bitwixe the hows of Saul; and Dauid profitide and euere was strongere than hym silf, forsothe the hows of Saul decreesside ech dai.
And sones weren borne to Dauid in Ebron; and his firste gendrid sone was Amon, of
Achynoem of Jezrael; and aftir hym was Celeab, of Abigail, wijf of Nabal of Carmele; sotheli the thrydde was Absolon, the sone of Maacha, douȝtir of Tholomay,
kyng of Gessur; forsothe the fourthe was Adonyas, the sone of Agith; and the fyuethe was Saphacias, the sone of Abitail;
and the sixte was Gethraam of Egla, the wijf of Dauid. These weren borne to Dauid in Ebron.
Therfor whanne batel was bytwixe the hows of Saul and the hows of Dauid, Abner, the sone of Ner, gouernyde the hows of Saul.
Sotheli a concubyn, that is, a secoundarie wijf, Respha bi name, the douȝtir of Achia, was to Saul; and Abner entride to hir.
And Isbosech seide to Abner, Whi entridist thou to the concubyn of my fadir? Which was wrooth greetli for the wordis of Isbosech, and seide, Whether Y am the heed of a dogge aȝens Juda to dai, and Y have do merci on the hous of Saul, thi fadir, and on hise britheren, and neiȝboris, and Y bitook not thee in to the hondis of David, and thou hast souȝt in me that, that thou schuldist repreue me for a womman to dai?
God do these thingis to Abner, and adde these thingis to hym, no but as the Lord swoor to Dauid, so
Y do with hym, that the rewme be translatid fro the hous of Saul, and the trone of Dauid be reisid on Israel and on Juda, fro Dan til to Bersabee.
And Isbosech myȝte not answere ony thing to Abner, for he dredde Abner.
Therfor Abner sente messangeris to Dauid, and thei seiden for hym, Whos is the lond? and that the messangeris schulden speke, Make thou frenschipis with me, and myn hond schal be with thee, and Y schal brynge al Israel to thee.
And Dauid seide, Best Y schal make frenschipis with thee, but Y axe of thee o thing, and seie, Thou schalt not se my face, bifore that thou brynge Mycol, the douȝter of Saul, and so thou schalt come, and schalt se me.
Therfor Dauid sente messangeris to Isbosech, the sone of Saul, and seide, Ȝelde thou my wijf Mycol, whom Y spouside to me for an hundryd prepucies of Filisteis.
Therfor Isbosech sente, and took hir fro hir hosebonde,
Faltiel, son of Lais; and hir hosebonde suede hir and wepte til Bahurym. And Abner seide to hym, Go thou, and turne aȝen; and he turnede aȝen.
Also Abner brouȝte in a word to the eldere men of Israel, and seide, Bothe ȝistirdai and the thridde dai ago ȝe souȝten Dauid, that he schulde regne on ȝou.
Now therfor do ȝe; for the Lord spak to Dauid, and seide, In the hond of my seruaunt Dauid Y schal saue my puple Israel fro the hond of Filisteis, and of alle his enemyes.
Forsothe Abner spak also to Beniamyn, and he ȝede, that he schulde speke to Dauid, in Ebron, alle thingis that plesiden Israel and al Beniamin.
And he cam to Dauid in Ebron with twenti men. And Dauid made a feeste to Abner, and to the men that camen with hym.
And Abner seide to Dauid, Y schal rise, that Y gadere al Israel to thee, my lord the kyng, and that Y make boond of pees with thee, and that thou regne on alle, as thi soule desirith. Therfor whanne Dauid hadde ledde forth Abner, and he hadde
go in pees, anoon the children of Dauid and Joab camen with a ful grete prey, whanne theues weren slayn; sotheli Abner was not with Dauid, in Ebron, for Dauid hadde left hym, and he ȝede forth in pees.
And Joab, and the oostis that weren with hym, camen aftirward; therfor it was teld to Joab of telleris, Abner, the sone of Ner, cam to the kyng, and the kyng lefte hym, and he ȝede in pees.
And Joab entride to the kyng, and seide, What hast thou do? Lo! Abner cam to thee; whi leftist thou hym, and he ȝede, and departide?
Knowist thou not Abner, the sone of Ner, for herto he cam to thee, that he schulde disseyue thee, and that he schulde knowe thi going out and thin entryng, and schulde knowe alle thingis whiche thou doist?
Therfor Joab ȝede out fro Dauid, and sente messangeris aftir Abner; and ledde hym aȝen fro the cisterne of Cyrie, while Dauid knew not.
And whanne Abner hadde come aȝen in to Ebron, Joab ledde hym asidis half to the myddil of the ȝate, that he schulde speke to hym in gile; and he smoot Abner there in the schar, and he was deed, in to the veniaunce of the blood of his brother Asahel.
That whanne Dauid hadde herd the thing doon, he seide, Y am clene and my rewme anentis God til in to with outen ende fro the blood of Abner, sone
of Ner; and come it on the heed of Joab, and on al the hows of his fadir; a man suffrynge flux of seed, and a leprouse man, holdynge spyndil, and fallynge bi swerd, and hauynge nede to breed, that is, suffrynge hungur, faile not of the hows of Joab.
Therfor Joab, and Abisay, his brother, killiden Abner, for he hadde slayn Asahel, her brother, in Gabaon, in batel.
Forsothe Dauid seide to Joab, and to al the puple that was with hym, To rende ȝe ȝour clothis, and be ȝe gird with sackis, and biweile ȝe bifor the heersis, ether dirige, of Abner. Forsothe kyng Dauid suede the beere.
And whanne thei hadden biried Abner in Ebron, kyng Dauid reiside his vois, and wepte on the biriel of Abner; forsothe and al the puple wepte.
And the kyng biweilide, and bymorenyde Abner, and seide, Abner, thou diedist not as dredeful men, ethir cowardis, ben wont to die.
Thin hondis weren not boundun, and thi feet weren not greuyd with stockis, but thou feldist doun, as men ben wont to falle bifor the sones of wickidnesse. And al the puple doublide togidere, and wepte on hym.
And whanne al the multitude cam to take mete with Dauid, while the dai was ȝit cleer, Dauid swoor, and seide, God do to me these thingis, and adde these thingis, if Y schal taast breed ethir ony othir thing bifor the going doun of the sune.
And al the puple herde; and alle thingis which the kyng dide in the siȝt of al the puple plesiden
hem; and al the comyn puple and al Israel knewe in that day, that it was not doon of the kyng, that Abner, the sone of Ner, was slayn.
Also the kyng seide to hise seruauntis, Whether ȝe witen not, that the prince and gretteste felde doun to dai in Israel?
Forsothe Y am delicat, ether tendir, ȝit and anoyntid kyng; sotheli these sones of Saruye ben hard to me; the Lord ȝelde to hym that doith yuel bi his malice.
Forsothe Isbosech, the sone of Saul, herde that Abner hadde falde doun in Ebron; and hise hondis weren discoumfortid, and al Israel was disturblid.
Forsothe twei men, princes of theues, weren to the sone of Saul; name to oon was Baana, and name to the tother was Rechab, the sones of Remmon Berothite, of the sones of Beniamyn; for also Beroth is arettid in Beniamyn.
And men of Beroth fledden in to Gethaym; and thei weren comelyngis there til to that tyme.
Forsothe a sone feble in feet was to Jonathas, the sone of Saul; forsothe he was fyue ȝeer eld, whanne the messanger cam fro Saul and Jonathas, fro Jezrael. Therfor his nurse took hym, and fledde; and whanne sche hastide to fle, sche felde doun, and the child was maad lame; and he hadde a name Myphibosech.
Therfor Rechab and Baana, sones of Remmon of Beroth, camen, and entriden in the hoot dai in to the hows of Isbosech, that slepte on his bed in myd dai, and the womman oischer of the hous clensynge wheete, slepte strongli.
Forsothe thei entriden into the hows pryueli, and token eeris of whete; and Rechab, and Baana, his brother, smytiden Isbosech in the schar, and fledden.
Sotheli whanne thei hadden entrid in to the hous, he slepte on his bedde in a closet; and thei smytiden and killiden hym; and whanne his heed was takun, thei ȝeden bi the weie of deseert in al the nyȝt.
And thei brouȝten the heed of Isbosech to Dauid, in Ebron, and thei seiden to the kyng, Lo! the heed of Isbosech, sone of Saul, thin enemy, that souȝte thi lijf; and the Lord ȝaf to dai to oure lord the kyng veniaunce of Saul and of his seed.
Forsothe Dauid answeride to Rechab, and Baana, his brother, the sones of Remmon of Beroth, and seide to hem, The Lord lyueth, that delyueride
my lijf fro al angwisch; for Y helde hym that telde to me, and seide, Saul is deed, which man gesside hym silf to telle prosperitees, and Y killide hym in Sichelech, to whom it bihofte me ȝyue meede
for message; hou myche more now, whanne wickid men han slayn a giltles man in his hows on his bed, schal I not seke his blood of ȝoure hond, and schal Y do awey ȝou fro erthe?
Therfor Dauid comaundide to his children, and thei killiden hem; and thei kittiden awei the hondis and feet of hem, and hangiden hem ouer the cisterne in Ebron. Forsothe thei token the heed of Isbosech, and birieden in the sepulcre of Abner, in Ebron.
And alle the lynagis of Israel camen to Dauid, in Ebron, and seiden, Lo! we ben thi boon and thi fleisch.
But also ȝistirdai and the thridde day ago, whanne Saul was kyng on vs, thou leddist out, and leddist aȝen Israel; forsothe the Lord seide to thee, Thou schalt fede my puple Israel, and thou schalt be duyk on Israel.
Also and the eldere men of Israel camen to the kyng, in Ebron; and kyng Dauid smoot with hem boond of pees in Ebron, bifor the Lord; and thei anoyntiden Dauid in to kyng on Israel.
Dauid was a sone of thretti ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne, and he regnyde fourti
ȝeer in Ebron; he regnede on Juda seuene ȝeer and sixe monethis; forsothe in Jerusalem he regnede thretti and thre ȝeer, on al Israel and Juda.
And the kyng ȝede, and alle men that weren with hym, in to Jerusalem, to Jebusey, dweller of the lond. And it was seide of hem to Dauid, Thou schalt not entre hidur, no but thou do awei blynde men and lame, seiynge, Dauid schal not entre hydur.
Forsothe Dauid took the tour of Syon; this is the citee of Dauid.
For Dauid hadde sette forth meede in that dai to hym, that hadde smyte Jebusei, and hadde touchid the goteris of roouys, and hadde take awey lame men and blynde, hatynge the lijf of Dauid. Therfor it is seid in prouerbe, A blynde man and lame schulen not entre in to the temple.
Forsothe Dauid dwellide in the tour, and clepide it the citee of Dauid; and he bildide bi cumpas fro Mello, and with ynne.
And he entride profitynge and encreessynge; and the Lord God of oostis was with hym.
Also Hyram, kyng of Tire, sent messangeris to Dauid, and cedre trees, and crafti men of trees, and crafti men of stoonus to wallis; and thei bildiden the hows of Dauid.
And Dauid knew, that the Lord hadde confermed hym kyng on Israel, and that he hadde enhaunsid his rewme on his puple Israel.
Therfor Dauid took ȝit concubyns, and wyues of Jerusalem, after that he cam fro Ebron; and also othere sones and douȝtris weren borun to Dauid.
And these ben the names of hem that weren borun to hym in Jerusalem; Samua, and Sobab,
and Nathan, and Salomon, and Jobaar,
and Helisua, and Repheg, and Japhia, and Helysama, and Holida, and Heliphelech.
Therfor Filisteis herden, that thei hadden anoyntid Dauid kyng on Israel, and alle Filisteis stieden to seke Dauid. And whanne Dauid hadde herd this, he ȝede doun into a strong hold.
Forsothe Filisteis camen, and weren spred abrood in the valei of Raphaym.
And Dauid counseilide the Lord, and seide, Whether Y schal stie to Filisties, and whether thou schalt ȝyue hem in myn hond? And the Lord seide to Dauid, Stie thou, for Y schal bitake, and Y schal ȝyue Filisteis in thin hond.
Therfor Dauid cam in to Baal Farasym, and smoot hem there, and seide, The Lord departide myn enemyes bifor me, as watris ben departid. Therfor the name of that place was clepid Baal Farasym.
And thei leften there her sculptils, whiche Dauid took, and hise men.
And Filisteis addiden ȝit, that thei schulden stie, and thei weren spred abrood in the valey of Raphaym.
Sotheli Dauid councelide the Lord, and seide, Whether Y schal stie agens Filisties, and whether thou schalt bitake hem in to myn hondis? Which answeride, Thou schalt not stie aȝens hem, but cumpasse thou bihynde her bak, and thou schalt come to hem on the contrarie side of the pere trees.
And whanne thou schalt here the sown of cry goynge in the cop of pere trees, thanne thou schalt biginne batel; for thanne the Lord schal go out befor thi face, that he smyte the castels of Filisteis.
Therfor Dauid dide as the Lord comaundide to hym; and he smoot Filisteys fro Gabaa til the while thei camen to Jezer.
Forsothe Dauid gaderide eft alle the chosun men of Israel, thritti thousynde.
And Dauid roos, and ȝede, and al the puple that was with hym of the men of Juda, to brynge the arke of God, on which the name of the Lord of oostis, sittynge in cherubyn on that arke, was clepid.
And thei puttiden the arke of God on a newe wayn, and thei token it fro the hows of Amynadab, that was in Gabaa. Forsothe Oza and Haio, the sons of Amynadab, dryueden the newe wayn.
And whanne thei hadden take it fro the hows of Amynadab, that was in Gabaa, and kepte the arke of God, Haio ȝede bifor the arke.
Forsothe Dauid and al Israel pleieden byfor the Lord, in alle trees maad craftili, and harpis, and sitols, and tympans, and trumpis, and cymbalis.
Forsothe after that thei camen to the corn floor of Nachor, Oza helde forth the hond to the arke of God, and helde it, for the oxun kikiden, and bowiden it.
And the Lord was wrooth bi indignacioun aȝens Oza, and smoot hym on the foli; and he was deed there bisidis the arke of God.
Forsothe Dauid was sori, for the Lord hadde smyte Oza; and the name of that place was clepid the Smytyng of Oza til in to this dai.
And Dauid dredde the Lord in that dai, and seide, Hou schal the arke of the Lord entre to me?
And he nolde turne the arke of the Lord to hym silf in to the citee of Dauid, but he turnede it in to the hows of Obethedom of Geth.
And the arke of the Lord dwellide in the hows of Obethedom of Geth thre monethis; and the Lord blessid Obethedom, and al his hows.
And it was teld to kyng Dauid, that the Lord hadde blessid Obethedom, and alle thingis of hym, for the arke of God. And Dauid seide, Y schal go, and brynge the arke with blessyng in to myn hows. Therfor Dauid ȝede, and brouȝte the arke of God fro the hows of Obethedom in to the citee of Dauid with ioye; and ther weren with Dauid seuen cumpanyes, and the slain sacrifice of a calff.
And whanne thei, that baren the arke of the Lord, hadden stied six paaces, thei offriden an oxe and a ram. And Dauid smoot in organs boundun to the arm;
and daunside with alle strengthis bifor the Lord; sotheli Dauid was clothid with a lynnun surplis.
And Dauid, and al the hows of Israel, ledden forth the arke of testament of the Lord in hertli song, and in sown of trumpe.
And whanne the arke of the Lord hadde entride in to the citee of Dauid, Mychol, the douȝtir of Saul, bihelde bi a wyndow, and sche siȝ the kyng skippynge and daunsynge bifor the Lord; and sche dispiside hym in hir herte.
And thei brouȝten in the arke of the Lord, and settiden it in his place, in the myddis of tabernacle, which tabernacle Dauid hadde maad redy therto; and Dauid offride brent sacrifices and pesible bifor the Lord.
And whanne Dauid hadde endid tho, and hadde offrid brent sacrifices and pesible, he blesside the puple in the name of the Lord of oostis.
And he ȝaf to al the multitude of Israel, as wel to man as to womman, to ech o thinne loof, and o part rostid of bugle fleisch, and flour of wheete fried with oile; and al the puple ȝede, ech man in to his hows.
And Dauid turnede aȝen to blesse his hows, and Mychol, the douȝtir of Saul, ȝede out in to the comyng of Dauid, and seide, Hou glorious was the kyng of Israel to day vnhilynge hym silf bifor the handmaidis of hise seruauntis, and he was maad nakid, as if oon of the harlotis be maad nakid?
And Dauid seide to Mychol, The Lord lyueth, for Y schal pley bifor the Lord, that chees me rathere than thi fadir, and than al the hows of hym, and comaundide to me, that Y schulde be duyk on the puple of the
Lord of Israel; and Y schal pleie, and Y schal be maad vilere more than Y am maad, and Y schal be meke in myn iȝen, and Y schal appere gloriousere with the handmaydys, of whiche thou spakist.
Therfor a sone was not borun to Mychol, the douȝtir of Saul, til in to the dai of hir deeth.
Forsothe it was doon, whanne the kyng Dauid hadde sete in his hows, and the Lord hadde ȝoue reste to hym on ech
side fro alle hise enemyes, he seyde to Nathan the prophete, Seest thou not, that Y dwelle in an hows of cedre, and the arke of God is put in the myddis of skynnys?
And Nathan seide to the kyng, Go thou, and do al thing which is in thin herte, for the Lord is with thee.
Forsothe it was don in that niȝt, and lo! the word of the Lord, seiynge to Nathan,
Go thou, and speke to my servaunt Dauid, The Lord seith these thingis, Whether thou schalt bilde to me an hows to dwelle ynne?
For Y dwellide not in an hows fro the dai in which Y ledde the sones of Israel out of the lond of Egipt til in to this dai; but Y ȝede in tabernacle and
in tent, bi alle places, to whiche Y passyde with alle the sones of Israel? Whether Y spekynge spak to oon of the lynagis of Israel, to whom Y comaundyde, that he schulde feede my puple Israel, and seide, Whi bildidist thou not an hows of cedre to me?
And now thou schalt seie these thingis to my seruaunt Dauid, The Lord of oostis seith these thingis, Y took thee fro lesewis suynge flockis, that thou schuldist be duyk on my puple Israel,
and Y was with thee in alle thingis, where euere thou ȝedist, and Y killide alle thin enemyes fro thi face, and Y made to thee a greet name bi the name
of grete men that ben in erthe; and Y schall sette a place to my puple Israel, and Y schal plaunte hym, and Y schal dwelle with hym, and he schal no more be troblid, and the sones of wickidnesse schulen not adde, that thei turmente
hym as bifor, fro the dai in which Y ordenede iugis on my puple Israel; and Y schal ȝyue reste to thee fro alle thin enemyes. And the Lord biforseith to thee, that the Lord schal mak an hows to
thee; and whanne thi daies be fillid, and thou hast slept with thi fadris, Y schal reyse thi seed aftir thee, which schal go out of thi wombe, and Y schal make stidfast his rewme.
He schal bilde an hows to my name, and Y schal make stable the troone of his rewme til in to
with outen ende; Y schal be to hym in to fadir, and he schal be to me in to a sone; and if he schal do ony thing wickidli, Y schal chastise hym in the ȝerde of men, and in the woundis of the sones of men.
Forsothe Y schal not do awey my mercy fro hym, as Y dide awei fro Saul, whom Y remouede fro my face.
And thin hows schal be feithful, and thi rewme schal be til in to with outen ende bifor my face, and thi trone schal be stidfast contynueli.
By alle these wordys, and bi al this reuelacioun, so Nathan spak to Dauid.
Forsothe Dauid the kyng entride, and satt bifor the Lord, and seide, Who am Y, my Lord God, and what is myn hows, that thou brouȝtist me hidur to?
But also this is seyn litil in thi siȝt, my Lord God; no but thou schuldist speke also of the hows of thi seruaunt in to long tyme. Forsothe this is the lawe of
Adam, Lord God; what therfor may Dauid adde ȝit, that he speke to thee? For thou, Lord God, knowist thi seruaunt; thou hast do alle these grete
thingis, for thi word, and bi thin herte, so that thou madist knowun to thi seruaunt.
Herfor, Lord God, thou art magnyfied, for noon is lijk thee, ne there is no God outakun thee, in alle thingis whiche we herden with oure eeris.
Sotheli what folk in erthe is as the puple of Israel, for which the Lord God ȝede, that he schulde aȝenbie it to him in to a puple, and schulde sette to hym silf a name, and schulde do to it grete thingis, and orible on erthe, in castinge out therof the folk and goddis therof fro the face of thi puple, which thou aȝen bouȝtist to thee fro Egipt?
And thou confermidist to thee thi puple Israel in to a puple euerlastynge, and thou, Lord, art maad in to God to hem.
Now therfor, Lord God, reise thou withouten ende the word that thou hast spoke on thi seruaunt and on his hows, and do as
thou hast spoke; and thy name be magnyfied til in to withouten ende, and be it seid, The Lord of oostis is God on Israel; and the hows of thi seruaunt Dauid
schal be stablischid byfor the Lord; for thou, Lord of oostis, God of Israel, hast maad reuelacioun to the eere of thi seruaunt, and seidist, Y schal bilde an hows to thee; therfor thi seruaunt foond his herte, that he schulde preie thee bi this preier.
Now therfor, Lord God, thou art veri God, and thi wordis schulen be trewe; for thou hast spoke these goodis to thi
seruaunt; therfor bigynne thou, and blesse the hows of thi seruaunt, that it be withouten ende bifor thee; for thou, Lord God, hast spoke these thingis, and bi thi blessyng the hows of thi seruaunt schal be blessid withouten ende.
Forsothe it was doon aftir these thingis, Dauid smoot Filisteis, and made low hem; and Dauid took awei the bridil of tribute fro the hond of Filisteis.
And Dauid smoot Moab, and mat hem with a coorde, and made euene to the erthe; forsothe he mat twey cordis, oon to sle, and oon to quikene. And Moab seruyde Dauid vndur tribute.
And Dauid smoot Adadezer, sone of Roob, kyng of Soba, whanne he ȝede forth to be lord ouer the flood Eufrates.
And whanne a thousynde and seuene hundrid kniȝtis of his part weren takun, and twenti thousynde of foot men, Dauid hoxide alle drawynge beestis in charis; but Dauid lefte of tho an hundrid charis, that is, the horsis of an hundrid charis.
Also Sirie of Damask cam, that it schulde bere help to Adadezer, kyng of Soba; and Dauid smoot of Sirie two and twenti thousynde of men.
And Dauid settide strengthe in Sirie of Damask, and Sirie was maad seruynge Dauid vndur tribute. And the Lord kepte Dauid in alle thingis, to what euer thingis he ȝede forth.
And Dauid took goldun armeris and bies, whiche the seruauntis of Adadezer hadden, and he brouȝte tho in to Jerusalem.
And of Bethe, and of Beroth, citees of Adadezer, Dauith the kyng took ful myche metal; of the whiche Salomon made alle the brasen vessels in the temple, and the brasen see, and the pilers, and the auter.
Forsothe Thou, kyng of Emath, herde that Dauid hadde smyte al the strengthe of Adadezer.
And Thou sente Joram, his sone, to kyng Dauid, that he schulde grete hym, and thanke, and do thankyngis, for he hadde ouercome Adadezer, and hadde smyte hym; for Thou was enemy to Adadeser; and vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of bras weren in his hond.
And the same vessels kyng Dauid halewid to the Lord, with the siluer and gold, whiche he hadde halewid of alle hethene men, whiche hethene men he made suget
of Sirye, and Moab, and the sones of Amon, and Filisteis, and Amalech, and of the spuylis of Adadezer, sone of Roob, kyng of Soba.
Also Dauid made to hym a name, whanne he turnede aȝen, whanne Sirie was takun, for eiȝtene thousynde weren slayn in the valey, where salt is maad, and in Gebelem, to thre and twenti thousynde.
And he settide keperis in Ydumee, and ordeinede strong hold, and al Ydumee was maad seruynge to Dauid; and the Lord kepte Dauid in alle thingis, to whateuer thingis he ȝede forth.
And Dauid regnede on al Israel, and Dauid dide doom, and riȝtfulnesse to al his puple.
Forsothe Joab, the sone of Saruy, was ouer the oost; sotheli Josaphat, sone of Achilud, was chaunceler;
and Sadoch, sone of Achitob, and Achymelech, sone of Abiathar, weren preestis; and Saraye was scryuyn.
Forsothe Bananye, sone of Joiada, was ouer Cerethi and Pherethi, that is, ouer archeris and arblasteris; sotheli the sones of Dauid weren prestis
And Dauid seide, Whether ony man is, that lefte of the hows of Saul, that Y do mercy with hym for Jonathas?
Forsothe a seruaunt, Siba bi name, was of the hous of Saul; whom whanne the kyng hadde clepid to hym silf, the kyng seide to hym, Whethir thou art not Siba? And he answeride, Y am thi seruaunt.
And the kyng seide, Whether ony man lyueth of the hows of Saul, that Y do with hym the mercy of God? And Siba seide to the kyng, A sone of Jonathas lyueth, feble in the feet.
The kyng seide, Where is he? And Siba seide to the kyng, Lo! he is in the hows of Machir, sone of Amyel, in Lodabar.
Therfor Dauid the kyng sente, and took hym fro the hows of Machir, sone of Amyel, fro Lodobar.
Forsothe whanne Myphibosech, the sone of Jonathas, sone of Saul, hadde come to Dauid, he felde in to his face, and worschipide. And Dauid seide, Myphibosech! Which answeride, Y am present, thi seruaunt.
And Dauid seide to hym, Drede thou not, for Y doynge schal do mersi to thee for Jonathas, thi fadir; and Y schal restore to thee alle the feeldis of Saul, thi fadir, and thou schalt ete breed in my boord euere.
Which worschipide him, and seide, Who am Y, thi seruaunt, for thou hast biholde on a deed dogge lijk me?
Therfor the kyng clepide Siba, the child of Saul; and seide to hym, Y haue ȝoue to the sone of thi lord alle thingis, which euer weren of Saul, and al the hows of
hym; therfor worche thou the lond to hym, thou, and thi sones, and thi seruauntis, and thou schalt brynge in meetis to the sone of thi lord, that he be fed; forsothe Myphibosech, sone of thi lord, schal ete euer breed on my bord. Sotheli fiftene sones and twenti seruauntis weren to Siba.
And Siba seyde to the kyng, As thou, my lord kyng, hast comaundid to thi seruaunt, so thi seruaunt schal do; and Myphibosech, as oon of the sones of the kyng, schal ete on thi boord.
Forsothe Myphibosech hadde a litil sone, Mycha bi name; sotheli al the meyne of the hows of Siba seruyde Myphibosech.
Forsothe Myphibosech dwellide in Jerusalem; for he eet contynueli of the kingis boord, and was crokid on either foot.
Forsothe it was doon aftir these thingis, that Naas, kyng of the sones of Amon, diede; and Anoon, his sone, regnede for hym. And
Dauid seide, Y schal do mercy with Anon, the sone of Naas, as his fadir dide mercy with me. Therfor Dauid sente coumfortynge hym by hise seruauntis on the deeth of the fadir. Sotheli whanne the seruauntis of Dauid hadden come in to the
lond of the sones of Amon, princes of the sones of Amon seiden to Anon, her lord, Gessist thou that for the onour of thi fadir Dauid sente coumfortouris to thee; and not herfor David sente hise seruauntis to thee, that he schulde aspie, and enserche the citee, and distrie it?
Therfor Anoon took the seruauntis of Dauid, and schauyde half the part of the beerd of hem, and he kittide awey the myddil clothis of hem til to the buttokis; and lefte hem.
And whanne this was teld to Dauid, he sente in to the comyng of hem, for the men weren schent ful vilensly. And Dauid comaundide to hem, Dwelle ȝe in Jerico, til ȝoure beerd wexe, and thanne turne ȝe aȝen.
Sotheli the sones of Amon sien, that thei hadden do wrong to Dauid, and thei senten, and hiriden bi meede Roob of Sirye, and Soba of Sirie, twenti thousynde of foot men, and of kyng Maacha, a thousynde men, and of Istob twelue thousynde of men.
And whanne Dauid hadde herd this, he sent Joab and al the oost of fiȝteris.
Therfor the sones of Amon ȝeden out, and dressiden scheltrun bifor hem in the entryng of the ȝate. Forsothe Soba, and Roob of Sirie, and Istob, and Maacha weren asidis half in the feeld.
Therfor Joab siȝ, that batel was maad redi aȝens hym, bothe euene aȝens and bihynde the bak; and he chees to hym silf of alle the chosun men of Israel, and ordeynede scheltrun aȝens Sirus.
Forsothe he bitook to Abisai, his brothir, the tother part of the puple, which dresside scheltrun aȝens the sones of Amon.
And Joab seide, If men of Sirie han the maistrie aȝens me, thou schalt be to me in to help; sotheli if the sones of Amon han the maistrie aȝens thee, Y schal helpe
thee; be thou a strong man, and fiȝte we for oure puple, and for the citee of oure God; forsothe the Lord schal do that, that is good in his siȝt.
Therfor Joab and his puple that was with hym, bigan batel aȝens men of Sirie, whiche fledden anoon fro his face.
Forsothe the sones of Amon sien, that men of Sirie hadden fled; and thei fledden also fro the face of Abisai, and entriden in to the citee; and Joab turnede aȝen fro the sones of Amon, and cam in to Jerusalem.
Forsothe men of Sirye sien that thei hadden feld bifor Israel, and thei weren gaderid to gidere.
And Adadezer sente, and ledde out men of Sirie that weren biȝende the flood, and he brouȝte the oost of hem; sotheli Sobach, mayster of the chyualrie of Adadezer, was the prince of hem.
And whanne this was teld to Dauid, he drow togidere al Israel, and passide Jordan, and cam in to Helama. And men of Sirie dressiden scheltrun aȝens Dauid, and fouȝten aȝens hym.
And Sireis fledden fro the face of Israel; and Dauid killide of Sireis seuene hundrid charis, and fourti thousynde of knyȝtis; and he smoot Sobach, the prince of chyualrie, which was deed anoon.
Forsothe alle kyngis, that weren in the help of Adadezer, siȝen that thei weren ouercomun of Israel, and thei maden pees with Israel, and serueden hem; and Sireis dredden to ȝyue help to the sones of Amon.
Forsothe it was doon, whanne the ȝeer turnede aȝen in that tyme wherynne kyngis ben wont to go forth to batels, Dauid sente Joab, and with hym hise seruauntis, and al Israel; and thei distrieden the sones of Amon, and bisegiden Rabath; forsothe Dauid dwellide in Jerusalem.
While these thingis weren doon, it befelde, that Dauid roos in a dai fro his bed after mydday, and walkide in the soler of the kyngis hows; and he siȝ a womman waischynge hir silf euen aȝens on hir soler; sotheli the womman was ful fair.
Therfor the kyng sente, and enqueride, what womman it was; and it was teld to hym, that sche was Bersabee, the douȝtir of Heliam, and was the wijf of Vrye Ethei.
Therfor bi messangeris sent Dauid took hir; and whanne sche entride to hym, he slepte with hir, and anoon sche was halewid fro hir vnclenesse.
And sche turnede aȝen in to hir hows, with child conseyued; and sche sente, and telde to Dauid, and seide, Y haue conseyued.
Forsothe Dauid sente to Joab, and seide, Sende thou Vrye Ethei to me; and Joab sente Vrye to Dauid.
And Vrie cam to Dauid; and Dauid axide, hou riȝtfuli Joab dide and the puple, and hou the batel was mynystrid.
And Dauid seide to Vrye, Go in to thin hows, and waische thi feet. Vrye ȝede out fro the hows of the kyng, and the kyngis mete suede hym.
Sotheli Vrye slepte bifor the ȝate of the kyngis hows with othere seruauntis of his lord, and ȝede not doun to his hows.
And it was teld to Dauid of men, seiynge, Vrye ȝede not to his hows. And Dauid seide to Vrye, Whether thou camest not fro the weye? whi ȝedist thou not doun in to thin hows?
And Vrie seide to Dauid, The arke of God, Israel and Juda dwellen in tentis, and my lord Joab, and the seruauntis of my lord dwellen on the face of erthe, and schal Y go in to myn hows, to ete and drynke, and slepe with my wijf? Bi thin helthe, and bi the helthe of thi soule, Y schal not do this thing.
Therfor Dauid seide to Vrye, Dwelle thou here also to dai, and to morewe Y schal delyuere thee. Vrie dwellide in Jerusalem in that day and the tothir.
And Dauid clepide hym, that he schulde ete and drynke bifor hym, and Dauid made drunkun Vrye; and he ȝede out in the euentid, and slepte in his bed with the seruauntes of his lord; and ȝede not doun in to his hows.
Therfor the morewtid was maad, and Dauid wroot epistle to Joab, and sente bi the hond of
Vrye, and wroot in the pistle, Sette ȝe Vrye euene aȝens the batel, where the batel is strongeste, that is, where the aduersaries ben stronge, and forsake ȝe hym, that he be smitun and perische.
Therfor whanne Joab bisegide the citee, he settide Vrie in the place where he wiste that strongeste men weren.
And men ȝeden out of the citee, and fouȝten aȝens Joab, and thei killiden of the puple of seruauntis of Dauid, and also Vrye Ethei was deed.
Therfor Joab sente, and
telde alle the wordis of the batel; and he comaundyde to the messanger, and seide, Whanne thou hast fillid alle wordis of
the batel to the kyng, if thou seest, that he is wrooth, and seith, Whi neiȝiden ȝe to the wal to fiȝte? whether ȝe wisten not, that many dartis ben sent fro aboue fro
the wal? who smoot Abymelech, sone of Gerobaal? whether not a womman sente on hym a gobet of a mylnestoon fro the wal, and killide hym in Thebes? whi neiȝiden ȝe bisidis the wal? thou schalt seie, Also thi seruaunt, Vrye Ethei, diede.
Therfor the messanger ȝede, and telde to Dauid alle thingis whiche Joab hadde comaundid to hym.
And the messanger seide to Dauid, Men hadden the maistri aȝens us, and thei ȝeden out to vs in to the feeld; sotheli bi fersnesse maad we pursueden hem til to the ȝate of the citee.
And archeris senten dartis to thi seruauntis fro the wal aboue, and summe of the kyngis seruauntis ben deed; forsothe also thi seruaunt, Vrye Ethei, is deed.
And Dauid seide to the messanger, Thou schalt seie these thingis to Joab, This thing breke not thee; for the bifallyng of batel is dyuerse, and swerd wastith now this man, now that man; coumforte thi fiȝteris aȝens the citee, that thou distrye it, and excite thou hem.
Forsothe the wijf of Vrye herde, that Vrye hir hosebond was deed, and sche biweilide hym.
And whanne the morenyng was passid, Dauid sente, and brouȝte hir in to his hows; and sche was maad wijf to hym, and sche childide a sone to hym. And this word which Dauid hadde do displeside bifor the Lord.
Therfor the Lord sente Nathan to Dauid; and whanne he hadde come to Dauid, he seide to Dauid, Answere thou doom to me; twei men weren in o citee; o man was riche, and the tother was pore.
The riche man hadde ful many
scheep, and oxun; sotheli the pore man hadde vttirli no thing, outakun o litil scheep, which he hadde bouȝt, and nurschid, and which hadde wexid at hym with hise sones, and eet togidere of his breed, and drank of his cuppe, and slepte in his bosum; and it was as a douȝter to hym.
Forsothe whanne a pilgrym hadde come to the riche man, he sparide to take of hise scheep and oxun, that he schulde make a feeste to that pilgrym, that cam to hym; and he took the scheep of the pore man, and made redi metis to the man that cam to hym.
Forsothe Dauid was ful wrooth with indignacioun aȝens that man, and seide to Nathan, The Lord lyueth, for the man
that dide this is the sone of deeth; he schal ȝelde the scheep in to foure folde, for he dide this word, and sparide not.
Forsothe Nathan seide to Dauid, Thou art thilke man, that hast do this thing. The Lord God of Israel seith these thingis, Y anoyntide thee in to kyng on Israel, and Y delyuerede thee fro the
hond of Saul, and Y ȝaf to thee the hows of thi lord, and the wyues of thi lord in thi bosum, and Y ȝaf to thee the hows of Israel, and of Juda; and if these thingis ben litil, Y schal adde to thee myche grettere thingis.
Whi therfor hast thou dispisid the word of the Lord, that thou didist yuels in my siȝt? Thou hast smyte by swerd Vrye Ethei, and thou hast take his wijf in to wijf to thee, and thou hast slayn hym with the swerd of the sones of Amon.
Wherfor swerd schal not go awey fro thin hows til in to with outen ende; for thou dispysidist me, and tokist the wijf of Vrye Ethei, that sche schulde be thi wijf.
Therfor the Lord seith these thingis, Lo! Y schal reise on thee yuel of thin hows, and Y schal take thi wyues in thin iȝen, and Y schal ȝyue to thi neiȝbore, and he schal slepe with thi wyues in the iȝen of this sunne, that is, opynli bifor alle men, as in xv. chapitre.
For thou hast do priueli; forsothe Y schal do this word in the siȝt of al Israel, and in the siȝt of this sunne.
And Dauid seide to Nathan, Y haue synned to the Lord. And Nathan seide to Dauid, Also the Lord hath turned awei thi synne; thou schalt not die.
Netheles for thou madist enemyes to blasfeme the name of the Lord, for this word the child which is borun to thee schal die bi deeth.
And Nathan turnede aȝen in to his hows. And the Lord smoot the litil child, whom the wijf of Vrye childide to Dauid, and he dispeiride.
And Dauid preiede the Lord for the litil child; and Dauid fastide bi fastyng, and entride asidis half, and lai on the erthe.
Sotheli the eldere men of his hows camen, and constreyneden hym bi meke preieris, that he schulde rise fro the erthe; and he nolde, nethir he eet mete with hem.
Forsothe it bifelde in the seuenthe dai, that the ȝong child diede; and the seruauntis of Dauid dredde to telle to hym, that the litil child was deed; for thei seiden, Lo! whanne the litil child lyuede ȝit, we spaken to hym, and he herde not oure vois; hou myche more, if we seien the child is deed, he schal turment himsilf?
Therfore whanne Dauid hadde herd his seruauntis spekynge priueli, ether moterynge, he understood that the ȝong child was deed; and he seyde to his seruauntis, Whether the child is deed? Whiche answeriden to hym, He is deed.
Therfor Dauid roos fro the erthe, and was waischid, and anoyntid; and whanne he hadde chaungid cloth, he entride in to the hows of the Lord, and worschipide, and cam in to his hows; and he axide, that thei schulden sette breed to hym, and he eet.
Sothely his seruauntis seiden to hym, What is the word which thou hast do? Thou fastidist, and weptist for the ȝong child, whanne he lyuede ȝit; sotheli whanne the child was deed, thou risidist and etist breed?
And Dauid seide, Y fastide and wepte for the ȝong child, whanne he lyuyde ȝit; for Y seide, Who woot, if perauenture the Lord ȝyue hym to me, and the ȝong child lyue?
Now forsothe for he is deed, whi fast Y? whether Y schal mow aȝen clepe hym more? Y schal go more to hym, but he schal not turne aȝen to me.
And Dauid coumfortid Bersabee, his wijf; and he entride to hir, and slepte with hir. And sche gendride a sone, and Dauid clepide his name Salomon; and the Lord louyde hym.
And he sente Salomon in the hond of Nathan, the prophete; and he clepide his name Amyable to the Lord, for the Lord louyde hym.
Therfor Joab fauȝt aȝens Rabath, of the sones of Amon, and he fauȝt aȝens the kyngis citee.
And Joab sente messangeris to Dauid, and seide, Y fauȝte aȝens Rabath, and the citee of watris schal be takun.
Now therfor gadere thou the tother part of the puple, and bisege thou the citee, and take thou it, lest whanne the citee is wastid of me, the victorie be arettid to my name.
Therfor Dauid gaderide al the puple, and he ȝede forth aȝens Rabath; and whanne he hadde fouȝte, he took it.
And he took the diademe of the kyng of hem fro his heed, bi weiȝte a talent of gold, hauynge preciouseste peerlis; and it was put on the heed of Dauid, that is, aftir that it was weldid and purgid bi fier ; but also Dauid bar awey ful myche prey of the citee.
Also he ledde forth the puple therof, and sawide, and dide aboute hem yrun instrumentis of turment, and departide with knyues, and ledde ouer bi the licnesse of tijl stoonus; so he dide to alle the citees of the sones of Amon. And Dauid turnede aȝen, and al his oost, in to Jerusalem.
Forsothe it was doon aftir these thingis, that Amon, the sone of Dauid, louyde the faireste sistir, Thamar bi name, of Absolon, sone of Dauid.
And Amon perischide greetli for hir, so that he was sijk for the loue of hir. For whanne she was a virgyn, it semyde hard to hym, that he schulde do ony thing vnonestli with hir.
Forsothe a freend, Jonadab bi name, sone of Semmaa, brother of Dauid, was to Amon; Jonadab was a ful prudent man.
Which seide to Amon, Sone of the kyng, whi art thou maad feble so bi leenesse bi alle daies? whi schewist thou not to me? And Amon seide to him, Y loue Thamar, the sister of my brother Absolon.
And Jonadab answeride to hym, Li thou on thi bed, and feyne thou sikenesse; and whanne thi fadir cometh, that he visyte thee, seie thou to hym, Y preye, come Thamar, my sister, that sche ȝyue mete to me, and make a seew, that Y ete of hir hond.
Therfor Amon lay doun, and bigan as to be sijk. And whanne the kyng hadde come to visite him, Amon seide to the kyng, Y biseche, come Thamar, my sistir, that sche make twei soupyngis bifor my iȝen, and that Y take of hir hond meete maad redi.
Therfor Dauid sente to the hows of Thamar, and seide, Come thou in to the hows of Amon, thi brother, and make thou seew to hym.
And Thamar cam in to the hows of Amon, hir brother. Sotheli he lai; and sche took mele, and medlide, and made moist bifor hise iȝen,
and sethide soupyngis; and sche took that, that sche hadde sode, and helde out, and settide byfor hym, and he nolde ete. And Amon seide, Putte ȝe out alle men fro me. And whanne thei hadden put out
alle men, Amon seide to Thamar, Bere the mete in to the closet, that Y ete of thin hond. Therfor Thamar took the soupingis whiche sche hadde maad, and brouȝte in to Amon, hir brother, in the closet.
And whanne sche hadde proferid mete to hym, he took hir, and seide, Come thou, my sistir, li thou with me.
And sche answeride to hym, My brother, nyle thou, nyle thou oppresse me, for this is not leueful in Israel; nyle thou do this foli.
For Y schal not mow bere my schenschip, and thou schalt be as oon of the vnwise men in Israel; but rather speke thou to the kyng, and he schal not denye me to thee.
Sotheli he nolde assente to hir preieris; but he was strengere in myȝtis, and oppresside hir, and lay with hir.
And Amon hadde hir hateful bi ful grete haterede, so that the hatrede was gretter, bi which he hatide hir, than the loue bi which he louyde hir bifor. And Amon seide to hir, Rise thou, and go.
And sche answeride to hym, This yuel is more which thou doist now aȝens me, and puttist me out, than that, that thou didist bifore. And he nolde here hir;
but whanne the child was clepide, that mynystride to hym, he seide, Putte thou out this womman fro me, and close thou the dore aftir hir.
And sche was clothid with a coote doun to the heele; for the kyngis douȝtris virgyns vsiden siche clothis. Therfor the mynystre of Amon puttide hir out, and closide the dore aftir hir.
And sche spreynte aische to hir heed, whanne the coote to the heele was to-rent, and whanne the hondis weren put on hir heed, and sche ȝede entrynge and criynge.
Forsothe Absolon, hir brother, seide to hir, Whether Amon, thi brothir, hath leyn with thee? But now, sister, be stille; he is thi brother, and turmente not thin herte for this thing. Therfor Thamar dwellide morenynge in the hows of Absolon, hir brothir.
Forsothe whanne kyng Dauid hadde herd these wordis, he was ful sori, and he nolde make sore the spyrit of Amon, his sone; for he louyde Amon, for he was the firste gendrid to hym.
Forsothe Absolon spak not to Amon, nether yuel nether good; for Absolon hatide Amon, for he hadde defoulid Thamar, his sistir.
Forsothe it was doon aftir the tyme of twei ȝeer, that the scheep of Absolon weren shorun in Baalasor, which is bisidis Effraym. And Absolon clepide alle the sones of the kyng.
And he cam to the kyng, and seide to hym, Lo! the scheep of thi seruaunt ben schorun; Y preye, come the king with hise seruauntis to his seruaunt.
And the kyng seide to Absolon, Nyle thou, my sone, nyle thou preye, that alle we come, and greeue thee. Forsothe whanne he constreynede Dauid, and he nolde go, he blesside Absolon.
And Absolon seide to Dauid, If thou nylt come, Y byseche, come nameli Amon, my brother, with vs. And the kyng seide to hym, It is no nede, that he go with thee.
Therfor Absolon constreynede hym; and he delyuerede with him Amon, and alle the sones of the kyng. And Absolon hadde maad a feeste as the feeste of a kyng.
Sotheli Absolon comaundide to hise children, and seide, Aspie ȝe, whanne Amon is drunkun of wyn, and Y seie to ȝou, Smyte ȝe, and sle hym. Nyle ȝe drede, for Y am that comaunde to ȝou; be ȝe strengthid, and be ȝe stronge men.
Therfor the children of Absolon diden aȝens Amon, as Absolon hadde comaundide to hem; and alle the sones of the kyng risiden, and stieden ech on his mule, and fledden.
And whanne thei ȝeden ȝit in the weie, fame cam to the kyng, and seide, Absolon hath kild alle the sones of the king, and nameli not oon lefte of hem.
Therfor the kyng roos, and torente hise clothis, and felde doun on the erthe; and alle hise seruauntis that stoden nyȝ to hym, to-renten her clothis.
Sotheli Jonadab, sone of Semmaa, brother of Dauid, answeride and seide, My lord the kyng, gesse not, that alle the children, and sones of the kyng, ben slayn; Amon aloone is deed, for he was set in hatrede to Absolon, fro the day in which he oppresside Thamar, his sistir.
Now therfor, my lord the kyng, set not this word on his herte, and seie, Alle the sones of the kyng ben slayn; for Amon aloone is deed. Forsothe Absolon fledde.
And a child aspiere reiside hise iȝen, and bihelde, and lo! myche puple cam bi a weye out of the comyn weie bi the side of the hil.
And Jonadab seide to the kyng, Lo! the sones of the kyng comen; bi the word of thi seruaunt, so it is doon.
And whanne he hadde ceessid to speke, also the sones of the kyng apperiden; and thei entriden, and reisiden her vois, and wepten; but also the kyng and alle his seruauntis wepten bi ful greet wepyng.
Forsothe Absolon fledde, and ȝede to Tholmai, sone of Amyur, the kyng of Gessur. Therfor Dauid biweilide his sone Amon in many daies.
Forsothe Absolon, whanne he hadde fled, and hadde come in to Gessur, was there thre ȝeer.
And Dauid ceesside to pursue Absolon, for he was coumfortid on the deeth of Amon.
Forsothe Joab, the sone of Saruye, vndirstood, that the herte of the kyng
was turned to Absolon; and he sente to Thecua, and took fro thennus a wise womman, and he seide to hir, Feyne thee to morene, and be thou clothid with clooth of duyl, and be thou anoyntid with oile, that thou be as a womman by morenynge now in ful myche tyme a deed man.
And thou schalt entre to the kyng, and thou schalt speke to hym siche wordis. Sotheli Joab puttide the wordis in hir mouth.
Therfor whanne the womman of Thecua hadde entrid to the kyng, sche felde bifor hym on the erthe, and worschipide, and seide, A! kyng, kepe me.
And the kyng seide to hir, What hast thou of cause? And sche answeride, Alas! Y am a womman widewe, for myn
hosebonde is deed; and tweyne sones weren of thin handmayde, whiche debatiden aȝens hem silf in the feeld, and noon was that myȝte forbede hem, and oon smoot the tother, and killide hym.
And lo! al the kynrede risith aȝens thin handmayde, and seith, Ȝyue thou hym that killide his brothir, that we sle hym for the lijf of his brother whom he killide, and that we do awei the eir; and thei seken to quenche my sparcle whych is lefte, that name dwelle not to myn hosebonde, and relikis, ethir remenauntis, be not to him on erthe.
And the kyng seide to the womman, Go in to thin hows, and Y schal comaunde for thee.
And the womman of Thecua seide to the kyng, My lord the kyng, this wickidnesse be on me, and on the hows of my fadir; forsothe the kyng and his trone be innocent.
And the kyng seide, Brynge thou hym to me, that aȝenseith thee, and he schal no more adde that he touche thee.
And sche seide, The kyng haue mynde on his Lord God, and the nexte men of blood to take veniaunce be not multiplied, and thei schulen not sle my sone. And the kyng seide, The Lord lyueth, for noon of the heeris of thi sone schal falle on the erthe.
Therfor the womman seide, Thin handmayde speke a word to my lord the kyng. And the kyng seide, Speke thou.
And the womman seide, Whi thouȝtist thou sich a thing aȝens the puple of God? and the kyng spak this word, that he do synne, and brynge not aȝen his sone cast out?
Alle we dyen, and as watris that schulen not turne aȝen, we sliden in to erthe; and God nyl that a soule perische, but he withdrawith, and thenkith lest he perische outirly, which is cast awey.
Now therfor come thou, that Y speke to my lord the kyng this word, while the puple is present; and thin handmaide seide, Y schal speke to the kyng, if in ony maner the kyng do the word of his handmayde.
And the kyng herde the wordis, that he schulde delyuere his handmayde fro the hondis of alle men, that wolden do awei me, and my sone togidere, fro the eritage of the Lord.
Therfor thin hand mayde seie, that the word of my lord the kyng be maad as sacrifice, that is, that the sentence ȝouun of hym be plesaunt to God, as sacrifice plesith God; for as an aungel of the Lord, so is my lord the kyng, that he be not mouyd bi blessyng nether bi cursyng. Wherfor and thi Lord God is with thee.
And the kyng answeride, and seide to the womman, Hide thou not fro me the word which Y axe thee. And the womman seide to hym, Speke thou, my lord the kyng.
And the kyng seide, Whether the hond of Joab is with thee in alle these thingis? The womman answeride, and seide, Bi the helthe of thi soule, my lord the kyng, nether to the left side nether to the riȝt side is ony thing of alle these thingis, whiche my lord the kyng spak. For thi seruaunt Joab hym silf comaundide to me, and he puttide alle these wordis in to the
mouth of thin handmaide, that Y schulde turne the figure of this word; for thi seruaunt Joab comaundide this thing. Forsothe thou, my lord the kyng, art wijs, as an aungel of God hath wisdom, that thou vnderstonde alle thingis on erthe.
And the kyng seide to Joab, Lo! Y am plesid, and Y haue do thi word; therfor go thou, and aȝen clepe thou the child Absolon.
And Joab felde on his face to erthe, and worschipide, and blesside the kyng; and Joab seide, Thi seruaunt hath vndirstonde to dai, that Y foond grace in thin iȝen, my lord the kyng, for thou hast do the word of thi seruaunt.
Therfor Joab roos, and ȝede in to Gessur, and brouȝte Absolon in to Jerusalem.
Forsothe the kyng seide, Turne he aȝen in to his hows, and se not he my face.
Therfor Absolon turnede aȝen in to his hows, and siȝ not the face of the kyng. Sotheli no man in al Israel was so fair as Absolon, and ful comeli; fro the step of the foot til to the top, no
wem was in hym; and in as myche as he clippide more the heeris, bi so myche thei wexiden more; forsothe he was clippid onys in the ȝeer, for the heer greuede him. And whanne he clippide the heeris, he weiȝide the heeris of his heed bi twei hundrid siclis with comyn weiȝte.
Forsothe thre sones, and a douȝter, Thamar bi name, of excellent forme weren borun to Absolon.
And Absolon dwellide in Jerusalem twei ȝeer, and he siȝ not the face of the kyng.
Therfor he sente to Joab, that he schulde sende hym to the kyng; which Joab nolde come to hym. And whanne he hadde sent the secounde tyme, and Joab nolde
come, Absolon seide to hise seruauntis, Ȝe knowen the feeld of Joab bisidis my feeld hauynge ripe barli; therfor go ȝe, and brenne ȝe it with fier. Therfor the seruauntis of Absolon brenten the corn with fier. And the seruauntis of Joab camen with her clothis to-rent, and seiden, The seruauntis of Absolon han brent the part of
feeld bi fier. And Joab roos, and cam to Absolon in to his hows, and seide, Whi
han thi seruauntis brent my corn bi fier? And Absolon answeride to Joab, Y sente to thee, and bisouȝte that thou schuldist come to me, and that Y schulde sende thee to the kyng, that thou schuldist seie to hym, Whi cam Y fro Gessur? It was betere to me to be there; therfor Y biseche, that Y se the face of the kyng, that if he is myndeful of my wickidnesse, sle he me.
Joab entride to the kyng, and telde to hym. And Absolon was clepid, and entryde to the kyng, and worschipide on the face of erthe bifor hym, and the kyng kisside Absolon.
Therfor aftir these thingis Absolon made a chaar to hym, and knyȝtis, and fifti men, that schulden go bifor hym.
And Absolon roos eerli, and stood bisidis the entryng of the ȝate in the weie; and Absolon clepide to hym ech man, that hadde a cause that he schulde come to the doom of the kyng, and Absolon seide, Of what citee art thou? Which answeride, and seide, Of o lynage of Israel Y am, thi seruaunt.
And Absolon answeride to hym, Thi wordis semen to me good and iust, but noon is ordeyned of the kyng to here thee. And Absolon seide,
Who schal ordeyne me iuge on the lond, that alle men that han cause come to me, and Y deme iustly?
But whanne a man cam to Absolon to greete hym, he helde forth the hond, and took, and kisside that
man; and Absolon dide this to al Israel, that cam to doom to be herd of the kyng; and Absolon drow awei the hertis of men of Israel.
Forsothe aftir foure ȝeer Absolon seide to kyng Dauid, Y schal go, and Y schal ȝelde my vowis, whiche Y
vowide to the Lord in Ebron; for thi seruaunt vowynge vowide, whanne he was in Gessur of Sirie, and seide, If the Lord bryngith aȝen me in to Jerusalem, Y schal make sacrifice to the Lord.
And the kyng seide to hym, Go thou in pees. And Absolon roos, and ȝede in to Ebron.
Forsothe Absolon sente aspieris in to al the lynage of Israel, and seide, Anoon as ȝe heren the sown of clarioun, seye ȝe, Absolon schal regne in Ebron.
Forsothe twei hundrid men clepid of Jerusalem ȝeden with Absolon, and ȝede with symple herte, and outirli thei knewen not the cause.
Also Absolon clepide Achitofel of Gilo, the councelour of Dauid, fro his citee Gilo. And whanne he offride sacrifices a strong swerynge togidere was maad, and the puple rennynge togidere was encreessid with Absolon.
Therfor a messanger cam to Dauid, and seide, With al herte al Israel sueth Absolon.
And Dauid seide to hise seruauntis that weren with hym in Jerusalem, Rise ȝe, and flee we; for noon ascaping schal be to us fro the face of Absolon; therfor haste ȝe to go out, lest he come, and ocupie vs, and fille on vs fallynge, and smyte the citee bi the scharpnesse of swerd.
And the seruauntis of the kyng seiden to hym, We thi seruauntis schulen performe gladli alle thingis, what euer thingis oure lord the kyng schal comaunde.
Therfor the kyng ȝede out, and al his hous, on her feet; and the king lefte ten wymmen concubyns, that is, secundarie wyues, to kepe the hous.
And the king ȝede out, and al Israel, on her feet, and the kyng stood fer fro the hous.
And alle hise seruauntis ȝeden bisidis him, and the legiouns of Cerethi and of Ferethi, and alle men of Geth strong fiȝters, sixe hundrid men, that sueden him fro Geth, ȝeden on foote bifor the kyng.
Forsothe the kyng seide to Ethai of Geth, Whi comest thou with vs? Turne thou aȝen, and dwelle with the kyng, for thou art a pilgrym, and thou ȝedist out fro thi place.
Thou camest ȝistirdai, and to dai thou art compellid to go out with vs. Sotheli Y schal go, whidur Y schal go; turne aȝen, and lede aȝen thi britheren with thee, and the Lord do mercy and treuthe with thee, for thou schewidist grace and feith.
And Ethai answeride to the kyng, and seide, The Lord lyueth, and my lord the kyng lyueth, for in what euer place thou schalt be, my lord the kyng, ether in deeth ethir in lijf, there thi seruaunt schal be.
And Dauid seide to Ethay, Come thou, and passe. And Ethai of Geth passide, and the kyng, and alle men that weren with hym, and the tother multitude.
And alle men wepten with greet vois, and al the puple passide; and the kyng ȝede ouer the strond of Cedron, and al the puple ȝede aȝens the weie of the olyue tree, that biholdith to deseert.
Forsothe and Sadoch the preest cam, and alle the dekenes with hym, and thei baren the arke of boond of pees of God, and thei diden doun the arke of God; and Abiathar stiede, til al the puple was passid that ȝede out of the citee.
And the kyng seide to Sadoch, Bere aȝen the arke of God in to the citee; if Y schal fynde grace in the iȝen of the Lord, he schal lede me aȝen, and he schal schewe to me that arke and his tabernacle.
Sotheli if the Lord seith, Thou plesist not me; Y am redi, do he that, that is good bifor hym silf.
And the kyng seide to Sadoch, preest, A! thou seere, that is, profete, turne aȝen in to the citee, with pees; and Achymaas, thi sone, and Jonathas, the sone of Abiathar, ȝoure twei sones, be with ȝou.
Lo! Y schal be hid in the feeldi places of deseert, til word come fro ȝou, and schewe to me.
Therfor Sadoch and Abiathar baren aȝen the arke of God in to Jerusalem, and dwelliden there.
Forsothe Dauid stiede on the hil of olyue trees, stiynge and wepynge, with the heed hilyd, and goynge with nakid feet; but also al the puple that was with hym, stiede with the heed hilid, and wepte.
Forsothe it was teld to Dauid, that Achitofel was in the sweryng togidere with Absolon; and Dauid seide, Lord, Y byseche, make thou fonned the counsel of Achitofel.
And whanne Dauid stiede in to the hiȝenesse of the hil, in which he schulde worschipe the Lord, lo! Cusi of Arath, with the cloth to-rent, and with the heed ful of erthe, cam to hym.
And Dauid seide to hym, If thou comest with me, thou schalt be to me to charge;
sotheli if thou turnest aȝen in to the citee, and seist to Absolon, Y am thi seruaunt, kyng, suffre thou me to lyue; as Y was the seruaunt of thi fadir, so Y schal be thi seruaunt; thou schalt distrye the counsel of Achitofel.
Forsothe thou hast with thee Sadoch and Abiathar, preestis; and thou schalt schewe ech word, what euer word thou schalt here in the hows of the kyng, to Sadoch and Abiathar, preestis.
Sotheli twei sones of hem ben with hem, Achymaas, sone of Sadoch, and Jonathan, sone of Abiathar; and ȝe schulen sende bi hem to me ech word which ȝe schulen here.
Therfor whanne Chusi, freend of Dauid, cam in to the citee, also Absolon entryde in to Jerusalem.
And whanne Dauid hadde passid a litil the cop of the hil, Siba, the child of Mysphobosech, apperide in to his comyng, with tweyne assis, that weren chargid with twei hundrid looues, and with an hundrid bundels of dried grapis, and with an hundrid gobetis of pressid figus, and with twei vessels of wyn.
And the kyng seide to Siba, What wolen these thingis to hem silf? And Siba answeride, My lord the kyng, the assis ben to the meyneals of the kyng, that thei sitte; the looues and figis pressid ben to thi children to ete; forsothe the wyn is, that if ony man faile in deseert, he drynke.
And the kyng seide, Where is the sone of thi lord? And Siba answeride to the kyng, He dwellide in Jerusalem, and seide, To dai the Lord of the hows of Israel schal restore to me the rewme of my fadir.
And the kyng seide to Siba, Alle thingis that weren of Mysphibosech ben thine. And Siba seide, Y preye, fynde Y grace bifor thee, my lord the kyng.
Therfor kyng Dauid cam til to Bahurym, and lo! a man of the meynee of the hows of Saul, Semey bi name, sone of Gera, ȝede out fro thennus; he ȝede forth goynge out, and curside.
And he sente stoonys aȝens Dauid, and aȝens alle seruauntis of kyng Dauid; forsothe al the puple, and alle fiȝteris ȝeden at the riȝtside and at the left side of the king.
Sotheli Semey spak so, whanne he curside the kyng, Go out, go out, thou man of bloodis, and man of Belial!
The Lord hath ȝolde to thee al the blood of the hows of Saul, for thou rauyschedist the rewme fro hym; and the Lord ȝaf the rewme in to the hond of Absolon, thi sone; and lo! thin yuels oppressen thee, for thou art a man of blodis.
Forsothe Abisay, the sone of Saruye, seide to the kyng, Whi cursith this dogge, that schal die, my lord the kyng? Y schal go, and Y schal girde of his heed.
And the kyng seide, Ȝe sones of Saruye, what is to me and to ȝou? Suffre ye hym, that he curse; for the Lord comaundide to hym, that he schulde curse Dauid; and who is he that dare seie, Whi dide he so?
And the kyng seide to Abysay, and to alle hise seruauntis, Lo! my sone, that ȝede out of my wombe, sekith my lijf; hou myche more now this sone of Gemyny? Suffre ȝe hym, that he curse bi comaundement
of the Lord; if in hap the Lord biholde my turmentyng, and ȝelde good to me for this cursyng of this dai.
Therfor Dauid ȝede, and hise felowis, bi the weie with hym; forsothe Semey ȝede bi the slade of the hil bi the side aȝens hym; and curside, and sente stoonus aȝens him, and spreynte erthe.
And so Dauid the king cam, and al the puple weery with hym, and thei weren refreischid there.
Forsothe Absolon, and al the puple of Israel entriden in to Jerusalem, but also Achitofel with hym.
Sotheli whanne Chusi of Arath, the frend of Dauid, hadde come to Absolon, he spak to Absolon,
Heil, kyng! heil, kyng! To whom Absolon seide, This is thi grace to thi freend; whi ȝedist thou not with thi freend?
And Chusi answeride to Absolon, Nay, for Y shal be seruaunt of hym, whom the Lord hath chose, and al this puple, and al Israel; and Y schal dwelle with him.
But that Y seie also this, to whom schal Y serue? whethir not to the sone of the kyng? as Y obeiede to thi fadir, so Y schal obeie to thee.
Forsothe Absolon seide to Achitofel, Take ȝe counsel, what we owen to do.
And Achytofel seide to Absolon, Entre thou to the concubyns of thi fadir, whiche he lefte to kepe the hows; that whanne al Israel herith, that thou hast defoulid thi fadir, the hondis of hem be strengthid with thee.
Therfor thei tildeden Absolon a tabernacle in the soler, and he entride to the concubyns of his fadir bifor al Israel.
Sotheli the counsel of Achitofel, which he ȝaf in tho daies, was as if a man counselide God; so was al the counsel of Achitofel, bothe whanne he was with Dauid, and whanne he was with Absolon.
Therfor Achitofel seide to Absolon, Y schal chese twelue thousynde of men to me, and Y schal rise, and pursue Dauid in this nyȝt.
And Y schal falle on hym, for he is wery, and with vnboundun hondis Y schal smyte hym. And whanne al the puple fleeth which is with hym, Y schal smyte the kyng desolat, ether left aloone.
And Y schal lede aȝen al the puple, as o man is wont to turne aȝen; for thou sekist o man, and al the puple schal be in pees.
And the word of him plesyde Absolon, and alle the grete men in birthe of Israel.
Forsothe Absolon seide, Clepe ȝe also Chusy of Arath, and here we what also he seith. And whanne Chusi hadde
come to Absolon, Absolon seide to hym, Achitofel spak siche a word; owen we do, ethir nay? what counsel ȝyuest thou?
And Chusi seide to Absolon, This is not good counsel, which Achitofel ȝaf in this tyme.
And eft Chusi seide, Thou knowist, that thi fadir, and the men that ben with him, ben moost stronge, and in bitter soule, as if a femal bere is fers in the forest, whanne the whelpis ben rauyschid; but also thi fader is a man werriour, and he schal not dwelle with the puple.
In hap now he is hid in the dichis, ethir in o place, in which he wole; and whanne ony man fallith in the bigynnyng, who euer schal here, he schal here, and schal seie, Wounde is maad in the puple that suede Absolon.
And ech strongeste man, whos herte is as the herte of a lioun, schal be discoumfortid for drede; for al the puple of Israel knowith, that thi fadir is strong, and that alle men ben stronge, that ben with him.
But this semeth to me to be riȝtful counsel; al Israel be gaderid to thee, fro Dan til to Bersabee, vnnoumbrable as the soond of the see; and thou schalt be in the myddis of hem.
And we schulen falle on hym, in what euer place he is foundun, and we schulen hile hym, as dew is wont to falle on the erthe; and we schulen not leeue of the men that ben with hym, sotheli not oon.
That if he entrith in to ony citee, al Israel schal cumpasse that citee with roopis, and we schulen drawe it in to the stronde, that no thing be foundun, sotheli not a litil stoon therof.
And Absolon seide, and alle the men of Israel, The counsel of Chusi of Arath is betere than the counsel of Achitofel; sotheli the profitable counsel of Achitofel was destried bi Goddis wille, that the Lord schulde brynge in yuel on Absolon.
And Chusi seide to Sadoch and to Abiathar, preestis, Achitofel ȝaf counsel to Absolon, and to the eldere men of Israel in this and this maner, and Y ȝaf sich and sich counsel.
Now therfor sende ȝe soone, and telle ȝe to Dauid, and seie ȝe, Dwelle thou not this nyȝt in the feeldi places of deseert, but passe thou with out delay; lest perauenture the kyng be destried, and al the puple which is with hym.
Forsothe Jonathas and Achymaas stoden bisidis the welle of Rogel; an handmaide ȝede, and telde to hem, and thei ȝeden forth to telle the message to kyng Dauid; for thei myȝten not be seyn, nether entre in to the citee.
Forsothe a child siȝ hem, and he schewide to Absolon; sotheli thei entriden with swift goyng in to the hows of sum man in Bahurym, that hadde a pit in his place, and thei ȝeden doun in to that pit.
Forsothe a womman took, and spred abrood an hilyng of the mouth of the pit as driynge barli with the pile takun a wey, and so the thing was hid.
And whanne the seruauntis of Absolon hadde come in to the hows, thei seiden to the womman, Where is Achymaas and Jonathas? And the womman answeride to hem, Thei passiden hastily, whanne watir was tastid a litil. And whanne thei that souȝten hem hadden not founde, thei turneden aȝen in to Jerusalem.
And whanne thei that souȝten hadden go, thei stieden fro the pit; and thei ȝeden, and telden to kyng Dauid, and seiden, Rise ȝe, passe ȝe soone the flood, for Achitofel ȝaf sich counsel aȝens ȝou.
