Forsothe Zamri gendride Moosa, and Moosa gendride Banaa, whos sone was Raphaia, of whom was gendrid Elesa, that gendride Asel.
Sotheli Asel hadde sixe sones bi these names, Esricham, Bochru, Ismael, Saria, Abadia, Aman; alle these weren the sones of Asel.
Forsothe the sones of Asa, his brothir, weren Vlam, the firste gendride sone, and Hus, the secounde, and Eliphales, the thridde.
And the sones of Vlam weren strongeste men, and beendynge a bouwe with greet strength, and hauynge many sones, and sones of sones, til to an hundrid and fifti. Alle these weren the sones of Beniamyn.
Therfor al Israel was noumbrid, and the summe of hem was writun in the book of kyngis of Israel and of Juda; and thei weren translatid in to Babiloyne for her synne.
Sotheli thei that dwelliden first in her citees, and in the possessiouns of Israel, and the preestis, and the dekenes, and Natyneys, dwelliden in Jerusalem.
Of the sones of Juda, and of the sones of Beniamyn, also of the sones of Effraym,
and of Manasses; Othi, the sone of Amyud, sone of Semry, sone of Omroy, sone of Bonny, of the sones of Phares, the sone
of Juda; and of Sylom, Asia, the firste
gendrid, and his sones; sotheli of the sones of Zaray, Heuel, and hise britheren; sixe hundrid fourescore and ten.
Forsothe of the sones of Beniamyn; Salo, the sone of Mosollam, the sones of Odoia, the
sones of Asana, and Jobanya, the sone of Jerobam, and Ela, the sone of Ozi, the sones of Mochozi, and Mosollam, the sone of Saphacie, sone of Rahuel, sone of Jebanye,
and the britheren of hem, bi her meynees; nyne hundrid sixe and fifti. Alle these weren princes of her kynredis by the housis of her fadris.
Forsothe of the
preestis, Joiada, Jozarib, and Jachym; and Azarie, the sone of Helchie, sone of Mosollam, sone of Sadoch, sone of Maraioth, sone of Achitob, was bischop of the hows of the Lord.
Forsothe Adaias, sone of Jeroam, sone of Phasor, sone of Melchia, and Masaia, sone of Adihel, sone of Jezra, sone of Mosollam, sone of Mosselamoth,
sone of Emyner, also her britheren, prynces bi her meynees, weren a thousynde seuene hundrid and fourescoore, men strongeste in bodili myȝt, to make the werk of seruyce in the hows of the Lord.
Forsothe of dekenes, Semeya, the sone of Assub, sone of Ezricam, sone of Asebyn,
of the sones of Merary; also Balthasar the carpenter, and Galebeth, and Machama, sone of Mycha, sone of Zechri,
sone of Asaph, and Obdias, sone of Semey, sone of Calaal, sone of Idithum, and Barachie, the sone of Asa, sone of Helcana, that dwellide in the porchis of Methophati.
Sotheli the porteris weren Sellum, and Achub, and Thelmon, and Achyman, and the britheren of hem; Sellum was the
prince; til to that tyme thei kepten bi her whilis in the ȝate of the kyng at the eest, of the sones of Leuy.
Sellum forsothe, the sone of Chore, sone of Abiasaph, sone of Chore, with hise britheren, and with the hows of his fadir; these ben the sones of Chore on the werkis of the seruyce, keperis of the porchis of the tabernacle, and the meynees of hem kepten bi whilis the entryng of the castelis of the Lord.
Forsothe Phynees, the sone of Eleazar, was the duyk of hem bifor the Lord.
Sotheli Zacarie, the sone of Mosollam, was porter of the ȝate of the tabernacle of witnessyng.
Alle these chosun in to porteris bi ȝatis weren twei hundrid and twelue, and weren discryued in her owne townes, which dekenes Dauid and Samuel, the prophete, ordeyneden in her
feith, both hem and the sones of hem in the doris of the hows of the Lord, and in the tabernacle of witnessyng, bi her whiles.
Porteris weren bi foure coostis, that is, at the eest, and at the west, and at the north, and at the south.
Forsothe her britheren dwelliden in townes, and camen in her sabatis fro tyme til to tyme.
Al the noumbre of porteris was bitakun to these foure dekenes, and thei kepten the chaumbris, and the tresours of the hows of the Lord.
Also thei dwelliden in her kepyngis bi the cumpas of the temple of the Lord, that whanne tyme were, thei schulden opene the ȝatis eerli.
Men of her kyn weren also on the vessels of seruyce; for the vessels weren borun in at noumbre, and weren borun out of hem.
And thei that hadden the vesselis of seyntuarie bitakun to her kepyng, weren souereyns on flour, and wyn, and oile, and encense, and swete smellinge spyceries.
Sotheli the sones of preestis maden oynementis of swete smellynge spiceries.
And Mathatias dekene, the firste gendrid sone of Sellum of the kynrede of Chore, was the souereyn of alle thingis that weren fried in the friyng panne.
Sotheli men of the sones of Caath, the britheren of hem, weren on the looues of settyng forth, that thei schulden make redi euere newe looues bi ech sabat.
These ben the princis of chauntouris bi the meynees of Leuytis, that dwelliden in chaumbris, so that thei schulden serue contynueli dai and nyȝt in her seruyce.
The heedis of Leuitis bi her meynees, the princes, dwelliden in Jerusalem.
Forsothe there dwelliden in Gabaon; Jaiel, the fadir of Gabaon,
and the name of his wijf Maacha; Abdon, his firste gendrid sone, and Sur, and Cys,
and Baal, and Ner, and Nadab, and Gedor, and Ahaio, and Zacharie, and Macelloth;
forsothe Macelloth gendride Semmaa; these dwelliden euene aȝens her britheren in Jerusalem, with her britheren.
Sotheli Ner gendride Cys, and Cys gendride Saul, and Saul gendride Jonathan, and Melchisue, and Abynadab, and Hisbaal. Forsothe the sone of Jonathan was Myribaal,
and Myribaal gendride Mycha.
Sotheli the sones of Micha weren Phiton, and Malech, and Thara; forsothe Aaz
gendride Jara, and Jara gendride Alamath, and Azmoth, and Zamri; and Zamri gendride Moosa, sotheli Moosa
gendride Baana, whose sone Raphaia gendride Elisa, of whom Esel was gendrid.
Forsothe Esel hadde sixe sones bi these names, Ezricam, Bochru, Hismael, Saria, Obdia, Anan; these weren the sones of Hesel.
Forsothe Filisteis fouȝten aȝens Israel, and the sones of Israel fledden Palestyns, and felden doun woundid in the hil of Gelboe.
And whanne Filisteis hadde neiȝed pursuynge Saul and hise sones, thei killiden Jonathan, and Abynadab, and Melchisue, the sones of Saul.
And the batel was agreggid aȝens Saul; and men archeris foundun hym, and woundiden hym with dartis.
And Saul seide to his squiere, Drawe out thi swerd, and sle me, leste these vncircumcidid men come, and scorne me. Sothli his squyer was aferd bi drede, and nolde do this; therfor Saul took a swerd, and felde on it.
And whanne his squyer hadde seyn this, that is, that Saul was deed, he felde also on his swerd, and was deed.
Therfor Saul perischide, and hise thre sones, and al his hows felde doun togidere.
And whanne the men of Israel, that dwelliden in feeldi places, hadden seyn this, thei fledden; and whanne Saul and hise sones weren deed, thei forsoken her citees, and weren scaterid hidur and thidur; and Filisteis camen, and dwelliden in tho.
Therfor in the tother day Filisteis drowen awei the spuylis of slayn men, and founden Saul and hise sones liggynge in the hil of Gelboe.
And whanne thei hadden spuylid hym, and hadden gird of the heed, and hadden maad hym nakid of armeris, thei senten in to her lond, that it schulde be borun aboute, and schulde be schewid in the
templis of idols and to puplis; forsothe thei halewiden his armeris in the temple of her god, and thei settiden the heed in the temple of Dagon.
Whanne men of Jabes of Galad hadden herd this, that is, alle thingis whiche the Filisteis diden on
Saul, alle stronge men risiden togidere, and took the deed bodies of Saul and of hise sones, and brouȝten tho in to Jabes; and thei birieden the boonus of hem vndur an ook, that was in Jabes; and thei fastiden seuene daies.
Therfor Saul was deed for hise wickidnessis, for he brak the comaundement of the Lord, whiche he comaundide, and kepte not it, but ferthirmore also he took counsel at a womman hauynge a feend spekynge in the wombe,
and he hopide not in the Lord; for which thing both the Lord killide hym, and translatide his rewme to Dauid, sone of Ysay.
Therfor al Israel was gaderid to Dauid in Ebron, and seide, We ben thi boon and
thi fleisch; also ȝisterdai and the thridde dai ago, whanne Saul regnede ȝit on Israel, thou it were that leddist out and leddist in Israel; for thi Lord God seide to thee, Thou schalt fede my puple Israel, and thou schalt be prince on it.
Therfor alle the gretter in birthe of Israel camen to the kyng in Ebron; and Dauid maad with hem a boond of pees bifor the Lord, and thei anoyntiden hym kyng on Israel, bi the word of the Lord, which he spak in the hond of Samuel.
Therfor Dauid ȝede, and al Israel, in to Jerusalem; this Jerusalem is Jebus, where Jebuseis enhabiteris of the lond weren.
And thei that dwelliden at Jebus seiden to Dauid, Thou schalt not entre hidur. Forsothe Dauid took the hiȝ tour of Syon, which is the
citee of Dauid; and he seide, Ech man that sleeth first Jebusei, schal be prince and duyk. Therfor Joab, sone of Saruye, stiede first, and was maad prince.
Sotheli Dauid dwellide in the hiȝ tour, and therfor it was clepid the cytee of Dauid;
and he bildide the citee in cumpas fro Mello til to the cumpas; forsothe Joab bildide the tother part of the citee.
And Dauid profitide goynge and wexynge, and the Lord of oostis was with hym.
These ben the princes of the stronge men of Dauid, that helpiden hym, that he schulde be kyng on al Israel, bi the word of the Lord which he spak to Israel.
And this is the noumbre of the stronge men of Dauid; Jesbaam, the sone of Achamony, was prince among thretti; this reiside his schaft ethir spere on thre hundrid woundid men in o tyme.
And after hym was Eleazar, the sone of his fadris brothir, and was a man of Ahoit, which Eleazar was among thre miȝti men.
This was with Dauid in Aphesdomyn, whanne Filisteis weren gaderid to o place in to batel; and a feeld of that cuntrey was ful of barli, and the puple fledde fro the face of Filisteis.
This Eleazar stood in the myddis of the feeld, and defendide it; and whanne he hadde slayn Filisteis, the Lord ȝaf greet helthe to his puple.
Sotheli thre of thritti princes ȝeden doun to the stoon, wher ynne Dauid was, to the denne of Odolla, whanne Filisteis settiden tentis in the valey of Raphaym.
Forsothe Dauid was in a strong hold, and the stacioun, that is, the oost gaderid, of Filisteis was in Bethleem.
Therfor Dauid desiride watir, and seide, Y wolde, that sum man ȝaf to me water of the cisterne of Bethleem, which is in the ȝate.
Therfor these thre ȝeden thoruȝ the myddil of the castelis of Filisteis, and drowen watir of the cisterne of Bethleem, that was in the ȝate, and thei brouȝten to Dauid, that he schulde drynke; and Dauid nolde drynke it, but rather he offride it to the
Lord, and seide, Fer be it, that Y do this thing in the siȝt of my God, and that Y drynke the blood of these men, for in the perel of her lyues thei brouȝten watir to me; and for this cause he nolde drynke. Thre strongeste men diden these thingis.
Also Abisai, the brother of Joab, he was the prince of thre men, and he reiside his schaft aȝens thre hundrid woundid men; and he was moost named among
thre, among the secounde thre he was noble, and the prince of hem; netheles he cam not til to the firste thre.
Banaye, the sone of Joiada, strongest man of Capsael, that dide many werkis; he killide two stronge men of Moab; and he ȝede doun, and killide a lioun in the myddil of a cisterne,
in the tyme of snow; and he killide a man of Egipt, whos stature was of fyue cubitis, and he hadde a spere as the beem of webbis; therfor Banaye ȝede doun to hym with a ȝerde, and rauyschide the spere, which he held in the hond, and killide hym with his owne spere.
Banaye, the sone of Joiada, dide these thingis, that was moost named among thre stronge
men, and was the firste among thretti; netheles he cam not til to the thre; sotheli Dauid settide hym at his eere.
Forsothe the strongeste men in the oost weren Asael, the brother of Joab, and Eleanan, the sone of his fadris brothir of

Also these camen to Dauid in Sichelech, whanne he fledde ȝit fro Saul, the sone of Cys; whiche weren strongeste men and
noble fiȝterys, beendynge bouwe, and castynge stoonys with slyngis with euer either hond, and dressynge arowis; of the britheren
of Saul of Beniamyn, the prince Achieser, and Joas, the sones of Samaa of Gabaath, and Jazachel, and Phallech, the sones of Azmod, and Barachie, and Jehu
of Anathot; also Samay of Gabaon was the strongeste among thretti and aboue thretti; Jeremy, and Jezihel, and Johannan,

But also of Gaddi strongeste men, and beste fiȝteris, holdynge scheld and spere, fledden ouer to Dauid, whanne he was hid in deseert; the faces of hem as the face of a lioun, and thei weren swift as capretis in hillis.
Ozer was the prince, Obdias the secounde,
Eliab the thridde, Masmana the fourthe,
Jeremye the fyuethe, Becchi the sixte,
Heliel the seuenthe, Johannan the eiȝthe,
Helzedad the nynthe, Jeremye the tenthe,
Bachana the euleuenthe; these of the sones of Gad weren princes of the oost; the laste was souereyn ouer an hundrid knyȝtis, and the moost was souereyn ouer a thousynde.
These it ben that passiden ouer Jordan in the firste monethe, whanne it was wont to flowe ouer hise brynkis; and thei dryueden awei alle men that dwelliden in the valeis at the eest coost and west coost.
Sotheli also men of Beniamyn and of Juda camen to the stronge hoold, whereyn Dauid dwellide.
And Dauid ȝede out aȝens hem, and seide, If ȝe ben comyn pesible to me, for to helpe me, myn herte be ioyned to ȝou; forsothe if ȝe setten aspies to me for myn aduersaries, sithen Y haue not wickidnesse in the hondis, God of our fadris se and deme.
Forsothe the spirit clothide Amasay, the prynce among thritti, and he seide, A! Dauid, we ben thin, and thou, sone of Ysai, we schulen be with thee; pees, pees to thee, and pees to thin helperis, for thi Lord God helpith thee. Therfor Dauid resseyuede hem, and made princes of the cumpeny.
Forsothe men of Manasses fledden ouer to Dauid, whanne he cam with Filisteis to fiȝte aȝens Saul, and he fauȝte not with hem, for after that the princes of Filisteis hadden take counsel, thei senten hym aȝen, and seiden, With perel of oure heed he schal turne aȝen to Saul his lord.
Therfor whanne Dauid turnede aȝen in to Sichelech, men of Manasses fledden ouer to hym, Eduas, and Jozabad, Jedihel, and Mychael, and Naas, and Jozabath, and Helyu, and Salathi, princes of knyȝtis in Manasses.
These men ȝauen help to Dauid aȝens theues; for alle weren strongeste men, and thei weren maad prynces in the oost.
But also bi ech dai men camen to Dauid, for to helpe hym, til that the noumbre was maad greet as the oost of God.
Also this is the noumbre of princes of the oost that camen to Dauid, whanne he was in Ebron, that thei schulden translate the rewme of Saul to hym, bi the word of the Lord;
the sones of Juda, berynge scheeld and spere, sixe thousynde and eiȝte hundrid,
redi to batel; of the sones of Simeon, seuene thousinde and an hundrid, of strongeste
men to fiȝte; of the sones of Leuy,
foure thousynde and sixe hundrid; also Joiada, prince of the generacioun of Aaron, and thre thousynd and seuene hundrid
with hym; also Sadoch, a child of noble wit, and the hows of his fadir, twei and
twenti princes; forsothe of the sones of Beniamyn, britheren of Saul, thre thousynde; for a greet part of hem suede ȝit
the hows of Saul; forsothe of the sones of Effraym, twenti thousynde and eiȝte hundrid, strongeste men in bodili myȝt,
men named in her meynees; and of the half part of the lynage of Manasses, eiȝtene thousynde; alle camen bi her names, to
make Dauid kyng; also of the sones of Ysacar, two hundrid princes, lernd men, that knewen ech tyme to comaunde what the puple of Israel ouȝt to do; sotheli al the residue lynage suede the counseils of
hem; forsothe of Zabulon camen fifti thousynde in to helpe, not in double herte, which ȝeden out to batel, and stoden in the scheltrun, and weren maad redi with
armuris of batel; and of Neptalym a thousynde prynces, and with hem camen seuene and thritti thousynde men, arayed
with scheeld and speere; also of Dan, eiȝte and twenti thousynde and sixe hundrid
men, maad redi to batel; and of Aser fourti thousynde men, goynge out to batel, and stirynge to batel in the scheltrun.
Forsothe biȝende Jordan, of the sones of Ruben, and of Gad, and of the half part of the lynage of Manasses, sixe scoore thousynde men, araied with armuris of batel.
Alle these men werriouris and redi to batel camen with perfit herte in to Ebron, to make Dauid kyng on al Israel; but also alle the residue of Israel weren of oon herte, that Dauid schulde be maad king on al Israel.
And thei weren ther at Dauid thre daies, and eten and drunken; for her britheren hadden maad redi to
hem; but also thei that weren niȝ hem, til to Isacar and Zabulon and Neptalym, brouȝten looues on assis, and camelis, and mulis, and oxis, for to ete; mele, bundelis of pressid figis, dried grapis, wyn, oile, oxis and wetheres, to al plentee; for ioy was in Israel.
Forsothe Dauid took counsel with tribunes, and centuriouns, and alle princes;
and seide to alle the cumpeny of the sones of Israel, If it plesith ȝou, and if the word which Y speke goith out fro oure Lord God, sende we to oure residue britheren to alle the cuntrees of Israel, and to preestis and dekenes that dwellen in the subarbis of citees, that thei be gaderid to
vs, and that we brynge aȝen to vs the arke of oure God; for we souȝten not it in the daies of Saul.
And al the multitude answeride, that it schulde be don so; for the word pleside al the puple.
Therfor Dauid gaderide togidere al Israel, fro Sior of Egipt til thou entre in to Emath, that he schulde brynge the arke of God fro Cariathiarim.
And Dauid stiede, and alle the men of Israel, to the hil of Cariathiarym, which is in Juda, that he schulde brynge fro thennus the arke of the Lord God sittynge on cherubyn, where his name was clepid.
And thei puttiden the arke of the Lord God on a newe wayn fro the hous of Amynadab; forsothe Oza and hise britheren driueden the wayn.
Forsothe Dauid and al Israel pleieden bifor the Lord, with al miȝt, in songis, and in harpis, and sautries, and tympans, and cymbalis, and trumpis.
Forsothe whanne thei hadden come to the cornfloor of Chidon, Oza strechide forth his hond to susteyne the arke; for the oxe wexynge wielde hadde bowid it a litil.
Therfor the Lord was wrooth aȝens Oza, and smoot hym, for he hadde touchide the ark; and he was deed there bifor the Lord.
And Dauid was sori, for the Lord hadde departid Oza; and he clepide that place The Departyng of Oza til in to present dai.
And Dauid dredde the Lord in that tyme, and seide, How may Y brynge in to me the arke of the Lord?
And for this cause he brouȝte not it to hym, that is, in to the citee of Dauid, but he turnede it in to the hows of Obededom of Geth.
Therfor the arke of God dwellide in the hous of Obededom of Geth thre monethis; and the Lord blessid his hows, and alle thingis that he hadde.
And Iram, the kyng of Tyre, sente messageris to Dauid, and he sente trees of cedre, and werk men of wallis and of trees, that thei schulden bilde to hym an hows.
And Dauid knewe that the Lord hadde confermyd hym in to kyng on Israel; and that his rewme was reisid on his puple Israel.
And Dauid took othere wyues in Jerusalem, and gendride sones and douȝtris.
And these ben the names of hem that weren borun to hym in Jerusalem; Sammu, and Sobab, Nathan, and
Salomon, Jeber, and Elisu, and Heli, and
Eliphalech, and Noga, and Napheg, and
Japhie, and Elisama, and Baliada, and Eliphelech.
Forsothe the Filisteis herden that Dauid was anoyntid in to kyng on al Israel, and alle stieden to seke Dauid. And whanne Dauid hadde herd this thing, he ȝede out aȝens hem.
Forsothe Filisteis camen, and weren spred abrood in the
valey of Raphaym; and Dauid counselide the Lord, and seide, Whether Y schal stie to Filisteis? and whether thou schalt bitake hem in to myn hondis? And the Lord seide to hym, Stie thou, and Y schal bitake hem in thin hond.
And whanne thei hadden styed in to Baal Pharasym, Dauid smoot hem there, and seide, God hath departid myn enemyes bi myn hond, as watris ben departid. And therfor the name of that place was clepid Baal Pharasym;
and thei leften there her goddis, which Dauid comaundide to be brent.
Forsothe another tyme Filisteis felden in, and
weren spred abrood in the valei; and eft Dauid counseilide the Lord, and the Lord seide to hym, Thou schalt not stie aftir hem; go awei fro hem, and thou schalt come aȝens hem euen aȝens the pere trees.
And whanne thou schalt here the sowun of a goere in the cop of the pere trees, thanne thou schalt go out to batel; for the Lord is go out byfor thee, to smyte the castels of Filisteis.
Therfor Dauid dide as God comaundide to hym, and he smoot the castels of Filisteis fro Gabaon til to Gazara.
And the name of Dauid was puplischid in alle cuntreis, and the Lord ȝaf his drede on alle folkis.
And he made to hym housis in the citee of Dauid, and he bildide a place to the arke of the Lord, and araiede a tabernacle to it.
Thanne Dauid seide, It is vnleueful, that the arke of God be borun of ony thing no but of the dekenes, whiche the Lord chees to bere it, and for to mynystre to hym til in to with outen ende.
And he gaderide togidere al Israel in to Jerusalem, that the arke of God schulde be brouȝt in to his place, which
he hadde maad redy to it; also and he gaderide togidere the sones of Aaron,
and the dekenes; of the sones of Caath Vriel was prince, and hise britheren two
hundrid and twenti; of the sones of Merari Asaya was prince, and hise britheren
two hundrid and thritti; of the sones of Gerson the prince was Johel, and hise
britheren an hundrid and thretti; of the sones of Elisaphan Semei was prynce,
and hise britheren two hundrid; of the sones of Ebroun Heliel was prince, and
hise britheren foure score; of the sones of Oziel Amynadab was prince, and hise britheren an hundrid and twelue.
And Dauid clepide Sadoch and Abiathar preestis, and the dekenes Vriel, Asaie, Johel, Semeie, Eliel, and Amynadab;
and seide to hem, Ȝe that ben princes of the meynees of Leuy, be halewid with ȝoure britheren, and brynge ȝe the arke of the Lord God of Israel to the place, which
is maad redi to it; lest, as at the bigynnyng, for ȝe weren not present, the Lord smoot vs, and now it be don, if we don ony vnleueful thing
Therfor the preestis and dekenes weren halewid, that thei schulden bere the arke of the Lord God of Israel.
And the sones of Leuy token the arke of God with barris on her schuldris, as Moises comaundide bi the word of the Lord.
And Dauid seide to the princes of dekenes, that thei schulden ordeyne of her britheren syngeris in orguns of musikis, that is, in giternes, and harpis, and symbalis; that the sown of gladnesse schulde sowne an hiȝ.
And thei ordeyneden dekenes, Heman, the sone of Johel, and of hise britheren, Asaph, the sone of Barachie; sotheli of the sones of Merary, britheren of hem, thei ordeyneden
Ethan, the sone of Casaye, and the britheren of hem with hem; in the secunde ordre thei ordeyneden Zacarie, and Ben, and Jazihel, and Semyramoth, and Jahiel, and Am, Heliab, and Benaye, and Maasie, and Mathathie, and Eliphalu, and Mathenye, and Obededon, and Jehiel, porteris;
forsothe thei ordeyneden the syngeris Eman, Asaph, and Ethan, sownynge
in brasun cymbalis; sotheli Zacarie, and Oziel, and Semyramoth, and Jahihel, and Ham, and Eliab, and Maasie, and Banaie, sungun pryuetees in giternes;
forsothe Mathathie, and Eliphalu, and Mathenye, and Obededom, and Jehiel, and Ozazym, sungen in harpis for the eiȝtithe, and epynychion, that is,
victorie be to God ouercomere; forsothe Chinonye, the prince of dekenes, and of profecie, was souereyn to biforsynge melodie,
for he was ful wijs; and Barachie, and Elchana, weren porters of the arke;
forsothe Sebenye, and Josaphath, and Mathanael, and Amasaye, and Zacarie, and Banaye, and Eliezer, preestis, sowneden with trumpis bifor the arke of the Lord; and Obededom, and Achymaas, weren porteris of the arke.
Therfor Dauid, and the grettere men in birthe of Israel, and the tribunes, ȝeden to brynge the arke of boond of pees of the Lord fro the hows of Obededom with gladnesse.
And whanne God hadde helpid the dekenes that baren the arke of boond of pees of the Lord, seuene bolis and seuene rammes weren offrid.
Forsothe Dauid was clothid with a white stole, and alle the dekenes that baren the arke, and the syngeris, and Chononye, the prince of profecie among syngeris, weren clothid in white stolis; forsothe also Dauid was clothid with a lynun surplijs.
And al Israel ledden forth the arke of boond of pees of the Lord, and sowneden in ioiful song, and in sown of clariouns, and in trumpis, and cymbalis, and giternis, and harpis.
And whanne the arke of boond of pees of the Lord hadde come to the citee of Dauid, Mychol, the douȝtir of Saul, bihelde forth bi a wyndowe, and sche siȝ king Dauyd daunsynge and pleiynge; and sche dispiside hym in hir herte.
Therfor thei brouȝten the arke of God, and settiden it in the myddis of the tabernacle, that Dauid hadde araied therto; and thei offriden brent sacrifices and pesible sacrifices bifor the Lord.
And whanne Dauid offrynge brent sacrifices and pesible sacrifices hadde fillid, he blesside the puple
in the name of the Lord; and departide to alle to ech bi hym silf fro a man til to a womman o cake of breed, and a part of rostid fleisch of a bugle, and flour fried in oile.
And he ordeynede bifor the arke of the Lord, of the Leuytis, that schulden mynystre, and haue mynde of the werkis of the Lord, and glorifie and
preyse the Lord God of Israel; he ordeynede Asaph the prince, and Zacharie his secounde; forsothe he ordeynede Jahiel, and Semiramoth, and Jahel, and Mathathie, and Eliab, and Banaye, and Obededom, and Jehiel, on the orguns, on the sautrie, and on the harpis; but he ordeynede
Asaph to sowne with cymbalis; sotheli he ordeynede Banaye and Aziel, preestis, bifor the arke of the boond of pees of the Lord, for to trumpe contynueli.
In that dai Dauid made Asaph prince, and hise britheren, for to knowleche to the Lord.
Knowleche ȝe to the Lord, and inwardli clepe ȝe his name; make ȝe hise fyndyngis knowun among puplis.
Synge ȝe to hym, and seie ȝe salm to hym, and telle ȝe alle his merueylis.
Preise ȝe his hooli name; the herte of men sekynge the Lord be glad.
Seke ȝe the Lord and his vertu; seke ȝe euere his face.
Haue ȝe mynde of hise merueilis whiche he dide; of his signes, and of the domes of his mouth.
The seed of Israel, his seruaunt, preise thou God; the sones of Jacob, his chosun, preise ȝe God.
He is oure Lord God; hise domes ben in ech lond.
Haue ȝe mynde with outen ende of his couenaunt; of the word whiche he couenauntide in to a thousynde generaciouns.
Which word he couenauntide with Abraham; and of his ooth to Ysaac.
And he ordeynede that to Jacob in to a comaundement; and to Israel in to euerlastynge couenaunt.
And seide, To thee Y schal ȝyue the lond of Canaan; the part of ȝoure erytage.
Whanne thei weren fewe in noumbre; litle, and pilgrims therof.
And thei passiden fro folk in to the folk; and fro a rewme to another puple.
He suffride not ony man falseli chalenge hem; but he blamyde kyngis for hem.
Nyle ȝe touche my cristis; and nyle ȝe do wickidli aȝens my prophetis.
Al erthe, singe ȝe to the Lord; telle ȝe fro dai into dai his helthe.
Telle ȝe among hethen men his glorie; hise merueylis among alle puplis.
For the Lord is greet, and worthi to be preisid ful myche; and he is orible, ethir griseful, ouer alle goddis.
For alle the goddis of puplis ben idols; but the Lord made heuenes.
Knoulechyng and greet doyng ben bifor hym; strengthe and ioy ben in the place of hym.
Ȝe meynees of puplis, bringe ȝe to the Lord; brynge ȝe to the Lord glorie and empire.
Ȝyue ȝe glorie to his name, reise ȝe sacrifice, and come ȝe in his siȝt; and worschipe ȝe the Lord in hooli fairnesse.
Al erthe be mouyd fro his face; for he foundide the world vnmouable.
Heuenes be glad, and the erthe ioy fulli; and seie thei among naciouns, The Lord schal regne.
The see thundre, and his fulnesse; the feeldis fulli ioye, and alle thingis that ben in tho.
Thanne the trees of the forest schulen preyse bifor the Lord; for he cometh to deme the erthe.
Knouleche ȝe to the Lord, for he is good; for his mersi is withouten ende.
And seie ȝe, Thou God oure sauyour, saue vs, and gadere vs, and delyuere vs fro hethen men; that we knowleche to thin hooli name, and be fulli glade in thi songis.
Blessid be the Lord God of Israel fro with oute bigynnyng and til in to with outen ende; and al the puple seie, Amen, and seie heriyng to God.
Therfor Dauid lefte there, bifor the arke of boond of pees of the Lord, Asaph and hise britheren, for to mynystre in the siȝt of the arke contynueli bi alle daies and her whilis.
Forsothe he ordeynede porteris, Obededom and hise britheren, eiȝte and sixti, and Obededom, the sone of Idithum, and Oza.
Sotheli he ordeynede Sadoch preest, and hise britheren, preestis bifor the tabernacle of the Lord, in the hiȝ
place that was in Gabaon, for to offre brent sacrifices to the Lord on the auter of brent sacrifice contynueli, in the morwetid and euentid, bi alle thingis that ben writun in the lawe of the Lord, which he comaundide to Israel.
And aftir hym Dauyd ordeynede Eman, and Idithum, and other chosene, ech man bi his name, for to knowleche to the Lord; for his mercy is withouten ende.
Also he ordeynede Eman, and Idithum, trumpynge, and schakynge cymbalis, and alle orguns of musikis, for to synge to God; forsothe he made the sones of Idithum to be portours, ether bereris.
And al the puple turnede aȝen in to her hows, and Dauid turnede aȝen, to blesse also his hows.
Forsothe whanne Dauid dwellide in his hows, he seide to Nathan, the prophete, Lo! Y dwelle in an hows of cedris; sotheli the arke of boond of pees of the Lord is vndur skynnys.
And Nathan seide to Dauid, Do thou alle thingis that ben in thin herte, for God is with thee.
Therfor in that nyȝt the word of the Lord
was maad to Nathan, and seide, Go thou, and speke to Dauid, my seruaunt, The Lord seith these thingis, Thou schalt not
bilde to me an hows to dwelle in; for Y dwellide not in an hows, fro that tyme in which Y ledde Israel out of the lond of Egipt til to this dai, but euere Y chaungide places of tabernacle, and dwellide in a tente with al Israel.
Where I spak nameli to oon of the iugis of Israel, to which I comaundide that thei schulde fede my puple, and seide, Whi bildidist thou not to me an hous of cedre?
Now therfor thou schalt speke thus to my seruaunt Dauid, The Lord of oostis seith these thingis, Y took thee, whanne thou suedist the floc in the lesewis, that thou schuldist be duyk on my
puple Israel; and Y was with thee whidur euere thou ȝedist, and Y killide alle thin enemyes bifor thee, and Y made to thee an name as of oon of the grete men that ben maad worschipful, ether famouse, in erthe.
And Y ȝaf a place to my puple Israel; it schal be plauntid, and schal dwelle there ynne, and it schal no more be moued, and the sones of wickydnesse schulen not
defoule hem, as fro the bigynnyng, fro the daies in whiche Y ȝaf iugis to my puple Israel; and Y made lowe alle thin enemyes. Therfor Y telle to thee, that the Lord schal bilde an hows to thee.
And whanne thou hast fillid thi daies, that thou go to thi fadris, Y schal reise thi seed after thee, that schal be of thi sones,
and Y schal stablische his rewme; he schal bilde to me an hows, and Y schal make stidefast his seete til in to with outen ende.
Y schal be to hym in to a fadir, and he schal be to me in to a sone; and Y schal not do my mersi fro hym, as Y took awei fro hym that was bifore
thee; and Y schal ordeyne hym in myn hows and in my rewme til in to with outen ende; and his trone schal be moost stidefast with outen ende.
Bi alle these wordis, and bi al this reuelacioun, so Nathan spak to Dauid.
And whanne kyng Dauid hadde come, and hadde sete bifore the Lord, he seide, Lord God, who am Y, and what is myn hows, that thou schuldist ȝyue siche thingis to me?
But also this is seyn litil in thi siȝt, and therfor thou spakest on the hows of thi seruaunt, ȝhe, in to tyme to comynge; and hast maad me worthi to be biholdun ouer alle men.
My Lord God, what may Dauid adde more, sithen thou hast so glorified thi seruaunt, and hast knowe hym?
Lord, for thi seruaunt thou hast do bi thin herte al this grete doyng, and woldist that alle grete thingis be knowun.
Lord, noon is lijk thee, and noon other God is with oute thee, of alle whiche we herden with oure eeris.
For who is anothir as thi puple Israel, o folc in erthe, to whom God ȝede, to delyuere and make a puple to hym silf, and to caste out bi his greetnesse and dredis naciouns fro the face therof, which he delyuerede fro Egipt?
And thou hast set thi puple Israel in to a puple to thee til in to with outen ende, and thou, Lord, art maad the God therof.
Now therfor, Lord, the word which thou hast spoke to thi seruaunt, and on his hows, be confermed with outen ende, and do, as thou
spake; and thi name dwelle, and be magnefied with outen ende; and be it seid, The Lord of oostis is God of Israel, and the hous of Dauid, his seruaunt, dwellynge bifor hym.
For thou, my Lord God, hast maad reuelacioun to the eere of thi seruaunt, that thou woldist bilde to hym an hous; and therfor thi seruaunt foond trist, that he preie bifor thee.
Now therfor, Lord, thou art God, and hast spoke
to thi seruaunt so grete benefices; and thou hast bigunne to blesse the hous of thi seruaunt, that it be euer bifore thee; for, Lord, for thou blessist, it schal be blessid with outen ende.
Forsothe it was doon aftir these thingis, that Dauid smoot Filisteis, and made hem lowe, and took awey Geth and vilagis
therof fro the hond of Filisteis; and that he smoot Moab; and Moabitis weren maad seruauntis of Dauid, and brouȝten ȝiftis to hym.
In that tyme Dauid smoot also Adadezer, kyng of Soba, of the cuntrey of Emath, whanne he ȝede for to alarge his empire til to the flood Eufrates.
Therfor Dauid took a thousynde foure horsid cartis of his, and seuene thousynde of horsmen, and twenti thousynde of foot men; and he hoxide alle the horsis of charis, outakun an hundrid foure horsid cartis, whiche he kepte to hym silf.
Forsothe also Sirus of Damask cam aboue, to ȝyue help to Adadezer, kyng of Soba, but Dauid smoot also of hise two and
twenti thousynde of men; and he settide kniȝtis in Damask, that Sirie also schulde serue hym, and brynge ȝiftis. And the Lord helpide hym in alle thingis to whiche he ȝede.
And Dauid took goldun arowe caasis, whiche the seruauntis of Adadezer hadden, and he brouȝte tho in
to Jerusalem; also and of Thebath and of Chum, the citees of Adadezer, he took ful myche of bras, wherof Salomon made the brasun see, that is, waischynge vessel, and pileris, and brasun vessels.
And whanne Thou, kyng of Emath, hadde herd this thing, that is, that Dauid hadde smyte al the oost of Adadezer,
kyng of Soba, he sente Aduram, his sone, to Dauid the kyng, for to axe of hym pees, and for to thanke hym, for he hadde ouercome and hadde smyte Adadezer; for whi king Adadezer was aduersarie of Thou.
But also kyng Dauid halewide to the Lord alle the vessels of gold, and of siluer, and of bras; and the siluer, and the gold, which the kyng hadde take of alle folkis, as wel of Idumee and Moab, and of the sones of Amon, as of Filisteis and Amalech.
Forsothe Abisai, the sone of Saruye, smoot Edom in the valei of salt pittis, ten and eiȝte thousynde.
And he settide strong hold in Edom, that Ydumei schulde serue Dauid. And the Lord sauide Dauid in alle thingis, to whiche he ȝede.
Therfor Dauid regnede on al Israel, and dide doom and riȝtwisnesse to al his puple.
Forsothe Joab, the sone of Saruye, was on the oost; and Josaphat, the sone
of Ayluth, was chaunceler; forsothe Sadoch, the sone of Achitob, and Achymalech, the sone of Abyathar, weren preestis;
and Susa was scribe; and Banaye, the sone of Joiada, was on the legiouns Cerethi and Phelethi; sotheli the sones of Dauid weren the firste at the hond of the kyng.
Forsothe it bifelde, that Naas, kyng of the sones of Amon, diede, and his sone regnyde for him.
And Dauid seide, Y schal do mercy with Anoon, the sone of Naas; for his fadir ȝaf merci to me. And Dauid sente messageris, to coumforte hym on the deeth of his fadir. And whanne thei weren comen in to the lond of the sones
of Amon, for to coumforte Anon, the princes of the sones of Amon seiden to Anon, In hap thou gessist, that Dauid for cause of onour in to thi fadir sente men, that schulden coumforte thee; and thou perseyuest not, that hise seruauntis ben comen to thee to aspie, and enquere, and seche thi lond.
Therfor Anoon made ballid and schauyde the children of Dauid, and kittide the cootis of hem fro the buttokis of hem til to the feet; and lefte hem.
And whanne thei hadden go, and hadden sent this to Dauid, he sente in to the meting of hem; for thei hadden suffrid greet dispit; and he comaundide, that thei schulden dwelle in Gerico, til her berde wexide, and thanne thei schulden turne aȝen.
Forsothe the sones of Amon sien, that thei hadden do wrong to Dauid, bothe Anoon and the tother puple, and thei senten a thousynde talentis of siluer, for to hire to hem charis and horsmen of Mesopotanye and Sirie, of Maacha and
of Soba; and thei hiriden to hem two and thretti thousynde of charis, and the kyng of Maacha with his puple. And whanne thei weren comen, thei settiden tentis euene aȝens Medaba; and the sones of Amon weren gaderid fro her citees, and camen to batel.
And whanne Dauid hadde herd this, he sente Joab, and al the oost of stronge men.
And the sones of Amon ȝeden out, and dressiden scheltrun bisidis the ȝate of the citee; but the kyngis, that weren comen to helpe, stoden asidis half in the feeld.
Therfor Joab vndurstood, that batel was maad aȝens hym euene aȝens and bihynde the bak, and he chees the strongeste men of al Israel,
and ȝede aȝens Sirus; sotheli he ȝaf the residue part of the puple vnder the hond of Abisai, his brother; and thei ȝeden aȝens the sones of Amon.
And Joab seide, If Sirus schal ouercome me, thou schalt helpe me; sotheli if the sones of Amon schulen ouercome thee, Y schal helpe thee;
be thou coumfortid, and do we manli for oure puple, and for the citees of oure God; forsothe the Lord do that, that is good in his siȝt.
Therfor Joab ȝede, and the puple that was with hym, aȝens Sirus to batel, and he droof hem awei.
Sotheli the sones of Amon sien, that Sirus hadde fled, and thei fledden fro Abisay, his brother, and entriden in to the citee; and Joab turnede aȝen in to Jerusalem.
Forsothe Sirus siȝ, that he felde doun bifor Israel, and he sente messageris, and brouȝte Sirus, that was biȝende the flood; sotheli Sophath, the prynce of chyualrie of Adadezer, was the duyk of hem.
And whanne this was teld to Dauid, he gaderide al Israel, and passide Jordan; and he felde in on hem, and dresside scheltrun euene aȝens hem, fiȝtynge aȝenward.
Forsothe Sirus fledde fro Israel, and Dauid killide of men of Sirie seuene thousynde of charis, and fourti thousynde of foot men, and Sophath, the prince of the oost.
Sotheli the seruauntis of Adadezer siȝen, that thei weren ouercomun of Israel, and thei fledden ouer to Dauid, and seruiden hym; and Sirie wolde no more ȝyue helpe to the sones of Amon.
Forsothe it was doon after the ende of a ȝeer, in that tyme wherinne kyngis ben wont to go forth to batels, Joab gederide the oost, and the strengthe of chyualrie, and he wastide the lond of the sones of Amon, and ȝede, and bisegide Rabath; forsothe Dauid dwellide in Jerusalem, whanne Joab smoot Rabath, and distriede it.
Forsothe Dauid took the coroun of Melchon fro his heed, and foond therynne the weiȝt of gold a talent, and moost precious iemmes, and he made therof a diademe to hym silf; also he took ful many spuylis of the citee.
Sotheli he ledde out the puple that was therynne, and made breris, ethir instrumentis bi whiche cornes ben brokun, and sleddis, and irone charis, to passe on hem, so that alle men weren kit in to dyuerse partis, and weren al to-brokun; Dauid dide thus to alle the cytees of the sones of Amon, and turnede aȝen with al his puple in to Jerusalem.
Aftir these thingis a batel was maad in Gazer aȝens Filisteis, wherynne Sobochai Vsachites slow Saphai of the kyn of Raphym, and mekide hem.
Also another batel was don aȝens Filisteis, in which a man ȝouun of God, the sone of forest, a man of Bethleem, killide Goliath of Geth, the brother of giauntis, of whos schaft the tre was as the beem of webbis.
But also another batel bifelde in Geth, in which a ful long man was, hauynge sixe fyngris, that is, togidere foure and twenti, and he was gendrid of the
generacioun of Raphaym; he blasfemyde Israel, and Jonathan, the sone of Samaa, brother of Dauid, killide hym. These ben the sones of Raphaym in Geth, that felden doun in the hond of Dauid and of hise seruauntis.
stiride Dauid for to noumbre Israel.
And Dauid seide to Joab, and to the princes of the puple, Go ȝe, and noumbre Israel fro Bersabe til to Dan, and brynge ȝe the noumbre to me, that Y wite.
And Joab answeride, The Lord encresse his puple an hundrid fold more than thei ben; my lord the kyng, whether alle ben not thi seruauntis? Whi sekith my lord this thing, that schal be arettid in to synne to Israel?
But the word of the kyng hadde more the maistrie; and Joab ȝede out, and cumpasside al Israel, and turnede aȝen in to Jerusalem.
And he ȝaf to Dauid the noumbre of hem, which he hadde cumpassid; and al the noumbre of Israel was foundun a thousynde thousande, and an hundrid thousynde of men, drawynge out swerd; forsothe of Juda weren thre hundrid thousynde, and seuenti thousynde of werriouris.
For Joab noumbride not Leuy and Beniamyn, for aȝens his wille he dide the comaundement of the kyng.
Forsothe that that was comaundid displeside the Lord, and he smoot Israel.
And Dauid seide to God, Y synnede greetli that Y wolde do this; Y biseche, do thou awey the wickidnesse of thi seruaunt, for Y dide folili.
And the Lord spak to Gad, the
profete of Dauid, and seide, Go thou, and speke to Dauid, and seie to him, The Lord seith these thingis, Y ȝeue to thee the chesyng of thre thingis; chese thou oon which thou wolt, that Y do to thee.
And whanne Gad was comen to Dauid, he seide to Dauid, The Lord seith these thingis, Chese thou that that thou wolt,
ether pestilence thre ȝeer, ether that thre monethis thou fle thin enemyes and mow not ascape her swerd, ether that the swerd of the Lord and deeth regne thre daies in the lond, and that the aungel of the Lord slee in alle the coostis of Israel. Now therfor se thou, what Y schal answere to hym that sente me.
And Dauid seide to Gad, Angwischis oppresse me on ech part, but it is betere to me, that Y falle in to the hondis of the Lord, for his merciful doynges ben manye, than in to the hondis of men.
Therfor the Lord sente pestilence in to Israel, and seuenti thousynde of men felden doun of Israel.
Also he sente an aungel in to Jerusalem, that he schulde smyte it; and whanne it was smytun, the Lord siȝ, and hadde merci on the greetnesse of yuel; and comaundide to the aungel that smoot, It suffisith, now thin hond ceesse. Forsothe the aungel of the Lord stood bisidis the cornfloor of Ornam Jebusey.
And Dauid reiside hise iȝen, and siȝ the aungel of the Lord stondynge bitwixe heuene and erthe, and a drawun swerd in his hond, and turnede aȝens Jerusalem. And bothe he and the grettere men in birthe weren clothid with heiris, and felden doun lowe on the erthe.
And Dauid seide to the Lord, Whether Y am not that comaundide that the puple schulde be noumbrid? Y it am that synnede, Y it am that dide yuel; what disseruid this floc? My Lord God, Y biseche, thin hond be turned in to me, and in to the hows of my fadir; but thi puple be not smytun.
Forsothe an aungel of the Lord comaundide Gad, that he schulde seie to Dauid, that he schulde stie, and bilde an auter to the Lord God in the cornfloor of Ornam Jebusei.
Therfor Dauid stiede bi the word of Gad, which he spak to hym bi the word of the Lord.
Forsothe whanne Ornam hadde biholde, and hadde seyn the aungel, and hise foure sones with hym hadde seyn, thei hidden hem, for in that tyme he threischide whete in the cornfloor.
Therfor whanne Dauid cam to Ornam, Ornam bihelde Dauid, and ȝede forth fro the cornfloor aȝens hym, and worschipide hym, lowli on the ground.
And Dauid seide to hym, Ȝyue the place of thi cornfloor to me, that Y bilde ther ynne an auter to the Lord; so that thou take as myche siluer as it is worth, and that the veniaunce ceesse fro the puple.
Forsothe Ornam seide to Dauid, Take thou, and my lord the kyng do what euer thing plesith hym; but also Y ȝyue oxis in to brent sacrifice, and instrumentis of tree, wherbi cornes ben throischun, in to trees, and wheete in to sacrifice; Y ȝyue alle thingis wilfully.
And Dauid the kyng seide to hym, It schal not be don so, but Y schal ȝyue siluer as myche as it is worth; for Y owe not take awei fro thee, and offre so to the Lord brent sacrifices freli ȝouun.
Therfor Dauid ȝaf to Ornam for the place sixe hundrid siclis of gold of most iust weiȝte.
And he bildide there an auter to the Lord, and he offride brent sacrifice and pesible sacrifices, and he inwardli clepide God; and God herde hym in fier fro heuene on the auter of brent sacrifice.
And the Lord comaundide to the aungel, and he turnede his swerd in to the schethe.
Therfor anoon Dauid siȝ, that the Lord hadde herd hym in the corn floor of Ornam Jebusey, and he offride there slayn sacrifices.
Forsothe the tabernacle of the Lord, that Moyses hadde maad in the deseert, and the auter of brent sacrifices, was in that tempest in the hiȝ place of Gabaon; and Dauid
myȝte not go to the auter, to biseche God there, for he was aferd bi ful greet drede, seynge the swerd of the aungel of the Lord.
And Dauid seide, This is the hows of God, and this auter is in to brent sacrifice of Israel.
And he comaundide that alle conuersis fro hethenesse to the lawe of Israel schulden be gaderid of the lond of Israel; and he ordeynede of hem masouns for to kytte stoonys and for to polische, that the hows of the Lord
schulde be bildid; also Dauid made redy ful myche yrun to the nailes of the ȝatis, and to the medlyngis and ioyntouris,
and vnnoumbrable weiȝte of bras; also the trees of cedre myȝten not be gessid, whiche the men of Sidonye and the men of Tyre brouȝten to Dauid.
And Dauid seide, Salomon, my sone, is a litil child and delicat; sotheli the hows, which Y wole be bildid to the Lord, owith to be sich, that it be named in alle cuntrees; therfor Y schal make redi necessaries to hym. And for this cause Dauid bifor his deeth made redi alle costis.
And he clepide Salomon, his sone, and comaundide to hym, that he schulde bilde an hows to the Lord God of Israel.
And Dauid seide to Salomon, My sone, it was my wille to bilde an hows to the name of my Lord
God; but the word of the Lord was made to me, and seide, Thou hast sched out myche blood, and thou hast fouȝt ful many batels; thou mayst not bilde an hows to my name, for thou hast sched out so
myche blood bifor me; the sone that schal be borun to thee, schal be a man most pesible, for Y schal make hym to haue reste of alle hise enemyes bi cumpas, and for this cause he schal be clepid pesible, and Y schal ȝyue pees and reste in Israel in alle hise daies.
He schal bilde an hows to my name; he schal be to me in to a sone, and Y schal be to hym in to a fadir, and Y schal make stidefast the seete of his rewme on Israel withouten ende.
Now therfor, my sone, the Lord be with thee, and haue thou prosperite, and bilde thou an hows to thi Lord God, as he spak of thee.
And the Lord ȝyue to thee prudence and wit, that thou mow gouerne Israel, and kepe the lawe of thi Lord God.
For thanne thou maist profite, if thou kepist the comaundementis and domes, whiche the Lord comaundide to Moises, that he schulde teche Israel; be thou coumfortid, and do manli, drede thou not with outforth, nether drede thou with ynne.
Lo! in my pouert Y haue maad redi the costis of the hows of the Lord; an hundrid thousinde talentis of gold, and a thousynde thousynde talentis of siluer; sotheli of bras and irun is no weiȝte, for the noumbre is ouercomun bi greetnesse; Y haue maad redi trees and stoonys to alle costis.
Also thou hast ful many crafti men, masouns, and leggeris of stonys, and crafti men of trees, and of
alle craftis, most prudent to make werk, in gold, and siluer, and bras, and in yrun, of which is no noumbre; therfor rise thou, and make, and the Lord schal be with thee.
Also Dauid comaundide to alle the princis of Israel, that thei schulden
helpe Salomon, his sone, and seide, Ȝe seen, that ȝoure Lord God is with ȝou, and hath ȝoue to ȝou reste by cumpas, and hath bitake alle enemyes in ȝoure hoond, and the erthe is suget bifor the Lord, and bifor his puple.
Therfor ȝyue ȝoure hertis and ȝoure soulis, that ȝe seke ȝoure Lord God; and rise ȝe togidere, and bilde ȝe a seyntuarie to ȝoure Lord God, that the arke of boond of pees of the Lord be brouȝt in, and that vessels halewid to the Lord be brouȝt in to the hows, which is bildid to the name of the Lord.
Therfor Dauid was eld and ful of daies, and ordeynede Salomon, his sone, kyng on Israel.
And he gaderide togidere alle the princes of Israel, and the preestis, and
dekenes; and the dekenes weren noumbrid fro twenti ȝeer and aboue, and eiȝte and thretti thousynde of men weren foundun.
And foure and twenty thousynde men weren chosun of hem, and weren departid in to the seruyce of the hows of the Lord; sotheli of souereyns,
and iugis, sixe thousynde; forsothe foure thousynde porteris weren, and so many syngeris, syngynge to the Lord in orguns, whiche Dauid hadde maad for to synge.
And Dauid departide hem bi the whilis of the sones of Leuy, that is, of Gerson, and of Caath, and Merary.
And the sones of Gerson weren Leedan and Semeye.
The sones of Leedan weren thre, the prince Jehiel, and Ethan, and Johel.
The sones of Semei weren thre, Salamyth, and Oziel, and Aram; these weren the princes of the meynees of Leedan.
Forsothe the sones of Semeye weren Leeth, and Ziza, and Yaus, and Baria, these foure weren the sones of Semei.
Sotheli Leeth was the formere, and Ziza the secounde; forsothe Yaus and Baria hadden not ful many sones, and therfor thei weren rikenyd in o meynee and oon hows.
The sones of Caath weren foure, Amram, and Ysaac, Ebron, and Oziel.
The sones of Amram weren Aaron and Moyses; and Aaron was departid, that he schulde mynystre in the hooli thing of hooli thingis, he and hise sones with outen ende, and to brenne encense to the Lord bi his custom, and to blesse his name with outen ende.
Also the sones of Moyses, man of God, weren noumbrid in the lynage of Leuy.
The sones of Moises weren Gerson and Elieser.
The sones of Gerson; Subuhel the firste.
Sotheli the sones of Eliezer weren Roboya the firste, and othere sones weren not to Eliezer; forsothe the sones of Roboia weren multipliede ful miche.
The sones of Isaar; Salumuth the firste.
The sones of Ebron; Jerian the firste, Amarias the secounde, Jaziel the thridde, Jethamaan the fourthe.
The sones of Oziel; Mycha the firste, Jesia the secounde.
The sones of Merari weren Mooli and Musi. The sones of Mooli weren Eleazar, and Cys.
Sotheli Eleazar was deed, and hadde not sones, but douȝtris; and the sones of Cys, the britheren of hem, weddiden hem.
The sones of Musi weren thre, Mooli, and Heder, and Jerymuth.
These weren the sones of Leuy in her kynredis and meynees, prynces bi whilis, and noumbre of alle heedis, that diden the trauel of the seruyce of the hows of the Lord, fro twenti ȝeer and aboue.
For Dauid seide, The Lord God of Israel hath ȝoue reste to his puple, and a dwellyng in
Jerusalem til in to with outen ende; and it schal not be the office of dekenes for to bere more the tabernacle, and alle vessels therof for to mynystre.
Also bi the laste comaundementis of Dauid the noumbre of the sones of Leuy schulen be rikened
fro twenti ȝeer and aboue; and thei schulen be vndir the hond of the sones of Aaron in to the worschipe of the hows of the Lord, in porchis, and in chaumbris, and in the place of clensyng, and in the seyntuarie, and in alle werkis of the seruyce of the temple of the Lord.
Forsothe preestis schulen be ouer the looues of proposicioun, and to the sacrifice of flour, and to the pastis sodun in watir, and to the therf looues, and friyng panne, and to hoot flour, and to seenge, and ouer al weiȝte and mesure.
Forsothe the dekenes schulen be, that thei stonde eerli, for to knowleche and synge to the Lord, and
lijk maner at euentide, as wel in the offryng of brent sacrifices of the Lord, as in sabatis, and kalendis, and othere solempnytees, bi the noumbre and cerymonyes of eche thing contynueli bifor the Lord; and that thei kepe the obseruaunces of the tabernacle of the boond of pees of the Lord, and the custum of the seyntuarie, and the obseruaunce of the sones of Aaron, her britheren, that thei mynystre in the hows of the Lord.
Forsothe to the sones of Aaron these porciouns schulen be; the sones of Aaron weren Nadab, and Abyud, Eleazar, and
Ythamar; but Nadab and Abyud weren deed with out fre children bifor her fadir, and Eleazar and Ythamar weren set in presthod.
And Dauith departide hem, that is, Sadoch, of the sones of Eleazar, and Achymelech, of the sones of Ithamar,
by her whiles and seruyce; and the sones of Eleazar weren founden many mo in the men princes, than the sones of Ythamar. Forsothe he departide to hem, that is, to the sones of Eleazar, sixtene prynces bi meynees; and to the sones of Ythamar eiȝte prynces bi her meynees and howsis.
Sotheli he departide euer eithir meynees among hem silf bi lottis; for there weren princes of the seyntuarye, and princes of the hows of God, as wel of the sones of Eleazar as of the sones of Ithamar.
And Semeye, the sone of Nathanael, a scribe of the lynage of Leuy, discriuede hem bifore the king and pryncis, and bifor Sadoch, the preest, and Achymelech, the sone of Abiathar, and to the prynces of meynees of the preestis and of the dekenes; he discriuyde oon hows of Eleazar, that was souereyn to othere, and the tother hows of Ithamar, that hadde othere vndir hym.

These weren the whilis of hem bi her mynysteries, that thei entre in to the hows of God, and bi her custom vndur the hond of Aaron, her fadir, as the Lord God of Israel comaundide.
Forsothe Sebahel was prince of the sones of Leuy that weren resydue, of the sones of Amram; and the
sone of Sebahel was Jedeie; also Jesie was prince of the sones of Roobie.
Sotheli Salomoth was prince of Isaaris; and the
sone of Salamoth was Janadiath; and his firste sone was Jeriuans, Amarie the secounde, Azihel the thridde, Jethmoan the fourthe.
The sone of Ozihel was Mycha;
the sone of Mycha was Samyr; the brother of Mycha was Jesia; and the sone of Jesia was Zacharie.
The sones of Merary weren Mooli and Musi; the sone
of Josyan was Bennon; and the sone of Merarie was Ozian, and Soen, and Zaccur, and Hebri.
Sotheli the sone of Mooli was Eleazar, that hadde not fre sones;
forsothe the sone of Cys was Jeremyhel;
the sones of Musy weren Mooli, Eder, Jerymuth. These weren the sones of Leuy, bi the housis of her meynees.
Also and thei senten lottis aȝens her britheren, the sones of Aaron, bifor Dauid the kyng, and bifor Sadoch, and Achymelech, and the princes of meynees of preestis and of dekenes; lot departide euenli alle, bothe the gretter and the lesse.
Therfor Dauid, and the magestratis of the oost, departiden in to the seruyce the sones of Asaph, and of Eman, and of Idithum, whiche schulden profecye in harpis, and sawtrees, and cymbalis, bi her noumbre, and serue the office halewid to hem.
Of the sones of Asaph; Zaccur, and Joseph, and Nathania, and Asarela; sotheli the sones of Asaph vndir the hond of Asaph profesieden bisidis the kyng.
Forsothe the sones of Idithum weren these; Idithum, Godolie, Sori, Jesie, and Sabaie, and Mathatie, sixe; vndur the hond of hir fadir Idithum, that profesiede in an harpe on men knoulechynge and preysynge the Lord.
Also the sones of Heman weren Heman, Boccia, Mathanya, Oziel, Subuhel, and Jerymoth, Ananye, Anan, Elyatha, Gaeldothi, and Romenthi, Ezer, and Jesbacasi, Melothy, Othir, Mazioth;
alle these sones of Heman weren profetis of the kyng in the wordis of God, that he schulde enhaunse the horn. And God ȝaf to Heman fourtene sones, and thre douȝtris.
Alle vndur the hond of her fadir weren delid, ethir asigned, to synge in the temple of the Lord, in cymbalis, and sawtrees, and harpis, in to the seruyces of the hows of the Lord nyȝ the kyng, that is to seie, Asaph, and Idithum, and Heman.
Sotheli the noumbre of hem with her britheren, that tauȝten the songe of the Lord, alle the techeris, was twey hundrid foure scoor and eiȝte.
And thei senten lottis bi her whiles euenli, as wel the gretter as the lesse, also a wijs man and vnwijs.
And the firste lot ȝede out to Joseph, that was of Asaph; the secounde to Godolie, to hym, and hise
sones and hise britheren twelue; the thridde to Zaccur, to hise sones and hise
bretheren twelue; the fourthe to Isary, to hise sones and hise britheren twelue;

Forsothe these weren the departingis of porteris; of the sones of Chore, Mellesemye was the sone of Chore, of the sones of Asaph.
The sones of Mellesemie weren Zacharie the firste gendrid, Jedihel the secounde, Zabadie the thridde,
Yathanyel the fourthe, Aylam the fifthe, Johannan the sixte, Helioenay the seuenthe.
Forsothe the sones of Ebededom weren these; Semey the firste gendrid, Jozabab the secounde, Joaha the thridde, Seccar the fourthe, Nathanael
the fyuethe, Amyhel the sixte, Isachar the seuenthe, Pollathi the eiȝthe, for the Lord blesside hym.
Forsothe to Semeye, his sone, weren borun sones, souereyns of her meynees; for thei weren ful stronge men.
Therfor the sones of Semeye weren Othyn, and Raphael, and Obediel, and Zabad; and hise britheren, ful stronge men; also Helyu, and Samathie.
Alle these weren of the sones of Obededom; thei and her sones and britheren, ful stronge men for to serue, two and sixti of Obededom.
Sotheli of Mellesemeye, the sones and britheren, ful stronge, weren eiȝtene.
Forsothe of Oza, that is, of the sones of Merarie, Sechri was prince; for he hadde no firste gendrid, and therfor his fadir
settide hym in to prince; and Elchias the secounde, Thebelias the thridde, Zacarie the fourthe; alle these threttene weren the sones and britheren of Osa.
These weren departid in to porteris, that euere the princes of kepyngis, as also her britheren, schulden mynystre in the hows of the Lord.
Therfor lottis weren sent euenly, bothe to the litle and to the grete, bi her meyneeis, in to ech of the ȝatis.
Therfor the lot of the eest bifelde to Semelie; forsothe the north coost bifelde bi lot to Zacarie, his sone, a ful prudent
man and lernd; sotheli to Obededom and hise sones at the southe, in which part of the hows the counsel of
the eldre men was; Sephyma and Thosa weren at the west, bisidis the ȝate that ledith to the weie of stiyng, kepyng aȝens kepyng.
Sotheli at the eest weren sixe dekenes, and at the north weren foure bi dai; and at the south also weren foure at the myddai; and, where the counsel was, weren tweyne and tweyne.
And in the sellis, ethir litle housis, of porteris at the west, weren foure in the weie, and tweyne bi the sellis.
These weren the departyngis of porteris, of the sones of Chore and of Merary.
Forsothe Achias was ouer the tresours of the hows of the Lord, and ouer the vessels of hooli thingis.
The sones of Leedan, the sone of Gerson; of Leedan weren the princis of meynees of Leedan, and of Gerson, and of Jehiel.
The sones of Jehiel weren, Zethan, and Johel, his brother, ouer the tresours
of the hows of the Lord, Amramytis, and Isaaritis, and Ebronytis, and Ezielitis.
Forsothe Subahel, the sone of Gerson, sone of Moises, was souereyn of
the tresour; and his brother, Eliezer; whos sone was Raabia; and his sone was Asaye; his sone was Joram; and his sone was Zechry; but and his sone was Selemith.
Thilke Selemith, and his britheren, weren ouer the tresours of hooli thingis, whiche Dauid the kyng halewide, and the princes of meynees, and the tribunes, and the centuriouns,
and the duykis of the oost, of the batels, and of the spuylis of batels, whiche thei halewiden to the reparacioun and purtenaunce of the temple of the Lord.
Forsothe Samuel, the prophete, halewide alle these thingis, and Saul, the sone of Cys, and Abner, the sone of Ner, and Joab, the sone of Saruye; and alle halewiden tho thingis bi the hond of Salemyth, and of his britheren.
Sotheli Chonenye was souereyn and hise sones to Isaaritis, to the werkis with outforth on Israel, to teche and to deme hem.
Sotheli of Ebronytis, Asabie, and Sabie, and hise britheren, ful stronge men, a thousynde and seuene hundrid, weren souereyns on Israel biȝende Jordan aȝens the weste, in alle the werkis of the Lord, and in to the seruyce of the kyng.
Forsothe Herie was prynce of Ebronytis, bi her meynees and kynredis. In the fourtithe ȝeer of the rewme of Dauid there weren noumbred and foundun ful stronge men in Jazer
Galaad; and hise britheren, of strongere age, twei thousynde and seuene hundrid, princes of meynees. Sotheli Dauid the kyng made hem souereyns of Rubenytis and Gaditis, and of the half lynage of Manasses, in to al the seruyce of God and of the kyng.
Forsothe the sones of Israel bi her noumbre, the princes of meynees, the tribunes, and centuriouns, and prefectis, that mynystriden to the kyng bi her cumpenyes, entrynge and goynge out bi ech monethe in the ȝeer, weren souereyns, ech bi hym silf, on foure and twenti thousynde.
Isiboam, the sone of Zabdihel, was souereyn of the firste cumpenye in the firste monethe, and vndur hym weren
foure and twenti thousynde; of the sones of Fares was the prince of alle princes in the oost, in the firste monethe.
Dudi Achoites hadde the cumpany of the secounde monethe, and aftir hym silf he hadde another man, Macelloth bi name, that gouernede a part of the oost of foure and twenti thousynde.
And Bananye, the sone of Joiada, the preest, was duyk of the thridde cumpenye in the thridde monethe, and four and twenti thousynde
in his departyng; thilke is Bananye, the strongest among thritti, and aboue thritti; forsothe Amyzadath, his sone, was souereyn of his cumpenye.
In the fourthe monethe, the fourthe prince was Asahel, the brother of Joab, and Zabadie, his sone, aftir hym, and foure and twenti thousynde in his cumpeny.
In the fifthe monethe, the fifthe prince was Samoth Jezarites, and foure and twenti thousynde in his cumpenye.
In the sixte monethe, the sixte prince was Ira, the sone of Actes, Techuytes, and foure and twenti thousynde in his cumpeny.
In the seuenthe monethe, the seuenthe prince was Helles Phallonites, of the sones of Effraym, and foure and twenti thousynde in his cumpeny.
In the eiȝthe monethe, the eiȝthe prince was Sobothai Assothites, of the generacioun of Zarai, and foure and twenti thousynde in his cumpeny.
In the nynthe monethe, the nynthe prince was Abiezer Anathotites, of the generacioun of Gemyny, and foure and tweynti thousynde in his cumpeny.
In the tenthe monethe, the tenthe prince was Maray, and he was Neophatites, of the generacioun of Zaray, and foure and twenti thousynde in his cumpany.
In the elleuenthe monethe, the elleuenthe prince was Banaas Pharonytes, of the sones of Effraym, and foure and twenti thousynde in his cumpeny.
In the tweluethe monethe, the tweluethe prince was Holdia Nethophatites, of the generacioun of Gothonyel, and foure and twenti thousynde in his cumpeny.
Forsothe these weren souereyns of the lynages of Israel; duyk Eliezer, sone of Zechri, was souereyn to Rubenytis; duyk Saphacie, sone of Maacha, was souereyn
to Symeonytis; Asabie, the sone of Chamuel, was souereyn to Leuytis; Sadoch
was souereyn to Aaronytis; Elyu, the brothir of Dauid, was souereyn to the lynage of Juda; Amry, the sone of Mychael,
was souereyn to Isacharitis; Jesmaye, the sone of Abdie, was souereyn to Zabulonytis; Jerymuth, the sone of Oziel,
was souereyn to Neptalitis; Ozee, the sone of Ozazym, was souereyn to the sones of Effraym; Johel, the sone of Phatae, was souereyn to the half lynage of
Manasses; and Jaddo, the sone of Zacarie, was souereyn to the half lynage of Manasses in Galaad; sotheli Jasihel, the sone of Abner, was souereyn to Beniamyn;
forsothe Ezriel, the sone of Jeroam, was souereyn to Dan; these weren the princes of the sones of Israel.
Forsothe Dauid nolde noumbre hem with ynne twenti ȝeer, for the Lord seide, that he wolde multiplie Israel as the sterris of heuene.
Joab, the sone of Saruye, bigan for to noumbre, and he fillide not; for ire fel on Israel for this thing, and therfor the noumbre of hem, that weren noumbrid, was not teld in to the bookis of cronyclis of kyng Dauid.
Forsothe Azymoth, the sone of Adihel, was on the tresouris of the kyng; but Jonathan, the sone of Ozie, was souereyn of these tresours, that weren in cytees, and in townes, and in touris.
Sotheli Ezri, the sone of Chelub, was souereyn on the werk of hosebondrie, and on erthe tiliers, that tiliden
the lond; and Semeye Ramathites was souereyn on tilieris of vyneris; sotheli Zabdie Aphonytes was souereyn on
the wyn celeris; for Balanam Gadaritis was on the olyue placis, and fige places, that weren in the feeldi places; sotheli Joas was on the schoppis, ether celeris,
of oile; forsothe Cethray Saronytis was souereyn of the droues, that weren lesewid in Sarena; and Saphat, the sone of
Abdi, was ouer the oxis in valeys; sotheli Vbil of Ismael was ouer the camelis; and Jadye Meronathites was ouer the assis;
and Jazir Aggarene was ouer the scheep; alle these weren princes of the catel of kyng Dauid.
Forsothe Jonathas, brother of Dauithis fader, was a councelour, a myȝti man, and prudent, and lettrid; he and Jahiel, the sone of Achamony, weren with the sones of the kyng.
Also Achitofel was a counselour of the kyng; and Chusi Arachites was a frend of the kyng.
Aftir Achitofel was Joiada, the sone of Banaye, and Abyathar; but Joab was prince of the oost of the kyng.
Therfor Dauid clepide togidere alle the princes of Israel, the duykis of lynagis, and the souereyns of cumpenyes, that mynystriden to the kyng, also the tribunes, and centuriouns, and hem that weren souereyns ouer the catel and possessiouns of the kyng, and hise sones, with nurchis, and techeris, and alle the myȝti and strongeste men in the oost of Jerusalem.
And whanne the kyng hadde rise, and hadde stonde, he seide, My britheren and my puple, here ȝe me. Y thouȝte for to bilde an hows, wherynne the arke of boond of pees of the Lord, and the stool of the feet of oure God schulde reste; and Y made redi alle thingis to bilde.
But God seide to me, Thou schalt not bilde an hows to my name, for thou art a man werriour, and hast sched blood.
But the Lord God of Israel chees me of al the hows of my fadir, that Y schulde be kyng on Israel with outen ende; for of Juda he chees princes, sotheli of the hows of Juda he chees the hows of my fadir, and of the sones of my fadir it pleside hym to chese me kyng on al Israel.
But also of my sones, for the Lord ȝaf to me many sones, he chees Salomon, my sone, that he schulde sitte in the troone of the rewme of the Lord on Israel.
And he seide to me, Salomon, thi sone, schal bilde myn hows, and myn auters; for Y haue chose hym to me in to a sone, and Y schal be
to hym in to a fadir; and Y schal make stidefast his rewme til in to with outen ende, if he schal contynue to do myn heestis and domes, as and to dai.
Now therfor bifor al the cumpeny of Israel, Y seie these thingis that suen in the heryng of God, kepe ȝe and seke ȝe alle the comaundementis of ȝoure Lord God, that ȝe haue in possessioun a good lond, and that ȝe leeue it to ȝoure sones aftir ȝou til in to with outen ende.
But thou, Salomon, my sone, knowe the God of thi fadir, and serue thou hym with perfit herte, and wilful soule; for the Lord serchith alle hertis, and vndirstondith alle thouȝtis of soulis; if thou sekist hym, thou schalt fynde hym; forsothe if thou forsakist hym, he schal caste thee awei with outen ende.
Now therfor, for the Lord chees thee, for to bilde the hows of seyntuarie, be thou coumfortid, and parforme.
Forsothe Dauid ȝaf to Salomon, his sone, the discryuyng, ether ensaumple, of the porche, and of the temple, and of celeris, and of the soler, and of closetis in pryuy places, and of the hows
of propiciacioun, that is, of mersi; also and of alle thingis whiche he thouȝte of the large places, and of chaumbris bi cumpas, in to the tresours of the hows of the Lord, and in to the tresours of holi
thingis, and of the departyngis of preestis and of dekenes, in to alle the werkis of the hows of the Lord, and alle vessels of the seruyce of the temple of the Lord.
Of gold in weiȝte bi ech vessel of the seruyce, and of siluer, for dyuersitee of vessels,
and of werkis; but also to goldun candilstikis, and to her lanternes, he ȝaf gold, for the mesure of ech candilstike and lanternes; also and in silueren candilstikis, and in her lanternes, he bitook the weiȝte of siluer, for the dyuersite of mesure.
Also and he ȝaf gold in to the bord of settyng forth, for the dyuersite of mesure, also and he ȝaf siluer in to othere
siluerne boordis; also to fleisch hookis, and viols, and censeris of pureste gold; and to litle goldun lyouns, for the maner of mesure, he departide a weiȝte in to a litil lyoun and a litil lioun; also and in to siluerne liouns he departide dyuerse weiȝte of siluer.
Forsothe he ȝaf pureste gold to the auter, wherynne encense was brent, that a lickenesse of the cart of cherubyns, holdinge forth wyngis, and hilynge the arke of boond of pees of the Lord, schulde be maad therof.
Dauid seide, Alle thingis camen writun bi the hond of the Lord to me, that Y schulde vndirstonde alle the werkis of the saumpler.
And Dauid seide to Salomon, his sone, Do thou manli, and be thou coumfortid, and make; drede thou not with outforth, nether drede thou with ynne; for my Lord God schal be with thee, and he schal not leeue thee, nether schal forsake thee, til thou performe al the werk of the seruyce of the hows of the Lord,
Lo! the departyngis of prestis and of dekenes, in to al the werk of the seruyce of the hows of the Lord, schulen stonde niȝ thee; and thei ben redi, and bothe the princes and the puple kunnen do alle thi comaundementis.
And kyng Dauid spak to al the chirche, God hath chose Salomon, my sone, ȝit a child and tendre; forsothe the werk is greet, and a dwellyng is not maad redi to man but to God.
Sotheli Y in alle my myȝtis haue maad redi the costis of the hows of my God; gold to goldun vessels, siluer in to siluerne vessels, bras in to brasun vessels, irun in to irun vessels, tre in to trenun vessels, onychyn stonys, and stonys as of the colour of wymmens oynement, and ech precious stoon of dyuerse colouris, and marbil of dyuerse colouris, most plenteuously.
And ouer these thingis Y ȝyue gold and siluer in to the temple of my God, whiche Y offride of my propir catel in to the hows of my God, outakun these thingis whiche
Y made redi in to the hooli hows, thre thousynde talentis of gold, of the gold of Ophir, and seuene thousynde of talentis of siluer most preuyd, to ouergilde the wallis
of the temple; and werkis be maad bi the hondis of crafti men, where euere gold is nedeful, of gold, and where euere siluer is nedeful, of siluer; and if ony man offrith bi his fre wille, fille he his hond to dai, and offre he that that he wole to the Lord.
Therfor the princes of meynees, and the duykis of the lynagis of Israel, and the tribunes, and the centuriouns, and the princes of the possessiouns of the
kyng, bihiȝten; and thei ȝauen in to the werkis of the hows of the Lord, fyue thousynde talentis of gold, and ten thousynde schyllyngis; ten thousynde talentis of siluer, and eiȝtene thousynde talentis of bras, and an hundrid thousynde of talentis of irun.
And at whom euere stoonys were foundun, thei ȝauen in to the tresour of the hows of the Lord, bi the hond of Jehiel Gersonyte.
And the puple was glad, whanne thei bihiȝten avowis bi her fre wille, for with al the herte thei offriden tho to the Lord. But also kyng Dauid was glad with greet ioye,
and blesside the Lord bifor al the multitude, and seide, Lord God of Israel, oure fadir, thou art blessid fro with outen bigynnyng
in to with outen ende; Lord, worthi doyng is thin, and power, and glorie, and victorie, and heriyng is to thee; for alle thingis that ben in heuene and in erthe ben thine; Lord, the rewme is thin, and thou art ouer alle princes;
ritchessis ben thin, and glorie is thin; thou art Lord of alle; in thin hond is vertu, and power, and in thin hond is greetnesse, and lordschipe of alle.
Now therfor, oure God, we knoulechen to thee, and we herien thi noble name.
Who am Y, and who is my puple, that we moun bihete alle these thingis to thee? Alle thingis ben thine, and we han ȝoue to thee tho thingis, whiche we token of thin hond.
For we ben pilgrimes and comelyngis bifor thee, as alle oure fadris; oure daies ben as schadewe on the erthe, and no dwellyng is.
Oure Lord God, al this plentee which we han maad redi, that an hows schulde be byldid to thin hooli name, is of thin hond; and alle thingis ben thin.
My God, Y woot, that thou preuest hertis, and louest symplenesse of herte; wherfor and Y, in the symplenesse of myn herte, haue offrid gladli alle these thingis; and Y siȝ with greet ioye thi puple, which is foundun here, offre ȝiftis to thee.
Lord God of Abraham, and of Ysaac, and of Israel, oure fadris, kepe thou with outen ende this wille of her hertis; and this mynde dwelle euere in to the worschipyng of thee.
Also ȝyue thou to Salomon, my sone, a perfit herte, that he kepe thin heestis, and witnessyngis, and thi ceremonyes; and do alle thingis, and that he bilde the hows, whose costis Y haue maad redi.
Forsothe Dauid comaundide to al the chirche, Blesse ȝe oure Lord God. And al the chirche blesside the Lord God of her fadris, and thei bowiden hem silf, and worschipiden God, aftirward the kyng.
And thei offriden slayn sacrifices to the Lord, and thei offriden brent sacrifices in the dai suynge; a thousynde boolis, and a thousynde rammes, and a thousynde lambren, with her fletynge sacrifices, and al the custom, most plenteuously, in to al Israel.
And thei eten and drunken bifor the Lord in that dai, with greet gladnesse. And thei anoyntiden the secounde tyme Salomon, the sone of Dauid; and thei anoyntiden hym in to prince to the Lord, and Sadoch in to bischop.
And Salomon sat on the trone of the Lord in to kyng, for Dauid, his fadir; and it pleside alle men, and al Israel obeiede to hym.
But also alle princes, and myȝti men, and alle the sones of kyng Dauid, ȝauen hond, and weren suget to Salomon the kyng.
Therfor the Lord magnefiede Salomon on al Israel, and ȝaue to hym glorie of the rewme, what maner glorie no kyng of Israel hadde bifor hym.
Therfor Dauid, the sone of Ysai, regnede on al Israel;
and the daies in whiche he regnede on Israel weren fourti ȝeer; in Ebron he regnede seuene ȝeer, and in Jerusalem thre and thretti ȝeer.
And he diede in good eelde, and was ful of daies, and richessis, and glorie; and Salomon, his sone, regnede for hym.
Forsothe the formere and the laste dedis of Dauid ben writun in the book of Samuel, the prophete, and in the book of Nathan, prophete, and in the
book of Gad, the prophete; and of al his rewme, and strengthe, and tymes, that passiden vndur hym, ethir in Israel, ethir in alle rewmes of londis.
THERFOR Salomon, the sone of Dauid, was coumfortid in his rewme, and the Lord was with hym, and magnefiede hym an hiȝ.
And Salomon comaundide to al Israel, to tribunes, and centuriouns, and to duykis, and domesmen of al Israel,
and to the princes of meynees; and he ȝede with al the multitude in to the hiȝ place of Gabaon, where the tabernacle of boond of pees of the Lord was, which tabernacle Moyses, the seruaunt of the Lord, made in wildirnesse.
Forsothe Dauid hadde brouȝt the arke of God fro Cariathiarym in to the place which he hadde maad redy to it, and where he hadde set a tabernacle to it, that is, in to Jerusalem.
And the brasun auter, which Beseleel, the sone of Vri, sone of Vr, hadde maad, was there bifor the tabernacle of the Lord; whiche also Salomon and al the chirche souȝte.
And Salomon stiede to the brasun autir, bifor the tabernacle of boond of pees of the Lord, and offride in it a thousynde sacrifices.
Lo! forsothe in that nyȝt God apperide to hym, and seide, Axe that that thou wolt, that Y ȝyue to thee.
And Salomon seide to God, Thou hast do greet mersi with Dauid, my fadir, and hast ordeyned me kyng for hym.
Now therfor, Lord God, thi word be fillid, which thou bihiȝtist to Dauid, my fadir; for thou hast maad me kyng on thi greet puple, which is so vnnoumbrable as the dust of erthe.
Ȝiue thou to me wisdom and vndurstondyng, that Y go in and go out bifor thi puple; for who may deme worthili this thi puple, which is so greet?
Sotheli God seide to Salomon, For this thing pleside more thin herte, and thou axidist not richessis, and catel, and glorie, nether the lyues of them that hatiden thee, but nether ful many daies of lijf; but thou axidist wisdom and kunnyng, that thou maist deme my puple, on which Y ordeynede
thee kyng, wisdom and kunnyng ben ȝouun to thee; forsothe Y schal ȝyue to thee richessis, and catel, and glorie, so that noon among kyngis, nether bifor thee nethir aftir thee, be lijk thee.
Therfor Salomon cam fro the hiȝ place of Gabaon in to Jerusalem, bifor the tabernacle of boond of pees, and he regnede on Israel.
And he gaderide to hym chaaris and knyȝtis, and a thousynde and foure hundrid charis weren maad to hym, and twelue thousynde of knyȝtis; and he made hem to be in the citees of cartis, and with the kyng in Jerusalem.
And the kyng ȝaf in Jerusalem gold and siluer as stoonys, and cedris as sicomoris, that comen forth in feeldi places in greet multitude.
Forsothe horsis weren brouȝt to hym fro Egipt, and fro Choa, bi the marchauntis of the kyng, which ȝeden, and
bouȝten bi prijs, a foure horsid carte for sixe hundrid platis of siluer, and an hors for an hundrid and fifti. In lijk maner biyng was maad of alle the rewmes of citees, and of the kingis of Sirie.
Forsothe Salomon demyde to bilde an hows to the name of the Lord, and a paleis to hym silf.
And he noumbride seuenti thousynde of men berynge in schuldris, and fourescore thousynde that schulden kitte stoonys in hillis; and the souereyns of hem thre thousynde and sixe hundrid.
And he sente to Iram, kyng of Tire, and seide, As thou didist with my fadir Dauid, and sentist to hym trees of cedre, that he schulde bilde to hym
an hows, in which also he dwellide; so do thou with me, that Y bilde an hows to the name of my Lord God, and that Y halewe it, to brenne encense bifor hym, and to make odour of swete smellynge spiceries, and to euerlastynge settynge forth of looues, and to brent sacrifices in the morewtid and euentid, and in sabatis, and neomenyes, and solempnytees of oure Lord God in to with outen ende, that ben comaundid to Israel.
For the hows which Y coueyte to bilde is greet; for oure Lord God is greet ouer alle goddis.
Who therfor may haue myȝt to bilde a worthi hows to hym? For if heuene and the heuenes of heuenes moun not take hym, hou greet am Y, that Y may bilde an hows to hym, but to this thing oonli, that encense be brent bifor hym?
Therfor sende thou to me a lernd man, that can worche in gold, and siluer, bras, and yrun, purpur, rede silke, and iacynct; and that can graue in grauyng with these crafti men, which Y haue with me in Judee and Jerusalem, whiche Dauid, my fadir, made redi.
