But also sende thou to me cedre trees, and pyne trees, and thyne trees of the Liban; for Y woot, that thi seruauntis kunnen kitte trees of the Liban; and my seruauntis schulen be with
thi seruauntis, that ful many trees be maad redi to me; for the hows which Y coueyte to bilde is ful greet and noble.
Ferthermore to thi seruauntis, werk men that schulen kitte trees, Y schal ȝyue in to meetis twenti thousynde chorus of whete, and so many chorus of barli, and twenti thousynde mesuris of oile, that ben clepid sata.
Forsothe Iram, king of Tire, seide bi lettris whiche he sente to Salomon, For the Lord louyde his puple, therfor he made thee to regne on it.
And he addide, seiynge, Blessid be the Lord God of Israel, that made heuene and erthe, which ȝaf to Dauid the kyng a wijs sone, and lernd, and witti, and prudent, that he schulde bilde an hows to the Lord, and a paleis to hym silf.
Therfor Y sente to thee a prudent man and moost kunnynge,
Iram, my fadir, the sone of a womman of the lynage of Dan, whos fadir was a man of Tire; whiche Iram can worche in gold, and siluer, bras, and irun, and marble, and trees, also in purpur, and iacynct, and bijs, and rede silke; and which Iram can graue al grauyng, and fynde prudentli, what euer thing is nedeful in werk with thi crafti men, and with the crafti men of my lord Dauid, thi fadir.
Therfor, my lord, sende thou to thi seruauntis the whete, and barli, and oyle, and wyn, whiche thou bihiȝtist.
Sotheli we schulen kitte trees of the Liban, how many euere thou hast nedeful; and we schulen brynge tho in schippis bi the see in to Joppe; forsothe it schal be thin to lede tho ouer in to Jerusalem.
Therfor Salomon noumbride alle men conuertid fro hethenesse, that weren in the lond of Israel, aftir the noumbryng which Dauid, his fadir, noumbride; and an hundrid thousynde and thre and fifti thousynde and sixe hundrid weren foundun.
And he made of hem seuenti thousynde, that schulden bere birthuns in schuldris, and foure score thousynde, that schulden kitte stonys in hillis; sotheli he made thre thousynde and sixe hundrid souereyns of werkis of the puple.
And Salomon bigan to bilde the hows of the Lord in Jerusalem, in the hil of Moria, that was schewid to Dauid, his fadir, in the place which Dauid hadde maad redi in the corn floor of Ornam Jebusei.
Forsothe he bigan to bilde in the secounde monethe, in the fourthe ȝeer of his rewme.
And these weren the foundementis, whiche Salomon settide, that he schulde bilde the hous of God; sixti cubitis of lengthe in the firste mesure, twenti cubitis of breede.
Forsothe he bildide a porche bifor the frount, that was stretchid forth along bisidis the mesure of the breede of the hows, of twenti cubitis, sotheli the hiȝnesse was of an hundrid and twenti cubitis; and he ouergilde it with inne with clennest gold.
Also he hilide the gretter hows with tablis of beech, and he fastnede platis of gold of beste colour al aboute; and he grauyde therynne palmtrees, and as smale chaynes biclipynge hem silf togidere.
And he arayede the pawment of the temple with most preciouse marble, in myche fairenesse.
Forsothe the gold was moost preued, of whose platis he hilide the hows, and the beemys therof, and the postis, and the wallis, and the doris; and he grauyde cherubyns in the wallis.
Also he made an hows to the holi of holi thingis, in lengthe bi the breede of the hows, of twenti cubitis, and the breed also of twenti cubitis; and he hilide it with goldun platis, as with sixe hundrid talentis.
But also he made goldun nailis, so that ech nail peiside fifti siclis; and he hilide the solers with gold.
Also he made in the hows of the hooli of hooli thingis twei cherubyns bi the werk of an ymage makere, and hilide hem with gold.
The wyngis of cherubyns weren holdun forth bi twenti cubitis, so that o wynge hadde fyue cubitis, and touchide the wal of the hows; and the tother wynge hadde fyue cubitis, and touchide the wynge of the tother cherub.
In lijk maner the wynge of the tother cherub hadde fyue cubitis, and touchide the wal, and the tother wynge therof of fyue cubitis touchide the wynge of the tothir cherub.
Therfor the wyngis of euer eithir cherub weren spred abrood, and weren holdun forth bi twenti cubitis; sotheli thilke cherubyns stoden on the feet reisid, and her faces weren turned to the outermere hows.
Also he made a veil of iacynct and purpur, of reed seelk and bijs; and weuyde cherubyns therynne.
Also bifor the ȝate of the temple he made twei pilers, that hadden fyue and thretti cubitis of heiȝthe; forsothe the heedis of tho weren of fyue cubitis.
Also he made and as litle chaynes in Goddis answeryng place, and puttide tho on the heedis of the pilers; also he made an hundrid pumgarnadis, whiche he settide bitwixe the litle chaynes.
And he settide tho pilers in the porche of the temple, oon at the riȝtside, and the tother at the leftside; he clepide that that was at the riȝtside Jachym, and that that was at the leftside he clepide Booz.
Also he made a brasun auter of twenti cubitis of lengthe, and of twenti cubitis of
breede, and of ten cubitis of heiȝthe; he made also a ȝotun see of ten cubitis fro brynke til to brynke, round bi cumpas; it hadde fyue cubitis of heiȝthe; and a coorde of thritti cubitis cumpasside the cumpas therof.
And the licnesse of oxis was vndur it, and bi ten cubitis summe grauyngis with outforth cumpassiden the brynke of the see as with tweyne ordris; sotheli the oxis weren ȝotun.
And thilke see was set on twelue oxis, of whiche oxis thre bihelden to the north, and othere thre to the west, sotheli thre othere bihelden the south, and thre that weren residue bihelden the eest, and hadden the see set aboue; but the hyndrere partis of the oxis weren with ynne vndur the see.
Sotheli the thicknesse therof hadde the mesure of a pawm of the hond, and the brynke therof was as the brynke of a cuppe, ethir of a lilie crokid aȝen, and it took thre thousynde metretis of mesure.
Also he made ten holowe vessels, and settide fyue at the riȝtside, and fyue at the leftside, that thei schulden waische in tho alle thingis, whiche thei schulden offre in to brent sacrifice; sotheli the preestis weren waischun in the see.
Sotheli he made ten goldun candilstikis bi the licknesse which he hadde comaundid to be maad, and he settide tho in the temple, fyue at the riȝtside and fyue at the leftsid.
And he made also ten boordis, and settide tho in the temple, fyue at the riȝtside and fyue at the leftside.
Also he made an hundrid goldun viols. Also he made a large place of preestis, and a greet hows, and doris in the greet hows, which he hilide with bras.
Forsothe he settide the see in the riȝtsyde aȝens the eest at the south.
Also Iram made cawdruns, and fleischokis, and viols, and he fillide al the werk of
the kyng in the hows of God, that is, twei pilers, and pomels, and heedis, and as summe nettis, that hiliden the heedis aboue
the pomels; also he made fourti pumgarnadis, and twei werkis lijk nettis, so that two ordris of pumgarnadis weren ioyned to ech werk like nettis, which hiliden the pomels, and heedis of the pilers.
He made also foundementis, and holow vessels, whiche he settide on the
foundementis; he made o see, and twelue
oxis vndur the see, and caudruns, and fleischookis, and viols. Iram, the fadir of Salomon, made to hym alle vessels in the hows of the Lord of clennest bras.
The kyng ȝetide tho in the cuntrey of Jordan, in cleiy lond bitwixe Socoth and Saredata.
Forsothe the multitude of vessels was vnnoumbrable, so that the weiȝte of bras was not knowun.
And Salomon made alle the vessels of Goddis hows, the goldun auter, and bordis, and loouys of
settyng forth on tho; and candilstikis of purest gold, with her lanternes, that tho schulden schyne bifor Goddis answering
place bi the custom; and he made summe werkis lijk flouris, and lanternes, and goldun tongis; alle thingis weren maad
of clennest gold; also he made pannes for colis to brenne encense, and censeris, and viols, and morters, of pureste gold. And he grauyde doris of the ynnere temple, that is, in the hooli of hooli thingis, and the goldun doris of the temple with out forth; and so al the werk was fillid that Salomon made in the hows of the Lord.
Therfor Salomon brouȝte in alle thingis, siluer and gold, whiche Dauid, his fadir, hadde avowid; and he puttide alle vesselis in the tresouris of the hows of the Lord.
After whiche thingis he gaderide togidere alle the grettere men in birthe of Israel, and alle the princes of lynagis, and the heedis of meynees, of the sones of Israel, in to Jerusalem, that thei schulden brynge the arke of boond of pees of the Lord fro the citee of Dauid, which is Syon.
Therfor alle men of Israel camen to the kyng, in the solempne dai of the seuenthe monethe.
And whanne alle the eldre men of Israel weren comen, the dekenes
baren the arke, and brouȝten it in, and al the aray of the tabernacle. Forsothe the preestis with the dekenes baren the vessels of seyntuarie, that weren in the tabernacle.
Sotheli kyng Salomon, and alle the cumpenyes of Israel, and alle that weren gaderid to gidere, offriden bifor the arke wetheris and oxis with outen ony noumbre; for the multitude of slayn sacrifices was so greet.
And preestis brouȝten the arke of boond of pees of the Lord in to his place, that is, to Goddis answeryng place of the temple, in to the hooli of hooli thingis, vndur the wyngis of
cherubyns; so that cherubyns spredden forth her wyngis ouer the place, in which the arke was put, and hiliden thilke arke with hise barris.
Sotheli the heedis, by which the arke was borun, weren opyn bifor Goddis answeryng place, for tho heedis weren a litil lengere; but if a man hadde be a litil with out forth, he myȝt not se tho barris. Therfor the
arke was there til in to present dai; and noon other thing was in the arke, no but twei tablis, whiche Moyses hadde put in Oreb, whanne the Lord ȝaf the lawe to the sones of Israel goynge out of Egipt.
Forsothe the prestis ȝeden out of the seyntuarie, for alle preestis, that myȝten be foundun there, weren halewid, and the whiles, and the ordre of seruyces among hem was not departid ȝit in that
tyme; bothe dekenes and syngeris, that is, bothe thei that weren vndur Asaph, and thei that weren vndur Eman, and thei that weren vndur Idithum, her sones and britheren, clothid with white lynun clothis, sownyden with cymbalis and sautrees and harpis, and stoden at the west coost of the auter, and with hem weren sixe score preestis trumpynge.
Therfor whanne alle sungen togidur both with trumpis, and vois, and cymbalis, and orguns, and of dyuerse kynde of musikis, and reisiden the vois an hiȝ, the sown was herd fer, so that whanne thei hadden bigunne to preyse the Lord, and to seie, Knouleche ȝe to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy is in to the world, ether, with outen ende; the hows of God was fillid with a cloude,
and the preestis miȝten not stonde and serue for the derknesse; for the glorie of the Lord hadde fillid the hows of the Lord.
Thanne Salomon seide, The Lord bihiȝte, that he wolde dwelle in derknesse;
forsothe I haue bilde an hows to his name, that he schulde dwelle there with outen ende.
And Salomon turnede his face, and blesside al the multitude of Israel; for al the cumpeny stood ententif;
and he seide, Blessid be the Lord God of Israel, for he fillide in werk that thing, that he spak to Dauid, my fadir, and
seide, Fro the dai in which Y ledde my puple out of the lond of Egipt, Y chees not a citee of alle the lynagis of Israel, that an hows schulde be bildid therynne to my name, nether Y chees ony other man, that he schulde be duyk on my puple
Israel; but Y chees Jerusalem, that my name be therynne, and Y chees Dauid, to ordeyne hym on my puple Israel.
And whanne it was of the wille of Dauid, my fadir, to bilde an hows to the name of the
Lord God of Israel, the Lord seide to hym, For this was thi wille, that thou woldist bilde an hows to my name, sotheli thou
didist wel, hauynge suche a wil, but thou schalt not bilde an hows to me; netheles the sone, that schal go out of thi leendis, he schal bilde an hows to my name.
Therfor the Lord hath fillid his word, which he spak; and Y roos for Dauid, my fader, and Y sat on the trone of Israel, as the Lord spak, and Y bildide an hous to the
name of the Lord God of Israel; and I haue put therynne the arke, in which is the couenaunt of the Lord, which he couenauntide with the sones of Israel.
Therfor Salomon stood bifor the auter of the Lord euene aȝens al the multitude of Israel, and stretchide forth his hondis.
For Salomon hadde maad a brasun foundement, and hadde set it in the myddis of the greet hows, and it hadde fyue cubitis of lengthe, and fyue of breede, and thre cubitis of heiȝthe, and he stood theron; and fro that tyme he knelide aȝens al the multitude of Israel, and reiside the hondis
in to heuene, and seide, Lord God of Israel, noon is lijk thee; thou art God in heuene and in erthe, which kepist couenaunt and mercy with thi seruauntis, that
goon bifor thee in al her herte; which hast ȝoue to Dauid thi seruaunt, my fadir, what euer thingis thou hast spoke to hym, and thow hast fillid in werk tho thingis, whiche thou bihiȝtist bi mouth, as also present tyme preueth.
Now therfor, Lord God of Israel, fille thou to thi seruaunt my fadir Dauid, what euer thingis thou hast spoke, seiynge, A man of thee schal not faile bifor me, that schal sitte on the trone of Israel; so netheles if thi sones kepen my weies, and goon in my lawe, as and thou hast go bifor me.
And now, Lord God of Israel, thi word be maad stidefast, which thou spakist to thi seruaunt Dauid.
Therfor whether it is leueful, that the Lord dwelle with men on erthe? If heuene and the heuenes of heuenes taken not thee, how myche more this hows, which Y haue bildid?
But herto oneli it is maad, that thou, my Lord God, biholde the preier of thi seruaunt, and the bisechyng of hym, and that thou here the preieris, whiche thi seruaunt
schedith bifor thee; that thou opyne thin iȝen on this hows bi dayes and nyȝtis, on the place in which thou bihiȝtist, that
thi name schulde be clepid, and that thou woldist here the preier, which thi seruaunt preieth therynne. Here thou the preieris of thi seruaunt, and of thi puple Israel; who euer preieth in this place, here thou fro thi dwellyng place, that is, fro heuenes, and do thou merci.
If ony man synneth aȝens his neiȝbore, and cometh redi to swere aȝens him, and byndith hym silf with cursyng bifor the auter in this
hows, thou schalt here fro heuene, and schalt do the doom of thi seruauntis; so that thou ȝelde to the wickid man his weie in to his owne heed, and that thou venge the iust man, and ȝelde to hym after his riȝtfulnesse.
If thi puple Israel is ouercomen of enemyes, for thei schulen do synne aȝens thee, and if thei conuertid doen penaunce, and bisechen thi name,
and preien in this place, thou schalt here fro heuene, and do thou mercy to the synne of thi puple Israel, and brynge hem aȝen in to the lond, which thou hast ȝoue to hem, and to the fadris of hem.
If whanne heuene is closid, reyn come not doun for the synne of thi puple, and thei bisechen thee in this place, and knowlechen to thi name, and ben turned fro her synnes, whanne thou hast turmentid
hem, here thou, Lord, fro heuene, and forȝyue thou synnes to thi seruauntis, and to thi puple Israel, and teche thou hem a good weie, bi which thei schulen entre, and ȝyue thou reyn to the lond, which thou hast ȝoue to thi puple to haue in possessioun.
If hungur risith in the lond, and pestilence, and rust, and wynd distriynge cornes, and a locuste, and bruke cometh, and if enemyes bisegen the ȝatis of the citee, aftir that the cuntreis ben distried, and al veniaunce and sikenesse
oppressith; if ony of thi puple Israel bisechith, and knowith his veniaunce and sikenesse, and if he spredith abrood hise
hondis in this hows, thou schalt here fro heuene, that is, fro thin hiȝe dwellyng place, and do thou mercy, and ȝelde thou to ech man aftir hise weies, whiche thou knowist, that he hath in his herte; for thou aloone knowist the hertis of the
sones of men; that thei drede thee, and go in thi weies in alle daies, in which thei lyuen on the face of erthe, which thou hast ȝoue to oure fadris.
Also thou schalt here fro heuene, thi moost stidfast dwellyng place, a straunger, which is not of thi puple Israel, if he cometh fro a fer lond for thi greet name, and for thi stronge hond, and arm holdun forth, and
preye in this place; and thou schalt do alle thingis, for which thilke pilgrym inwardli clepith thee, that alle the puplis of erthe knowe thi name, and drede thee, as thi puple Israel doith; and that thei knowe, that thi name is clepid on this hows, which Y haue bildid to thi name.
If thi puple goith out to batel aȝens hise aduersaries, bi the weie in which thou sendist hem, thei schulen worschipe thee aȝens the weie in which this citee is, which thou hast chose, and the hows
which Y bildide to thi name, that thou here fro heuene her preieris and bisechyng, and do veniaunce.
Forsothe if thei synnen aȝens thee, for no man is that synneth not, and if thou art wrooth to hem, and bitakist hem to enemyes; and enemyes leden hem prisoneris in to a fer
lond, ether certis which lond is nyȝ; and if thei ben conuertid in her herte in the lond, to which thei ben led prisoneris, and thei don penaunce, and bisechen thee in the lond of her caitifte, and seien, We han synned, we han do wickidly, we
diden vniustli; and if thei turnen aȝen to thee in al her herte, and in al her soule, in the lond of her caitifte, to which thei ben led, thei schulen worschipe thee aȝens the weie of her lond, which thou hast ȝoue to the fadris of hem, and of the citee which thou hast chose, and of the hows which Y bildide to thi name;
that thou here fro heuene, that is, fro thi stidefast dwellyng place, the preieris of hem, and that thou make dom, and forȝyue to thi puple, thouȝ it be synful;
for thou art my God; Y biseche, be thin iȝen openyd, and thin eeris be ententif to the preier which is maad in this place.
Now therfor, Lord God, rise in to thi reste, thou and the arke of thi strengthe; Lord God, thi preestis be clothid with helthe, and thi hooli men be glad in
goodis. Lord God, turne thou not a weie the face of thi crist; haue thou mynde on the mercyes of Dauid thi seruaunt.
And whanne Salomon schedynge preyeris hadde fillid, fier cam doun fro heuene, and deuouride brent sacrifices, and slayn sacrifices; and the maieste of the Lord fillide the hows.
And preestis myȝten not entre in to the temple of the Lord; for the maieste of the Lord hadde fillid the temple of the Lord.
But also alle the sones of Israel sien fier comynge doun, and the glorie of the Lord on the hows, and thei felden down lowe to the erthe on the pawment araied with stoon, and thei worschipiden, and preisiden the Lord, For he is good, for his merci is in to al the world.
Forsothe the kyng and al the puple offriden slayn sacrifices bifor the Lord.
Therfor king Salomon killide sacrifices of oxis two and twenti thousynd, of wetheris sixe score thousynde; and the kyng and al the puple halewiden the hows of God.
Forsothe the preestis stoden in her offices, and dekenes in orguns of songis of the Lord, whiche kyng Dauid made to preise the Lord, For his merci is in to the world; and thei sungen the ympnes of Dauid bi her hondis; sotheli the prestis sungen with trumpis bifor hem, and al the puple of Israel stood.
Therfor Salomon halewide the myddil of the large place bifor the temple of the Lord; for he hadde offrid there brent sacrifices, and the ynnere fatnesses of pesible sacrifices, for the brasun auter which he hadde maad myȝte not susteyne the brent sacrifices, and sacrifices, and the innere fatnessis of pesible sacrifices.
Therfor Salomon made a solempnyte in that tyme in seuene dayes, and al Israel with hym, a ful greete chirche, fro the entryng of Emath til to the stronde of Egipt.
And in the eiȝthe dai he made a gaderyng of money, that is, for necessaries of the temple, for he hadde halewid the auter in seuene daies, and hadde maad solempnytee in seuene daies.
Therfor in the thre and twentithe dai of the seuenthe monethe he lete the puplis go to her tabernaclis, ioiynge and gladynge on the good that God hadde do to Dauid, and to Salomon, and to his puple Israel.
And Salomon parformyde the hows of the Lord, and the hows of the kyng, and alle thingis which he hadde disposid in his herte for to do in the hows of the Lord and in his owne hows; and he hadde prosperite.
Forsothe the Lord aperide to hym in the nyȝt, and seide, Y haue herd thi preiere, and Y haue chose this place to me in to an hows of sacrifice.
If Y close heuene, and reyn cometh not doun, and if Y sende, and comaunde to a locuste, that he deuoure the lond, and if
Y send pestilence in to my puple; forsothe if my puple is conuertid, on whiche my name is clepid, and if it bisechith me, and sekith my face, and doith penaunce of hise werste weies, Y schal here fro heuene, and Y schal be merciful to the synnes of hem, and Y schal heele the lond of hem.
And myn iȝen schulen be openyd, and myn eeren schulen be reisid to the preiere of hym,
that preieth in this place; for Y haue chose, and halewid this place, that my name be there with outen ende, and that myn iȝen and myn herte dwelle there in alle daies.
Also if thou gost bifore me, as Dauid thi fadir ȝede, and doist bi alle thingis whiche Y comaundide to thee, and kepist my riȝtwisnessis and domes,
Y schal reise the trone of thi rewme, as Y bihiȝte to Dauid thi fadir, and seide, A man of thi generacioun schal not be takun awei, that schal be prince in Israel.
But if ȝe turnen awey, and forsake my riȝtwisnessis and my comaundementis whiche Y settide forth to ȝou, and ȝe goen, and seruen alien goddis, and worschipen
hem, Y schal drawe ȝou awey fro my lond, which Y ȝaf to ȝou, and Y schal caste awey fro my face this hows which Y haue bildid to my name, and Y schal ȝyue it in to a parable, and in to ensaumple to alle puplis.
And this hows schal be in to a prouerbe to alle men passynge forth; and thei schulen seie, wondringe, Whi dide the Lord so to this lond, and to this hows?
And thei schulen answere, For thei forsoken the Lord God of her fadris, that ledde hem out of the lond of Egipt, and thei token alien goddis, and worschipiden, and herieden hem; therfor alle these yuelis camen on hem.
Forsothe whanne twenti ȝeer weren fillid, aftir that Salomon bildide the hows
of the Lord, and his owne hows, he bildide the citees, whiche Iram hadde ȝoue to Salomon; and he made the sones of Israel to dwelle there.
Also he ȝede in to Emath of Suba, and gat it.
And he bildide Palmyram in deseert, and he bildide othere citees maad ful stronge in Emath.
And he bildide the hiȝere Betheron and the lowere Betheron, wallid citees, hauynge
ȝatis and lockis and barris; also he bildide Balaath, and alle citees ful stronge that weren of Salomon; and alle the citees of cartis, and the citees of knyȝtis kyng Salomon bildide, and disposide alle thingis whiche euere he wolde, in Jerusalem, and in the Liban, and in al the lond of his power.
Salomon made suget in to tributaries til in to this dai al the puple that was left of Etheis, and Amorreis, and Phereseis, and Eueis, and of Jebuseis, that weren not of the generacioun of Israel,
and of the sones of hem, and of the aftircomers of hem, whiche the sones of Israel hadden not slayn.
Sotheli of the sones of Israel he settide not, that thei schulden serue the werkis of the kyng; for thei weren men werriours, and the firste duykis, and princes of charis, and
of hise knyȝtis; forsothe alle the princes of the oost of kyng Salomon weren two hundrid and fifti, that tauȝten the puple.
Sotheli he translatide the douȝter of Farao fro the citee of Dauid in to the hows, which he hadde bildid to hir; for the kyng seide, My wijf schal not dwelle in the hows of Dauid, kyng of Israel, for it is halewid, for the arke of the Lord entride in to that hows.
Thanne Salomon offride brent sacrifices to the Lord on the auter of the Lord, which he hadde
bildid bifor the porche, that bi alle daies me schulde offre in it, bi the comaundement of Moises, in sabatis, and in kalendis, and in feeste daies, thries bi the ȝeer, that is, in the solempnyte of the therflooues, and in the solempnyte of woukis, and in the solempnyte of tabernaclis.
And he ordeynede bi the ordynaunce of Dauid, his fadir, the officis of preestis in her seruyces, and the dekenes in her ordre, that thei schulden preise and mynystre bifor preestis bi the custom of ech dai; and he ordeynede porteris in her departyngis bi ȝate and ȝate. For Dauid, the man of God,
hadde comaundid so; and bothe preestis and dekenes passiden not fro the comaundementis of the kyng of alle thingis whiche he hadde comaundid.
And Salomon hadde alle costis maad redi in the kepingis of tresouris, fro that dai in whiche he foundide the hows of the Lord til in to the dai in which he perfourmyde it.
Thanne Salomon ȝede in to Asiongaber, and in to Hailath, at the brynke of the reed see, which is in the lond of Edom.
Therfor Iram sente to hym, by the hondis of his seruauntis, schippis, and schippe men kunnyng of the see, and thei ȝeden with the seruauntis of Salomon in to Ophir, and thei token fro thennus foure hundrid and fifti talentis of gold, and brouȝten to kyng Salomon.
Also the queen of Saba, whanne sche hadde herd the fame of Salomon, cam to tempte hym in derk figuris in to Jerusalem, with grete ritchessis, and camels, that baren swete smellynge spices, and ful myche of gold, and preciouse iemmes, ether peerlis. And whanne sche was comun to Salomon, sche spak to hym what euer thingis weren in hir herte.
And Salomon expownede to hir alle thingis whiche sche hadde put forth, and no thing was, which he made not opyn to hir.
And aftir that sche siȝ these thingis, that is, the wisdom of Salomon, and the
hows which he hadde bildid, also and the metis of his boord, and the dwellyng places of seruauntis, and the offices of hise mynystris, and the clothis of hem, and the boteleris, and her clothis, and the sacrifices whiche he offride in the hows of the Lord, spirit was no more in hir for wondryng.
And sche seide to the kyng, The word is trewe, which Y herde in
my lond, of thi vertues and wisdom; Y bileuyde not to telleris, til Y my silf hadde come, and myn yȝen hadden seyn, and Y hadde preued that vnnethis the half of thi wisdom was teld to me; thou hast ouercome the fame bi thi vertues.
Blessid ben thi men, and blessid ben thi seruauntis, these that stonden bifor thee in al tyme, and heren thi wisdom.
Blessid be thi Lord God, that wolde ordeyne thee on his trone kyng of the puple of thi Lord God; treuli for God loueth Israel, and wole saue hym with outen ende, therfor he hath set thee kyng on hym, that thou do domes and riȝtfulnesse.
Forsothe sche ȝaf to the kyng sixe scoore talentis of gold, and ful many swete smellynge spices, and moost preciouse iemmes; ther weren not siche swete smellynge spices, as these whiche the queen of Saba ȝaf to kyng Salomon.
But also the seruauntis of Iram with the seruauntis of Salomon brouȝten gold fro Ophir, and trees of thyne, and most preciouse iemmes;
of whiche, that is, of the trees of thyne, the kyng made grees in the hows of the Lord, and in the hows of the kyng, harpis also, and sautrees to syngeris; siche trees weren neuere seyn in the lond of Juda.
Forsothe Salomon ȝaf to the queen of Saba alle thingis whiche sche wolde, and whiche sche axide, many moo than sche hadde brouȝt to hym. And sche turnede aȝen, and ȝede in to hir lond with hir seruauntis.
Forsothe the weiȝt of gold, that was brouȝt to Salomon bi ech ȝeer, was sixe hundrid and sixe and sixti talentis of
gold, outakun that summe whiche the legatis of dyuerse folkis, and marchauntis weren wont to brynge, and alle the kyngis of Arabie, and the princes of londis, that brouȝten togidere gold and siluer to Salomon.
Therfor kyng Salomon made two hundrid goldun speris of the summe of sixe hundrid floreyns, ether peesis of gold, that weren spendid in ech spere;
and he made thre hundrid goldun scheeldis of thre hundrid floreyns, with whiche ech scheeld was hilid; and the kyng puttide tho in the armure place, that was set in the wode.
Also the kyng made a greet seete of yuer, and clothide it with clennest
gold; and he made sixe grees, bi whiche me stiede to the seete, and a goldun stool, and tweyne armes, oon aȝens the tother, and twei liouns stondynge bisidis
the armes; but also he made twelue othere litle liouns stondynge on sixe grees on euer either side. Siche a seete was not in alle rewmes.
And alle the vessels of the feeste of the kyng weren of gold, and the vessels of the hows of the forest of the Liban weren of pureste gold; for siluer in tho daies was arettid for nouȝt.
For also the schippis of the kyng ȝeden in to Tharsis with the seruauntis of Iram onys in thre ȝeer, and brouȝten fro thennus gold, and siluer, and yuer, and apis, and pokokis.
Therfor kyng Salomon was magnyfied ouer alle kyngis of erthe for richessis and glorie.
And alle the kyngis of londis desireden to se the face of Salomon, for to here the wisdom which God hadde ȝoue in his herte;
and thei brouȝten to hym ȝiftis, vessels of siluer and of gold, clothis and armuris, and swete smellynge spices, horsis and mulis, bi ech ȝeer.
Also Salomon hadde fourti thousynde of horsis in stablis, and twelue thousynde of charis and of knyȝtis; and he ordeynede hem in the citees of charis, and where the kyng was in Jerusalem.
Forsothe he vside power on alle the kyngis, fro the flood Eufrates til to the lond of Filisteis, and til to the termes of Egipt.
And he ȝaf so greet plente of siluer in Jerusalem, as of stoonys, and so greet multitude of cedris, as of sycomoris that growen in feeldi places.
Forsothe horsis weren brouȝt fro Egipt, and fro alle cuntreis.
Sotheli the residue of the formere werkis and the laste of Salomon ben writun in the wordis of Nathan, the prophete, and in the wordis of Achie of Silo, and in the visioun, ether prophesie, of Addo, the prophete, aȝens Jeroboam, sone of Nabath.
Sotheli Salomon regnede in Jerusalem on al Israel fourti ȝeer, and he slepte with his fadris; and thei birieden hym in the citee of Dauid, and Roboam, his sone, regnyde for hym.
Forsothe Roboam ȝede forth in to Sichem; for al Israel came togidere thidur to make hym kyng.
And whanne Jeroboam, the sone of Nabath, that was in Egipt, for he fledde thidur bifor Salomon, hadde herd this, he turnyde aȝen anoon.
And thei clepiden hym, and he cam with al Israel, and thei spaken to Roboam, and
seiden, Thi fadir oppresside vs with ful hard ȝok; comaunde thou liȝtere thingis than thi fader, that settide on vs a greuouse seruage; and releese thou a litil of the birthun, that we serue thee. And
he seide, After thre daies turne ȝe aȝen to me. And whanne the puple was goon,
he took counsel with elde men, that stoden bifor his fadir Salomon, while he lyuyde ȝit, and seide, What counsel ȝyuen ȝe, that Y answere to the puple?
And thei seiden to hym, If thou plesist this puple, and makist hem softe bi meke wordis, thei schulen serue thee in al tyme.
And he forsook the counsel of elde men, and bigan to trete with ȝonge men, that weren nurischid with hym, and weren in his cumpenye.
And he seide to hem, What semeth to ȝou? ether what owe Y answere to this puple, that seide to me, Releese thou the ȝok, which thi fadir puttide on vs?
And thei answeriden, as ȝonge men and nurschyd with hym in delicis, and seiden, Thus thou schalt speke to the puple that seide to thee, Thi fadir made greuouse oure ȝok, releese thou; and thus thou schalt answere to hem, My leeste fyngur is gretter than the leendis of
my fader; my fadir puttide on ȝou a greuouse ȝok, and Y schal leie to a gretter birthun; my fadir beet ȝou with scourgis, forsothe Y schal bete ȝou with scorpiouns, that is, hard knottid roopis.
Therfor Jeroboam and al the puple cam to Roboam in the thridde dai, as he hadde comaundid to hem.
And the kyng answeride harde thingis, after that he hadde
forsake the counsel of the eldere men, and he spak bi the wille of the ȝonge men, My fadir puttide on ȝou a greuouse ȝok, which Y schal make greuousere; my fadir beet ȝou with scourgis, sotheli Y schal bete ȝou with scorpiouns.
And he assentide not to the preieris of the puple; for it was the wille of God, that his word schulde be fillid, which he hadde spoke bi the hond of Ahie of Silo to Jeroboam, sone of Nabath.
Sotheli whanne the kyng seide hardere thingis, al the puple spak thus to hym, No part is to vs in Dauid, nether eritage in the sone of Isai; Israel, turne thou aȝen in to thi tabernaclis, sotheli thou, Dauid, feede thin hows. And Israel ȝede in to hise tabernaclis.
Forsothe Roboam regnede on the sones of Israel, that dwelliden in the citees of Juda.
And kyng Roboam sente Adhuram, that was souereyn ouer the tributis; and the sones of Israel stonyden hym, and he was deed. Certis kyng Roboam hastide to stie in to the chare, and fledde in to Jerusalem.
And Israel ȝede awei fro the hows of Dauid til to this dai. Forsothe it was doon, whanne al Israel hadde herd, that Jeroboam turnede aȝen, thei senten, and clepiden hym, whanne the cumpeny was gaderid, and thei ordeyneden him king on al Israel; and no man, outakun the lynage of Juda aloone, suede the hows of Dauid.
Forsothe Roboam cam in to Jerusalem, and clepide togidere al the hows of Juda and of Beniamyn, til to nyne scoore thousynde of chosen men and werriouris, for to fiȝte aȝens Israel, and for to turne his rewme to hym.
And the word of the Lord was maad to Semeye, the man of
God, and seide, Speke thou to Roboam, the sone of Salomon, kyng of Juda, and to al Israel, which is in Juda and Beniamyn;
The Lord seith these thingis, Ȝe schulen not stie, nethir ȝe schulen fiȝte aȝens ȝoure britheren; ech man turne aȝen in to his hows, for this thing is doon bi my wille. And whanne thei hadden herd the word of the Lord, thei turneden aȝen, and ȝeden not aȝens kyng Jeroboam.
Forsothe Roboam dwellide in Jerusalem,
and he bildide wallid citees in Juda; and bildide Bethleem, and Ethan, and Thecue,
and Bethsur;
and Sochot, and Odollam;
also and Jeth, and Maresa, and Ziph; but
also Huram, and Lachis, and Azecha; and Saraa, and Hailon, and Ebron, that weren in Juda and Beniamyn, ful strong citees.
And whanne he hadde closid tho with wallis, he settide in tho citees princes, and bernes of metis, that is, of oile, and of wyn.
But also in ech citee he made placis of armuris of scheeldis, and speris, and he made tho strong with most diligence; and he regnyde on Juda and Beniamyn.
Sotheli the preestis and dekenes, that weren in al Israel, camen to hym
fro alle her seetis, and forsoken her subarbis and possessiouns, and thei passiden to Juda and to Jerusalem; for Jeroboam and hise aftir comeris hadden cast hem awey, that thei schulden not be set in
preesthod of the Lord; which Jeroboam made to hym preestis of hiȝe places, and of feendis, and of caluys, which he hadde maad.
But also of alle the linagis of Israel, whiche euer ȝauen her herte to seke the Lord God of Israel, thei camen to Jerusalem for to offre her sacrifices bifor the Lord God of her fadris.
And thei strengthiden the rewme of Juda, and strengthiden Roboam, the sone of Salomon, bi thre ȝeer; for thei ȝeden in the weies of Dauid, and of Salomon, oneli bi thre ȝeer.
Forsothe Roboam weddide a wijf Malaoth, the douȝtir of Jerymuth, sone of Dauid, and Abiail, the douȝtir of Heliab, sone of
Ysaye; and sche childide to hym sones, Yeus, and Somorie, and Zerei.
Also after this wijf he took Maacha, the douȝter of Abissalon, and sche childide to hym Abia, and Thai, and Ziza, and Salomyth.
Forsothe Roboam louyde Maacha, the douȝtir of Abissalon, aboue alle hise wyues and secundarie wyues. Forsothe he hadde weddid eiȝtene wyues, sotheli sixti secundarie wyues; and he gendride eiȝte and twenti sones, and sixti douȝtris.
Sotheli he ordeynede Abia, the sone of Maacha, in the heed, duyk ouer alle hise britheren;
for he thouȝte to make Abia kyng, for he was wisere and myȝtiere ouer alle hise sones, and in alle the coostis of Juda and of Beniamyn, and in alle wallid citees; and he ȝaf to hem ful many metis, and he had many wyues.
And whanne the rewme of Roboam was maad strong and coumfortid, he forsook the lawe of the Lord, and al Israel with hym.
Sotheli in the fyuethe ȝeer of the rewme of Roboam Sesach, the kyng of Egipt, stiede in to Jerusalem, for thei
synneden aȝens the Lord; and he stiede with a thousynde and two hundrid charys, and with sixti thousynde of horse men, and no noumbre was of the comyn puple, that cam with hym fro Egipt, that is, Libiens, and Trogoditis, and Ethiopiens.
And he took ful stronge citees in Juda,
and he cam til to Jerusalem. Forsothe Semei, the prophete, entride to Roboam, and to the princes of Juda, whiche fleynge fro Sesach weren gaderid togidere in to Jerusalem. And he seide to hem, The Lord seith these thingis, Ȝe han forsake me, and Y haue forsake ȝou in the hond of Sesach.
And the princes of Israel and the kyng weren astonyed, and seiden, The Lord is iust.
And whanne the Lord hadde seyn that thei weren mekid, the word of the Lord was maad to Semey, and seide, For thei ben mekid, Y schal not distrie hem, and Y schal ȝyue to hem a litil help, and my stronge veniaunce schal not droppe on Jerusalem bi the hond of Sesach.
Netheles thei schulen serue hym, that thei knowe the dyuersitee of my seruyce and of the seruyce of the rewme of londis.
Therfor Sesach, the kyng of Egipt, ȝede a wey fro Jerusalem, aftir that he hadde take awei the tresouris of the hows of the Lord, and of the kyngis hows; and he took alle thingis with hym, and the goldun
scheeldis whiche Salomon hadde maad, for whiche the kyng made brasun scheeldis, and took tho to the princes of scheeld makeris, that kepten the porche of the paleis.
And whanne the kyng entride in to the hows of the Lord, the scheeldmakeris camen, and token tho, and eft brouȝten tho to his armure place.
Netheles for thei weren mekid, the ire of the Lord was turned awei fro hem, and thei weren not don awei outirli; for good werkis weren foundyn also in Juda.
Therfor kyng Roboam was coumfortid in Jerusalem, and regnede. Forsothe he was of oon and fourti ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne, and he regnyde seuentene ȝeer in Jerusalem, the citee which the Lord chees of alle the lynagis of Israel, that he schulde conferme his name there. Forsothe the name of his modir was Naama Amanytis.
And he dide yuel, and he made not redi his herte to seke God.
Sotheli the firste and the laste werkis of Roboam ben writun, and diligentli declarid in the bookis of Semei the profete, and of Abdo the profete.
And Roboam and Jeroboam fouȝten in alle daies aȝens hem silf. And Roboam slepte with hise fadris, and was biried in the citee of Dauid; and Abia, his sone, regnede for hym.
Yn the eiȝtenthe ȝeer of kyng Jeroboam
Abia regnede on Juda; he regnede thre ȝeer in Jerusalem; and the name of hise modir was Mychaie, the douȝter of Vriel of Gabaa. And batel was bitwixe Abia and Jeroboam.
And whanne Abia hadde bigunne batel, and hadde most chyualrouse men, and four hundrid thousynde of chosun men, Jeroboam arayede aȝenward the scheltroun with eiȝte hundrid thousynde of men, and thei weren chosun men and most stronge to batels.
Therfor Abia stood on the hil Semeron, that was in Effraym, and seide, Here thou, Jeroboam
and al Israel; whether ȝe knowen not, that the Lord God of Israel ȝaf to Dauid the rewme on Israel with outen ende, to hym and to hise sones in to the couenaunt of salt, that is, stidefast and
stable? And Jeroboam, the sone of Nabath, the seruaunt of Salomon, sone of Dauid, roos, and rebellide aȝens his lord.
And most veyn men and the sones of Belial weren gaderid to hym, and thei hadden myȝt aȝens Roboam, the sone of Salomon. Certis Roboam was buystuouse, ether fonne, and of feerdful herte, and myȝte not aȝenstonde hem.
Now therfor ȝe seien, that ȝe moun aȝenstonde the rewme of the Lord, which he holdith in possessioun bi the sones of Dauid; and ȝe han a greet multitude of puple, and goldun caluys, whiche Jeroboam made in to goddis to ȝou.
And ȝe han caste awei the preestis of the Lord, the sones of Aaron, and dekenes, and ȝe han maad preestis to ȝou, as alle the puplis of londis han preestis; who euer cometh and halewith his hond in a bole, in oxis, and in seuene wetheris, anoon he is maad preest of hem that ben not goddis.
But oure Lord is God, whom we forsaken not; and preestis of the sones of Aaron mynystren to the Lord, and dekenes ben in
her ordre; and thei offren brent sacrifices to the Lord bi ech dai in the morewtid and euentid, and encense maad bi comaundementis of the lawe; and loues ben set forth in a moost clene boord; and at vs is the goldun candilstik and his lanterne, that it be teendid euere at euentid; forsothe we kepen the comaundementis of our God, whom ȝe han forsake.
Therfor God is duyk in oure oost, and hise preestis, that trumpen and sownen aȝens ȝou; nyle ȝe, sones of Israel, fiȝte aȝens the Lord God of ȝoure fadris, for it spedith not to ȝou.
While he spak these thingis, Jeroboam made redi tresouns bihynde; and whanne he stood euene aȝens the enemyes, he cumpasside with his oost Juda vnwitynge.
And Juda bihelde, and siȝ batel neiȝ euene aȝens, and bihynde the bak; and he criede to the Lord, and preestis bigunnen for to trumpe.
And alle the men of Juda crieden, and, lo! while thei crieden, God made aferd Jeroboam and al Israel, that stood euen aȝens Juda and Abia.
And the men of Israel fledden fro Juda, and God bitook hem in to the hondis of men of Juda.
Therfor Abia and his puple smoot hem with a greet wounde, and there felden doun of hem fyue hundrid thousynde of stronge men woundid.
And the sones of Israel weren maad lowe in that tyme, and the sones of Juda weren coumfortid ful greetli, for thei hadden hopid in the Lord God of her fadris.
Forsothe Abia pursuede Jeroboam fleynge, and took hise cytees, Bethel and hise vilagis, and Jesana with hise vilagis, and Ephron and hise vilagis;
and Jeroboam miȝte no more aȝenstonde in the daies of Abia, whom the Lord smoot, and he was deed.
Therfor Abia, whanne his empire was coumforted, took fourtene wyues, and he gendride two and twenti sones, and sixtene douȝtris.
The residue of wordis of Abia and of his weyes and werkis, ben writun ful diligentli in the book of Abdo, the profete.
Forsothe Abia slepte with hise fadris, and thei birieden hym in the citee of Dauid; and Asa, his sone, regnede for hym. In whos daies the lond restide ten ȝeer.
And Asa dide that, that was good and plesaunt in the siȝt of his God, and he destriede the auteris of straunge worschipyng,
and he destriede hiȝ places, and brak ymagis, and kittide doun woodis;
and he comaundide Juda to seke the Lord God of her fadris, and to do the lawe and alle comaundementis.
And he took awei fro alle the citees of Juda auteris and templis of idols, and he regnede in pees.
And he bildide stronge cytees in Juda; for he was in reste, and no batels risiden in his tymes, for the Lord ȝaf pees.
Forsothe he seide to Juda, Bilde we these cytees, and cumpasse we with wallis, and strengthe we with touris and ȝatis and lockis, as longe as alle thingis ben restful fro batel; for we han souȝte the Lord God of oure fadris, and he hath ȝoue to vs pees bi cumpas. Therfor thei bildiden, and no lettyng was in bildyng.
Sotheli Asa hadde in his oost thre hundrid thousynde of men of Juda berynge scheldis and speris, sotheli of Beniamyn he hadde two hundrid thousynde and fourscoore thousynde of scheeld beeris and of archeris; alle these weren ful stronge men.
Forsothe Zara of Ethiop ȝede out aȝens hem with his oost ten sithis an hundrid thousynde, and with thre hundrid charis, and cam til to Masera.
Certis Aza ȝede aȝens hem, and araiede scheltrun to batel in the valei Sephata, which is bisidis Masera. And he inwardli clepide the Lord
God, and seide, Lord, no dyuersitee is anentis thee, whether thou helpe in fewe, ethir in manye; oure Lord God, helpe thou vs, for we han trist in thee and in thi name, and camen aȝens this multitude; Lord, thou art oure God, a man haue not the maistrye aȝens thee.
Therfor the Lord made aferd Ethiopens bifor Asa and Juda, and Ethiopens fledden;
and Asa and his puple, that was with hym, pursuede hem til to Gerare. And Ethiopens felden doun til to deeth, for thei weren al to-brokun bi the Lord sleynge, and bi his oost fiȝtynge. Therfor
thei token many spuylis, and smitiden alle the citees bi the cumpas of Gerare; for greet drede hadde assailid alle men. And thei rifliden cytees, and baren a weye
myche prey; but also thei destrieden the fooldis of scheep, and token multitude without noumbre of scheep and of camels, and turneden aȝen in to Jerusalem.
Forsothe Azarie, the sone of Obeth, whanne the spirit of the Lord was comyn
in to hym, ȝede out in to the metyng of Asa; and seide to hym, Asa and al Juda and Beniamyn, here ȝe me; the Lord is with ȝou, for ȝe weren with hym; if ȝe seken hym, ȝe schulen fynde hym; sotheli if ȝe forsaken hym, he schal forsake ȝou.
Forsothe many daies schulen passe in Israel with outen veri God, and without preest, and without techere, and without lawe.
And whanne thei turnen aȝen in her angwisch, and crien to the Lord God of Israel, and seken hym, thei schulen fynde hym.
In that tyme schal not be pees to go out and to go in, but dredis on al side on alle the dwelleris of londis.
For a folk schal fiȝte aȝens folk, and a citee aȝens a citee, for the Lord schal
disturble hem in al anguysch; but be ȝe coumfortid, and ȝoure hondis be not slakid; for mede schal be to ȝoure werk.
And whanne Asa hadde herd this thing, that is, the wordis and profesye of Asarie, the sone of Obed, the profete, he was coumfortid, and he dide a wei alle the idols fro al the lond of Juda and of Beniamyn, and fro the citees whiche he hadde take of the hil of Effraym. And he halewide the auter of the Lord, that was bifor the porche of the hows of the Lord.
And he gaderide togidere al Juda and Beniamyn, and with hem the comelyngis of Effraym, and of Manasses, and of Symeon; for manye of Israel, seynge that his Lord God was with hym, fledden ouer to hym.
And whanne thei hadden comun in to Jerusalem, in the thridde monethe, in the fiftenthe ȝeer of the rewme
of Asa, thei offriden to the Lord in that dai, bothe of the spuylis and of the prey, which thei hadden brouȝt, seuene hundrid oxis, and seuene thousynde wetheris.
And Asa entride bi custom to make strong the boond of pees, that thei schulden seke the Lord God of her fadris in al her herte, and in al her soule.
Sotheli he seide, If ony man sekith not the Lord God of Israel, die he, fro the leeste til to the mooste, fro man til to womman.
And alle that weren in Juda sworen with cursyng to the Lord, with greet vois, in hertli song, and in sown of trumpe, and in
sown of clariouns; for thei sworen in al her herte, and in al the wille thei souȝten hym, and founden hym; and the Lord ȝaf to hem reste bi cumpas.
But also he puttide doun Maacha, the modir of Asa the kyng, fro the streit empire, for sche hadde made in a wode the symylacre, ether licnesse, of a mannus ȝerde; and he al to-brak al that symylacre, and pownede it in to gobetis, and brente it in the stronde of Cedron.
But hiȝ places weren left in Israel; netheles the herte of Asa was riȝtful in alle hise daies.
And he brouȝte in to the hows of the Lord tho thingis that his fadir avowide, siluer and gold, and dyuerse purtenaunce of vessels;
sotheli batel was not til to the threttithe ȝeer of the rewme of Asa.
Forsothe in the sixe and thrittithe ȝeer of his rewme Baasa, the kyng of Israel, stiede in to Juda, and cumpasside Rama with a wal, that no man of the rewme of Asa myȝte go out ether entre sikirli.
Sotheli Asa brouȝte forth gold and siluer fro the tresours of the hows of the Lord, and fro the kyngis tresouris; and sente to Benadab, kyng of Sirie, that dwellide in
Damask, and seide, Boond of pees is bitwixe me and thee, and my fadir and thi fadir hadden acordyng; wherfor Y sente to thee siluer and gold, that whanne thou hast broke the boond of pees, which thou hast with Baasa, king of Israel, thou make hym to go awei fro me.
And whanne this was foundun, Benadab sente princes of hise oostis to the citees of Israel, whiche smytiden Ahion, and Dan, and Abelmaym, and alle the wallid citees of Neptalym.
And whanne Baasa hadde herd this, he ceesside to bilde Rama, and left his werk.
Forsothe kyng Asa took al Juda, and thei token fro Rama the stonys and trees, whiche Baasa hadde maad redi to bildyng; and he bildide of tho Gabaa, and Maspha.
In that tyme Anany, the profete, cam to Asa, kyng of Juda, and seide to hym, For thou haddist trist in the kyng of Sirie, and not in thi Lord God, herfor the oost of the kyng of Sirie aschapide fro thin hond.
Whether Ethiopiens and Libiens weren not many mo in charis, and knyȝtis, and ful greet multitude; whiche whanne thou haddist bileuyd to the Lord, he bitook in to thin hondis?
For the iȝen of the Lord biholden al the erthe, and ȝyuen strengthe to hem, that with perfit herte bileuen in to hym. Therfor thou hast do folili, and for this, ȝhe, in present tyme batels schulen rise aȝens thee.
And Asa was wrooth aȝens the prophete, and comaundide hym to be sent in to stockis. Forsothe the Lord hadde indignacioun greetli on this thing, and killide ful many of the puple in that tyme.
Sotheli the firste and the laste werkis of Asa ben writun in the book of kyngis of Juda and of Israel.
Forsothe Asa was sijk ful gretli in the akynge of feet, in the nyne and thrittithe ȝeer of his rewme; and nether in his sikenesse he souȝte the Lord, but tristide more in the craft of lechis.
And Asa slepte with hise fadris, and he was deed in the oon and fourtithe ȝeer of his rewme.
And thei birieden him in his sepulcre, which he hadde maad to hym silf in the cytee of Dauid; and thei puttiden hym on his bed ful of swete smellynge spices and oynementis of hooris, that weren maad togidere bi the craft of oynement makeris, and thei brenten on hym with ful greet cost.
Forsothe Josaphat, his sone, regnyde for hym; and he hadde the maistrye aȝens Israel.
And he settide noumbris of knyȝtis in alle the citees of Juda, that weren cumpassid with wallis, and he disposide strong holdis in the lond of Juda, and in the citees of Effraym, whiche Asa, his fadir, hadde take.
And the Lord was with Josaphat, whiche ȝede in the firste weies of Dauid, his fadir; he hopide not
in Baalym, but in the Lord God of Dauid, his fadir, and he ȝede in the comaundementis of God, and not bi the synnes of Israel.
And the Lord confermyde the rewme in his hond; and al Juda ȝaf ȝiftis to Josaphat, and ritchessis with outen noumbre, and myche glorie weren maad to hym.
And whanne his herte hadde take hardynesse for the weies of the Lord, he took awei also hiȝ placis and wodis fro Juda.
Forsothe in the thridde ȝeer of his rewme he sente of hise princes Benail, and Abdie, and Zacarie, and Nathanael, and Mychee, that thei
schulden teche in the citees of Juda; and with hem he sente dekenes Semeye, and Nathanye, and Zabadie, and Azahel, and Semyramoth, and Jonathan, and Adonye, and Thobie, and Abadonye, dekenes; and with hem he sente Elisama and Joram,
preestis; and thei tauȝten the puple in Juda, and hadden the book of the lawe of the Lord; and thei cumpassiden alle the citees of Juda, and tauȝten al the puple.
Therfor the drede of the Lord was maad on al the rewmes of londis, that weren bi cumpas of Juda; and tho dursten not fiȝte aȝens Josaphat.
But also Filisteis brouȝten ȝiftis to Josaphat, and tol of siluer; and men of Arabie brouȝten scheep seuene thousynde, and seuene hundrid of wetheris, and so many buckis of geet.
Therfor Josaphat encreesside, and was magnified til in to an hiȝ; and he bildide in Juda housis at the licnesse of touris, and stronge citees;
and he made redi many werkis in the citees of Juda. Also men werriouris and
stronge men weren in Jerusalem; of whiche this is the noumbre, bi the housis and meynees of alle in Juda. Duyk Eduas was prince of the oost, and with hym weren thre hundrid thousynde ful stronge men.
Aftir hym was Johannan prince, and with hym weren two hundrid thousynde and foure scoore thousynde.
After this also Amasye, the sone of Zechri, was halewid to the Lord, and with hym weren two hundrid thousynde of stronge men.
Eliada myȝti to batels suede this Amasie, and with hym weren two hundrid thousynde of men holdynge bouwe and scheeld.
Aftir this was also Josaphat, and with hym weren an hundrid thousynde and foure scoore thousynde of redi knyȝtis.
Alle these weren at the hond of the kyng, outakun othere, whiche he hadde put in wallid cytees and in al Juda.
Therfor Josaphat was riche and ful noble, and bi affynyte, ethir alie, he was ioyned to Achab.
And aftir ȝeeris he cam doun to hym in to Samarie; at whos comyng Achab killide ful many wetheris and oxis, and to the puple that cam with hym; and he counseilide hym to stie in to Ramoth of Galaad.
And Achab, the kyng of Israel, seide to Josaphat, kyng of Juda, Come thou with me in to Ramoth of Galaad. To whom he answeride, As and Y am, thou art; as thi puple, so and my puple; and we schulen be with thee in batel.
And Josaphat seide to the kyng of Israel, Y biseche, counsele thou in present tyme the word of the Lord.
Therfor the kyng of Israel gaderide togidere foure hundrid men of prophetis, and seide to hem, Owen we to go in to Ramath of Galaad for to fiȝte, ethir take reste? And thei seiden, Stie ȝe, and God schal bitake in the hond of the king.
And Josaphat seide, Whether no profete of the Lord is here, that we axe also of hym?
And the kyng of Israel seide to Josaphat, O man is, of whom we moun axe the wille of the Lord, but and Y hate hym, for he prophecieth not good, but yuel to me in al tyme; sothely it is Mychee, the sone of Jebla. And Josaphat seide to hym, Kyng, speke thou not in this maner.
Therfor the kyng of Israel clepide oon of the geldyngis, and seide to hym, Clepe thou soone Mychee, the sone of Jebla.
Forsothe the kyng of Israel and Josaphat, the kyng of Juda, saten euer eithir in his seete, and weren clothid in kyngis aray; forsothe thei saten in the cornfloor, ether large hows, bisidis the ȝate of Samarie; and alle the prophetis profesieden bifor hem.
Forsothe Sedechie, the sone of Cananee, made to hym yrone hornes, and seide, The Lord seith these thingis, With these thou schalt wyndewe Sirie, til thou al to-brake it.
And alle prophetis profesieden in lijk maner, and seiden, Stie thou in to Ramoth of Galaad, and thou schalt haue prosperite; and the Lord schal bitake hem in to the hondis of the kyng.
Forsothe the messanger, that ȝede to clepe Mychee, seide to hym, Lo! the wordis of alle prophetis tellen with o mouth goodis to the kyng; therfor, Y preye thee, that thi word disente not fro hem, and that thou speke prosperitees.
To whom Mychee answeride, The Lord lyueth, for what euer thingis my Lord spekith to me, Y schal speke these thingis. Therfor he cam to the kyng.
To whom the kyng seide, Mychee, owen we go in to Ramoth of Galaad to fiȝte, ether take reste? To whom he answeride, Stie ȝe, for alle prosperitees schulen come, and enemyes schulen be bitakun in to ȝoure hondis.
And the kyng seide, Eft and eft Y charge thee, that thou speke not to me no but that that is soth in the name of the Lord.
And he seide, Y siȝ al Israel scaterid in the hillis, as scheep with out scheepherde. And the Lord seide, These men han not lordis; ech man turne aȝen in to his hows in pees.
The kyng of Israel seide to Josaphat, Whether Y seide not to thee, that he profesiede not ony good to me, but tho thingis that ben yuele?
And therfor Mychee seide, Here ȝe the word of the Lord. Y siȝ the Lord sittynge in his trone, and al the oost of heuene stondynge nyȝ him at the riȝtside and leftside.
And the Lord seide, Who schal disseyue Achab, the kyng of Israel, that he stie, and falle doun in Ramoth of Galaad? And whanne oon seide in this maner, and another seide in another maner,
a spirit cam forth, and stood bifor the Lord, and seide, Y schal disseyue hym. To whom the Lord seide, Wherynne, therfor schalt thou disseyue?
And he answeride, Y schal go out, and Y schal be a fals spirit in the mouth of alle hise profetis. And the Lord seide, Thou schalt disseyue, and thou schalt haue the maystri; go thou out, and do so.
Now therfor, lo! the Lord hath ȝoue a spirit of leesyng in the mouth of alle thi prophetis, and the Lord spak yuels of thee.
Forsothe Sedechie, the sone of Chananee, neiȝide, and smoot the cheke of Mychee, and seide, Bi what weye passide the Spirit of the Lord fro me to speke to thee?
And Mychee seide, Thou thi silf schalt se in that dai, whanne thou schalt entre fro closet in to closet, that thou be hid.
Sotheli the kyng of Israel comaundide, seiynge, Take ȝe Mychee, and lede ȝe hym to Amon, prince of the citee, and to Joas,
the sone of Amalech; and ȝe schulen seie, The kyng seith these thingis, Sende ȝe this man in to prisoun, and ȝyue ȝe to hym a litil of breed, and a litil of watir, til Y turne aȝen in pees.
And Mychee seide, If thou turnest aȝen in pees, the Lord spak not in me. And he seide, Alle puplis here ȝe.
Therfor the kyng of Israel, and Josaphat, the kyng of Juda, stieden in to Ramoth of Galaad.
And the kyng of Israel seide to Josaphat, Y schal chaunge clothing, and so Y schal go to fiȝte; but be thou clothid in thi clothis. Therfor whanne the kyng of Israel hadde chaungid clothing, he cam to batel.
Forsothe the kyng of Sirie comaundide to the duykis of his multitude of knyȝtis, and seide, Fiȝte ȝe not aȝens the leeste, nether aȝens the mooste; no but aȝens the kyng aloone of Israel.
Therfor whanne the princes of the multitude of knyȝtis hadden seyn Josaphat, thei seiden, This is the kyng of Israel; and thei cumpassiden hym, and fouȝten. And he criede to the Lord; and the Lord helpide hym, and turnede hem awey fro hym.
Sotheli whanne the duykis of the multitude of knyȝtis hadden herd, that it was not the kyng of Israel, thei leften hym.
Forsothe it bifelde, that oon of the puple schette an arewe in to vncerteyn, and smoot the kyng of Israel bitwixe the necke and the schuldris. And he seide to his charietere, Turne thin hond, and lede me out of the scheltrun; for Y am woundid.
And the batel was endid in that dai. Certis the kyng of Israel stood in his chare aȝens men of Sirye til to euentid, and he diede, whanne the sunne ȝede doun.
Forsothe Josaphat, kyng of Juda, turnede aȝen pesibli in to his hows in to Jerusalem.
Whom the profete Hieu, the sone of Ananye, mette, and seide to hym, Thou ȝyuest help to a wickid man, and thou art ioyned bi frendschip to hem that haten the Lord; and therfor sotheli thou deseruedist
the wraththe of the Lord; but good werkis ben foundyn in thee, for thou didist awey wodis fro the lond of Juda, and thou hast maad redi thin herte, for to seke the Lord God of thi fadris.
Therfor Josaphat dwellide in Jerusalem; and eft he ȝede out to the puple fro Bersabee til to the hil of Effraym, and he clepide hem aȝen to the Lord God of her fadris.
And he ordeynede iugis of the lond in alle the strengthid citees of Juda, bi ech place.
And he comaundide to the iugis, and seide, Se ȝe, what ȝe doen; for ȝe vsen not the doom of man, but of the Lord; and what euere thing ȝe demen,
schal turne in to ȝou; the drede of the Lord be with ȝou, and do ȝe alle thingis with diligence; for anentis ȝoure Lord God is no wickidnesse, nether takynge of persoones, nether coueitise of ȝiftis.
Also in Jerusalem Josaphat ordeynede dekenes, and preestis, and the princes of meynees of Israel, that thei schulden deme the doom and cause of the Lord to the dwellers of it.
And he comaundide to hem, and seide, Thus ȝe schulen do in the drede of the Lord, feithfuli and in perfite herte.
Ech cause that cometh to ȝou of ȝoure britheren, that dwellen in her citees, bitwixe kynrede and kynrede, where euere is questioun of the lawe, of the comaundement, of cerymonyes, ether sacrifices, of iustifyingis, schewe ȝe to hem, that thei do not synne aȝens the Lord, and that wraththe com not on ȝou and on ȝoure britheren. Therfor ȝe doynge thus schulen not do synne.
Forsothe Amarie, ȝoure preest and bischop, schal be souereyn in these thingis, that perteynen to God. Sotheli Zabadie, the sone of Ismael, which is duyk in the hows of Juda, schal be on tho werkis that perteynen to the office of the kyng, and ȝe han maistris dekenes bifor ȝou; be ȝe coumfortid, and do ȝe diligentli, and the Lord schal be with ȝou in goodis.
Aftir these thingis the sones of Moab, and the sones of Amon, and with hem of Idumeis, weren gaderid togidere to Josaphat, for to fiȝte aȝens hym.
And messangeris camen, and schewiden to Josaphat, and seiden, A greet multitude of tho placis that ben biȝondis the see, and of Sirie, is comun aȝens thee; and, lo! thei stonden in Asasonthamar, which is Engaddi.
Forsothe Josaphat was aferd by drede, and ȝaf hym silf al for to preye the Lord, and prechide fastynge to al Juda.
And Juda was gaderid togidere for to preye the Lord, but also alle men camen fro her citees for to biseche hym.
And whanne Josaphat hadde stonde in the myddis of the cumpeny of Juda and of Jerusalem, in the hows of the Lord, bifor
the newe large place, he seide, Lord God of oure fadris, thou art God in heuene, and thou art lord of alle rewmes of folkis; strengthe and power ben in thin hond, and noon may aȝenstonde thee.
Whether not thou, oure God, hast slayn alle the dwelleris of this lond bifor thi puple Israel, and hast ȝoue it to the seed of Abraham, thi freend, withouten ende?
And thei dwelliden therynne, and bildiden therinne a seyntuarie to thi name, and
seiden, If yuelis comen on vs, the swerd of doom, pestilence, and hungur, we schulen stonde bifor this hows withouten ende in thi siȝt, in which hows thi name is clepid, and we schulen crie to thee in oure tribulaciouns; and thou schalt here vs, and schalt make vs saaf.
Now therfor lo! the sones of Amon and of Moab and the hil of Seir, bi whiche thou grauntidist not to the sones of Israel for to passe, whanne thei ȝeden out of Egipt, but thei bowiden awei fro hem, and killiden not
hem, thei doon aȝenward, and enforsen to caste vs out of the possessioun, which
thou, oure God, hast ȝoue to vs; therfor whether thou schalt not deme hem? Treuli in vs is not so greet strengthe, that we moun aȝenstonde this multitude, that felde yn on vs; but sithen we witen not what we owen to do, we han oneli this residue, that we dresse oure iȝen to thee.
Sotheli al Juda stood bifor the Lord, with her litle children and wyues and fre children.
Forsothe Hiaziel, the sone of Zacarie, sone of Ananye, sone of Hieyel, sone of Machanye, was a dekene, and of the sones of Asaph, on whom the Spirit of the Lord was maad in the
myddis of the cumpeny, and he seide, Al Juda, and ȝe that dwellen in Jerusalem, and thou, king Josaphat, perseyue ȝe, the Lord seith these thingis to ȝou, Nyle ȝe drede, nether be ȝe aferd of this multitude, for it is not ȝoure batel, but Goddis batel.
To morewe ȝe schulen stie aȝens hem; for thei schulen stie bi the side of the hil, bi name Seys, and ȝe schulen fynde hem in the hiȝnesse of the stronde, which is aȝens the wildirnesse of Jheruhel.
For it schulen not be ȝe, that schulen fiȝte; but oneli stonde ȝe trustili, and ȝe schulen se the help of the Lord on ȝou. A! Juda and Jerusalem, nyle ȝe drede, nether be ȝe aferd; to morewe ȝe schulen go out aȝens hem, and the Lord schal be with ȝou.
Therfor Josaphat, and Juda, and alle the dwelleris of Jerusalem, felden lowli on the erthe bifor the Lord, and worschypiden hym.
Forsothe the dekenes of the sones of Caath, and of the sones of Chore, herieden the Lord God of Israel with greet vois an hiȝ.
And whanne thei hadden rise eerli, thei ȝeden not bi the deseert of Thecue; and whanne thei hadden gon forth, Josaphat stood in the myddis of hem, and seide, Juda and alle the dwelleris of Jerusalem, here ȝe me; bileue ȝe in ȝoure Lord God, and ȝe schulen be sikur; bileue ȝe to hise prophetis, and alle prosperitees schulen come.
And he ȝaf counsel to the puple, and he ordeynede the syngeris of the Lord, that thei schulden herye hym in her cumpanyes, and that thei schulden go bifor the oost, and seie with acordynge vois, Knouleche ȝe to the Lord, for he is good; for his merci is in to the world.
And whanne thei bigunnen to synge heriyngis, the Lord turnede the buyschementis of hem in to hem silf, that is, of the sones of Amon and of Moab and of the hil of Seir, that ȝeden out to fiȝte aȝens Juda; and thei weren slayn.
For whi the sones of Amon and of Moab risiden togidere aȝens the dwelleris of the hil of Seir, to sle, and to do awey hem; and whanne thei hadden do this in werk, thei weren turned also in to hem silf, and felden doun togidere bi woundis ech of othere.
Certis whanne Juda was comun to the denne, that biholdith the wildirnesse, he siȝ afer al the large cuntrei ful of deed bodies, and that noon was left, that miȝte ascape deeth.
Therfor Josaphat cam, and al the puple with hym, to drawe awey the spuylis of deed men, and thei founden among the deed bodies dyuerse purtenaunce of houshold, and clothis, and ful preciouse vessels; and thei rauyischiden in dyuerse maneres, so that thei myȝten not bere alle thingis, nether thei myȝten take awei the spuylis bi thre daies, for the greetnesse of prey.
Sotheli in the fourthe dai thei weren gaderid togidere in the valey of Blessyng; forsothe for thei blessiden the Lord there, thei clepiden that place the valei of Blessyng til in to present dai.
And ech man of Juda turnede aȝen, and the dwelleris of Jerusalem, and Josaphat bifor hem, in to Jerusalem with greet gladnesse; for the Lord God hadde ȝoue to hem ioye of her enemyes.
And thei entriden in to Jerusalem with sawtrees, and harpis, and trumpis, in to the hows of the Lord.
Forsothe the drede of the Lord felde on alle the rewmes of londis, whanne thei hadden herd, that the Lord hadde fouȝte aȝens the enemies of Israel.
And the rewme of Josaphat restide; and the Lord ȝaf pees to hym bi cumpas.
Therfor Josaphat regnede on Juda; and he was of fyue and thritti ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne; sotheli he regnede fyue and twenti ȝeer in Jerusalem; and the name of his modir was Azuba, the douȝtir of Selathi.
And he ȝede in the weie of Asa his fadir, and bowide not fro it, and he dide what euer thingis weren plesaunt bifor the Lord.
Netheles he dide not awei hiȝ thingis; ȝit the puple hadde not dressid her herte to the Lord God of her fadris.
Forsothe the residue of the formere and the laste dedis of Josaphat ben writun in the book of Hieu, the sone of Anany, which he ordeynede in the book of kyngis of Israel.
After these thingis Josaphat, kyng of Juda, made frendschipis with Ocozie, kyng of Israel, whose werkis weren ful
yuele; and he was parcener that thei maden schippis, that schulden go in to Tharsis; and thei maden o schip in to Asiongaber.
Sotheli Eliezer, sone of Dodan, of Maresa, profesiede to Josaphat, and seide, For thou haddist boond of pees with Ocozie, the Lord smoot thi werkis; and the schippis ben brokun, and myȝten not go in to Tharsis.
Forsothe Josaphat slepte with hise fadris, and was biried with hem in the citee of Dauid; and Joram, his sone, regnede for hym.
And he hadde britheren, the sones of Josaphat, Azarie, Jahiel, and Zacarie, Anany, and Mychael, and Saphatie; alle these weren the sones of Josaphat, kyng of Juda.
And her fadir ȝaf to hem many ȝiftis of gold and of siluer, and rentis, with strongeste citees in Juda; but he ȝaf the rewme to Joram, for he was the firste gendrid.
Forsothe Joram roos on the rewme of his fadir; and whanne he hadde confermyd hym silf, he killide alle hise britheren bi swerd, and summe of the princes of Juda.
Joram was of two and thritti ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne; and he regnede eiȝte ȝeer in Jerusalem.
And he ȝede in the weies of the kyngis of Israel, as the hows of Achab hadde do, for the douȝter of Achab was his wijf; and he dide yuel in the siȝt of the Lord.
But the Lord nolde distrie the hows of Dauid, for the couenaunt which he hadde maad with Dauid, and for he hadde bihiȝte to ȝyue to hym a lanterne, and to hise sones in al tyme.
In tho daies Edom rebellide, that it was not suget to Juda, and it ordeynede a kyng to it silf.
And whanne Joram hadde passide with hise princes, and al the multitude of knyȝtis, that was with hym, he roos bi niȝt, and smoot Edom, that cumpasside him, and alle hise duykis of his multitude of knyȝtis.
Netheles Edom rebellide, that it was not vndir the lordschip of Juda til to this dai. In that tyme also Lobna ȝede awei, that it was not vndur the hond of hym; for he hadde forsake the Lord God of hise fadris.
Ferthermore he made hiȝe places in the citees of Juda, and made the dwelleris of Jerusalem to do fornycacioun, that is, idolatrie, and Juda to breke the lawe.
Forsothe lettris weren brouȝt to hym fro Elie, the prophete, in whiche it was writun, The Lord God of
Dauid, thi fadir, seith these thingis, For thou ȝedist not in the weies of Josaphat, thi fadir, and in the weie of Asa, kyng of Juda, but thou ȝedist bi the weie of the kyngis of Israel, and madist Juda and the dwelleris of Jerusalem to do fornicacioun, and suedist the fornicacioun of the hows of Achab; ferthermore and thou hast slayn thi britheren and the hows of thi
fadir, that weren betere than thou; lo! the Lord schal smyte thee with a greet veniaunce, and thi puple, and thi sones,
and wyues, and al thi catel; sotheli thou schalt be sijk with the worste sorewe of wombe, til thin entrailis go out litil and litil bi ech dai.
Therfor the Lord reiside aȝens Joram the spirit of Filisteis and Arabeis, that marchen with Ethiopiens;
and thei stieden in to the lond of Juda, and wastiden it, and thei token awei al the catel, that was foundun in the hows of the kyng, ferthermore and hise sones, and wyues; and no sone was left to hym, no but Joachaz, that was the leeste in birthe.
And ouer alle these thingis the Lord smoot hym with vncurable sorewe of the wombe.
And whanne dai cam aftir a dai, and the spaces of tymes weren turned aboute, the cours of twey ȝeer was fillid; and so he was wastid bi long rot, so that he castide out also his entrailis, and so he wantide sorewe and liyf togidere, and he was deed in the werste sikenesse. And the puple dide not to hym seruyce of deed men bi the custom of brennyng, as it hadde do to hise grettere, ether auncetris.
He was of two and thritti ȝeer whanne he bigan to regne, and he regnede eiȝte ȝeer in Jerusalem, and he ȝede not riȝtfuli; and thei birieden hym in the citee of Dauid, netheles not in the sepulcre of kingis.
Forsothe the dwelleris of Jerusalem ordeyneden Ocozie, his leeste sone, kyng for hym; for theues of Arabeis, that felden in to the castels, hadden slayn alle the grettere in birthe, that weren bifor hym. And Ocozie, the sone of Joram, kyng of Juda, regnede.
Ocozie was of two and fourti ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne, and he regnede o ȝeer in Jerusalem; the name of his modir was Athalia, the douȝter of Amry.
But he entride bi the weie of the hows of Achab; for his modir compellide hym to do yuele.
Therfor he dide yuel in the siȝt of the Lord, as the hows of Achab; for thei weren counselouris to hym in to his perischyng, aftir the deth of his fadir;
and he ȝede in the counsele of hem. And he ȝede with Joram, the sone of Achab, kyng of Israel, in to batel aȝens Azahel, kyng of Sirye, in to Ramoth of Galaad. And men of Sirie woundiden Joram;
which turnede aȝen for to be heelid in Jezrahel; for he hadde take many woundis in the forseid batel. Therfor Ocozie, kyng of Juda, the sone of Joram, ȝede doun to visite Joram, the sone of
Achab, sijk in Jezrahel; for it was Goddis wille aȝens Ocozie, that he cam to Joram. And whanne he was comun, he ȝede out with hym aȝens Hieu, the sone of Namsi, whom God anoyntide, that he schulde do awey the hows of Achab.
Therfor whanne Hieu destriede the hows of Achab, he foond the princis of Juda, and the sones of the britheren of Ocozie, that mynystriden to hym; and he killide hem.
And he souȝte thilke Ocozie, and cauȝte him hid in Samarie, and after that he was brouȝt to Hieu, Hieu killide hym; and thei birieden hym, for he was the sone of Josaphat, that hadde souȝt God in al his herte. And noon hope was more, that ony of the generacioun of Ocozie schulde regne.
For Athalia, his modir, siȝ, that hir sone was deed, and sche roos, and killide alle the kyngis generacioun of the hows of Joram.
Forsothe Josabeth, the douȝter of the kyng, took Joas, the sone of Ocozie, and stal hym fro the myddis of the sones of the kyng, whanne thei weren slayn; and sche hidde hym with his nurse in the closet of beddis. Forsothe Josabeth, that hadde hid hym, was the douȝtir of kyng Joram, and wijf of Joiada, the bischop, and the sister of Ocozie; and therfor Athalia killide not hir.
Therfor he was hid with hem in the hows of God sixe ȝeer, in whiche Athalia regnede on the lond.
Forsothe in the seuenthe ȝeer Joiada was coumfortid, and took centuriouns, that is, Azarie, sone of Jeroboam, and Ismael, the sone of Johannam, and Azarie, the sone of Obeth, and Maasie, the sone of Adaie, and Elisaphat, the sone of Zechri; and he made with hem a counsel and a boond of pees.
Which cumpassiden Juda, and gaderiden togidere dekenes of alle the citees of Juda, and the princes of the meynees of Israel, and camen in to Jerusalem.
Therfor al the multitude made couenaunt in the hows of the Lord with the kyng. And Joiada seide to hem, Lo! the sone of the kyng schal regne, as the Lord spak on the sones of Dauid.
Therfor this is the word, which ȝe schulen do.
The thridde part of ȝou that ben comun to the sabat, of preestis, and of dekenes, and of porterys, schal be in the ȝatis; sotheli the thridde part schal be at the hows of the kyng; and the thridde part schal be at the ȝate, which is clepid of the foundement. Forsothe al the tother comyn puple be in the large places of
the hows of the Lord; and noon other man entre in to the hows of the Lord, no but preestis, and thei that mynystren of the dekenes; oneli entre thei, that ben halewid, and al the tother comyn puple kepe the kepyngis of the Lord.
Forsothe the dekenes cumpasse the kyng, and ech man haue hise armuris; and if ony othere man entrith in to the temple, be he slayn; and be thei with the kyng entrynge and goynge out.
Therfor the dekenes and al Juda diden bi alle thingis, which Joiada, the bischop, hadde comaundid; and alle token the men, that weren with hem, and camen bi the ordre of sabat with hem, that hadden fillid now the sabat, and schulen go out.
For Joiada, the bischop, suffride not the cumpenyes to go awei, that weren wont to come oon after the tother bi ech wouke. And Joiada, the preest, ȝaf to the centuriouns speris, and scheeldis, and bokeleris of kyng Dauid, whiche he hadde halewid in to the hows of the Lord.
And he ordeynede al the puple, of hem that helden swerdis, at the riȝt side of the temple til to the left side of the temple, bifor the auter and the temple, bi cumpas of the king.
And thei ledden out the sone of the kyng, and settiden a diademe on hym; and thei ȝauen to hym in his hond the lawe to be holdun, and thei maden hym kyng. And Joiada, the bischop, and his sones anoyntiden hym; and thei preiden hertli, and seiden, The kyng lyue!
And whanne Athalia hadde herd this thing, that is, the vois of men rennynge and preisynge the kyng, sche entride to the puple, in to the temple of the Lord.
And whanne sche hadde seyn the kyng stondynge on the grees in the entryng, and the princes and cumpenyes of knyȝtis aboute hym, and al the puple of the lond ioiynge, and sownynge with trumpis, and syngynge togidere with orguns of dyuerse kynde, and the vois of men preisynge, sche to-rente hir clothis, and seide, Tresouns! tresouns!
Sotheli Joiada, the bischop, ȝede out to the centuriouns, and princes of the oost, and seide to hem, Lede ȝe hir with out the purseyntis, ethir closyngis, of the temple, and be sche slayn with outforth bi swerd; and the preest comaundide, that sche schulde not be slayn in the hows of the Lord.
And thei settiden hondis on hir nol; and whanne she hadde entrid in to the ȝate of the horsis, of the kyngis hows, thei killiden hir there.
Forsothe Joiada couenauntide a boond of pees bitwixe him silf and al the puple and the kyng, that it schulde be the puple of the Lord.
Therfor al the puple entride in to the hows of Baal, and distrieden it, and braken the auteris and symylacris therof; but thei killiden bifor the auteris Mathan, the preest of Baal.
Forsothe Joiada ordeynede souereyns in the hows of the Lord, that vndur the hondis of preestis, and of dekenes, whiche Dauid departide in the hows of the Lord, thei schulden offre brent sacrifices to the Lord, as it is writun in the book of Moises, in ioie and songis, by the ordynaunce of Dauid.
Also he ordeynede porteris in the ȝatis of the hows of the Lord, that an vnclene man in ony thing schulde not entre in to it.
And he took the centuriouns, and strongeste men, and princes of the puple, and al the comyn puple of the lond. And thei maden the kyng to go doun fro the hows of the Lord, and to entre bi the myddis of the hiȝere ȝate in to the hows of the kyng; and thei settiden hym in the kyngis trone.
And al the puple of the lond was glad, and the citee restide; forsothe Athalia was slayn bi swerd.
Joas was of seuene ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne, and he regnyde fourti ȝeer in Jerusalem; the name of his modir was Sebia of Bersabee.
And he dide that, that was good bifor the Lord, in alle the daies of Joiada, the preest.
Sotheli and Joas took twei wyues, of whyche he gendride sones and douȝtris.
After whiche thingis it pleside Joas to reparele the hows of the Lord.
And he gaderide togidere preestis and dekenes, and seide to hem, Go ȝe out to the citees of Juda, and gadere ȝe of al Israel money, to the reparelyng of the temple of ȝoure Lord God, bi ech ȝeer; and do ȝe this hiȝyngli. Certis the dekenes diden necgligentli.
And the kyng clepide Joiada, the prince, and seide to hym, Whi was it not charge to thee, to constreyne the dekenes to brynge yn money of Juda and of Jerusalem, which money was ordeyned of Moises, the seruaunt of the Lord, that al the multitude of Israel schulde brynge it in to the tabernacle of witnessyng?
For the worste Athalia, and hir sones, distrieden the hows of God; and of alle thingis, that weren halewid to the temple of the Lord, thei ourneden the temple of Baalym.
Therfor the kyng comaundide, and thei maden an arke, and settiden it bisidis the ȝate of the Lord with out forth.
And it was prechid in Juda and Jerusalem, that ech man schulde brynge to the Lord the prijs, which Moyses, the seruaunt of God, ordeynede on al Israel, in deseert.
And alle the princes and al the puple weren glad, and thei entriden, and brouȝten, and senten in to the arke of the Lord, so that it was fillid.
And whanne it was tyme, that thei schulden bere the arke bifor the kyng bi the hondis of dekenes, for thei sien myche money, the clerk of the kyng entride, and he whom the firste preest hadde ordeynede, and thei schedden out the money, that was in the arke; sotheli thei baren aȝen the arke to his place. And so thei diden bi alle daies, and money with
out noumbre was gaderid togidere; which the kyng and Joiada ȝauen to hem that weren souereyns of the werkis of the hows of the Lord. And thei hiriden therof kitteris of stonys, and crafti men of alle werkis, that thei schulden reparele the hows of the Lord; also thei hiriden smythis of yrun, and of bras, that that thing schulde be vndurset, that bigan to falle.
