Thei that wrouȝten diden craftili, and the crasyng of the wallis was stoppid bi the hondis of hem; and thei reisiden the hows of the Lord in to the formere staat, and maden it to stonde stidfastli.
And whanne thei hadden fillid alle werkis, thei brouȝten bifor the kyng and Joiada the tother part of the money, of which money vessels weren maad in to the seruyce of the temple, and to brent sacrifices; also viols, and othere vessels of gold and of siluer weren maad therof. And brent sacrifices weren offrid in the hows of the Lord contynueli, in alle the daies of Joiada.
Forsothe Joiada ful of daies wexide eld, and he was deed, whanne he was of an hundrid ȝeer and thritti;
and thei birieden hym in the citee of Dauid with kyngis; for he hadde do good with Israel, and with his hows.
But aftir that Joiada diede, the princes of Juda entriden, and worschipiden the kyng, which was flaterid with her seruices, and assentide to hem.
And thei forsoken the temple of the Lord God of her fadris, and seruyden idols in wodis, and grauen ymagis; and the ire of the Lord was maad aȝens Juda and Jerusalem for this synne.
And he sente to hem profetis, that thei schulen turne aȝen to the Lord; whiche profetis witnessynge thei nolden here. Therfor the Spirit of the Lord
clothide Zacharie, the preest, the sone of Joiada; and he stood in the siȝt of the puple, and seide to hem, The Lord seith these thingis, Whi breken ȝe the comaundement of the Lord, which thing schal not profite to ȝou, and ȝe han forsake the Lord, that he schulde forsake ȝou?
Whiche weren gaderide togidere aȝens hym, and senten stonys, bi comaundement of the kyng, in the large place of the hows of the Lord.
And kyng Joas hadde not mynde on the merci which Joiada, the fadir of Zacharie, hadde doon with hym; but he killide the sone of Joiada. And whanne Zacharie diede, he seide, The Lord se, and seke.
And whanne a ȝeer was turned aboute, ether endid, the oost of Sirie stiede aȝens Joas, and it cam in to Juda and in to Jerusalem, and it killide alle the princes of the puple; and thei senten al the prey to the kyng, to Damask.
And certeyn, whanne a ful litle noumbre of men of Sirie was comun, the Lord bitook in her hondis a multitude with out noumbre, for thei hadden forsake the Lord God of her fadris. Also thei vsiden schameful domes
in Joas; and thei ȝeden awei, and leften hym in grete sorewis. Sotheli hise seruauntis risiden aȝens hym, in to veniaunce of the blood of the sone of Joiada, preest; and killiden hym in his bed, and he was deed. And thei birieden hym in the citee of Dauid, but not in the sepulcris of kyngis.
Forsothe Sabath, the sone of Semath of Amon, and Josabeth, the sone of Semarith of Moab, settiden tresouns to hym.
Sotheli hise sones, and the summe of money that was gaderid vndur hym, and the reparelyng of the hows of God, ben writun diligentli in the book of Kyngis.
Forsothe Amasie, his sone, regnede for hym; Amasie was of fyue and twenti ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne, and he regnyde nyne and twenti ȝeer in Jerusalem; the name of his modir was Joiaden, of Jerusalem.
And he dide good in the siȝt of the Lord, netheles not in perfit herte.
And whanne he siȝ the empire strengthid to hym silf, he stranglide the seruauntis,
that killiden the kyng, his fadir; but he killide not the sones of hem; as it is writun in the book of the lawe of Moises, where the Lord comaundide, seiynge, Fadris schulen not be slayn for the sones, nether the sones for her fadris; but ech man schal die in his owne synne.
Therfor Amasie gaderide togidere Juda, and ordeynede hem bi meynees and tribunes and centuriouns, in al Juda and Beniamyn; and he noumbride fro twenti ȝeer and aboue, and he foonde thritti thousynde of ȝonge men, that ȝeden out to batel, and helden spere and scheeld.
Also for mede he hiride of Israel an hundrid thousynde of stronge men, for an hundrid talentis of siluer, that thei schulden fiȝte aȝens the sones of Edom.
Forsothe a man of God cam to hym, and seide, A! kyng, the oost of Israel go not out with thee, for the Lord is not with Israel and
with alle the sones of Effraym; for if thou gessist that batels stonden in the myȝt of oost, the Lord schal make thee to be ouercomun of enemyes, for it is of God for to helpe, and to turne in to fliȝt.
And Amasie seide to the man of God, What therfor schal be doon of the hundrid talentis, which Y ȝaf to the knyȝtis of Israel? And the man of God answeride to hym, The Lord hath, wherof he may ȝelde to thee myche mo thingis than these.
Therfor Amasie departide the oost that cam to hym fro Effraym, that it schulde turne aȝen in to his place; and thei weren wrooth greetli aȝens Juda, and turneden aȝen in to her cuntrei.
Forsothe Amasie ledde out tristili his puple, and ȝede in to the valei of makyngis of salt, and he killide of the sones of Seir ten thousynde.
And the sones of Juda token othere ten thousynde of men, and brouȝten to the hiȝ scarre of summe stoon; and castiden hem doun fro the hiȝeste in to the pit; whiche alle braken.
And thilke oost whom Amasie hadde sent aȝen, that it schulde not go with him to batel, was spred abrood in the citees of Juda fro Samarie til to Betheron; and aftir that it hadde slayn thre thousynde, it took awey a greet preie.
And Amasie, after the sleyng of Idumeis, and after that he hadde brouȝt the goddis of the sones of Seir, ordeynede hem in to goddis to hym silf, and worschipide hem, and brente encense to hem.
Wherfor the Lord was wrooth aȝens Amasie, and sente to hym a profete, that seide to hym, Whi worschipist thou goddis that delyueriden not her puple fro thin hond?
Whanne the profete spak these thingis, Amasie answeride to hym, Whether thou art a counselour of the king? ceesse thou, lest perauenture Y sle thee. Therfor the profete ȝede awei, and seide, Y woot, that the Lord thouȝte to sle thee; for thou didist this yuel, and ferthermore thou assentidist not to my counsel.
Therfor Amasie, the king of Juda, whanne he hadde take a ful yuel counsel, sente to the kyng of Israel Joas, the sone of Joachaz, the sone of Hieu, and seide, Come thou, se we vs togidere.
And he sente aȝen messangeris, and seide, A cardue, ether a tasil, which is in the Liban sente to the cedre of the Liban, and seide, Ȝyue thi douȝter a wijf to my sone; and lo! beestis that weren in the wode of the Liban ȝeden and defouliden the cardue.
Thou seidist, Y haue smyte Edom, and therfor thin herte is reysid in to pride; sitte thou in thin hows; whi stirist thou yuel aȝens thee, that thou falle, and Juda with thee?
Amasie nolde here, for it was the wille of the Lord, that he schulde be bitakun in to the hondis of enemyes, for the goddis of Edom.
Therfor Joas, kyng of Israel, stiede, and thei siȝen hem silf togidere. Sotheli Amasie, the kyng of Juda, was
in Bethsames of Juda; and Juda felde doun bifor Israel, and fledde in to his tabernaclis.
Certis the kyng of Israel took in Bethsames Amasie, the kyng of Juda, the sone of Joas, sone of Joachaz, and brouȝte in to Jerusalem; and he destriede the wallis therof fro the ȝate of Effraym til to the ȝate of the corner, bi foure hundrid cubitis.
And be ledde aȝen in to Samarie al the gold and siluer, and alle vessels whiche he foond in the hows of the Lord, and at Obededom, in the tresouris also of the kyngis hows, also and the sones of ostagis.
Forsothe Amasie, kyng of Juda, the sone of Joas, lyuede fiftene ȝeer aftir that Joas, kyng of Israel, the sone of Joachaz, was deed.
Sotheli the residue of the formere and the laste wordis of Amasie ben writun in the book of kyngis of Juda and of Israel.
And aftir that he ȝede awei fro the Lord, thei settiden to hym tresouns in Jerusalem; and whanne he hadde fledde to Lachis, thei senten and
killiden hym there; and thei brouȝten aȝen on horsis, and birieden hym with his fadris in the citee of Dauid.
Forsothe al the puple of Juda made kyng, Ozie, his sone, of sixtene ȝeer, for his fader Amasie.
He bildide Hailath, and restoride it to the lordschipe of Juda, after that the kyng slepte with hise fadris.
Ozie was of sixtene ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne; and he regnede two and fifti ȝeer in Jerusalem; the name of his modir was Hiechelia, of Jerusalem.
And he dide that, that was riȝtful in the siȝt of the Lord, bi alle thingis whiche Amasie, his fadir, hadde do.
And he souȝte the Lord in the daies of Zacarie, vndurstondynge and seynge God; and whanne he souȝte God, God reulide hym in alle thingis.
Forsothe he ȝede out, and fauȝt aȝens Filisteis, and distriede the wal of Geth, and the wal of Jabyne, and the wal of Azotus; and he bildide stronge places in Azotus and in Filistiym.
And the Lord helpide hym bothe aȝens Filisteis, and aȝens Arabeis that dwelliden in Garbahal, and aȝenus Amonytis.
Amonytis paieden ȝiftis to Ozie, and his name was pupplischid til to the entryng of Egipt for ofte victories.
And Ozie bildide touris in Jerusalem ouer the ȝate of the corner, and ouer the ȝate of the valey, and othere touris in the same side of the wal; and made tho stidefast.
Also he bildide touris in the wildirnesse, and he diggide ful many cisternes; for he hadde many beestis as wel in the feeldi places as in the wastnesse of deseert. Also he hadde vyneris and tiliers of vynes in the hilles, and in Carmele; for he was a man ȝouun to erthetilthe.
Forsothe the oost of hise werriours, that ȝeden forth to batels, vndur the hond of Heiel, scribe, and of Masie, techere, and vndur the hond of Ananye that was of the duykis of the kyng; and al the noumbre of princes, by her meynees, was of stronge men two thousynde and sixe hundrid.
And vndur hem was al the oost, thre hundrid thousynde and seuen thousynde and fyue hundrid, that weren able to batel, and fouȝten for the king aȝens aduersaries.
And Ozie made redi to hem, that is, to al the oost, scheldis, and speris, and basynetis, and haburiouns, and bouwis, and slyngis to caste stonys.
And he made in Jerusalem engynes of dyuerse kynde, which he settide in touris, and in the corneris of wallis, that tho schulden caste arowis and grete stoonys; and his name ȝede out fer, for the Lord helpide hym, and hadde maad him strong.
But whanne he was maad strong, his herte was reisid in to his perischyng; and he dispiside his Lord God; and he entride in to the temple of the Lord, and wolde brenne encense on the auter of encense.
And anoon Azarie, the preest, entride after hym, and with hym the preestis of the
Lord, seuenti men ful noble; whiche aȝenstoden the kyng, and seiden, Ozie, it is not of thin office, that thou brenne encense to the Lord, but of the preestis of the Lord, that is, of the sones of Aaron, that ben halewid to siche seruyce; go thou out of the seyntuarye; dispise thou not; for this thing schal not be arettid of the Lord God to thee in to glorie.
And Ozie was wrooth, and he helde in the hond the censere for to offre encence, and manaasside the preestis; and anoon lepre was sprungun forth in his forheed, bifor the preestis in the hows of the Lord on the auter of encense.
And whanne Azarie, the bischop, hadde biholde hym, and alle othere preestis hadden biholde him, thei sien lepre in his forheed, and hiyngli thei puttiden hym out; but also he was aferd, and hastide to go out; for he feelide anoon the veniaunce of the Lord.
Therfor kyng Ozie was leprouse til to the dai of his deeth, and dwellide in an hows bi it silf, and he was ful of lepre; for which he was cast out of the hows of the Lord. Forsothe Joathan, his sone, gouernyde the hows of the kyng, and demyde the puple of the lond.
Sotheli Ysaie, the prophete, the sone of Amos, wroot the residue of the formere and of the laste wordis of Ozie.
And Ozie slepte with hise fadris, and thei birieden not hym in the feeld of the kyngis sepulcris, for he was leprouse; and Joathan, his sone, regnyde for hym.
Joathan was of fyue and twenti ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne, and he regnede sixtene ȝeer in Jerusalem; the name of his modir was Jerusa, the douȝter of Sadoch.
He dide that, that was riȝtful bifor the Lord, bi alle thingis whiche Ozie, his fadir, hadde do; outakun that he entride not in to the temple of the Lord, and the puple trespasside ȝit.
He bildide the hiȝ ȝate of the hous of the Lord, and he bildide
manye thingis in the wal of Ophel; also he bildide citees in the hillis of Juda, and he bildide castels and touris in forestis.
He fauȝt aȝens the kyng of the sones of Amon, and ouercam hym; and the sones of Amon ȝauen to hym in that tyme an hundrid talentis of siluer, and ten thousynde choris of barli, and so many of wheete; the sones of Amon ȝauen these thingis to hym in the secounde and in the thridde ȝeer.
And Joathan was maad strong, for he hadde dressid hise weies bifor his Lord God.
Forsothe the residue of wordis of Joathan, and alle hise batels, and werkis, ben writun in the book of kyngis of Israel and of Juda.
He was of fyue and twenti ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne, and he regnede sixtene ȝeer in Jerusalem.
And Joathan slepte with hise fadris, and thei birieden hym in the citee of Dauid; and Achaz, his sone, regnede for him.
Achaz was of twenti ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne, and he regnede sixtene ȝeer in Jerusalem; he dide not riȝtfulnesse in the siȝt of the Lord, as Dauid,
his fadir, dide; but he ȝede in the weies of the kyngis of Israel. Ferthermore and he ȝetyde ymagis to Baalym.
He it is that brente encense in the valey of Beennon, and purgide hise sones bi fier bi the custom of hethene men, whiche the Lord killide in the comyng of the sones of Israel.
Also he made sacrifice, and brente encense in hiȝ places, and in hillis, and vndur ech tree ful of bowis.
And his Lord God bitook hym in the hond of the kyng of Sirie, which smoot Achaz, and took a greet preie of his empire, and brouȝten in to Damask. Also Achaz was bitakun to the hondis of the kyng of Israel, and was smytun with a greet wounde.
And Facee, the sone of Romelie, killide of Juda sixe scoore thousynde in o dai, alle the men werriours; for thei hadden forsake the Lord God of her fadris.
In the same tyme Zechry, a myȝti man of Effraym, killide Maasie, the sone of Rogloth, the kyng; and he killide Ezrica, the duyk of his hows, and Elcana, the secounde fro the kyng.
And the sones of Israel token of her britheren two hundrid thousynde of wymmen and of children and of damysels, and prey with out noumbre; and baren it in to Samarie.
In that tempest a profete of the Lord, Obed bi name, was there, which ȝede out aȝens the oost comynge in to Samarie, and seide to hem, Lo! the Lord God of ȝoure fadris was wrooth aȝens Juda, and bitook hem in ȝoure hondis; and ȝe han slayn hem crueli, so that ȝoure cruelte stretchide forth in to heuene.
Ferthermore ȝe wolen make suget to ȝou the sones of Juda and of Jerusalem in to seruauntis and handmaidis; which thing is not nedeful to be doon; for ȝe han synned on this thing to ȝoure Lord God.
But here ȝe my councel, and lede aȝen the prisounneris, whyche ȝe han brouȝt of ȝoure britheren; for greet veniaunce of the Lord neiȝith to ȝou.
Therfor men of the princes of the sones of Effraym, Azarie, the sone of Johannan, Barachie, the sone of Mosollamoth, Jesechie, the sone of Sellum, and Amasie, the sone of Adali, stoden
aȝens hem that camen fro the batel; and seiden to hem, Ȝe schulen not brynge in hidur the prisoneris, lest we doen synne aȝens the Lord; whi wolen ȝe ley to on ȝoure synnes, and heepe elde trespassis? For it is greet synne; the ire of the strong veniaunce of the Lord neiȝeth on Israel.
And the men werriouris leften the prey, and alle thingis whiche thei hadden take, bifor the princes and al the multitude.
And the men stoden, whiche we remembriden bifore, and thei token the prisounneris, and clothiden of the spuylis alle that weren nakid; and whanne thei hadden clothid hem, and hadden schod, and hadden refreschid with mete and drynke, and hadden anoyntid for trauel, and hadden ȝoue cure, ether medecyn , to hem; thei puttiden hem on horsis, whiche euere myȝten not go, and weren feble of bodi, and brouȝten to Jerico, a citee of palmes, to the britheren of hem; and thei turneden aȝen in to Samarie.
In that tyme kyng Achaz sente to the kyng of Assiriens, and axide help.
And Ydumeis camen, and killiden many men of Juda, and token greet prey.
Also Filisteis weren spred abrood bi citees of the feeldis, and at the south of Juda; and thei token Bethsames, and Hailon, and Gaderoth, and Socoth, and Thannan, and Zamro, with her villagis; and dwelliden in tho.
For the Lord made low Juda for Achaz, the kyng of Juda; for he hadde maad him nakid of help, and hadde dispisid the Lord.
And the Lord brouȝte aȝens him Teglat Phalasar, kyng of Assiriens, that turmentide hym, and waastide hym, while no man aȝenstood.
Therfor Achaz, after that he hadde spuylid the hows of the Lord, and the hows of the kyng and of princes, ȝaf ȝiftis to the kyng of Assiriens, and netheles it profitide no thing to hym.
Ferthermore also in the tyme of his angwisch he encreesside dispit aȝens God; thilke kyng Achaz bi
hym silf offride sacrifices to the goddis of Damask, hise smyteris, and seide, The goddis of the kyngis of Sirie helpen hem, whiche goddis Y schal plese bi sacrifices, and thei schulen help me; whanne aȝenward thei weren fallyng to hym, and to al Israel.
Therfor aftir that Achaz hadde take awei, and broke alle the vessels of the hows of God, he closide the ȝatis of Goddis temple, and made auteris to hym silf in alle the corneris of Jerusalem.
And in alle citees of Juda he bildide auteris to brenne encence, and he stiride the Lord God of hise fadris to wrathfulnesse.
Sotheli the residue of hise wordis and of alle hise werkis, the formere and the laste, ben writun in the book of kyngis of Juda and of Israel.
And Achaz slepte with hise fadris, and thei birieden hym in the citee of Jerusalem; for thei resseyueden not hym in the sepulcris of the kyngis of Israel; and Ezechie, his sone, regnede for hym.
Therfor Ezechie bigan to regne, whanne he was of fyue and twenti ȝeer, and he regnede in Jerusalem nyne and twenti ȝeer; the name of his modir was Abia, the douȝtir of Zacharie.
And he dide that, that was pleasaunt in the siȝt of the Lord, bi alle thingis whiche Dauid, his fadir, hadde do.
In that ȝeer and the firste monethe of his rewme he openyde the ȝatis of the hows of the Lord, and
restoride tho; and he brouȝte the preestis and dekenes, and gaderide hem
in to the eest strete, and seide to hem, Sones of Leuy, here ȝe me, and be ȝe halewid; clense ȝe the hows of the Lord God of ȝoure fadris; do ȝe awei al vnclennesse fro the seyntuarie.
Oure fadris synneden, and diden yuel in the siȝt of oure Lord God, and forsoken hym; thei turneden awei her faces fro the tabernacle of oure Lord God, and ȝauen the bak.
Thei closiden the doris that weren in the porche, and quenchiden the lanternes; and thei brenten not encense, and thei offriden not brent sacrifices in the seyntuarie of God of Israel.
Therfor the stronge veniaunce of the Lord was reisid on Juda and Jerusalem; and he ȝaf hem in to stiryng, and in to perischyng, and in to hisshing, ether scornyng, as ȝe seen with ȝoure iȝen.
Lo! oure fadris felden doun bi swerdis; oure sones, and oure douȝtris, and wyues ben led prisouneris for this greet trespas.
Now therfor it plesith me, that we make a boond of pees with the Lord God of Israel, and that he turne fro vs the stronge veniaunce of his ire.
My sones, nyle ȝe be reccheles; the Lord hath chose ȝou, that ȝe stonde bifor hym, and serue hym, that ȝe herie hym, and brenne encense to hym.
Therfor the dekenes risiden, Mahat, the sone of Amasie, and Johel, the sone of Azarie, of the sones of Caath; sotheli of the sones of Merarye, Cys, the sone of Abdai, and Azarie, the sone of Jelaleel; forsothe of the sones of Jerson, Joha, the sone of Zemma, and
Hedem, the sone of Johaa; and sotheli of the sones of Elisaphan, Samri, and Jahiel; and of the sones of Asaph, Zacharie,
and Mathanye; also of the sones of Heman, Jahiel, and Semei; but also of the sones of Iditum, Semei, and Oziel.
And thei gaderiden to gidere her britheren, and weren halewid; and thei entriden bi comaundement of the kyng, and bi comaundement of the Lord, for to clense the hows of the Lord.
Also preestis entriden in to the temple of the Lord, for to halewe it, and thei baren out al vnclennesse, which thei founden ther ynne in the porche, ethir large place, of the hows of the Lord; which vnclennesse the dekenes token, and baren out to the stronde of Cedron with outforth.
Sotheli thei bigunnen to clense in the firste dai of the firste monethe, and in the eiȝte dai of the same monethe thei entriden in to the porche of the hows of the Lord, and thei clensiden the temple eiȝte daies; and in the sixtenthe dai of the same monethe thei filliden that, that thei hadden bigunne.
And thei entriden to Ezechie, the king, and seiden to hym, We han halewid al the hows of the Lord, and the auter of brent sacrifice therof, and the vessels therof, also and the boord of settyngforth with
alle hise vessels, and al the purtenaunce of the temple, which purtenaunce king Achaz hadde defoulid in his rewme, aftir that he brak the lawe; and lo! alle thingis ben set forth bifor the auter of the Lord.
And Ezechie, the kyng, roos in the morwetid, and gaderide togidere alle the princes of the citee, and stiede in to the
hows of the Lord; and thei offriden togidere seuene bolis, and seuene rammes, seuene lambren, and seuene buckis of geet, for synne, for the rewme, for the seyntuarye, and for Juda. And he seide to preestis, the sones of Aaron, that thei schulden offre on the auter of the Lord.
Therfor thei killiden bolis, and the preestis tooken the blood, and schedden it on the auter; also thei killiden rammes, and the preestis schedden the blood of tho on the auter; thei offriden lambren, and the preestis schedden the blood on the auter.
And thei brouȝten buckis of geet for synne bifor the kyng and al the multitude, and thei settiden her
hondis on tho; and the preestis offriden tho, and spreynten the blood of tho bifor the auter, for the clensyng of al Israel. For the king comaundide, that brent sacrifice shulde be made for al Israel, and for synne.
Also he ordeynede dekenes in the hows of the Lord, with cymbalis, and sawtrees, and harpis, bi the ordenaunce of Dauid the kyng, and of Gad, the profete, and of Nathan, the profete; for it was the comaundement of the Lord bi the hond of hise prophetis.
And the dekenes stoden, and helden the orguns of Dauid; and preestis helden trumpis.
And Ezechie comaundide, that thei schulden offre brent sacrifices on the auter; and whanne brent sacrifices weren offrid, thei bigunnen to synge preisyngis to the Lord, and to sowne with trumpis, and in dyuerse orguns, whiche Dauid, the kyng of Israel, hadde maad redi for to sowne.
Forsothe whanne al the cumpenye worschipide, syngeris and thei that helden trumpis weren in her office, til the brent sacrifice was fillid.
And whanne the offryng was endid, the kyng was bowid, and alle that weren with hym, and thei worschipiden God.
And Ezechie and the princes comaundiden to the dekenes, that thei schulden preise the Lord with the wordis of Dauith, and of Asaph, the profete; whiche preisiden hym with greet gladnesse, and kneliden, and worschipiden.
Sothely Ezechie addide also these thingis, Ȝe han fillid ȝoure hondis to the Lord; neiȝe ȝe, and offre sacrifices and preisyngis in the hows of the Lord.
Therfor al the multitude offride with deuoute soule sacrifices, and preisyngis, and brent sacrifices. Sotheli this was the noumbre of brent sacrifices, whiche the multitude offride; seuenti bolis, and an hundrid rammes, two hundrid lambren.
Also thei halewiden to the Lord sixe hundrid oxis, and thre thousynde sheep.
Forsothe the preestis weren fewe, and myȝten not suffice for to drawe awei the skynnes of brent sacrifices; wherfor and the dekenes her britheren helpiden hem, til the werk was fillid, and the preestis weren halewid; for the dekenes ben halewid bi liȝtere custom than the preestis.
Therfor there weren ful many brent sacrifices, ynnere fatnessis of pesible sacrifices, and the moyste sacrifices of brent sacrifices, and the worschip, ethir ournyng, of the Lordis hows was fillid.
And Ezechie was glad, and al the puple, for the seruyce of the Lord was fillid; for it pleside, that this was doon sodeynly.
And Ezechie sente to al Israel and to Juda, and he wroot pistlis to Effraym and to Manasses, that thei schulden come in to the hous of the Lord in Jerusalem, and make paske to the Lord God of Israel.
Therfor whanne counseil was takun of the kyng, and of princes, and of al the cumpeny of Jerusalem, thei demyden to make paske in the secounde moneth.
For thei demyden not to do in his tyme; for the preestis that myȝten suffice weren not halewid, and the puple was not ȝit gaderid in to Jerusalem.
And the word pleside the king, and al the multitude.
And thei demyden to sende messangeris in to al Israel, fro Bersabee til to Dan, that thei schulden come, and make pask to the Lord God of Israel in Jerusalem; for many men hadden not do, as it is bifor writun in the lawe.
And corouris ȝeden forth with pistlis, bi comaundement of the kyng and of hise princis, in to al Israel and Juda, and prechiden bi that, that the kyng hadde comaundid, Sones of Israel, turne ȝe aȝen to the Lord God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Israel; and he schal turne aȝen to the residue men, that ascapiden the hondis of the kyng of Assiriens.
Nyle ȝe be maad as ȝoure fadris and britheren, that ȝeden awei fro the Lord God of her fadris; and he ȝaue hem in to perischyng, as ȝe seen.
Nyle ȝe make hard ȝoure nollis, as ȝoure fadris diden; ȝyue ȝe hondis to the Lord, and come ȝe to his seyntuarie, which he halewide withouten ende; serue ȝe the Lord God of ȝoure fadris, and the ire of his strong veniaunce schal be turned awey fro ȝou.
For if ȝe turnen aȝen to the Lord, ȝoure britheren and ȝoure sones schulen haue mercy, bifor her lordis that ledden hem prisoneris; and thei schulen turne aȝen in to this lond. For oure Lord God is pitouse, ethir benygne, and merciful; and he schal not turne awey his face fro ȝou, if ȝe turne aȝen to hym.
Therfor the corours ȝeden swiftli fro cytee in to citee thorou the lond of Effraym and of Manasses til to Zabulon, while thei scorniden and bimowiden hem.
Netheles sum men of Aser, and of Manasses, and of Zabulon, assentiden to the counsel, and camen in to Jerusalem.
Forsothe the hond of the Lord was maad in Juda, that he ȝaf to hem oon herte, and that thei diden the word of the Lord, bi the comaundement of the kyng and of the princes.
And many puplis weren gaderid in to Jerusalem, for to make the solempnyte of therf looues in the secounde monethe.
And thei risiden, and destrieden the auteris, that weren in Jerusalem; and thei destriynge alle thingis in whiche encense was brent to idols, castiden forth in to the stronde of Cedron.
Forsothe thei offriden pask in the fourtenthe dai of the secounde monethe; also the preestis and the dekenes weren halewid at the laste, and offriden brent sacrifices in the hows of the Lord.
And thei stoden in her ordre, bi the ordynaunce and lawe of Moises, the man of God. Sothely the preestis token of the hondis of
dekenes the blood to be sched out, for myche cumpeny was not halewid; and therfor the dekenes offriden pask for hem, that myȝten not be halewid to the Lord.
Also a greet part of the puple of Effraym, and Manasses, and of Ysachar, and of Zabulon, that was not halewid, eet pask not bi that that is writun. And Ezechie preyde for hem, and seide, The good Lord
schal do mercy to alle men, that seken in al the herte the Lord God of her fadris; and it schal not be arettid to hem, that thei ben not halewid.
And the Lord herde hym, and was plesid to the puple.
And the sones of Israel, that weren founden in Jerusalem, maden solempnyte of therf looues seuene daies in greet gladnesse, and herieden the Lord bi ech dai; and dekenes and preestis preisiden the Lord bi orguns, that acordiden to her offices.
And Ezechie spak to the herte of alle the dekenes, that hadden good vndurstondyng of the Lord; and thei eeten bi seuene daies of the solempnyte, offrynge sacrifices of pesible thingis, and heriynge the Lord God of her fadris.
And it pleside al the multitude to halewe also othere seuene daies; which thing also thei diden with greet ioye.
Forsothe Ezechie, kyng of Juda, ȝaf to the multitude a thousynde bolis, and seuene thousynde of scheep; sotheli the princes ȝauen to the puple a thousynde bolis, and ten thousynde scheep. Therfor ful greet
multitude of preestis was halewid; and al the cumpany of Juda was fillid with gladnesse, as wel of preestis and dekenes, as of al the multitude, that camen fro Israel, and of conuersis of the lond of Israel, and of dwelleris in Juda.
And greet solempnytee was maad in Jerusalem, which maner solempnyte was not in that citee fro the daies of Salomon, sone of Dauid, kyng of Israel.
Sotheli preestis and dekenes rysyden, and blessiden the puple; and the vois of hem was herd, and the preier cam in to the hooli dwelling place of heuene.
And whanne these thingis weren doon riȝtfuli, al Israel ȝede out, that was foundun in the citees of Juda; and thei braken simylacris, and kittiden doun woodis, and wastiden hiȝ places, and distrieden auteris, not oneli of al Juda and Beniamyn, but also and of Effraym and Manasses, til thei distrieden outirli. And alle the sones of Israel turneden aȝen in to her possessiouns and citees.
Forsothe Ezechie ordeynede cumpenyes of preestis and of dekenes bi her departyngis, ech man in his owne office, that is, as wel of preestis as of dekenes, to brent sacrifices and pesible sacrifices, that thei schulden mynystre, and knowleche, and synge in the ȝatis of the castels of the Lord.
Sotheli the part of the kyng was, that of his owne catel brent sacrifice schulde be offrid euere in the morewtid and euentide, also in sabatis, and calendis, and othere solempnytees, as it is writun in the lawe of Moises.
Also he comaundide to the puple of hem that dwelliden in Jerusalem, to ȝyue partis to the preestis and dekenes, that thei myȝten ȝyue tent to the lawe of the Lord.
And whanne this was knowun in the eeris of the multitude, the sones of Israel offriden ful many firste fruytis of wheete, of wyn, of oyle, and of hony; and of alle thingis whiche the erthe bringith forth, thei offriden tithis.
But also the sones of Israel and of Juda, that dwelliden in the citees of Juda, offriden tithis of oxis and of scheep, and the tithis of holi thingis, whiche thei avowiden to her Lord God, and thei brouȝten alle thingis, and maden ful many heepis.
In the thridde monethe thei bigunnen to leie the foundementis of the heepis, and in the seuenthe monethe thei filliden tho heepis.
And whanne Ezechie and hise princes hadden entrid, thei siȝen the heepis, and blessiden the Lord, and the puple of Israel.
And Ezechie axide the preestis and dekenes, whi the heepis laien so.
Azarie, the firste preest of the generacioun of Sadoch, answeride to hym, and seide, Sithen the firste fruytis bigunnen to be offrid in the hows of the Lord, we han ete and ben fillid, and ful many thingis ben left; for the Lord hath blessid his puple; sotheli this plentee, which thou seest, is of the relifs.
Therfor Ezechie comaundide, that thei schulden make redi bernes in the hows of the Lord; and
whanne thei hadden do this thing, thei brouȝten in feithfuly bothe the firste fruytis, and tithis, and what euere thingis thei hadden avowid. Forsothe Chonenye, the dekene, was the souereyn of tho; and
Semei his brother was the secounde; aftir whom Jehiel, and Azarie, and Nabath, and Asahel, and Jerimoth, and Jozabad, and Helyel, and Jesmahie, and Maath, and Banaie, weren souereyns vndur the hondis of Chonenye and Semei, his brother, bi the comaundement of Ezechie the kyng, and of Azarie, the bischop of the hows of the Lord, to whiche alle thingis perteyneden.
But Chore, the sone of Jemnya, dekene and portere of the eest ȝate, was souereyn of tho thingis that weren offrid bi fre wille to the Lord, and of the firste fruytis, and of thingis halewid in to hooli thingis of the noumbre of hooli
thingis; and vndur his cure weren Eden, and Beniamyn, Jesue, and Semeye, and Amarie, and Sechenye, in the citees of preestis, that thei schulden departe feithfuli to her britheren the partis, to the
lesse and the grettere, outakun malis fro three ȝeer and aboue, these thingis to alle that entriden in to the temple of the Lord, and what euer thing bi ech dai was hirid in the seruyce and obseruaunces bi her departyngis.
To preestis bi meynees, and to dekenes fro the twentithe ȝeer and aboue bi her ordris and cumpenyes,
and to alle the multitude, bothe to the wyues and fre children of hem of euer either kynde, metis weren ȝouun feithfuli of these thingis that weren halewid.
But also men of the sones of Aaron weren ordeyned bi the feeldis and subarbis of alle citees. whyche men schulden dele partis to al the male kynde of preestis and dekenes.
Therfor Ezechie dide alle thingis, whiche we seiden, in al Juda, and he wrouȝte that, that was riȝtful and good and trewe bifor his Lord
God, in al the religioun of the seruyce of the hows of the Lord, bi the lawe and cerymonyes; and he wolde seke his Lord God in al his herte, and he dide, and hadde prosperite.
Aftir whiche thingis and sich treuthe, Senacherib, the kyng of Assiriens, cam and entride in to Juda; and he bisegide stronge citees, and wolde take tho.
And whanne Ezechie hadde herd this thing, that is, that Senacherib was comun, and that al the fersnesse of batel was turned
aȝens Jerusalem, he took counsel with the princes and strongest men, that thei schulden stoppe the heedis of wellis, that weren without the citee; and whanne the
sentence of alle men demyde this, he gaderide togidere a ful greet multitude, and thei stoppiden alle the wellis, and the ryuer, that flowide in the myddis of the lond; and seiden, Lest the kyngis of Assiriens comen, and fynden abundance of watris.
Also he dide wittili, and bildide al the wal that was distride, and he bildide touris aboue, and an other wal withoutforth. And he reparilide Mello in the citee of Dauid; and made armure of al kynde, and scheldis.
And he ordeynede princes of werriouris in the oost; and he clepide togidere alle men in the street of the ȝate of the citee, and spake to the
herte of hem, and seide, Do ȝe manli, and be ȝe coumfortid; nyle ȝe drede, nether be ȝe aferd of the kyng of Assiriens, and of al the multitude which is with him; for many mo ben with vs than with him.
Fleischli arm is with him; oure Lord God is with vs, which is oure helpere, and schal fiȝte for vs. And the puple was coumfortid with sich wordis of Ezechie, kyng of Juda.
And aftir that these thingis weren doon, Sennacherib sente hise seruauntis to Jerusalem; for he with al the oost bisegide Lachis. He sente to Ezechie, kyng of Juda, and to al the puple
that was in the citee, and seide, Sennacherib, the kyng of Assiriens, seith these thingis, In whom han ȝe trist, and sitten bisegid in Jerusalem?
Whether Ezechie disseyueth ȝou, that he bitake ȝou to deeth in hungur and thirst, and affermeth, that ȝoure Lord God schal delyuere ȝou fro the hond of the kyng of Assyriens?
Whether not this is Ezechie, that distriede hiȝ places, and auteris of hym, and comaundide to Juda and to Jerusalem, and seide, Ȝe schulen worschipe bifor oon auter, and therynne ȝe schulen brenne encense?
Whether ȝe witen not what thingis Y haue do, and my fadir, to alle the puplis of londis? Whether the goddis of folkis and of alle londis myȝten delyuere her cuntrei fro myn hond?
Who is of alle goddis of folkis, whiche my fadris distrieden, that myȝte delyuere his puple fro myn hond, that also ȝoure God may delyuere ȝou fro this hond?
Therfor Ezechie disseyue not ȝou, nether scorne bi veyn counselyng, nethir bileue ȝe to hym; for if no god of alle folkis and cuntreis myȝte delyuere his puple fro myn hond, and fro the hond of my fadris, suyngli nether ȝoure God schal mowe delyuere ȝou fro this myn hond.
But also hise seruauntis spaken many othir thingis aȝenus the Lord God, and aȝens Ezechie, his seruaunte.
Also he wroot epistlis ful of blasfemye aȝens the Lord God of Israel, and he spak aȝens God, As the goddis of othere folkis myȝten not delyuere her puple fro myn hond, so and the God of Ezechie may not delyuere his puple fro myn hond.
Ferthermore and with greet cry in the langage of Jewis he sownede aȝens the puple, that sat on the wallis of Jerusalem, to make hem aferd, and to take the citee.
And he spake aȝens God of Israel, as aȝens the goddis of the puplis of erthe, the werkis of mennus hondis.
Therfor Ezechie, the kyng, and Ysaie, the profete, the sone of Amos, preieden aȝens this blasfemye, and crieden til in to heuene.
And the Lord sente his aungel, that killide ech strong man and werriour, and the prince of the oost of the kyng of Assiriens; and he turnede aȝen with schenship in to his lond. And whanne he hadde entrid in to the hows of his god, the sones, that ȝeden out of his wombe, killiden hym with swerd.
And the Lord sauyde Ezechie, and the dwelleris of Jerusalem, fro the hond of Senacherib, kyng of Assiriens, and fro the hond of alle men; and ȝaf to hem reste bi cumpas.
Also many men brouȝten offryngis and sacrifices to the Lord in to Jerusalem, and ȝiftis to Ezechie, kyng of Juda; which was enhaunsid aftir these thingis bifor alle folkis.
In tho daies Ezechie was sijk til to the deth, and he preiede the Lord; and he herde hym, and ȝaf to hym a
signe; but he ȝeldide not bi the benefices whiche he hadde take, for his herte was reisid; and ire was maad aȝens hym, and aȝens Juda, and aȝens Jerusalem.
And he was mekid aftirward, for his herte was reisid; bothe he was mekid, and the dwelleris of Jerusalem; and therfor the ire of the Lord cam not on hem in the daies of Ezechie.
Forsothe Ezechie was riche, and ful noble, and gaderide to hym silf ful many tresours of siluer, of gold, and of preciouse stoon, of swete smellynge spices, and of armuris of al kynde, and of vessels of greet prijs.
Also he bildide large housis of wheete, of wyn, and of oile, and cratchis of alle
beestis, and fooldis to scheep, and sixe citees. For he hadde vnnoumbrable flockis of scheep and of grete beestis; for the Lord hadde ȝoue to hym ful myche catel.
Thilke is Ezechie, that stoppide the hiȝere welle of the watris of Gion, and turnede tho awei vndur the erthe at the west of the citee of Dauid; in alle hise werkis he dide bi prosperite, what euer thing he wolde.
Netheles in the message of the princes of Babiloyne, that weren sent to hym for to axe of the grete wondir, that bifelde on the lond, God forsook hym, that he were temptid, and that alle thingis weren knowun that weren in his herte.
Sotheli the residue of wordis of Ezechie, and of hise mercies, ben writun in the profesie of Ysaie, the profete, sone of Amos, and in the book of kyngis of Juda and of Israel.
And Ezechie slepte with hise fadris, and thei birieden hym aboue the sepulcris of the sones of Dauid. And al Juda and alle the dwelleris of Jerusalem maden solempne the seruyces of his biriyng; and Manasses, his sone, regnide for him.
Manasses was of twelue ȝeer, whanne he bygan to regne, and he regnyde in Jerusalem fyue and fifti ȝeer.
Forsothe he dide yuel bifor the Lord bi abhomynaciouns of hethene men, whiche the Lord destriede bifor the sones of Israel.
And he turnede, and restoride the hiȝe places, whiche Ezechie, his fadir, hadde destried. And he bildide auteris to Baalym, and made wodis, and worschipide al the knyȝthod of heuene, and heriede it.
And he bildide auteris in the hows of the Lord, of which the Lord hadde seid, My name schal be in Jerusalem with outen ende.
Sotheli he bildide tho auteris to al the knyȝthod of heuene in the twei large places of the hows of the Lord.
And he made hise sones to passe thorouȝ the fier in the valei of Beennon; he kepte dremes; he suede fals diuynyng bi chiteryng of briddis; he seruyde witche craftis; he hadde with hym astronomyeris and enchaunteris, ethir trigetours, that disseyuen mennus wittis, and he wrouȝte many yuelis bifor the Lord to terre hym to wraththe.
Also he settide a grauun signe and a ȝotun signe in the hows of the Lord, of which hows God spak to Dauid, and to Salomon, his sone, and seide, Y schal sette my name with outen ende in this hows and in Jerusalem, which Y chees of alle the lynagis
of Israel; and Y schal not make the foot of Israel to moue fro the lond which Y ȝaf to her fadris, so oneli if thei kepen to do tho thingis whiche Y comaundide to hem, and al the lawe, and cerymonyes, and domes, bi the hond of Moises.
Therfor Manasses disseyuede Juda, and the dwelleris of Jerusalem, that thei diden yuel, more than alle hethene men, whiche the Lord hadde distriede fro the face of the sones of Israel.
And the Lord spak to hym, and to his puple; and thei nolden take heed.
Therfor the Lord brouȝte on hem the princes of the oost of the kyng of Assiriens; and thei token Manasses, and bounden hym with chaynes, and stockis, and ledden hym in to Babiloyne.
And aftir that he was angwischid, he preiede his Lord God, and dide penaunce gretli bifor the God of hise fadris.
And he preiede God, and bisechide ententifli; and God herde his preier, and brouȝte hym aȝen in to Jerusalem in to his rewme; and Manasses knew, that the Lord hym silf is God.
Aftir these thingis he bildide the wal with out the citee of Dauid, at the west of Gion, in the valei, fro the entryng of the ȝate of fischis, bi cumpas til to Ophel; and he reiside it gretli; and he ordeynede princes of the oost in alle the stronge citees of Juda.
And he dide awei alien goddis and symylacris fro the hows of the Lord; and he dide awei the auteris, whiche he hadde maad in the hil of the hows of the Lord, and in Jerusalem, and he castide awei alle with out the citee.
Certis he restoride the auter of the Lord, and offride theronne slayn sacrifices, and pesible sacrifices, and preisyng; and he comaundide Juda to serue the Lord God of Israel.
Netheles the puple offride ȝit in hiȝ places to her Lord God.
Forsothe the residue of dedis of Manasses, and his bisechyng to his Lord God, and the wordis of profetis, that spaken to hym in the name of the Lord God of Israel, ben conteyned in the wordis of the kyngis of Israel.
And his preier, and the heryng, and alle synnes, and dispisyng, also the places in whiche he bildide hiȝ thingis, and made wodis and ymagis, bifor that he dide penaunce, ben writun in the bokis of Ozai.
Forsothe Manasses slepte with hise fadris, and thei birieden hym in his hows; and Amon, his sone, regnyde for hym.
Amon was of two and twenti ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne; and he regnyde twei ȝeer in Jerusalem.
And he dide yuel in the siȝt of the Lord, as Manasses, his fadir, hadde do; and he offride, and seruyde to alle the idols, whiche Manasses hadde maad.
And he reuerenside not the face of the Lord, as Manasses, his fadir, reuerenside; and he dide mych gretter trespassis.
And whanne his seruauntis hadden swore to gyder aȝens hym, thei killiden hym in his hows.
Sotheli the residue multitude of the puple, aftir that thei hadden slayn hem that hadden slayn Amon, ordeyneden Josie, his sone, kyng for hym.
Josie was of eiȝte ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne, and he regnede in Jerusalem oon and thritti ȝeer.
And he dide that, that was riȝtful in the siȝt of the Lord; and ȝede in the waies of Dauid, his fadir, and bowide not to the riȝt side nether to the left side.
Forsothe in the eiȝtethe ȝeer of the rewme of his empire, whanne he was ȝit a child, he bigan to seke God of his fadir Dauid; and in the tweluethe ȝeer after that he bigan, he clenside Juda and Jerusalem fro hiȝ places, and wodis, and similacris, and grauun ymagis.
And thei destrieden bifor hym the auteris of Baalym, and thei destrieden the symylacris, that weren put aboue. Also he hewide doun the wodis, and grauun ymagis, and brak to smale gobetis; and scateride abrood the smale gobetis on the birielis of hem, that weren wont to offre to tho.
Ferthermore he brente the boonys of preestis in the auteris of idols, and he clenside Juda and Jerusalem.
But also he destriede alle idols in the citees of Manasses, and of Effraym, and of Symeon, til to Neptalym.
And whanne he hadde scateride the auteris, and hadde al to-broke in to gobetis the wodis, and grauun ymagis, and hadde destried alle templis of ydols fro al the lond of Israel, he turnede aȝen in to Jerusalem.
Therfor in the eiȝtenthe ȝeer of his rewme, whanne the lond and temple of the Lord was clensid nowe, he sente Saphan, the sone of Helchie, and Masie, the prince of the citee, and Joa, the sone of Joachaz, chaunceler, that thei schulden reparele the hous of his Lord God.
Whiche camen to Helchie, the grete preest; and whanne thei hadden take of hym the money, which was brouȝt in to the hows of the Lord; and which monei the dekenes and porteris hadden gaderid of Manasses, and of Effraym, and of alle the residue men of Israel, and of al Juda and Beniamyn,
and of the dwelleris of Jerusalem, thei ȝauen it in the hondis of hem that weren souereyns of the werk men in the hows of the Lord, that thei schulden restore the temple, and reparele alle feble thingis.
And thei ȝauen that monei to the crafti men and masouns, for to bie stoonys hewid out of the delues, ether quarreris, and trees to the ioynyngis of the bildyng, and to the coupling of housis, whiche the kingis of Juda hadden destried.
Whiche men diden feithfuli alle thingis. Sotheli the souereyns of worcheris weren Jabath, and Abdie, of the sones of Merari; Zacarie, and Mosallam, of the sones of Caath; whiche hastiden the werk; alle weren dekenes, kunnynge to synge with orguns.
Sotheli ouer them that baren birthuns to dyuerse vsis weren the scribis, and maistris of the dekenes, and porteris.
And whanne thei baren out the monei, that was borun in to the temple of the Lord, Helchie, the preest, foond the book of the lawe of the Lord bi the hond of Moises.
And he seide to Saphan, the writere, Y haue founde the book of the lawe in the hows of the Lord.
And Helchie took to Saphan, and he bar in the book to the king; and telde to hym, and seide, Lo! alle thingis ben fillid, whiche thou hast ȝoue in to the hondis of thi seruauntis.
Thei han wellyd togidere the siluere, which is foundun in the hous of the Lord; and it is ȝouun to the souereyns of the crafti men, and makynge
dyuerse werkis; ferthermore Helchie, the preest, took to me this book. And whanne he hadde rehersid this book in the presence
of the kyng, and he hadde herd the wordis of the lawe, he to-rente hise clothis;
and he comaundide to Helchie, and to Aichan, the sone of Saphan, and to Abdon, the sone of Mycha, and to Saphan, the scryuen, and to Asaie, the seruaunt of the
kyng, and seide, Go ȝe, and preie the Lord for me, and for the resydue men of Israel and of Juda, on alle the wordis of this book, which is foundun. For greet veniaunce of the Lord hath droppid on vs, for oure fadris kepten not the wordis of the Lord, to do alle thingis that ben writun in this book.
Therfor Helchie ȝede, and thei that weren sent togidere of the king, to Olda, the prophetesse, the wijf of Sellum, sone of Thecuath, sone of Asra, kepere of clothis, which Olda dwellide in Jerusalem in the secounde warde; and thei spaken to hir the wordis, whiche we telden bifore.
And sche answeride to hem, The Lord God of Israel seith these thingis, Seie ȝe to the man,
that sente ȝou to me, The Lord seith these thingis, Lo! Y schal brynge ynne yuels on this place, and on the dwelleris therof, and alle the cursyngis that ben writun in this book, which thei redden bifor the kyng of Juda.
For thei han forsake me, and han sacrified to alien goddis, for to terre me to wrathfulnesse in alle the werkis of her hondis; therfor my strong veniaunce schal droppe on this place, and it schal not be quenchid.
But speke ȝe thus to the kyng of Juda, that sente ȝou to preye the Lord, The Lord God of Israel seith these thingis, For thou
herdist the wordis of the book, and thin herte is maad neisch, and thou art mekid in the siȝt of the Lord of these thingis that ben seide aȝens this place and the dwelleris of Jerusalem, and thou hast reuerensid my face, and hast to-rente thi clothis, and hast wepte bifor me; also Y haue herd thee, seith the Lord.
For now Y schal gadere thee to thi fadris, and thou schalt be borun in to thi sepulcre in pees; and thin iȝen schulen not se al yuel, which Y schal brynge yn on this place, and on the dwelleris therof. Therfor thei telden to the king alle thingis, whiche Olda hadde seid.
And aftir that he hadde clepid togidere alle the eldere
men of Juda and of Jerusalem, he stiede in to the hows of the Lord, and togidere alle the men of Juda, and the dwelleris of Jerusalem, preestis, and dekenes, and al the puple, fro the leeste til to the moste; to whiche herynge in the hows of the Lord, the kyng redde alle the wordis of the book.
And he stood in his trone, and smoot a boond of pees bifor the Lord, for to go aftir hym, and to kepe the comaundementis, and witnessyngis, and iustifiyngis of hym, in al his herte and in al his soule; and to do tho thingis that weren writun in that book, which he hadde red.
And he chargide greetli on this thing alle men, that weren foundun in Jerusalem and Beniamyn; and the dwellers of Jerusalem diden aftir the couenaunt of the Lord God of her fadris.
Therfor Josie dide awei alle abhomynaciouns fro alle the cuntreis of the sones of Israel; and he made alle men, that weren residue in Israel, to serue her Lord God; in alle the daies of his lijf thei ȝeden not awei fro the Lord God of her fadris.
Forsothe Josie made pask to the Lord in Jerusalem, that was offrid in the fourtenthe
dai of the firste monethe; and he ordeynede prestis in her offices; and he comaundide hem for to mynystre in the hows of the Lord.
And he spak to the dekenes, at whos techyng al Israel was halewid to the Lord, Sette ȝe the arke in the seyntuarie of the temple, which Salomon, kyng of Israel, the sone of Dauid, bildide; for ȝe schulen no more bere it. But now serue ȝoure Lord God
and his puple Israel, and make ȝou redi bi ȝoure housis and meynees in the departyngis of ech bi hym silf, as Dauid, king of Israel, comaundide, and Salomon,
his sone, discryuede; and serue ȝe in the seyntuarie bi the meynees and cumpenyes
of dekenes, and be ȝe halewid, and offre ȝe pask; also make redi ȝoure britheren, that thei moun do bi the wordis, whiche the Lord spak in the hond of Moyses.
Ferthermore Josie ȝaf to al the puple, that was foundun there in the solempnytee of pask, lambren, and kidis of the flockis, and of residue scheep he ȝaf thritti thousynde, and of oxis thre thousynde; these thingis of al the catel of the kyng.
And hise duykis offriden tho thingis whiche thei avowiden bi fre wille, as wel to the puple as to prestis and dekenes. Forsothe Elchie, and Zacharie, and Jehiel, princes of the hows of the Lord, ȝauen to preestis, to make pask in comyn, two thousynde and sixe hundrid scheep, and thre hundrid oxis.
Forsothe Chononye, and Semei, and Nathanael and hise britheren, also Asabie, Jahiel, and Josabaz, princis of dekenes, ȝauen to othere dekenes, to make pask, fyue thousynde of scheep, and fyue hundrid oxis.
And the seruyce was maad redi; and preestis stoden in her office, and dekenes in cumpenyes, bi comaundement of the kyng; and pask was offrid.
And preestis spreynten her hondis with blood, and dekenes drowen of the skynnes of sacrifices,
and departiden tho sacrificis, for to ȝyue bi the housis and meyneis of alle men; and that tho schulden be offrid to the Lord, as it is writun in the book of Moises; and of oxis thei diden in lijk maner.
And thei rostiden pask on the fier, bi that that is writun in the lawe. Sotheli thei sethiden pesible sacrifices in pannes, and cawdruns, and pottis, and
in haste thei deliden to al the puple; but thei maden redi aftirward to hem silf, and to prestis; for preestis weren occupied til to nyȝt in the offryng of brent sacrifices and of ynnere fatnessis. Wherfor dekenes maden redi to hem silf and to preestis, the sones of Aaron, the laste.
Forsothe syngeris, the sones of Asaph, stoden in her ordre, bi the comaundement of Dauid, and of Asaph, and of Eman, and of Yditum, the profetis of the kyng; but the porteris kepten bi ech ȝate, so that thei ȝeden not awei fro the seruice, sotheli in a poynt; wherfor and dekenes, her britheren, maden redi metis to hem.
Therfor al the religioun of the Lord was fillid riȝtfuli in that day, that thei maden pask, and offriden brent sacrifices on the auter of the Lord, bi the comaundement of kyng Josie.
And the sones of Israel, that weren foundun there, maden pask in that tyme, and the solempnite of therf looues seuene daies.
No pask was lijk this in Israel, fro the daies of Samuel, the prophete; but nethir ony of the kyngis of Israel made pask as Josie dide, to preestis and dekenes, and to al Juda and Israel, that was foundun, and to the dwelleris of Jerusalem.
This pask was halewid in the eiȝtenthe ȝeer of the rewme of Josie.
Aftir that Josie hadde reparelid the temple, Nechao, the kyng of Egipt, stiede to fiȝte in Carcamys bisidis Eufrates; and Josie ȝede forth in to his metyng.
And he seide bi messangeris sent to hym, Kyng of Juda, what is to me and to thee? Y come not aȝens thee to dai, but Y fiȝte aȝens another hows, to which God bad me go in haste; ceesse thou to do aȝens God, which is with me, lest he sle thee.
Josie nolde turne aȝen, but made redi batel aȝens hym; and he assentide not to the wordis of Nechao, bi Goddis mouth, but he ȝede for to fiȝte in the feeld of Magedo.
And there he was woundide of archeris, and seide to hise children, Lede ȝe me out of the batel, for Y am woundid greetli.
Whiche baren hym ouer fro the chare in to an other chare, that suede hym, bi custom of the kyng, and baren out hym in to Jerusalem; and he diede, and was biried in the sepulcre of hise fadris. And al Juda
and Jerusalem biweiliden hym, Jeremye moost, of whom alle syngeris and syngeressis til in to present dai rehersen lamentaciouns, ether weilyngis, on Josie; and it cam forth as a lawe in Israel, Lo! it is seid writun in Lamentaciouns.
Forsothe the residue of wordis of Josie, and of hise mercies, that ben comaundid in the lawe of the Lord, and hise werkis, the firste and the laste, ben wryten in the book of kyngis of Israel and of Juda.
Therfor the puple of the lond took Joachaz, the sone of Josie, and ordeynede hym kyng for his fadir in Jerusalem.
Joachaz was of thre and twenti ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne, and he regnede thre monethis in Jerusalem.
Sotheli the kyng of Egipt, whan he hadde come to Jerusalem, remouyde hym, and condempnede the lond in an hundrid talentis of siluer and in a talent of gold.
And he ordeynede for hym Eliachim, his brother, kyng on Juda and Jerusalem; and turnede his name Joakym. Sotheli he took thilk Joachaz with hym silf, and brouȝte in to Egipt.
Joakym was of fyue and twenti ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne, and he regnyde eleuene ȝeer in Jerusalem, and he dide yuel bifor his Lord God.
Nabugodonosor, kyng of Caldeis, styede aȝens this Joakym, and ledde hym boundun with chaynes in to Babiloyne.
To which Babiloyne he translatide also the vessels of the Lord, and settide tho in his temple.
Sotheli the residue of wordis of Joakym, and of hise abhomynaciouns whiche he wrouȝte, and that weren foundun in hym, ben conteyned in the book of kyngis of Israel and of Juda. Therfor Joachym, his sone, regnede for hym.
Joachym was of eiȝte ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne, and he regnede thre monethis and ten daies in Jerusalem, and he dide yuel in the siȝt of the Lord.
And whanne the cercle of the ȝeer was turned aboute, Nabugodonosor the kynge sente men, whiche also brouȝten hym in to Babiloyne, whanne the moost preciouse vessels of the hows of the Lord weren borun out togidir. Sotheli he ordeynede Sedechie, his fadris brother, kyng on Juda and Jerusalem.
Sedechie was of oon and twenti ȝeer, whanne he bigan to regne, and he regnede eleuene ȝeer in Jerusalem.
And he dide yuel in the siȝt of his Lord God, and he was not aschamed of the face of Jeremye, the prophete, spekynge to hym bi the mouth of the Lord.
Also he ȝede awey fro the kyng Nabugodonosor, that hadde made hym to swere bi God; and he made hard his nol and herte, that he nolde turne aȝen to the Lord of Israel.
But also alle the princes of preestis and the puple trespassiden wickidli, bi alle abhomynaciouns of hethene men; and thei defouliden the hows of the Lord, which he halewide to hym silf in Jerusalem.
Forsothe the Lord God of her fadris sente to hem bi the hond of hise messangeris, and roos bi nyȝt, and amonestide ech day; for he sparide his puple and dwellyng place.
And thei scorneden the messangeris of God, and dispisiden hise wordis, and scorneden hise prophetis; til the greet veniaunce of the Lord stiede on his puple, and noon heelyng were.
And he brouȝte on hem the kyng of Caldeis; and killide the ȝonge men of hem bi swerd in the hows of seyntuarie; he hadde not merci of a ȝong man, and of a vergyn, and of an eld man, and sotheli nether of a man niȝ the deth for eldnesse, but he bitook alle in the hond of that king of Caldeis.
And he translatide in to Babiloyne alle the vessels of the hows of the Lord, bothe the grettere and the lasse vessels, and the tresours of the temple, and of the kyng, and of the princes.
Enemyes brenten the hows of the Lord; thei distrieden the wal of Jerusalem; thei brenten alle the touris; and thei distrieden what euer thing was preciouse.
If ony man ascapide the swerd, he was led in to Babiloyne, and seruyde the kyng and hise sones; til
the kyng of Peersis regnyde, and the word of the Lord bi the mouth of Jeremye was fillid, and til the lond halewide hise sabatis. For in alle the daies of desolacioun it made sabat, til that seuenti ȝeer weren fillid.
Forsothe in the firste ȝeer of Cyrus, kyng of Persis, to fille the word of the Lord, which he hadde spoke bi the mouth of Jeremye, the Lord reiside the spirit of Cirus, king of Persis, that comaundide to be prechid in al his rewme, ȝhe, bi scripture, and seide,
Cirus, the king of Persis, seith these thingis, The Lord God of heuene ȝaf to me alle the rewmes of erthe, and he comaundide to me, that Y schulde bilde to hym an hows in Jerusalem, which is in Judee. Who of ȝou is in al his puple? his Lord God be with hym, and stie he in to Jerusalem.
IN the firste ȝeer of Cirus, kyng of Persis, that the word of the Lord bi the mouth of Jeremye schulde be fillid, the Lord reiside the spirit of Cyrus, kyng of Persis; and he pupplischide a vois in al his rewme, ȝe, bi the scripture, and seide,
Cirus, the kyng of Persis, seith these thingis, The Lord God of heuene ȝaf to me alle the rewmes of erthe, and he comaundide to me, that Y schulde bilde to hym an hows in Jerusalem, which is in Judee.
Who is among ȝou of al his puple? his God be with hym; stie he in to Jerusalem, which is in Judee, and bilde he the hows of the Lord God of Israel; he is God, which is in Jerusalem.
And alle othere men, that dwellen where euere in alle places, helpe hym; the men of her place helpe in siluer, and gold, and catel, and scheep, outakun that that thei offren wilfulli to the temple of God, which is in Jerusalem.
And the princis of fadris of Juda and of Beniamyn risiden, and the preestis, and dekenes, and ech man whos spirit God reiside, for to stie to bilde the temple of the Lord, that was in Jerusalem.
And alle men that weren in cumpas helpiden the hondis of hem, in vesselis of siluer, and of gold, in catel, in purtenaunce of houshold, and in alle werk beestis, outakun these thingis which thei offriden bi fre wille.
Forsothe kyng Cyrus brouȝte forth the vessels of the temple of the Lord, whiche Nabugodonosor hadde take fro Jerusalem, and hadde set tho in the temple of his god.
Sotheli Cyrus, the kyng of Persis, brouȝte forth tho bi the hond of Mytridatis, sone of Gazabar; and noumbride tho to Sasabazar, the prince of Juda.
And this is the noumbre of tho vessels; goldun violis, thritti; siluerne viols, a thousynde; grete knyues, nyne and twenti; goldun cuppis, thritti
; siluerne cuppis, two thousynde foure hundrid and ten; othere vessels, a thousynde;
alle the vessels of gold and siluere weren fyue thousynde foure hundrid. Sasabazar took alle vessels, with hem that stieden fro the transmygracioun of Babiloyne, in to Jerusalem.
Forsothe these ben the sones of prouynce, that stieden fro the caitifte, which Nabugodonosor, kyng of Babiloyne, hadde translatid in to Babiloyne; and thei turneden aȝen in to Jerusalem and in to Juda, ech man in to his citee,
that camen with Zorobabel; Jesua, Neemie, Saray, Rahelaie, Mardochaa, Belsan, Mesfar, Begnay, Reum, Baana. This is the noumbre of men of the sones of Israel;
