Deme thou not aȝens a iuge; for he demeth vp that, that is iust.
Go thou not in the weie with an hardi man, lest perauenture he agregge hise yuels in thee; for he goith aftir his wille, and thou schalt perische togidere with his foli.
Make thou not chidyng with a wrathful man, and go thou not in to desert with an hardi man; for whi blood is as nouȝt bifore hym, and where noon help is, he schal hurtle thee doun.
Haue thou not councel with foolis; for thei moun not loue, no but tho thingis that plesen hem.
Make thou not a counsel bifore a straunger; for thou noost, what he schal bringe forth. Make not thin herte knowun to ech man; lest perauenture he brynge to thee fals grace, and dispise thee.
Loue thou not gelousli the womman of thi bosum; lest sche schewe on thee the malice of yuel doctryn.
Ȝyue thou not to a womman the power of thi soule; lest sche entre in thi vertu, and thou be schent.
Biholde thou not a womman of many willis; lest perauenture thou falle in to the snaris of hir.
Be thou not customable with a daunseresse, nethir here thou hir; lest perauenture thou perische in the spedi werk of hir.
Biholde thou not a virgyn; lest perauenture thou be sclaundrid in the feirnesse of hir.
Ȝyue not thi soule to hooris in ony thing; lest thou leese thee, and thi soule, and thin eritage.
Nyle thou biholde aboute in the lanys of the cytee; nethir erre thou in the large streetis therof.
Turne awei thi face fro a womman wel arayed; and biholde thou not aboute the fairnesse of othere.
Many men han perischid for the fairnesse of a womman; and herbi couetise brenneth an hiȝ as fier.
Ech womman which is an hoore, ethir customable to fornycacioun, schal be defoulid as a fen in the weie.
Many men wondrynge on the fairnesse of an alien womman weren maad repreuable, for whi the speche of hir brenneth an hiȝ as fier.
Sitte thou not in ony maner with an alien womman, nether reste thou with
hir on a bed; and iangle thou not with hir in wyn, lest perauenture thin herte boowe in to hir, and thou falle in to perdicioun bi thi blood.
Forsake thou not an eld frend; for a newe frend schal not be lijk hym.
Newe wijn is a newe frend; it schal wexe eld, and thou schalt drinke it with swetnesse.
Coueyte thou not the glorie and richessis of a synnere; for thou noost, what distriyng of hym schal come.

Knowe thou the comynyng of deth; for thou schalt entre in to the myddis of snaris, and thou schalt go on the armuris of hem that sorewen.
Bi thi vertu kepe thee fro thi neiȝbore; and trete thou with wise men and prudent men.
Just men be gestis, ethir mete feris, to thee; and gloriyng be to thee in the dreed of God.
And the thouȝt of God be to thee in wit; and al thi tellynge be in the heestis of the hiȝeste.
Werkis schulen be preisid in the hond of crafti men, and the prince of the puple in the wisdom of his word; forsothe in the wit of eldere men a word.
A man, a ianglere, is dredeful in his citee; and a fool hardi man in his word schal be hateful.
A wijs iuge schal deme his puple; and the prinshed of a witti man schal be stidfast.
Aftir the iuge of the puple, so and hise mynystris; and what maner man is the gouernour of the citee, siche ben also men dwellinge ther ynne.
An vnwijs king schal leese his puple; and citees schulen be enhabitid bi the wit of prudent men.
The power of erthe is in the hond of God, and al the wickidnesse of hethene men is abhomynable; and he schal reise a profitable gouernour at a tyme on it.
The power of man is in the hond of God; and he schal sette his onour on the face of a wijs man in the lawe.
Haue thou not mynde on al the wrong of the neiȝbore; and do thou no thing in the werkis of wrong.
Pride is hateful bifore God and men; and al the wickidnesse of hethene men is abhomynable.
A rewme is translatid fro a folk in to folk, for vnriȝtfulnessis, and wrongis, and dispisyngis, and dyuerse gilis.
No thing is cursidere than an auerouse man. What art thou proude, thou erthe and aische?
No thing is worse, than for to loue monei; for whi this man hath also his soule set to sale, for in his lijf he hath cast awei hise ynneste thingis.
Ech power is schort lijf; lengere siknesse greueth the leche.
A leche kittith awei schort siknesse; so and a king is to dai, and to morewe he schal die.
Forsothe whanne a man schal die, he schal enherite serpentis, and beestis, and wormes.
The bigynnyng of pride of man was to be
apostata fro God; for his herte ȝede awei fro hym that made hym. For whi pride is the bigynnyng of al synne; he that holdith it, schal be fillid with cursyngis, and it schal distrye hym in to the ende.
Therfor the Lord hath schent the couentis of yuele men, and hath destried hem til in to the ende.
God destriede the seetis of proude duykis; and made mylde men to sitte for hem.
God made drie the rootis of proude folkis; and plauntide meke men of tho folkis.
The Lord destriede the londis of folkis; and loste tho til to the foundement.
He made drie the rootis of hem, and loste hem; and made the mynde of hem to ceesse fro the erthe.
God loste the mynde of proude men; and lefte the mynde of meke men in wit.
Pride was not maad to men; nether wrathfulnesse to the nacioun of wymmen.
This seed of men that dredith God, schal be onourid; but this seed schal be disonourid, that passith the comaundementis of the Lord.
In the myddis of britheren the gouernour of hem is in onour; and thei that dreden God, schulen be in hise iȝen.
The glorie of riche men onourid and of pore men is the drede of God.
Nyle thou dispise a iust pore man; and nyle thou magnefie a riche synful man.
The iuge is greet, and is miȝti in onour; and he is not grettere than that man that dredith God.
Fre children seruen a witti seruaunt; and a prudent man and lerned schal not grutche, whanne he is blamed, and an vnkunnynge man schal not be onourid.
Nyle thou enhaunse thee in thi werk to be don; and nyle thou be slow in the tyme of angwisch.

Sone, kepe thi soule in myldenesse; and ȝyue thou onour to it, aftir his merit.
Who schal iustifie hym that synneth aȝens his soule? and who schal onoure hym that disonourith his soule?
A pore man hath glorie bi his lernyng and drede; and ther is a man that is onourid for his catel.
Forsothe if a man hath glorie in pouert, hou myche more in catel? and he that hath glorie in catel, drede pouerte.
The wisdom of a man maad meke schal enhaunse his heed; and schal make hym to sitte in the middis of grete men.

Many tyrauntis han sete in trone; and a man of whom was no supposyng bar the diademe.
Many myȝty men ben oppressid strongli; and gloriouse men ben ȝouun in to the hondis of othere men.
Bifore that thou axe, blame thou not ony man; and whanne thou hast axid, blame thou iustli.
Bifor that thou here, answere thou not a word; and in the myddis of eldere men adde thou not to speke.
Stryue thou not, of that thing that disesith not thee; and stonde thou not in the dom of synnes.
Sone, thi dedis be not in many thingis; and if thou art riche, thou schalt not be with out part of gilt. For if thou suest, thou schalt not take; and thou schalt not ascape, if thou rennist bifore.
Ther is a man trauelynge, and hastynge, and sorewynge, and vnpitouse; and bi so myche more he schal not haue plentee.
Ther is a man fade, nedi of rekyueryng, failynge more in vertu, and plenteuouse in
pouert; and the iȝe of God bihelde hym in good, and reiside hym fro his lownesse, and enhaunsid his heed; and many men wondriden in him, and onouriden God.
Goodis and yuels, lijf and deth, pouert and oneste, ben of God.
Wisdom, and lernyng, and kunnyng of the lawe ben anentis the Lord; loue and the weies of goode men ben at him.
Errour and derknessis ben maad togidere to synneris; forsothe thei that maken ful out ioye in yuel, wexen eld togidere in to yuels.
The ȝifte of God dwellith to iust men; and encreessyngis of hym schulen haue prosperitees without ende.
A man is that is maad riche in doynge scarsli, and this is the
part of his mede, in that that he seith, Y haue founden reste to me, and now Y aloone schal ete of my goodis.
And he noot that tyme passith hym, and deth neiȝeth, and he schal leeue alle thingis to othere men, and schal die.
Stonde thou in thi testament, and speke thou togidere in it; and wexe thou eld in the werk of thin heestis.
Dwelle thou not in the werkis of synneris; but triste thou in God, and dwelle in thi place.
For it is esy in the iȝen of God, sudeynli to make onest a pore man.
The blessing of God haastith in to the meede of a iust man; and the going forth of hym makith fruyt in swift onour.
Seie thou not, What is nede to me? and what goodis schulen be me her aftir?
Seie thou not, Y am sufficient, and what schal Y be maad worse heraftir?
In the dai of goodis be thou not vnmyndeful of yuels, and in the dai of yuels be thou not vnmyndeful of goodis;
for it is esi bifor God to ȝelde in the dai of deth to ech man aftir hise weies.
The malice of oon our makith forȝeting of moost letcherie; and in the ende of a man is makyng nakid of hise werkis.
Preise thou not ony man bifore his deth; for whi a man is knowun in hise sones.
Brynge thou not ech man in to thin hous; for whi many tresouns ben of a gileful man.
For whi as the entrailis of stynkynge thingis breken out, and as a partrich is led in to a trap, ether net, and as a capret is led in to a snare, so and the herte of proude men; and as a biholdere seynge the fal of his neiȝbore.
For he turneth goodis in to yuels, and settith tresouns, and puttith a wem on chosun men.
Fier is encreessid of a sparcle, and blood is encreessid of a gileful man; for whi a synful man settith tresoun to blood.
Take heede to thee fro a gileful man, for he makith yuels; lest perauenture he bringe yn on thee scornyng with outen ende.
Resseyue thou an alien to thee, and he schal distrie thee in whirlwynd, and he schal make thee alien fro thin owne weies.
If thou doist wel, wite thou to whom thou doist; and miche grace schal be to thi goodis.
Do thou wel to a iust man, and thou schalt fynde greet ȝelding; thouȝ not of hym, certis of the Lord.
It is not wel to hym that is customable in yuels, and to hym that ȝyueth not almes; for whi the hiȝeste bothe hatith synneris, and doith merci to hem that doen penaunce.
Ȝyue thou to a merciful man, and resseyue thou not a synnere; God schal ȝelde veniaunce bothe to vnfeithful men and to synneris, kepynge hem in the dai of veniaunce.
Ȝyue thou to a good man, and resseyue thou not a synnere.
Do thou good to a meke man, and ȝyue thou not to an vnpitouse man; forbede thou to ȝyue looues to hym, lest in tho he be myȝtiere than thou.
For thou schalt fynde double yuels in alle goodis, whiche euere thou doist to hym; for whi the hiȝeste bothe hatith synneris, and schal ȝelde veniaunce to vnfeithful men.
A frend schal not be knowun in goodis, and an enemy schal not be hid in yuels.
In the goodis of a man hise enemyes ben sori; and a frend is knowun in the sorewe and malice of him.
Bileue thou neuer to thin enemy; for his wickidnesse roustith as irun.
Thouȝ he be maad meke, and go lowe, caste awei thi soule, and kepe thee fro him.
Sette thou not him bisidis thee, nether sitte he at thi riȝtside, lest he turne and stonde in thi place; lest perauenture he turne in to thi place, and enquere thi chaier, and in the laste tyme thou know mi wordis, and be prickid in my wordis.
Who schal do medecyn to an enchauntere smytun of a serpent, and to alle men that neiȝen to beestis, and to him that goith with an yuel man, and is wlappid in the synnes of him?
In oon our he schal dwelle with thee; sotheli if thou bowist awei, he schal not bere vp.
The enemy makith swete in hise lippis, and in his herte he settith tresoun to ouerturne thee in to the dich.
The enemy wepith in hise iȝen; and if he fyndith tyme, he schal not be fillid of blood.
If yuels bifallen to thee, thou schalt fynde hym the formere there.
The enemy schal wepe bifore thin iȝen, and he as helpynge schal vndurmyne thi feet.
He schal stire his heed, and he schal beete with hond; and he schal speke priuyli many yuels of thee, and schal chaunge his chere.
of it; and he that comyneth with a proude man, schal clothe pride.
He reisith a weiȝte on hym silf, that comyneth with a more onest man than hym silf; and be thou not felowe to a man richere than thou.
What schal a cawdroun comyne to a pot? for whanne tho hirtlen hem silf togidere, the pot schal be brokun.
A riche man schal do vniustli, and schal gnaste; but a pore man hirt schal be stille.
If thou ȝyuest, he schal take thee; and if thou hast not, he schal forsake thee.
If thou hast, he schal lyue togidere with thee, and schal make thee voide; and he schal not haue sorewe on thee.
If thou art nedeful to hym, he schal disseyue thee; and he schal flatere, and schal ȝyue hope, tellinge to thee alle goodis; and schal seie, What is nede to thee?
And he schal schende thee in hise metis, til he anyntische thee twies and thries, and at the laste he schal scorne thee; aftirward he schal se, and schal forsake thee, and he schal moue his heed to thee.
Be thou maad meke to God, and abide thou hise hondis.
Take heede, lest thou be disseyued, and be maad lowe in foli.
Nyle thou be lowe in thi wisdom, lest thou be maad low, and be disseyued in to foli.
Whanne thou art clepid of a miȝtiere man, go thou awei; for bi this he schal more clepe thee.
Be thou not greetli pressyng, lest thou be hurtlid doun; and be thou not fer fro hym, lest thou go in to forȝetyng.
Witholde thou not to speke with hym euenli, and bileue thou not to hise many wordis; for of myche speche he schal tempte thee, and he schal leiȝe priuyli, and schal axe thee of thin hid thingis.
His cruel soule schal kepe thi wordis, and he schal not spare of malice, and of bondis.
Be war to thee, and take heede diligentli to thin heryng; for thou goist with thi distriyng.
But thou heringe tho thingis, se as in sleep, and thou schalt wake.
In al thi lijf loue thou God, and inwardli clepe thou him in thin heelthe.
Ech beeste loueth a beeste lijk it silf; so and ech man owith to loue his neiȝbore.
Ech fleisch schal be ioyned to fleisch lijk it silf, and ech man schal be felouschipid to a man lijk hym silf.
As a wulf schal comyne sum tyme with a lomb, so a synnere with a iust man.
What comininge is of an hooli man to a dogge? ethir what good part is of a riche man to a pore man?
The huntyng of a lioun is a wielde asse in desert; so the lesewis of riche men ben pore men.
And as mekenesse is abhomynacioun to a proude man, so and a pore man is abhomynacioun of a riche man.
A riche man moued is confermed of hise frendis; but a meke man, whanne he fallith, schal be cast out, ȝhe, of knowun men.
Many rekyuereris ben to a riche man disseyued; he spak proudli, and thei iustifieden hym.
A meke man is disseiued, ferthermore also he is repreuyd; he spak wiseli, and no place was ȝouun to hym.
The riche man spak, and alle men weren stille; and thei schulen brynge his word til to the cloudis.
A pore man spak, and thei seien, Who is this? and if he offendith, thei schulen destrye hym.
Catel is good to hym, to whom is no synne in conscience; and the worste pouert is in the mouth of a wickid man.
The herte of a man chaungith his face, ethir in good ethir in yuel.
Of hard and with trauel thou schalt fynde the step of a good herte, and a good face.
Blessid is the man, that slood not bi the word of his mouth, and was not prickid in the sorewe of trespas.
He is blessid, that hath not sorewe of his soule, and fallith not doun fro his hope.
Catel is with out resoun to a coueitouse man, and hard nygard; and wherto is gold to an enuyouse man?
He that gaderith of his wille vniustli, gaderith to othere men; and another man schal mak wast in hise goodis.
To what othere man schal he be good, which is wickid to hym silf? and he schal not be myrye in hise goodis.
No thing is worse, than he that hath enuye to hym silf; and this is the ȝelding of his malice.
And if he doith good, he doith vnwityngli, and not wilfuli; and at the laste he schewith his malice.
The iȝe of an enuyous man is wickid, and turnynge awei the face, and dispisynge his soule.
The iȝe of the coueitouse man is neuere fillid; he schal not be fillid in to the part of wickidnesse, til he performe vnriȝtfulnesse, and make drie his soule.
An yuel iȝe to yuels, and the nedi man schal not be fillid of breed; and he schal be in sorewe on his table.
Sone, if thou hast, do wel with thi silf, and offre thou worthi offryngis to God.
Be thou myndeful that deth schal not tarie, and the testament of hellis, which is schewid to thee; for whi the testament of this world schal die bi deth.
Bifore deth do thou good to thi frend, and bi thi miȝtis stretche thou forth, and ȝyue to a pore man.
Be thou not disseyued of a good dai, and a litil part of a good day passe not thee.
Whether thou schalt not leeue to othere men thi sorewis, and trauels?
In the departyng of lot ȝyue thou, and take; and iustifie thi soule.
Bifore thi deth worche thou riȝtfulnesse; for at hellis it is not to fynde mete.
Ech man schal wexe eld as hey, and as a leef bryngynge fruit in a greene tree.
Othere ben gendrid, and othere ben cast doun; so the generacioun of fleisch and blood, another is endid, and another is borun.
Ech corruptible werk schal faile in the ende; and he that worchith it, schal go with it.
And al chosun werk schal be iustified; and he that worchith it, schal be onourid in it.
Blessid is the man, that schal dwelle in wisdom, and that schal bithenke in riȝtfulnesse, and schal thenke in wit the biholding of God.
Which thenkith out, ether fyndith out, the weies of hym in his herte, and schal be vndurstondynge in the hid thingis of hym; goynge as a serchere aftir it, and stondynge in the weies of it.
Which biholdith bi the wyndows therof, and herith in the
ȝatis therof; which restith nyȝ the hous therof, and settith a stak in the wallis therof. He schal sette his litil hous at the hondis of hym, and goodis schulen reste in his litil hous, bi duryng of the world;
he schal sette hise sones vndur the hilyng therof, and he schal dwelle vndur the
boowis therof; he schal be kyuerid vndur the hilyng therof fro heete, and he schal reste in the glorie therof.
He that dredith God, schal do goode werkis; and he that holdith riȝtfulnesse, schal take it.
And it as a modir onourid schal meete hym, and as a womman fro virgynyte it schal take hym.
It shal feede hym with the breed of lijf, and of vndurstonding; and it schal ȝyue drynke to hym with watir of heelful wisdom; it schal be maad stidfast in hym, and he schal not be bowid.
And it schal holde hym, and he schal not be schent; and it schal enhaunse hym at his neiȝboris.
And in the myddis of the chirche he schal opene his mouth; and God schal fille hym with the spirit of wisdom, and of vndurstonding, and schal clothe hym with the stoole of glorie.
God schal tresore on hym myrthe, and ful out ioiyng; and schal enherite hym with euerlastynge name.
Fonned men schulen not take that wisdom, and witti men schulen meete it. Fonned men schulen not se it; for whi it goith awey fer fro pride, and gile.
Men leesyngmongeris schulen not be myndful therof, and sothefast men ben foundun ther ynne; and schulen haue prosperite til to the biholding of God.
Preisyng is not fair in the mouth of a synnere, for he is not sent of the Lord.
For whi wisdom ȝede forth fro God; forsothe heriyng schal stonde nyȝ the wisdom of God, and it schal be plenteuouse in a feithful mouth, and the Lord schal ȝyue it to him.
Seie thou not, It goith awei bi God; for whi do thou not tho thingis, whiche God hatith.
Seie thou not, He made me for to erre; for whi wickid men ben not nedeful to hym.
The Lord hatith al cursidnesse of errour, and it schal not be amyable to hem, that dreden hym.
At the bigynnyng God made man, and lefte him in the hond of his councel.
He addide hise comaundementis,
and lawis; if thou wolt kepe the comaundementis, tho schulen kepe thee, and kepe plesaunt feith with outen ende.
He hath set to thee watir and fier; dresse thin hond to that, that thou wolt.
Bifor man is lijf and deth, good and yuel; that, that plesith hym, schal be ȝouun to hym.
For whi the wisdom of God is myche, and he is strong in power, and seeth alle men without ceessing.
The iȝen of the Lord ben to hem, that dreden hym; and he knowith al the trauel of man.
He comaundide not to ony man to do wickidli; and he ȝaf not to ony man space to do synne.
For he coueytith not the multitude of sones vnfeithful and vnprofitable.
Be thou not glad in wickid sones, if thei ben multiplied; nether delite thou on hem, if the drede of God is not in hem.
Bileue thou not to the lijf of hem, and biholde thou not in to the trauels of hem.
For whi betere is oon dredynge God, than a thousynde wickid sones.
And it is more profitable to die with out sones, than to leeue wickid sones.
A cuntrei shal be enhabitid of o witti man; and it schal be maad desert of thre wickid men.
Myn iȝe siȝ many othere thingis, and myn eere herde strongere thingis than these.
Fier schal brenne an hiȝ in the synagoge of synneris, and yre schal brenne an hiȝ in a folk vnbileuful.
Elde giauntis that weren distried, tristynge on her vertu, preieden
not for her synnes; and God sparide not the pilgrymage of hem, but he killide hem, and curside hem, for the pride of her word.
He hadde not merci on hem, and he loste al the folk enhaunsynge hem silf in her synnes.
And as he killide sixe hundrid thousynde of foot men, that weren gaderid togidere in the hardnesse of her herte; and if oon hadde be hard nollid, wondur if he hadde be giltles.
For whi merci and ire is with hym; preier is myȝti, and schedynge out ire.
Bi his merci, so is the chastisyng of ech man; he is demyd bi hise werkis.
A synnere in raueyn schal not ascape; and the sufferaunce of hym that doith merci schal not tarie.
Al merci schal make place to ech man, aftir the merit of his werkis, and aftir the vndurstonding of his pilgrymage.
Seie thou not, Y schal be hid fro God; and fro the hiȝeste, who schal haue mynde on me?
Seie thou not, Y schal not be knowun in a greet puple; for whi which is my soule in so greet a creature?
Lo! heuene, and the heuenes of heuenes, the greet occian, and al erthe, and tho thingis that ben in tho, schulen
be mouyd in his siȝt; munteyns togidere, and litle hillis, and the foundementis of erthe; and whanne God biholdith tho, tho schulen be schakun togidere with tremblyng.
And in alle these thingis the herte is vnwijs, and ech herte is vndurstondun of hym.
And who vndurstondith hise weies? and who vndurstondith a tempest, which the iȝe of man siȝ not?
For whi ful many werkis of hym ben in hid thingis, but who schal telle out the werkis of his riȝtfulnesse, ether who schal suffre? For whi the testament is fer fro summe men; and the axyng of men is in the endyng.
He that is maad litil in herte, thenkith veyn thingis; and a man vnprudent and a fool thenkith fonned thingis.
Sone, here thou me, and lerne thou techyng of wit, and ȝyue thou tent to my wordis in thin herte; and Y schal seie techyng in equyte, and Y schal seke to telle out wisdom. And ȝyue thou tent to
my wordis in thin herte; and Y seie in equyte of spirit the vertues, whiche God hath set on hise werkis at the bigynnyng, and in treuthe Y telle out the kunnyng of him.
In the doom of God ben hise werkis fro the bigynnyng; and in the ordynaunce of tho he departyde the partis of tho, and he departide the bigynnyngis of tho in hise folkis.
He ournede with outen ende the werkis of hem thei hungriden not, nether traueliden, and thei ceessiden not of her werkis.
Ech schal not make streit the nexte to hym, til in to with outen ende.
Be thou not vnbileueful to the word of him.
Aftir these thingis God bihelde in to the erthe, and fillide it with hise goodis.
Forsothe the soule of ech lyuynge thing teld bifore his face; and thilke soule is eft the turnyng aȝen of tho thinges.
God formede man of erthe; and aftir his ymage he made man.
And eft he turnede man in to that ymage; and aftir hym silf he clothide hym with vertu.
He ȝaf to hym the noumbre of daies, and tyme; and he ȝaf to him power of tho thingis that ben on erthe.
He settide the drede of man on al fleisch, and he was lord of beestis and fliynge briddis.
He formyde of man an help lijk hym; he ȝaf to hem councel, and tunge, and iȝen, and eeris, and herte to thenke out; and he fillide hem with techyng of vndurstondyng.
He made to hem the kunnyng of spirit, he fillide the herte of hem with wit; and he schewide to hem yuels and goodis.
He settide the iȝe of hem on the hertes of hem, to schewe to hem the grete
thingis of hise werkis, that thei preise togidere the name of halewyng; and to haue glorie in hise meruels, that thei telle out the grete thingis of hise werkis.
He addide to hem techyng; and he enheritide hem with the lawe of lijf.
He ordeynyde an euerlastynge testament with hem; and he schewide to hem hise riȝtfulnesse, and domes.
And the iȝe of hem siȝ the grete thingis of his onour, and the eeris of hem herden the onour of vois; and he seide to hem, Take heede to ȝou fro al wickid thing.
And he comaundide to hem, to ech man of his neiȝbore.
The weies of hem ben euere bifore hym; tho ben not hid fro hise iȝen.
On ech folk
he made souereyn a gouernour; and Israel was maad the opyn part of God.
And alle the werkis of hem ben as the sunne in the siȝt of God; and hise iȝen biholden with out ceessyng in the weies of hem.
Testamentis weren not hid fro the wickidnesse of hem; and alle the wickydnessis of hem weren in the siȝt of God.
The almes of a man is as a bagge with hym, and it schal kepe the grace of a man as
the appil of the iȝe; and afterward man schal rise aȝen, and it schal ȝelde to hem a ȝelding, to ech man in to the heed of hem; and schal turne in to the lower partis of erthe.
Forsothe it ȝaf to men repentinge the weie of riȝtfulnesse, and confermede men failynge to suffre, and ordeynede to hem the part of treuthe.
Turne thou to the Lord, and forsake thi
synnes; preye thou bifore the face of the Lord, and make thou lesse hirtingis.
Turne thou aȝen to the Lord, and turne thou awei fro thin vnriȝtfulnesse, and hate thou greetli cursyng.
And knowe thou the riȝtfulnessis, and domes of God; and stonde thou in the part of good purpos, and of preier of the hiȝeste God.
Go thou in to the partis of the hooli world, with men lyuynge, and ȝyuynge knouleching to God.
Dwelle thou not in the errour of wickid men. Knouleche thou bifore deth; knouleching perischith fro a deed man, as no thing.
Lyuynge thou schalt knouleche, lyuynge and hool thou schalt knowleche, and schalt herie God; and thou schalt haue glorie in the merciful doyngis of hym.
The merci of God is ful greet, and his help to hem that conuerten to hym.
For whi not alle thingis moun be in men; for whi the sone of man is not vndeedli, and malices plesiden in to vanyte.
What is clerere than the sunne? and this schal faile; ethir what is worse than that, that fleisch and blood thouȝte out? and of this he schal be repreued.
He biholdith the vertu of hiȝnesse of heuene; and alle men ben erthe and aische.
He that lyueth with out bigynnyng and ende, made of nouȝt alle thingis togidere; God alone schal be iustified, and he dwellith a king vnouercomun with outen ende.
Who schal suffice to telle
out his werkis? for whi who schal seke the grete thingis of hym?
But who schal telle out the vertu of his greetnesse? ether who schal leie to for to telle out his mercy?
It is not to make lesse, nether to leie to; nethir it is to fynde the grete thingis of God.
Whanne a man hath endid, thanne he schal bigynne; and whanne he hath restid, he schal worche.
What is a man, and what is the glorie of him? and what is good, ether what is the wickid thing of him?
The noumbre of the daies of men, that ben comynli an hundrid ȝeer, ben arettid as the dropis of the watir of the see; and as the stoon of grauel, so a fewe ȝeeris in the dai of euerlastyngnesse.
For this thing God is pacient in hem, and schedith out on hem his merci.
He siȝ the presumpcioun of her herte, for it was yuel; and he knew the distriyng of hem, for it was wickid.
Therfor he fillide his merci in hem, and schewide to hem the weie of equite.
The merciful doyng of man is aboute his neiȝbore; but the merci of the Lord is ouer ech fleisch.
He that hath merci, and techith, and chastisith as a scheepherde
his floc, do merci, takynge the techyng of merciful doyng; and he that hastith in the domes therof.
Sone, in goodis ȝyue thou not pleynt, and in ech ȝifte ȝyue thou not heuynesse of an yuel word.
Whether dew schal not kele heete? so and a word is betere than ȝifte.
Lo! whether a word is not aboue a good ȝifte? but euer ethir is with a man iustified.
A fool schal vpbreide scharpli; and the ȝifte of an vntauȝt man makith iȝen to faile.
Bifore the doom make thou redi riȝtfulnesse to thee; and lerne thou, bifore that thou speke.
Bifore sikenesse ȝyue thou medicyn; and bifore the doom axe thi silf, and thou schalt fynde merci in the siȝt of God.
Bifore sikenesse make the meke, and in the tyme of sikenesse schewe thi lyuyng.
Be thou not lettid to preye euere, and drede thou not to be iustified til to deth; for whi the meede of God dwellith with outen ende.
Bifore preier make redi thi soule; and nyle thou be as a man that temptith God.
Haue thou mynde of ire in the dai of endyng; and make thou in lyuyng the tyme of ȝelding.
Haue thou mynde of pouert in the dai of abundaunce; and the nede of pouert in the tyme of richessis.
Fro the morewtid til to the euentid the tyme schal be chaungid; and alle these thingis ben swift in the iȝen of God.
A wise man schal drede in alle thingis; and in the daies of trespassis he schal fle fro vnkunnyng, ether slouthe.
Ech fel man knowith wisdom; and to hym that fyndith it, he schal ȝyue knouleching.
Witti men in wordis also thei diden wiseli, and vndurstoden treuthe, and riȝtfulnesse; and bisouȝten prouerbis and domes.
Go thou not aftir thi coueitises; and be thou turned awei fro thi wille.
If thou ȝyuest to thi soule the coueitisis therof, it schal make thee in to ioie to thin enemyes.
Delite thou not in cumpenyes, nether in litle cumpenyes; for whi the synnyng of hem is contynuel.
Be thou not meene in the stryuyng of looue, and sum thing is to thee in the world; for whi thou schalt be enuyouse to thi soule.
A drunkelew werk man schal not be maad riche; and he that chargith not litle synnes, fallith doun litil and litil.
Wyn and wymmen maken to be apostataas, ȝhe, wise men; and thei repreuen witti men.
And he that ioyneth hym silf to hooris, schal be wickid; rot and wormes schulen enherite hym, and he schal be set an hiȝ in to more ensaumple, and his soule schal be takun awei fro noumbre.
He that bileueth soone, is vnstable in herte, and schal be maad lesse; and he that trespassith aȝens his soule, schal be had ferthermore.
He that ioieth in wickidnesse, schal be cursid; and he that hatith blamyng, schal be maad lesse in lijf; and he that hatith ianglyng, quenchith malice.
He that synneth aȝens his soule, schal repente; and he that is myrie in malice, schal be cursid.
Reherse thou not an hard word, and wickid; and thou schalt not be maad lesse.
Nyle thou telle thi wit to frend and enemye; and if trespas is to thee, nyle thou make nakid.
For he schal here thee, and schal kepe thee, and he as defendynge the synne schal hate thee; and so he schal be euere with thee.
Thou hast herd a word aȝens thi neiȝbore; die it togidere in thee, and triste thou that it schal not breke thee.
A fool trauelith greetli of the face of a word, as the sorewe of beryng of a ȝong child.
An arowe fastned in the hipe of a dogge, so a word in the herte of a fool.
Repreue thou a frend, lest perauenture he vndurstonde not, and seie, Y dide not; ether if he hath do, lest he adde to do eft.
Repreue thou a neiȝbore, lest perauenture he seie not; and if he seith, lest perauenture he reherse.
Repreue thou a frend, for whi
trespassynge is don ofte; and bileue thou not to ech word. Ther is a man that fallith bi his tunge, but not of wille.
For whi who is he, that trespassith not in his tunge? Repreue thou a neiȝbore,
bifore that thou manaasse; and ȝyue thou place to the drede of the hiȝeste. For whi al wisdom is the drede of God, and in that wisdom for to drede God; and the ordynaunce of lawe is in al wisdom.
And the teching of wickidnesse is not wisdom; and the prudence of synnes is not good thouȝt.
Ther is wickidnesse of prudence, and cursidnesse is ther ynne; and ther is an vnwijs man, which is maad litil in wisdom.
Betere is a man that hath litil in wisdom, and failynge in wit in the drede of God, than he that hath plentee of wit, and brekith the lawe of the hiȝeste.
Ther is certeyn sutilte, and it is wickid.
And ther is a man, that sendith out a certeyn word, tellynge out treuthe. Ther is a man, that mekith hym silf wickidly; and hise ynnere thingis ben ful of gile.
And ther is a iust man, that makith low greetli hym silf of myche mekenesse; and ther is a iust man, that bowith the face, and feyneth hym to se not that, that is vnknowun.
Thouȝ he is forbodun of feblenesse of strengthis to do synne; if he fyndith tyme to do yuele, he schal do yuel.
A man is knowun bi siȝt; and a witti man is knowun bi meetyng of face.
The clothing of bodi, and the leiȝyng of teeth, and the entring of a man, tellen out of hym.
Ther is fals repreuyng in the ire of a man ful of dispisyng; and ther is dom which is not preued to be good; and ther is a stille man, and he is prudent.
It is ful good to repreue, more than to be wrooth, and to forbede not a man knoulechyng in preiere.
The coueitise of a geldyng hath defoulid the maidynhed of
a ȝong womman, so he that makith wickid dom bi violence.
It is ful good, that a man that is repreued schewe opynli penaunce; for so thou schalt ascape wilful synne.
Ther is a stil man, which is foundun wijs; and he is hateful, which is fool hardi to speke.
Sotheli ther is a stille man, not hauynge wit of speche; and ther is a stille man, knowynge the sesoun of couenable tyme.
A wijs man schal be stille til to tyme; but a ioli man and vnprudent man schulen not kepe tyme.
He that vsith many wordis, hirtith his soule; and he that takith power to hym silf vniustli, schal be hatid.
Ther is goyng forth in yuels to a man vnlernyd; and ther is fyndyng in to peiryng.
Ther is a ȝifte, which is not profitable; and ther is a ȝifte, whos ȝeldyng is double.
Ther is makyng lesse for glorie; and ther is a man, which schal reise the heed fro mekenesse.
Ther is a man, that aȝen bieth many synnes for litil prijs, and restorith tho in seuenfold.
A wijs man in wordis makith hym silf amyable; but the graces of foolis schulen be sched out.
The ȝifte of an vnwijs man schal not be profitable to thee; for hise iȝen ben seuenfold.
He schal ȝyue litle thingis, and he schal vpbreide many thingis; and the openyng of his mouth is enflawming.
To dai a man leeneth, and to morewe he axith; and siche a man is hateful.
A frend schal not be to a fool, and grace schal not be to hise goodis.
For thei that eten his breed, ben of fals tunge; hou ofte and hou many men schulen scorne hym?
For he departith not bi euene wit that, that was worthi to be had; in lijk maner and that, that was not worthi to be had.
The falling of a fals tunge is as he that fallith in the pawment; so the fallis of yuele men schulen come hastili.
A man with out grace is as a veyn fable; and it schal be customable in the mouth of vnlerned men.
A parable schal be repreued of the mouth of a fool; for he seith not it in his tyme. Ther is a man, that is forbodun to do synne, for pouert; and he schal be prickid in his reste.
Ther is a man, that schal leese his soule for schame; and for the vnprudence of a persoone he schal leese it.
Forsothe he schal leese hym silf for the takyng of a persoone.
Ther is a man, that for schame biheetith to a frend; and he hath gete hym enemy with out cause.
Leesyng is a wickid schenschip in a man; and it schal be customabli in the mouth of vnlerned men.
Betere is a theef than the customablenesse of a man, a leesyngmongere; forsothe bothe thei schulen enherite perdicioun.
The maneres of men leesyngmongeris ben with outen onour; and her schenschype is with hem with out ceessyng.
A wijs man in wordis schal brynge forth hym silf; and a prudent man schal pleese grete men.
He that worchith his lond, shal make hiȝ the heep of fruytis; and he that worchith riȝtfulnesse, schal be enhaunsid. Sotheli he that plesith grete men, schal ascape wickidnesse.
Presentis and ȝiftis blynden the iȝen of iugis; and as doumb in the mouth it turneth awei the chastisyngis of hem.
Wisdom hid, and tresour vnseyn, what profit is in euer eithir?
He is betere, that hidith his vnwisdom, than a man that hidith his wisdom.
Sone, thou hast do synne? adde thou not eft; but biseche thou for the formere synnes, that tho be forȝouun to thee.
As fro the face of a serpent fle thou synnes; and if thou neiȝest to tho synnes, tho schulen take thee.
The teeth of a lioun ben the teeth therof, that sleen the soulis of men.
Al wickidnesse is as a scharp swerd on either syde; heelthe is not to the wounde therof.
Chidyngis and wrongis schulen distrie catel; and an houe that is ouer riche, schal be distriede bi pride; so the catel of a proude man schal be drawun vp bi the roote.
The preyer of a pore man schal come fro the mouth til to eeris; and doom schal come to hym hastili.
He that hatith repreuyng, is a step of the synnere; and he that dredith God, schal be turned to his herte.
A miȝti man with an hardi tunge is knowun afer; and a witti man kan kepe him silf fro that man.
He that bildith his hous with othere mennus costis, is as he that gaderith hise stonys in wyntir.
Scheuys gaderid togidere is the synagoge of synneris; and the endyng of hem is the flawme of fier.
The weie of synneris is set togidere with stoonys; and in the ende of hem ben hellis, and derknessis, and peynes.
He that kepith riȝtfulnesse, schal holde the wit therof.
The perfeccioun of Goddis drede is wisdom and wit.
He schal not be tauȝt, which is not wijs in good.
Forsothe vnwisdom is, which is plenteuouse in yuel; and wit is not, where is bittirnesse.
The kunnyng of a wijs man schal be plenteuouse as flowyng; and the councel of hym dwellith as a welle of lijf.
The herte of a fool is as a brokun vessel; and it schal not holde ony wisdom.
What euer wijs word a kunnynge man herith, he schal preise, and leie to. A letcherouse man herde, and it schal displese hym; and he schal caste it awei bihynde his bak.
The tellynge of a fool is as a birthun in the weie; for whi grace schal be foundun in the lippis of a wijs man.
The mouth of a prudent man is souȝt in the chirche; and men schulen thenke hise wordis in her hertis.
As an hous distried, so is wisdom to a fool; and the kunnyng of an vnwijs man is wordis that moun not be teld out.
Stockis in the feet is techyng to a fool; and as bondis of hondis on the riȝt hond.
A fool enhaunsith his vois in leiȝyng; but a wijs man schal leiȝe vnnethis stilli.
Techyng is a goldun ournement to a prudent man; and as an ournement of the arm in the riȝt arm.
The foot of a fool is liȝt in to the hous of a neiȝbore; and a wijs man schal be aschamed of the persoone of a miȝti man.
A fool biholdith fro the wyndow in to the hous; but a lerned man schal stonde with out forth.
It is foli of a man to herkene bi the dore; and a prudent man schal be greuyd bi dispisyng.
The lippis of vnprudent men schulen telle fonned thingis; but the wordis of prudent men schulen be weied in a balaunce.
The herte of foolis is in her mouth; and the mouth of wise men is in her herte.
Whanne a wickid man cursith the deuel, he cursith his owne soule.
A priuy bacbitere schal defoule his soule, and in alle thingis he schal be hatid, and he that dwellith, schal be hatid; a stil man and wijs schal be onourid.
A slow man is stonyd in a stoon of cley; and alle men schulen speke on the dispisyng of him.
A slow man is stonyd of the dung of oxis; and ech man that touchith hym, schal schake the hondis.
The schame of a fadir is of a sone vnlerned; but a fonned douȝter schal be in decreessyng.
A prudent douȝter is eritage to hir hosebonde; for sche that schendith hir hosebonde, is in dispisyng of the fadir.
A schameles womman schendith the fadir and hosebonde, and schal not be maad lesse than vnfeithful men; forsothe sche schal not be onourid of euer either.
Melodie in morenyng is vncouuenable tellyng; betyngis and techyng in al tyme with wisdom.
He that techith a fool, as he that glueth togidere a tiel stoon.
He that tellith a word to hym that herith not, is as he that reisith a man slepynge fro a greuouse sleep.
He that tellith wisdom to a fool, spekith with a man slepynge; and in the ende of the tellyng he schal seie, Who is this?
Wepe thou on a deed man, for whi his liȝt failide; and wepe thou on a fool, for he failide of wit.
Wepe thou a litil on a deed man, for he hath restid.
Forsothe the lijf of a ful wickid man is ful wickid, more than the deth of a fool.
The morenyng of a deed man is seuene daies; but the morenyng of a fool and of a wickid man is alle the daies of her lijf.
Speke thou not myche with a fool, and go thou not with an vnwijs man.
Keep thee fro hym, that thou haue not disese; and thou schalt not be defoulid in the synne of hym.
Boowe thou awei fro hym, and thou schalt fynde reste; and be thou not anoied by his foly.
What schal be maad heuyere than leed? and what othere name than a fool is to it?
It is liȝtere to bere grauel, and salt, and a gobet of yrun, than a man vnprudent, and a fool, and vnfeithful.
As an heep of trees, boundun togidere in the foundement of the bilding, schal not be vnboundun, so and an herte confermed in the thouȝt of counsel.
The thouȝt of a wijs man shal not be maad schrewid in ony tyme, nether drede.
As chaffis in hiȝe places, and soond with out medling of hym, set aȝens the face of wynd, schulen not dwelle;
so and a dreedful herte in the thouȝt of a fool aȝenstondith not aȝens the feersnesse of drede.
As ournyng, ether pargetyng, ful of grauel in a cleer wal, so and a ferdful herte in the thouȝt of a fool schal not drede in ony tyme; so and he that dwellith euere in the heestis of God.
He that prickith the iȝe, schal leede out teeris; and he that prickith the herte, bryngith forth wit.
He that castith a stoon to briddis, schal caste doun tho; so and he that doith wrong to a frend, departith frenschipe.
Thouȝ thou bryngist forth a swerd to a frend, dispeire thou not; for ther is going aȝen to the frend.
If he openeth a soreuful mouth, drede thou not; for whi ther is acordyng, outakun dispisynge, and schenschipe, and pride, and schewyng of preuyte, and a tretcherouse wounde; in alle these thingis a frend schal fle awei.
Haue thou feith with a frend in his pouert, that thou be glad also in hise goodis.
In the tyme of his tribulacioun dwelle thou feithful to hym, that also thou be euene eir in the eritage of hym.
Heete and smook of fier is maad hiȝ bifore the fier of a chymenei; so and cursyngis, and dispisyngis, and manaassis, comen bifore blood.
I schal not be aschamed for to grete a frend, and Y schal not hide me fro his face; thouȝ yuels comen to me bi hym, Y schal suffre.
Ech man that schal here, schal kepe warli hym silf fro hym.
Who schal ȝyue keping to my mouth, and a certeyn ceelyng on my lippis, that Y falle not bi tho, and that my tunge leese not me?
Lord, fadir, and lordli gouernour of my lijf, forsake thou me not in the thouȝt and counsel of hem; nether suffre thou me to falle in that schenschipe.
Who settith aboue in my thouȝt beetyngis, and in myn hert the techyng of wisdom, that in the vnkunnyngis of hem he spare not me, and that the trespassis of hem appere not?
Lest myn vnkunnyngis encreesse, and my trespassis be multiplied, and my synnes be plenteuouse; and lest Y falle in the siȝt of myn aduersaries, and myn enemy haue ioie.
Lord, fadir, and God of my lijf, forsake thou not me in the thouȝt of hem.
Ȝyue thou not to me enhaunsyng of myn iȝen; and turne thou awei fro me al schrewid desijr.
Do thou awei fro me the coueitisis of the wombe, and the coueitisis of letcherie take me not; and ȝyue thou not me to a soule vnreuerent and vndiscreet.
Sones, here ȝe the techyng of mouth; and he that kepith it, schal not perische bi hise lippis, nether schal be
sclaundrid in worste werkis A synnere and proude man schal be takun in his vanite; and a cursid man schal be sclaundrid in tho.
Thy mouth be not customable to swering; for whi many fallyngis ben ther ynne.
Forsothe the nemyng of God be not customable in thi mouth, and be thou not meddlid to the names of seyntis; for thou schalt not be giltles of hem.
For as a seruaunt that is axid bisili, schal not wante wannesse; so ech man swerynge and nemynge schal not be purgid of synne in al.
A man swerynge myche schal be fillid with wickidnesse; and veniaunce schal not go awei fro his hous.
And if he disseyueth a brother, his trespas schal be aboue hym; and if he feyneth, he schal trespasse doubli.
And if he swerith in veyn, he schal not be iustified; for whi his hous schal be fillid with worst ȝelding.
Also aȝenward another speche is in to deth; be it not found in the eritage of Jacob.
For whi alle these thingis schulen be don awei fro merciful men; and thei schulen not delite in trespassis.
Thi mouth be not customable to vnreuerent speche; for whi a word of synne is in it.
Haue thou mynde on thi fadir and modir; for thou stondist in the myddis of grete men.
Lest perauenture God forȝete thee in the siȝt of hem; and lest thou maad a fool bi thi customablenesse, suffre schenschipe, and haddist leuere to be not borun, and curse the dai of thi birthe.
A man customable in the wordis of schenschipe, in alle daies schal not be tauȝt.
Twei kyndis ben plenteuouse in synnes, and the thridde bringith ire and perdicioun.
An hoot soule brennynge as fier schal not be quenchid, til it
swolewe sum thing; and a wickid man in the mouth of his fleisch schal not faile, til he kyndle fier.
Ech breed is swete to a letcherouse man; he schal not be maad weri, trespassynge til to the ende.
Ech man that passith his bed, doith dispit aȝens his soule, and seith, Who seeth me?
Derknessis cumpassen me, and wallis kyueren me, and no man biholdith me. Whom drede Y? The hiȝeste schal not haue mynde on my synnes.
And he vndirstondith not, that the iȝe of him seeth alle thingis; for whi the drede of siche a man puttith awei fro him the drede of God, and the iȝen of men that dreden hym putten awei fro hym Goddis drede.
And he knew not, that the iȝen of the Lord ben myche more clerere than the sunne, and biholden alle the weies of men, and the depthe of the see, and biholden the hertis of men in to hid partis.
For whi alle thingis weren knowun to the Lord, bifore that thei weren maad of nouȝt; so and aftir the makyng he biholdith alle thingis.
This man schal be punyschid in the stretis of the citee; he schal be dryuun a wei as an horse colt, and he schal be takun, where he hopith not.
And he schal be schenschip to alle men; for he vndurstood not the drede of the Lord.
So and ech womman forsakynge hir hosebonde schal do synne, and ordeynynge eritage of an alien matrimonye.
For firste sche was vnbileueful in the lawe of the hiȝeste, and the secounde tyme sche forsook hir hosebonde; and the thridde tyme sche was defoulid in auowtrie, and ordeynede to hym sones of another man.
This womman schal be brouȝt in to the chirche, and me schal biholde on hir sones.
Hir sones schulen not ȝyue rootis, and hir braunchis schulen not ȝyue fruyt.
Thei schulen leeue the mynde of hir in to cursyng, and the schenschipe of hir schal not be don awei.
And thei that ben left schulen knowe, that no thing is betere than the drede of God, and nothing is swettere than to biholde in the comaundementis of the Lord.
It is greet glorie to sue the Lord; for whi lengthe of daies schulen be takun of hym.
Wisdom schal preise his soule, and he schal be onourid in God; and he schal haue glorie in the myddis of his puple.
And he schal opene his mouth in the chirchis of the hiȝeste; and he schal haue glorie in the siȝt of his vertu.
And he schal be enhaunsid in the myddis of his puple; and he schal wondre in hooli plentee.
And in the multitude of chosun men he schal haue preisyng; and among blessid
men he schal be blessid, and seie, I, the firste gendrid bifore ech creature, cam forth fro the mouth of the hiȝeste.
I made in heuenes, that liȝt neuere failynge roos vp, and as a cloude Y hilide al erthe.
Y dwellide in hiȝeste thingis, and my trone in a piler of cloude.
Y aloone ȝede aboute the cumpas of heuene, and Y perside the depthe of the see; and Y ȝede in the wawis
of the see, and Y stood in al the lond.
And Y hadde the firste dignite in ech puple,
and in ech folk; and Y trad bi vertu on the neckis of alle excelent men and meke; and in alle these men Y souȝte reste, and Y schal dwelle in the eritage of the Lord.
Thanne the creatour of alle comaundide, and seide to me; and he that formyde me, restide in my tabernacle;
and he seide to me, Dwelle thou in Jacob, and take thou eritage in Israel, and sende thou rootis in my chosun men.
Y was gendrid of the bigynnyng and bifore worldis, and Y schal not faile til to the world to comynge; and Y mynystride in an hooli dwellyng bifore hym.
And so Y was maad stidfast in Syon, and in lijk maner Y restide in a citee halewid, and my power was in Jerusalem.
And Y rootid in a puple onourid; and the eritage therof in to the partis of my God, and my witholding in the plentee of seyntis.
Y was enhaunsid as a cedre in Liban, and as a cipresse tree in the hil of Syon.
Y was enhaunsid as a palm tree in Cades, and as the plauntyng of roose in Jeryco.
As a fair olyue tree in feeldis; and Y was enhaunsid as a plane tree bisidis watir in stretis.
As canel and bawme ȝyuynge greet smelle, Y ȝaf odour; as chosun myrre Y ȝaf the swetnesse of odour.
And as storax, and galban, and vngula, and gumme, and as Liban not kit doun, Y made hoot my dwellyng place; and myn odour as bawme not meddlid.
Y as a terebynte stretchide forth my boowis; and my boowis ben boowis of onour, and of glorie.
Y as a vyne made fruyt the swetnesse of odour; and my flouris ben the fruytis of onour, and of oneste.
I am a modir of fair loue, and of drede, and of knowyng, and of hooli hope.
In me is al grace of weie, and of treuthe; in me is al hope of lijf and of vertu.
Alle ȝe that coueiten me, passe to me; and be ȝe fillid of my generaciouns.
For whi my spirit is swete aboue hony; and myn eritage is aboue hony, and hony comb.
My mynde is in the generacioun of worldis.
Thei that eten me, schulen hungre ȝit; and thei that drynken me, schulen thirste ȝit.
He that herith me, shal not be schent; and thei that worchen in me, schulen not do synne;
and thei that declaren me, schulen haue euere lastynge lijf.
Alle these thingis is the book of lijf, and the testament of the hiȝeste, and the knowyng of treuthe.
Moises comaundide a lawe in the comaundementis of riȝtfulnessis, and eritage to the hous of Jacob, and biheestis to Israel.
He settide to Dauid, his child, to reise of hym a kyng moost strong, and sittynge with outen ende in the trone of onour.
Which kyng fillith wisdom, as Phison schedith out watir; and as Tigris in the daies of newe thingis.
Which, as Eufrates, fillith wit; which multiplieth, as Jordan in the tyme of heruest.
Which sendith techyng as liȝt; and is niȝ alle men, as Gion in the dai of vendage.
Which makith perfitli first to knowe that wisdom; and a feblere man schal not enserche it.
For whi the thouȝt therof schal be plenteuouse of the see; and his counsel in the greet occian.
Y wisdom schedde out
floodis; Y as a weie of ful greet watir of the flood. Y as the flood Dorix, and as a watir cundit Y ȝede out of paradis.
Y seide, I schal watir my gardyn of plauntyngis; and Y schal greetli fille the fruyt of my child beryng.
And lo! a plenteuouse weie of watir is maad to me; and my flood neiȝede to the see.
For Y liȝtne techyng as the cheer morewtid to alle men; and Y schal telle out it til to fer.
Y schal perse alle the lowere partis of erthe, and Y schal biholde alle that slepen; and Y schal liȝtne alle that hopen in the Lord.
Ȝit Y schal schede out teching as profesie, and Y schal leeue it to hem that seken wisdom; and Y schal not faile in to the generaciouns of hem, til in to the hooli world.
Se ȝe, that Y trauelide not to me aloone, but to alle that seken out treuthe.
In thre thingis it is plesid to my spirit, which ben appreued bifore God and men;
acordyng of britheren, and loue of neiȝboris, a man and womman wel consentynge to hem silf.
My soule hatide thre spicis, and Y am greued greetli to the
soule of hem; a pore man proud, and a riche man liere, and an eld man a fool and vnwitti.
Hou schalt thou fynde in thin eelde tho thingis, whiche thou gaderist not in thi ȝongthe?
Doom is ful fair in hoornesse, and to preestis to knowe councel.
Wisdom is ful fair to eelde men, and gloriouse vndirstondyng, and councel.
The coroun of eelde men is in myche kunnyng; and the glorie of hem is the drede of God.
I magnefiede nyne thingis vnsuspect of the herte; and Y schal seie the tenthe thing bi tunge to men.
A man which lyuynge is myrie in sones, and seynge the distriyng of hise enemyes.
He is blessid that dwellith with a witty womman, and he that felle not bi his tunge, and he that seruyde not to men vnworthi to hym silf.
He is blessid that fyndith a very frend, and he that tellith out riȝtfulnesse to an eere heringe.
He is ful greet that fyndith wisdom and kunnyng; but he is not aboue him that dredith God.
The drede of God hath set it silf aboue alle thingis.
Blessid is the man to whom it is ȝouun to have the drede of God; to whom schal he be licned, that holdith that drede?
The drede of God is the bigynnyng of his loue; forsothe the bigynnyng of feith is to be faste ioyned therto.
The sorewe of herte is ech wounde; and the wickidnesse of a womman is al malice.
A leche shal se ech wounde, and not the wounde of herte;
and al wickidnesse, and not the wickidnesse
of a womman; and ech hilyng, and
not hilyng of hateris; and ech veniaunce, and not the veniaunce of enemyes.
Noon heed is worse than the heed of an eddre
dwellynge in schadewe; and noon ire is aboue the ire of a womman. It schal plese more to dwelle with a lioun and a dragoun, than to dwelle with a wickid womman.
The wickidnesse of a womman chaungith hir face; and sche blyndide her cheer as a beer doith, and sche schal schewe as a sak in the myddis of neiȝboris.
Hir hosebonde weilide; and his wickid wijf herde, and siȝȝide a litil.
Al malice is schort on the malice of a womman; the parte of synneris falle on hir.
As a stiynge ful of grauel in the feet of an elde man, so is a womman a greet ianglere to a pesible man.
Biholde thou not the fairnesse of a womman, and coueyte thou not a womman for fairnesse.
The ire and vnreuerence of a womman is grete schenschipe.
If a womman hath the firste dignyte, ethir cheef gouernail, sche is contrarie to hir hosebonde.
A low herte, and soreuful face, and wounde of deeth, is a wickid womman.
Feble hondis and knees vnboundun, a womman that blessith not hir hosebonde.
The bygynnyng of synne was maad of a womman; and alle we dien bi hir.
Ȝyue thou not issu to thi watir, ȝhe, not a litil issu; nether to a wickid womman fredom of goyng forth.
If sche goith not at thin hond, sche schal schende thee in the siȝt of enemyes.
Kitte hir a wei fro thi fleischis, lest euere sche mysvse thee.
The hosebonde of a good womman is blessid; for whi the noumbre of her ȝeeris is double.
A strong womman delitith hir hosebonde; and shal fille in pees the ȝeeris of his lijf.
A good womman is a good part; in the good part of hem that dreden God, sche schal be ȝouun to a man for goode dedis.
Forsothe the herte of a riche man and of a pore man is good; in al tyme her cheer is glad.
Myn herte dredde of thre thingis, and my face dredde in the fourthe thing.
Bitraiyng of a citee,
and the gadering togidere of puple, and fals chaleng; alle thingis greuouse on deth.
The sorewe of herte, and morenyng is a ielouse womman.
In a gelouse womman is betyng of tunge, and sche comyneth with alle men.
As a ȝok of oxis which is mouyd, so and a wickid womman; he that holdith hir, is as he that takith a scorpioun.
A drunkelew womman is greet ire, and dispisyng; and hir filthe schal not be hilid.
The fornycacioun of a womman is in the reisyng of yȝen; and schal be knowun in the iȝe liddis of hir.
Make thou sad kepyng in a douȝtir not turnynge a wei hir silf; lest sche mysvse hir silf, if sche fyndith occasioun.
Be thou war of al vnreuerence of hir iȝen; and wondre thou not, if sche dispisith thee.
As a weiegoere thirstynge schal opene the mouth at a welle, and schal drynke of ech watir next; and the forseid douȝtir schal sitte aȝens ech pale, and schal opene the arowe caas aȝens ech arowe, til sche faile.
The grace of a bisi womman schal delite hir hosebonde; and schal make fat hise boonus.
The kunnyng of hir is the ȝifte of God.
A wijs womman and stille is not chaungyng of a lernyd soule.
Grace on grace is an hooli womman, and schamfast.
Forsothe al weiyng is not worth a contynent soule.
As the sunne risynge in the world in the hiȝeste thingis of God, so the fairnesse of a good womman is in to the ournement of hir hous.
A lanterne schynynge on an hooli candilstike, and the fairnesse of a face on stidfast age.
Goldun pileris on siluerne foundementis, and stidfast feet on the soolis of a stidfast womman.
Euerlastynge foundementis on a sad stoon, and the heestis of God in the herte of an hooli womman.
In twei thingis myn herte was maad sori, and in the thridde thing wrathfulnesse cam to me.
A man a werriour failynge bi nedynesse, and a wijs man dispisid.
And God hath maad hym redi to the swerd, that passith ouer fro riȝtfulnesse to synne.
Twei spices apperiden harde and perilouse to me; a marchaunt is delyuered of hard fro his necgligence, and a tauerner schal not be iustified of synnes of lippis.
Many men han trespassid for nedynesse; and he that sekith to be maad riche, turneth a wei his iȝe.
As a stake is fastned in the myddis of a heep of stoonys, so and a man schal be angwischid bi synnes bitwixe the middis of sillyng and biyng.
Trespas schal be al to-brokun with hym that trespassith.
If thou holdist not thee diligentli in the drede of the Lord, thin hous schal soone be turned vpsedoun.
As dust schal dwelle in the hoolis of a riddil, so the angwisch of a man schal dwelle in the thouȝt of hym.
A furneis preueth the vessels of a pottere; and the temptacioun of tribulacioun preueth iust men.
As cherliche trauel aboute a tree schewith the fruyt therof, so a word of thouȝt schewith the herte of manj.
Preise thou not a man bifore a word; for whi this is the temptacioun of men.
If thou suest riȝtfulnesse, thou schalt take it; thou schalt clothe it as a long cloth of onour, and thou schalt dwelle with it, and it schal defende thee with outen ende, and in the dai of knowing thou shalt fynde stidfastnesse.
Volatilis comen togidere to briddis lijk hem silf; and treuthe schal turne aȝen to hem that worchen it.
A lioun settith aspies euere to huntyng; so synnes to hem that worchen wickidnesse.
An hooly man dwellith in wisdom, as the sunne dwellith stabli; for whi a fool is chaungid as the moone.
In the myddis of vnwise men kepe thou a word to tyme; but be thou bisi in the myddis of hem that thenken the lawe of God.
The tellyng of synneris is hateful; and the leiȝyng of hem is in the trespassis of synne.
Speche sweringe myche schal make stondyng up of heeris, for astonying, to the heed; and vnreuerence therof is stoppyng of eeris.
The schedyng out of blood is in the chidyng of proude men; and the cursyng of hem is greuouse heryng.
He that schewith opynli the priuytees of a frend, leesith feithfulnesse; and he schal not fynde a frend to his soule.
Loue thou a neiȝbore, and be thou ioyned with hym in feith.
For if thou schewist opynli the priuytees of hym, thou schalt not perfitli sue aftir hym.
For as a man that leesith his frend, so he that leesith the frenschipe of his neiȝbore.
And as a man that latith go a brid fro his hond, so thou that hast forsake thi neiȝbore, and thou schalt not take hym.
Thou schalt not sue hym, for he is fer absent; for he ascapid as a capret fro a snare, for the soule of hym is woundid.
Thou schalt no more mow bynde hym togidere; but of yuel seiyng is acordyng.
Sotheli to schewe opynli the pryuytees of a frend, is dispeir of a soule vnblessid.
He that twynclith with
the iȝe, makith wickid thingis; and no man schal caste hym awei. In the siȝt of thin iȝen he schal defoule his mouth, and he schal wondre on thi wordis; but at the laste he schal turne weiwerdli his mouth, and in his wordis he schal ȝyue sclaundre.
Y herde mani thingis, and Y made not euene to hym; and the Lord schal hate hym.
If a man throwith a stoon an hiȝ, it schal falle on his heed; and the gileful wounde of a gyleful man schal departe woundis.
And he that diggith a diche, schal falle in to it; and he that settith a stoon to a neiȝbore, schal offende therynne; and he that settith a snare to a nother man, schal perische ther ynne.
If a man makith worst councel, it schal be turned on hym; and he schal not knowe fro whennus it schal come to him.
The scornyng and dispisyng of proude men and veniaunce schal sette a spie to hym, as a lioun doith.
Thei that deliten in the fal of iust men, schulen perische bi a snare; forsothe sorewe schal waste hem, bifore that thei dien.
Ire and woodnesse, euer either ben abhomynable; and a synful man schal holde tho.
He that wole be vengid, schal fynde of the Lord veniaunce; and he kepynge schal kepe hise synnes.
Forȝyue thou to thi neiȝbore that anoieth thee, and thanne synnes schulen be releessid to thee preiynge.
A man kepith ire to man; and sekith he of God medicyn?
He hath no merci on a man lijk hym silf; and bisechith he the hiȝeste for hise owne synnes?
He the while he is fleisch, reserueth ire; and axith he of God merci? who schal preie for hise synnes?
Haue thou mynde on the laste thingis, and ceesse thou to be enemy.
For whi failyng and deth neiȝen not in the comaundementis of God.
Haue thou mynde on the drede of the Lord, and be thou not wrooth to the neiȝbore.
Haue thou mynde on the testament of the hiȝeste, and dispise thou the ignoraunce of thi neiȝbore.
Absteyne thee fro strijf, and thou schalt abregge synnes.
For whi a wrathful man kyndlith strijf; and a synful man schal disturble frendis, and he schal sende in enemyte in the myddis of men hauynge pees.
For whi aftir the trees of the wode, so fier schal brenne an hiȝ; and after the myȝte of a man, so his wrathfulnesse schal be, and aftir his catel he schal enhaunse his ire.
Hasti stryuyng schal kyndle fier, and hasti chidyng schal schede out blood; and a tunge berynge witnessing schal brynge deth.
If thou blowist, as fier it schal brenne an hiȝ; and if thou spetist theron, it schal be quenchid; euer either comen forth of the mouth.
A preuy bacbiter, and a double tungid man is cursid; for he disturblide many men hauynge pees.
The thridde tunge hath stirid many men, and hath scaterid hem fro folc in to folc.
It hath distried wallid citees of riche men, and hath myned doun the housis of grete men.
It hath kit doun the vertues of puplis, and hath vnknit strong folkis.
The thridde tunge hath cast out weddid wymmen, and hath priued hem of her trauelis.
He that biholdith the thridde tunge, schal not haue rest; nether schal haue a frend, in whom he schal reste.
The wounde of betyng makith wannesse; but the wounde of tunge schal make lesse the boonys.
Many men fellen doun bi the scharpnesse of swerd; but not so as thei that perischiden bi her tunge.
He is blessid that is kyuerid fro a wickid tunge; and he that passide not in the wrathfulnesse therof, and he that drow not the ȝok therof, and was not boundun in the bondis therof.
For whi the ȝok therof is an irun ȝok, and the boond therof is a brasun boond.
The deth therof is the worste deth; and helle is more profitable than it.
The perseueraunce therof schal not dwelle, but it schal holde the weies of vniust men; in his flawme it schal not brenne iust men.
Thei that forsaken God, schulen falle in to it; and it schal brenne greetli in hem, and it schal not be quenchid; and as a lioun it schal be sent in to hem, and as a parde it schal hirte hem.
Bisette thin eeris with thornes, and nyle thou here a wickid tunge; and make thou doris to thi mouth, and lockis to thin eeris.
Welle thou togidere thi gold, and thi siluer; and make thou a balaunce to thi wordis, and riȝtful bridels to thi mouth.
And take heede, lest perauenture thou slide in tunge, and falle in the siȝt of enemyes, settynge tresoun to thee, and thi falle be vncurable in to deth.
He that doith merci, leeneth to his neiȝbore; and he that is ful myȝti in hond, kepith the comaundementis.
Leene thou to thi neiȝbore in the tyme of his nede; and eft ȝelde thou to a neiȝbore in his tyme.
Conferme thou a word, and do thou feithfuli with hym; and in al tyme thou schalt fynde that, that is nedeful to thee.
Many men gessiden borewyng as fyndyng, and ȝauen disese to tho men that helpiden hem.
Til thei taken, thei kissen the hondis of the ȝyuer; and in biheestis thei maken meke her vois.
And in the time of ȝelding he schal axe tyme, and he schal speke wordis of anoie, and of grutchingis, and he schal calenge falsli the tyme.
Forsothe if he mai ȝelde, he schal be aduersarie; of a schilling vnnethis he schal ȝelde the half, and he schal rekyn that as fyndyng.
Ellis he schal defraude him in his monei, and the leenere schal haue him an enemy with outen cause.
And he schal ȝelde to hym, that is, to the leenere, wrongis and cursyngis; and for onour and benefice he schal ȝelde to hym dispisyng.
Many men lenten not to pore neiȝboris, not for cause of wickidnesse, but thei dredden to be defraudid with outen cause.
Netheles on a meke man in soule be thou strongere; and for almes drawe thou not hym.
For the comaundement of God take thou a pore man; and for his nedynesse leeue thou not hym voide.
Leese thou monei for a brother and frend, and hide thou not it vndur a stoon, in to perdicioun.
Putte thi tresour in the comaundementis of the hiȝeste; and it schal profite to thee more than gold schal profite.
Close thou almes in the bosum of a pore man; and this almes schal preye for thee to be delyuered of God fro al yuel.
The almes of a man is as a bagge with hym; and it schal kepe the grace of man as the appil of the iȝe.
And aftirward it schal rise aȝen, and schal ȝelde to hem a ȝelding, to ech man in to the heed of hem.
Aboue a scheld of the myȝti man, and aboue a spere it schal fiȝte aȝens thin enemye.
A good man makith feith to his neiȝbore; and he that leesith, schal leeue schame to hym.
Forȝete thou not the grace of the borewe; for he ȝaf his lijf for thee.
A synful man and vncleene fleeth the biheetere.
A synnere arretteth to hym silf the goode wordis of the borowe; and the vnkynde man in wit forsakith a man delyuerynge hym.
A man biheetith for his neiȝbore; and whanne the neiȝbore hath lost reuerence, the borew schal be forsakun of hym.
Worst biheest hath lost many louynge men, and hath moued hem as the wawis of the see.
It goynge in cumpas made myȝti men to passe ouer; and thei wandriden aboute among alien folkis.
A synnere brekynge the comaundement of the Lord schal falle in to a wickid biheest; and he that enforsith to do many thingis, schal falle in to dom.
Rekiuere thi neiȝbore bi thi vertu; and take heed to thi silf, lest thou falle.
The bigynnyng of lijf of a man is watir, and breed, and clothing, and hous hilynge filthe.
Betere is the lijflode of a pore man vndur the hilyng of sparris, than schynynge feestis in pilgrymage with outen hous.
The leeste thing pleese thee for a greet thing; and thou schalt not here the schenschipe of pilgrymage.
It is wickid lijf to seke herbore fro hous in to hous; and where he schal be herborid, he schal not do tristili, nethir he schal opene the mouth.
He schal be herborid, and he schal feede, and ȝyue drinke to vnkynde men; and ȝit he schal here bittir thingis.
Passe, thou that art herborid, and araye a table; and ȝyue thou meetis to othere men, tho thingis that thou hast in the hond.
Go thou out fro the face of the onour of my frendis, for the frendschipe, ethir affinyte, of myn hous; bi herboryng thou art maad a brother to me.
These thingis ben greuouse to a man hauynge wit; the repreuyng of hous, and the dispising of the vsurer.
He that loueth his sone, ȝyueth bisili betingis to hym, that he be glad in hise laste thing, and that the sone touche not the doris of neiȝboris.
He that techith his sone, schal be preisid in hym; and schal haue glorie in hym in the myddis of menyals.
He that techith his sone, sendith the enemye in to enuye; and in the myddis of frendis he schal haue glorie in that sone.
The fadir of hym is deed, and he is as not deed; for he hath left aftir hym a sone lijk hym.
He siȝ in his lijf, and was glad in hym; and in his deth he was not sori, nether was aschamed bifore enemyes.
For he lefte a defendere of the hous aȝens enemyes; and ȝeldynge grace to frendis.
For the soulis of sones he schal bynde togidere hise woundis; and hise entrails schulen be disturblid on ech vois.
An hors vntemyd, ether vnchastisid, schal ascape hard, and a sone vnchastisid schal ascape heedi.
Flatere thou the sone, and he schal make thee dredinge; pleie thou with hym, and he schal make thee sory.
Leiȝe thou not with hym, lest thou haue sorewe togidere, and at the laste thi teeth schulen be astonyed.
Ȝyue thou not power to hym in ȝongthe, and dispise thou not hise thouȝtis.
Boowe thou his necke in ȝongthe, and bete thou hise sidis, while he is a ȝong child; lest perauenture he wexe hard, and bileue not to thee, and he schal be sorewe of soule to thee.
Teche thi sone, and worche in hym; lest thou offende in to the filthe of hym.
Betere is a pore man hool, and strong in myȝtis, than a riche man feble, and betun with malice.
The helthe of soule is in the hoolynesse of riȝtfulnesse, and it is betere than ony gold and siluer; and a strong bodi is betere than ful myche catel.
No catel is aboue the catel of helthe of bodi; and no likyng is aboue the ioie of herte.
Betere is deth than bittir lijf, and euerlastinge reste is betere than siknesse dwellynge contynueli.
Goodis hid in a closid mouth ben as settyngis forth of metis set aboute a sepulcre.
What schal sacrifice profite to an idol? for whi it schal not ete, nether schal smelle.
So he that is dryuun awei fro the Lord, and
berith the medis of wickidnesse, seynge with iȝen and weilynge inwardli, as a geldynge biclippynge a virgyn, and siȝȝynge.
Ȝyue thou not sorewe to thi soule, and turmente not thi silf in thi counsel.
Mirthe of herte, this is the lijf of man, and is tresour of hoolynesse with outen failyng; and ful out ioiyng of a man is long lijf.
Haue thou mercy on thi soule, and plese thou God; and holde togidere and gadere togidere thin herte in the hoolynesse of hym, and putte fer awei sorewe fro thee.
For whi sorewe hath slayn many men; and noon heelthe is ther ynne.
Enuye and wrathfulnesse schulen make lesse daies; and thouȝtys schulen brynge eldnesse bifore the tyme.
A schynynge herte is good in metis; for whi meetis therof ben maad diligentli.
Wakyng of oneste schal make fleischis to faile; and thouȝt therof schal take awei sleep.
Thouȝt of bifore knowyng turneth awey wit; and greuouse siknesse makith sobre the soule.
A ryche man trauelide in the gaderyng of catel; and in his reste he schal be fillyd with hise goodis.
A pore man trauelide in decreessyng of lijflode; and in the ende he is maad nedi.
He that loueth gold, schal not be iustified; and he that sueth wastyng, schal be fillid therof.
Many men ben ȝouun in to the fallyngis of gold; and the perdicioun of hem was maad in the feirnesse therof.
A tre of offencioun is the gold of hem that maken sacrifice; wo to hem that suen it, and ech vnprudent man schal perische ther ynne.
Blissid is a riche man, which is foundun with out wem; and that ȝede not aftir gold, nether hopide in money, and tresouris.
Who is this, and we schulen preyse hym? for he dide merueils in his lijf.
Which is preued ther ynne, and is foundun perfit, and euerlastynge glorye schal be to hym? which myȝte trespasse, and trespasside not, and do yuels, and dide not.
Therfor hise goodis ben stablischid in the Lord; and al the chirche of seyntis schal telle out hise almesdedis.
Thou hast sete at a greet boord; opene thou not firste thi cheke on it.
Seie thou not, whether tho ben many thingis, that ben on it.
Haue thou mynde, that an yuel iȝe is weiward.
What thing worse, than an iȝe is maad? therfor of al his face he schal wepe, whanne he seeth.
Stretche thou not forth first thin hond; and thou defoulid bi enuye, be aschamed.
Be thou not oppressid of wyn in a feeste.
Vnderstonde of thi silf the thingis, that ben of thi neiȝbore.
Vse thou as a discreet and temperat man these thingis that ben set forth to thee; and be thou not hatid, whanne thou etist myche.
Ceesse thou first bicause of lernyng, ethir nurture; and nyle thou be outrageouse, lest perauenture thou offende.
And if thou hast sete in the myddis of many men, stretche not forth thin hond sunnere than thei; and axe thou not firste for to drynke.
A litil wyn is ful sufficient to a lerned man; and in slepynge thou schalt not trauele for that wyn, and thou schalt not feele trauel.
Wakyng, and colre, ether bittir moisture, and gnawyng to an vndiscreet either vntemperat man.
But the sleep of heelthe is in a scars man; he schal slepe til to the morewtid, and his soule schal delite with hym.
And if thou art constreyned in etyng myche, ryse thou fro the myddis, and brake thou; and it schal refreische thee, and thou schalt not brynge sikenesse to thi bodi.
Sone, here thou me, and dispise thou not me; and at the laste thou schalt fynde my wordis.
In alle thi werkis be thou swift; and al sikenesse schal not come to thee.
The lippis of many men schulen blesse a schynynge man in looues; and the witnessyng of his treuthe is feithful.
The citee schal grutche in the worste breed; and the witnessyng of wickidnesse therof is soth.
Nyle thou excite hem that ben diligent in wyn; for whi wyn hath distried many men.
Fier preueth hard irun; so wyn drunkun in drunkenesse schal repreue the hertis of proude men.
Euene lijf to men is wyn drunkun in sobrenesse; if thou drynkist it mesurably, thou schalt be sobre.
What is the lijf which is maad lesse bi wyn?
What defraudith lijf? deth.
Wyn was maad in gladnesse, not in drunkenesse, at the bigynnyng.
Wyn drunkun mesurabli is ful out ioiyng of soule and of bodi.
Sobre drynk is helthe of soule and of bodi.
Wyn drunkun myche makith avoiding, and ire, and many fallyngis.
Wyn drunkun myche is bitternesse of soule.
Strengthe of drunkenesse and hirting of an vnprudent man makith vertu lesse, and makynge woundis.
In the feeste of wyn repreue thou not a neiȝbore; and dispise thou not hym in his mirthe.
Seye thou not wordis of schenschipe to hym; and oppresse thou not hym in axynge.
Thei han set thee a gouernour, nyle thou be enhaunsid; be thou among hem as oon of hem.
Haue thou cure of hem, and so biholde thou; and whanne al thi cure is fillid, sitte thou to mete.
That thou be glad for hem, and take the ournement of grace; and gete coroun, and dignyte of congregacioun.
Speke thou the
gretter man in birthe; for whi the word of hym that loueth kunnyng bicome thee first; and lette thou not musik.
Where heryng is not, schede thou not out a word; and nyle thou be enhaunsid vncouenabli in thi wisdom.
A iemme of carbuncle in the ournement of gold; and comparisoun of musikis in the feeste of wyn.
As in the makyng of gold is a signe of smaragde, so the noumbre of musikis is in myrie and mesurable wyn.
Here thou stille, and good grace schal come to thee for reuerence.
Ȝonge man, speke thou vnnethis in thi cause, whanne nede is.
If thou art axid twies, the heed haue thin answere.
In many thingis be thou as vnkunnyng, and here thou stille togidere and axynge.
And presume thou not to speke in the myddis of grete men; and where elde men ben, speke thou not myche.
Leityng schal go bifore hail, and grace schal go bifore schamfastnesse, and good grace schal come to thee for reuerence.
And in the our of risyng tifle thee not; forsothe renne thou bifore first in to thin hous, and there clepe thou thee to answer, and there pleie thou.
And do thi conseitis, and not in synnes, and in a proud word.
On alle these thingis blesse thou the Lord, that made thee, and fillynge thee greetli of alle hise goodis.
He that dredith God, schal take his techyng; and thei that waken to hym, schulen fynde blessyng.
He that sekith the lawe, schal be fillid therof; and he that doith tretourousli, schal be sclaundrid ther ynne.
Thei that dreden God, schulen fynde iust dom; and schulen kyndle riȝtfulnesse as liȝt.
A synful man schal eschewe blamyng; and aftir his wille he schal fynde comparisoun.
A man of counsel schal not leese vndirstonding; a man alien and proud schal not drede dredyng.
Ȝhe, aftir that he hath do with that drede with out councel, and he schal be repreued bi hise suyngis.
Sone, do thou no thing with out councel; and aftir the dede thou schalt not repente.
Go thou not in the weie of fallyng, and offende thou not aȝens stoonys. Bitake thou not thee to a trauelouse weie, lest thou sette sclaundir to
thi soule; and be thou war of thi sones, and perseyue thou of thi meyneals.
In al thi werk bileue thou bi feith of thi soule; for whi this is the keping of comaundementis.
He that bileueth to God, takith heede to the comaundementis; and he that tristith in hym, schal not be maad lesse.
Iuelis schulen not come to hym that dredith God; but God schal kepe hym in temptacioun, and schal delyuere fro yuelis.
A wijs man hatith not the comaundementis, and riȝtfulnessis; and he schal not be hurtlid doun, as in the tempest of a schip.
A wijs man bileeueth to the lawe of God, and the lawe is feithful to hym.
He that makith opene axyng, schal make redi a word; and so he schal preie, and schal be herd, and he schal kepe techyng, and thanne he schal answere.
The entraylis of a fool ben as a wheel of a carte, and his thouȝtis as an extre able to turne aboute.
An hors a staloun, so and a frend a scornere, neiȝeth vndur ech sittynge aboue.
Whi a dai ouercometh a dai, and eft the liȝt ouercometh liȝt, and a ȝeer ouercometh a ȝeer, the sunne ouercometh the sunne?
Tho ben departid of the kunnyng of the Lord, bi the sunne maad, and kepynge the comaundement of God.
And it schal chaunge tymes and the feeste daies of hem, and in tho tymes the Jewis halewiden hali daies at an our.
God enhaunside and magnyfiede of tho hali daies; and of tho he settide in to the noumbre of daies; and God made alle men of sad erthe, and of neische erthe, whereof Adam was formed.
In the multitude of kunnyng of the Lord he departide hem, and chaungide the weies of hem.
Of hem God blesside, and enhaunside; and of hem he halewide, and chees to hym silf; of hem he curside, and made lowe, and turnyde hem fro the departyng of hem.
As cley of a pottere is in the hond of
hym, to make and dispose, that alle the weies therof ben aftir the ordynaunce of hym; so a man is in the hond of hym that made hym; and he schal ȝelde to hym bi his dom.
Aȝens yuel is good, and aȝens lijf is deth; so and a synnere is aȝens a iust man. And so biholde thou in to alle the werkis of the hiȝeste; twey thingis aȝens tweyne, and o thing aȝens oon.
And Y the laste wakide, and as he that gaderith draf of grapis, aftir the gadereris of grapis.
And Y hopide in the blessyng of God; and as he that gaderith grapis, Y fillide the pressour.
Biholde ȝe, for Y trauelide not to me aloone, but to alle that seken kunnyng.
Grete men, and alle puplis, here ȝe me; and ȝe gouernouris of the chirche, perseyue with eeris.
