Ȝyue thou not power ouer thee in thi lijf to a sone, and to a womman, to a brothir, and to a freend; and ȝyue thou not thi possessioun to another man, lest perauenture it repente thee, and thou biseche for tho.
While thou art alyue, and brethist ȝit, ech man schal not chaunge thee.
For it is betere, that thi sones preye thee, than that thou biholde in to the hondis of thi sones.
In alle thi werkis be thou souereyn; ȝyue thou not a wem in to thi
glorie. In the day of endyng of daies of thi lijf, and in tyme of thi goyng out departe thin erytage.
Metis, and a ȝerde, and birthun to an asse; breed, and chastisyng, and werk to a seruaunt.
He worchith in chastisyng, and sekith to haue reste; slake thou hondis to hym, and he sekith fredom.
A ȝok and bridil bowen doun an hard necke; and bisi worchingis bowen doun a seruaunt.
Turment and stockis to an yuel willid seruaunt; sende thou hym in to worchyng, lest he
be ydel; for whi idilnesse hath tauȝte miche malice.
Ordeyne thou hym in werk, for so it bicometh hym; that if he obeieth not, bowe thou doun hym in stockis, and make thou not hym large ouer ony man, but with out dom do thou no thing greuouse.
If a feithful seruaunt is to thee, be he as thi soule to thee; trete thou him so as a brother, for thou hast bouȝt hym in the blood of lijf.
If thou hurtist hym vniustli, he schal be turned in to fleyng
awei; and if he enhaunsynge goith awei, thou noost whom thou schalt seke, and in what weie thou schalt seke hym.
Veyn hope and a leesyng to an vnwijs man; and dremes enhaunsen vnprudent men.
As he that takith schadewe, and pursueth wynd, so and he that takith heede to leesyngis seyn.
Vpe this thing is the siȝt of dremes; bifore the face of a man is the licnesse of another man.
What schal be clensid of him that is vnclene, and what trewe thing schal be seid of a liere?
Fals dyuynyng of errour, and fals dyuynyngis bi chiteryng of briddis, and dremes of witchis, is vanyte.
And as the herte of a womman trauelynge of child, thin herte suffrith fantasies; no but visitacioun is sent out of the hiȝeste, ȝyue thou not thin herte in tho dremes.
For whi dremes han maad many men for to erre, and men hopynge in tho fellen doun.
The word of the lawe of God and of hise profetis, schal be maad perfit with out leesyng; and wisdom in the mouth of a feithful man schal be maad pleyn.
What kan he, that is not asaied? A man asaied in many thingis, schal thenke many thingis; and he that lernyde many thingis, schal telle out vndirstondyng.
He that is not asaied, knowith fewe thingis; forsothe he that is a fool in many thingis, schal multiplie malice.
What maner thingis kan he, that is not asaied? He that is not plauntid, schal be plenteuouse in wickidnesse.
I siȝ many thingis in tellyng out, and ful many customs of wordis.
Sum tyme Y was in perel til to deth, for the cause of these thingis; and Y was delyuered bi the grace of God.
The spirit of hem that dreden God is souȝt, and schal be blessid in the biholding of hym.
For whi the hope of hem is in to God sauynge hem; and the iȝen of the Lord ben in to hem, that louen hym.
He that dredith God, schal not tremble for ony thing, and he schal not drede; for whi God is his hope.
The soule of hym that dredith the Lord, is blessid.
To whom biholdith he, and who is his strengthe?
The iȝen of the Lord ben on hem that dreden hym. God is a defendere of myȝt, stidfastnesse of vertu, hilyng of heete, and a schadewyng
place of myddai; bisechyng of offendyng, and help of fallyng, enhaunsynge the soule, and liȝtnynge the iȝen, and ȝyuynge heelthe, and lijf, and blessyng.
The offryng of hym that offrith of wickid thing, is defoulid; and the scornyngis of vniust men ben not wel plesaunt.
The Lord aloone is to hem that abiden hym in the weie of treuthe, and of riȝtfulnesse.
The hiȝeste appreueth not the ȝiftis of wickid men, nethir biholdith in the offryngis of wickid men, nether in the multitude of her sacrifices he schal do mercy to synnes.
He that offrith sacrifice of the catel of pore men, is as he that sleeth the sone in the siȝt of his fadir.
The breed of nedi men is the lijf of a pore man; he that defraudith hym, is a man of blood.
He that takith awei breed in swoot, is as he that sleeth his neiȝbore.
He that schedith out blood, and he that doith fraude to an hirid man, ben britheren.
Oon bildynge, and oon distriynge; what profitith it to hem, no but trauel?
Oon preiynge, and oon cursynge; whos vois schal the Lord here?
What profitith the waischyng of hym, that is waischun for a deed bodi, and touchith eft a deed bodi?
So a man that fastith in hise synnes, and eft doynge the same synnes, what profitith he in mekynge hym silf? who schal here his preyer?
He that kepith the word, multiplieth preier.
Heelful sacrifice is to take heede to the comaundementis, and to departe fro al wickidnesse.
And to offre the plesyng of sacrifice for vnriȝtfulnesses, and bisechyng for synnes, is to go awey fro vnriȝtfulnesse.
He that offrith purest flour of wheete, schal ȝelde grace; and he that doith merci, offrith a sacrifice.
It is wel plesaunt to the Lord, to go a wei fro wickidnesse; and preier is to go a wei fro vnriȝtfulnesse.
Thou schalt not appere voide
bifore the siȝt of God; for whi alle these thingis ben doon for the heestis of God.
The offryng of a iust man makith fat the auter, and is odour of swetnesse in the siȝt of the hiȝeste.
The sacrifice of a iust man is acceptable, and the Lord schal not forȝete the mynde of hym.
With good wille ȝelde thou glorie to God, and make thou not lesse the firste fruytis of thin hondis.
In ech ȝifte make glad thi cheer, and in ful out ioiyng halewe thi tithis.
Ȝyue thou to the hiȝeste aftir his ȝifte; and with good iȝe make thou the fyndyng of thin hondis.
For whi the Lord is a ȝeldere, and he schal ȝelde seuene fold so myche to thee.
Nyle thou offre schrewid ȝiftis; for he schal not resseyue tho.
And nyle thou biholde an vniust sacrifice; for the Lord is iuge, and glorie of persoone is not at hym.
The Lord schal not take a persoone aȝens a pore man; and he schal here the preier of hym that is hirt.
He schal not dispise the preyeris of a fadirles child, nether a widewe, if sche schedith out speche of weilyng.
Whether the teeris of a widew goen not doun to the cheke, and the criyng of hir on hym that ledith forth tho teeris?
For whi tho stien fro the cheke til to heuene, and the Lord herere schal not delite in tho.
He that worschipith God in delityng, schal be resseyued; and his preyer schal neiȝe til to the clowdis.
The preier of hym that mekith hym silf schal perse clowdis, and til it neiȝeth, he schal not be coumfortid, and he schal not go awey, til the hiȝeste biholde.
And the Lord schal not be fer, but he schal iuge iust men, and schal make doom; and the strongeste schal not haue pacience in tho, that he troble the bak of hem.
And he schal ȝelde veniaunce to folkis, til he take awei the fulnesse of proude men, and troble togidere
the ceptris of wickid men; til he ȝelde to men aftir her dedis, and aftir the werkis of Adam, and aftir the presumpcioun of
hym; til he deme the dome of his puple, and schal delite iust men in his merci.
The merci of God is fair in the tyme of tribulacioun, as clowdis of reyn in the tyme of drynesse.
God of alle thingis, haue thou merci on vs; and biholde thou vs, and schewe thou to vs the liȝt of thi merciful doyngis.
And sende thi drede on hethene men, that souȝten not thee, that thei knowe that no God is, no but thou; that thei telle out thi grete dedis.
Reise thin hond on hethene men aliens, that thei se thi power.
For as thou were halewid in vs in the siȝt of hem, so in oure siȝt thou schalt be magnefyed
in hem; that thei knowe thee, as and we han knowe, that noon othere is God, outakun thee, Lord.
Make thou newe
signes, and chaunge thou merueilis; glorifie the hond, and the riȝt arm.
Reise thou stronge veniaunce, and schede out
ire; take awei the aduersarie, and turmente the enemye.
Haaste thou the tyme, and haue thou mynde on the ende, that thei telle out thi merueils.
And he that is sauyd, be deuourid in the ire of flawme; and thei that treten worst thi puple, fynde perdicioun.
Al to-breke thou the heed of princis, and of enemyes, seiynge, Noon othere is, outakun vs.
Gadere thou togidere alle the lynagis of Jacob, and knowe thei that no God is, no but thou, that thei telle out thi grete dedis; and thou schalt enherite hem, as at the bigynnyng.
Haue thou merci on thi puple, on which thi name is clepid in to help; and on Israel, whom thou madist euene to thi firste gendrid sone.
Haue thou merci on Jerusalem, the citee of thin halewyng, on the citee of thi reste.
Fille thou Syon with thi vertues, that moun not be teld out, and fille thi puple with thi glorie.
Ȝyue thou witnessyng, that at the bigynnyng thei weren thi creaturis; and reise thou preieris, whiche the formere profetis spaken in thi name.
Lord, ȝyue thou meede to hem that abiden thee, that thi prophetis be foundun trewe; and here thou the preier of thi seruauntis.
Aftir the blessyng of Aaron ȝyue thou to thi puple, and dresse thou vs in to the weie of riȝtfulnesse; that alle men wite, that dwellen in erthe, that thou art God, the biholdere of worldis.
The wombe schal ete alle mete, and o mete is betere than another mete.
Chekis touchen mete almest, and an vnwise herte resseyueth false wordis.
A schrewid herte schal ȝyue heuynesse, and a wijs man schal aȝenstonde it.
A womman schal take ech knaue child, and a douȝtir is betere than a sone.
The fairnesse of a womman makith glad the face of hir hosebonde, and sche schal brynge desir ouer al the coueitise of man.
If ther is a tunge of heelyng, ther is also of swagyng, and of merci; the hosebonde of hir is not aftir the sones of men.
He that hath in possessioun a good womman, bigynneth possessioun; sche is an help lijk hym, and a piler as reste.
Where an hegge is not, the possessioun schal be rauyschid awei; and where a womman is not, a nedi man weilith.
To whom bileueth he that hath no nest, and bowith doun where euer it is derk, as a theef girt, skippynge out fro citee in to citee?
Ech frend schal seie, And Y haue couplid frenschip; but that is a frend, a frend bi name aloone. Whether sorewe is not til to deth?
Forsothe a felowe of table and a frend schulen be turned to enemyte.
A! the worste presumpcioun, wherof art thou maad to hile drie malice, and the gilefulnesse therof?
A felowe of table schal be myrie with a frend in delityngis, and in the dai of tribulacioun he schal be aduersarie.
A felowe of table schal haue sorewe with a frend, for cause of the wombe; and he schal take scheeld aȝens an enemye.
Forȝete thou not thi frend in thi soule, and be thou not vnmyndeful of hym in thi werkis.
Nyle thou take councel with the fadir of thi wijf; and hide thou councel fro hem that han enuye to thee.
Ech councelour schewith councel, but ther is a councelour to hym silf.
Kepe thi soule fro an yuel counselour; firste wite thou, what is his nede, and what he
schal thenke in his soule; lest perauenture he sende a stake in to the erthe, and
seie to thee, Thi weie is good, and he stonde aȝenward, to se what schal bifalle to thee.
With an vnreligiouse man trete thou of holynesse, and with an vniust man of riȝtfulnesse, and with a womman of these thingis whiche sche hatith. With a ferdful man trete thou of batel, with a marchaunt, of cariyng ouer of marchaundies to chepyng; with a biere, of sillyng, with an enuyouse man, of graces to be
don; with an vnpitouse man, of pytee, with an vnonest man, of oneste, with a werk
man of the feeld, of ech werk; with a werk man hirid bi the ȝeer, of the endyng of the ȝeer, with a slowe seruaunt, of myche worchyng. Ȝyue thou not tent to these
men in al councel, but be thou bisi with an hooli man, whom euere thou knowist
kepynge Goddis drede, whos soule is aftir thi soule. Who euer doutith in derknessis, schal not haue sorewe with thee.
And stablische thou the herte of good councel with thee; for whi another thing is not more than it to thee.
The soule of an hooli man tellith out treuthis sum tyme; more than seuene biholderis sittynge an hiȝ for to biholde.
And in alle these thingis biseche thou the hiȝeste, that he dresse thi weie in treuthe.
Bifore alle werkis a sothefast word go bifore thee; and a stidfast councel go bifore ech dede.
A wickid word schal chaunge the herte, of which herte foure partis comen forth; good and yuel, lijf and deth; and a bisi tunge is lord of tho.
A wijs man hath tauȝt many men, and he is swete to his soule.
He that spekith bi soffym, is hateful; he schal be defraudid in ech thing.
For whi grace is not ȝouun of the Lord to hym, for he is defraudid of al wisdom.
A wijs man is wijs to his soule, and the fruytis of his wit ben worthi to be preisid.
A wijs man techith his puple, and the fruytis of his wit ben feithful.
A wijs man schal be fillid with blessyngis, and thei that seen hym schulen preise hym.
The lijf of a man is in the noumbre of daies; but the daies of Israel ben vnnoumbrable.
A wijs man in the puple schal enherite onour, and his name schal be lyuynge with outen ende.
Sone, asaie thi soule in thi lijf; and if it is wickid,
ȝyue thou not power to it; for whi not alle thingis speden to alle men, and not ech kynde plesith ech soule.
Nyle thou be gredi in ech etyng, and schede thou not out thee on ech mete.
For in many metis schal be sikenesse, and gredynesse schal neiȝe til to colrye.
Many men dieden for glotenye; but he that is abstinent, schal encreesse lijf.
Onoure thou a leche, for nede; for whi the hiȝeste hath maad hym.
For whi al medicyn is of God; and he schal take of the kyng a ȝifte.
The kunnyng of a leche schal enhaunse his heed; and he schal be preisid in the siȝt of grete men.
The hiȝeste hath maad of the erthe medicyn; and a prudent man schal not wlate it.
Whether bittir watir was not maad swete of a tre?
The vertu of tho thingis cam bi experience to the knowing of men; and the hiȝeste ȝaf kunnyng to men, for to be onourid in his merueils.
A man heelynge in these thingis schal aswage sorewe, and an oynement makere schal make pymentis of swetnesse, and schal make anoyntyngis of heelthe; and hise werkis schulen not be endid.
For whi the pees of God is on the face of erthe.
Mi sone, dispise not thi silf in thi sikenesse; but preie thou the Lord, and he schal heele thee.
Turne thou awei fro synne, and dresse thin hondis, and clense thin herte fro al synne.
Ȝyue thou swetnesse, and the mynde of cleene flour of wheete, and make thou fat offryng; and ȝyue thou place to a leche.
For the Lord made hym, and departe he not fro thee; for hise werkis ben nedeful to thee.
For whi tyme is, whanne thou schalt falle in to the hondis of hem.
Forsothe thei schulen biseche the Lord, that he dresse the werk of hem, and helthe for her lyuyng.
He that trespassith in the siȝt of hym, that made hym, schal falle in to the hondis of the leche.
Sone, brynge thou forth teeris on a deed man, and thou as suffrynge hard thingis bigynne to wepe; and bi doom hile thou the bodi of hym, and dispise thou not his biriyng.
But for bacbityng bere thou bittirli the morenyng of hym o dai; and be thou coumfortid for sorewe.
And make thou morenyng aftir his merit o dai, ether tweyne, for bacbityng.
For whi deth hastith of sorewe, and hilith vertu; and the sorewe of herte bowith the heed.
Sorewe dwellith in ledyng awei; and the catel of a nedi man is aftir his herte.
Ȝyue thou not thin herte in sorewe, but put it awei fro thee; and haue thou mynde on the laste thingis, and nyle thou forȝete.
For whi no turning is, and thou schalt no thing profite to this deed man; and thou schalt harme worste thi silf.
Be thou myndeful of mi dom; for also thin schal be thus, to me ȝistirdai, and to thee to dai.
In the reste of a deed man make thou hys mynde to haue reste; and coumforte thou hym in the goyng out of his spirit.
Write thou wisdom in the tyme of voidenesse; and he that is made lesse in dede, schal perseyue wisdom; for he schal be fillid of wisdom.
He that holdith the plow, and he that hath glorie in a gohode, dryueth oxis with a pricke, and he lyueth in the werkis of tho; and his tellyng is in the sones of bolis.
He schal ȝyue his herte to turne forewis; and his wakyng schal be aboute the fatnesse of kien.
So ech carpenter, and principal werk man, that passith the niȝt as the dai; that graueth ymagis grauun, and the bisynesse of hym dyuersith the peynture; he schal ȝyue his herte to the licnesse of peynture, and bi his wakyng he perfourmeth the werk.
So a smyth sittynge bisidis the anefelt, and biholdynge the werk of yrun, the heete of fier brenneth hise fleischis; and he stryueth in the heete of the furneis.
The vois of a hamer makith newe his eere; and his iȝe is aȝens the licnesse of a vessel.
He schal ȝyue his herte in to the perfourmyng of werkis; and bi his wakyng he schal ourne vnperfeccioun.
So a potter sittynge at his werk, turnynge a wheel with hise feet, which is put euere in bisynesse for his werk; and al his worchyng is vnnoumbrable.
In his arm he schal fourme clei; and bifore hise feet he schal bowe his vertu.
He schal ȝyue his herte to ende perfitli sum thing; and bi his wakyng he schal clense the furneis.
Alle these men hopiden in her hondis; and ech man is wijs in his craft.
A citee is not bildid with outen alle these men.
And thei schulen not dwelle, nether go; and thei schulen not skippe ouer in to the chirche.
Thei schulen not sitte on the seete of a iuge; and thei schulen not vndirstonde the testament of doom, nether thei schulen make opyn techyng and doom; and thei schulen not be foundun in parablis.
But thei schulen conferme the creature of the world, and her preyer is in the worching of craft; and thei ȝyuen her soule, and thei axen togidere in the lawe of the hiȝeste.
A wijs man schal seke out the wisdom of alle elde men; and he schal ȝyue tent in profetis.
He schal kepe the tellyng of named men; and he schal entre togidere in to the hard sentensis of parablis.
He schal seke out the pryuy thingis of prouerbis; and he schal be conuersaunt in the hid thingis of parablis.
He schal mynystre in the myddis of grete men; and he schal appere in the siȝt of the cheef iuge.
He schal passe in to the lond of alien folkis; for he schal asaie goodis, and yuels in alle thingis.
He schal ȝyue his herte to wake eerli to the Lord that made hym; and he schal biseche in the siȝt of the hiȝeste.
He schal opene his mouth in preier; and he schal biseche for hise trespassis.
For if the grete Lord wole, he schal fille hym with the spirit of vndurstondyng.
And he schal sende the wordis of his wisdom, as reynes; and in preier he schal knouleche to the Lord.
And he schal dresse his counsel, and techyng; and schal councele in hise hid thingis.
He schal make opene the wisdom of his techyng; and he schal haue glorie in the lawe of the testament of the Lord.
Many men schulen preyse his wisdom; and it schal not be don a wey til in to the world.
His mynde schal not go awei; and his name schal be souȝt fro generacioun in to generacioun.
Folkis schulen telle out his wisdom; and the chirche schal telle his preisyng.
If his name dwellith, he schal leeue more than a thousynde; and if he restith, it schal profite to hym.
Ȝit Y schal take councel to telle out, for Y am fillid as with woodnesse;
and myn ynnere spirit seith in vois, Ȝe fruytis of God, here me, and make ȝe fruyt, as roosis plauntide on the ryuers of watris.
Haue ȝe odour of swetnesse, as the Liban hath.
Bringe forth flouris, as a lilee; ȝyue ȝe odour, and make ȝe boowis in to grace. And preise ȝe togidere a song; and blesse ȝe the Lord in hise werkis.
Ȝyue ȝe greet onour to his name, and knouleche ȝe to him in the vois of ȝoure lippis, in songis of lippis, and in harpis; and thus ȝe schulen seie in knouleching,
Alle the werkis of the Lord ben ful goode.
Forsothe watir as an heepe of stoonys stood at his word; and as resettis of watris in the word of his mouth.
For whi pesiblenesse is maad in his comaundement; and no defaute is in the heelthe of hym.
The werkis of ech fleisch ben bifore hym; and no thing is hid fro hise iȝen.
He biholdith fro the world til in to the world; and no thing is wondurful in his siȝt.
It is not to seie, What is this thing, ether, What is that thing? for whi alle thingis schulen be souȝt in her tyme.
The blessyng of hym
schal flowe as a flood; and as the grete flood fillide greteli the erthe, so his yre schal enherite in folkis, that souȝten not hym.
As he turnede watris in to drynessis, and the erthe was dried, and hise weies weren dressid to the weies of hem; so offenciouns in his ire ben dressid to synneris.
Goode thingis weren maad at the bigynnyng to goode men; so goode thingis and yuele ben maad to worste men.
The bigynnyng of nedeful thing to the lijf of men, watir, fier, and yrun, and salt, and mylk, and breed of cleene flour of whete, and hony, and a clustre of grape, and oile, and cloth.
Alle these thingis schulen turne to hooli men in to goodis; so and to vnfeithful men and synneris in to yuels.
Spiritis ben that ben maad to veniaunce; and in her woodnesse thei confermyden her turmentis.
And in the tyme of endyng thei schulen schede out vertu; and thei schulen confounde the strong veniaunce of hym that made hem.
Fier, hail, hungur, and deth; alle these thingis ben maad to veniaunce;
the teeth of beestis, and scorpiouns, and serpentis, and a swerd punyschynge wickid men in to destriyng.
In the comaundementis of hym tho schulen ete, and tho schulen be maad redi on the erthe in nede; and in her tymes tho schulen not passe o word.
Therfor fro the bigynnyng Y was confermed; and Y counselide, and thouȝte, and lefte writun.
Alle the werkis of the Lord ben goode; and ech werk schal serue in his our.
It is not to seie, This is worse than that; for whi alle thingis schulen be preued in her tyme.
And now in al the herte and mouth preise ȝe togidere, and blesse ȝe the name of the Lord.
Greet occupacioun is maad to alle men, and an heuy ȝok on the sones of Adam, fro the dai of the goyng out of the wombe of her modir, til in to the dai of biriyng in to the modir of alle men.
The thouȝtis of hem, and the dredis of herte, fyndyngis of abidyng, and the dai of endyng;
fro hym that sittith bifore on a gloriouse seete, til to a man maad lowe in
to erthe and aische; fro hym that vsith iacynct, and berith a coroun, til to hym that is hilid with raw lynnun cloth, woodnesse, enuye, noise, doutyng, and drede of deth, wrathfulnesse dwellynge contynueli,
and strijf; and in the tyme of restyng in the bed, the sleep of nyȝt chaungith his kunnyng.
Forsothe a litil is as nouȝt in reste; biholdyng is of hym in sleep as in the dai.
He is disturblid in the siȝt of his herte, as he that ascapith in the dai of batel. He roos vp in the dai of his helthe, and dredynge not at ony drede,
with al fleisch, fro man til to beeste, and seuenefold schal come on synneris.
At these thingis, deth, blood, stryuyng, and swerd, oppressyngis, hungur, and sorewe,
and beetyngis; alle these thingis ben maad on wickid men, and the greet flood was maad for hem.
For whi alle thingis that ben of the erthe, schulen turne in to the erthe; and alle watris schulen turne in to the see.
Al ȝifte and wickidnesse schal be don awei; and feith schal stonde in to the world.
The richessis of vniust men schulen be maad drie as a flood; and schulen sowne as a greet thundur in reyn.
An vniust man schal be glad in openynge hise hondis; so trespassouris schulen faile in the ende.
The sones of sones of wickid men schulen not multiplie braunchis; and vncleene rootis sownen on the cop of a stoon.
Grenenesse bisidis ech watir; and at the brynk of the flood it schal be drawun out bi the roote bifor al hey.
Grace as paradiss in blessyngis; and merci dwellith in to the world.
The lijf of a werk man sufficient to hym silf schal be maad swete; and thou schalt fynde tresour ther ynne.
Bildyng of a citee schal conferme a name; and a womman with out wem schal be rikenyd aboue this.
Wyn and musik maken glad the herte; and loue of wisdom gladith aboue euer either.
Pipis and sawtree maken swete melodie; and a swete tunge aboue euer either.
An yȝe schal desire grace and fairnesse; and greene sowyngis aboue these thingis.
A frend and felowe comynge togidere in tyme; and a womman with man aboue euer either.
Britheren in to help in the tyme of tribulacioun coumforten myche; and merci schal delyuere more than thei.
Gold and siluer, and settyng of feet; and counsel wel plesing is aboue euer either.
Richessis and vertues enhaunsen the herte; and the drede of the Lord more than this.
Making lesse is not in the drede of the Lord; and in that drede it is not to seke help.
The drede of the Lord is as paradijs of blessyng; and the blessyngis of God kyueriden hym aboue al glorie.
Sone, in the tyme of thi lijf be thou not nedi; for it is betere to die, than to be nedi.
A man biholdinge in to another mannus boord, his lijf is not in the thouȝt of lijflode; for he susteyneth his lijf with othere mennus metis.
Forsothe a chastisid man and lernd schal kepe him silf.
Nedynesse schal be defoulid in the mouth of an vnprudent man; and fier schal brenne in his wombe.
A! deth, thi mynde is ful bittir to an vniust man, and hauynge pees in hise
richessis; to a restful man, and whose weies ben dressid in alle thingis, and ȝit myȝti to take mete.
A! deth, thi doom is good to a nedi man, and which is maad
lesse in strengthis, and failith for age, and to whom is care of alle thingis, and vnbileueful, that leesith wisdom.
Nyle thou drede the doom of deth; haue thou mynde what thingis weren byfore thee, and what thingis schulen come on thee; this dom is of the Lord to ech man.
And tho thingis that schulen come on thee in the good plesaunce of the hiȝeste; whethir ten ȝeer, ether an hundrid, ether a thousynde.
For whi noon accusyng of lijf is in helle.
The sones of abhomynaciouns ben the sones of synneris; and thei that dwellen bisidis the housis of wickid men.
The eritage of the sones of synneris schal perische; and the contynuaunce of schenschipe with the seed of hem.
Sones playnen of a wickid fadir; for thei ben in schenschip for hym.
Wo to ȝou, ȝe wickid men, that han forsake the lawe of the hiȝeste.
And if ȝe be borun, ȝe schulen be borun in cursidnesse; and if ȝe ben deed, ȝoure part schal be in cursidnesse.
Alle thingis that ben of the erthe, schulen turne in to the erthe; so wickid men schulen turne fro cursyng in to perdicioun.
The morenyng of men is in the bodi of hem; but the name of wickid men schal be doon awei.
Haue thou bisynesse of a good name; for whi this schal dwelle more with thee, than a thousynde tresouris grete and preciouse.
The noumbre of daies is the terme of good lijf; but a good name schal dwelle with outen ende.
Sones, kepe ȝe techyng in pees; for whi wisdom hid, and tresour vnseyn, what profit is in euer either?
Betere is a man that hidith his foli, than a man that hidith his wisdom.
Netheles turne ȝe aȝen in these thingis that comen forth of my mouth.
For it is not good to kepe alle vnreuerence, and not alle thingis plesen alle men in feith.
Be ȝe aschamed of fornycacioun, bifor fadir, and bifor modir; and of a leesyng, bifore a iustice,
and bifore a myȝti man; and of trespas, bifor a prince, and bifore a iuge; and of wickidnesse, bifore a synagoge, and a puple;
and of vnriȝtwisnesse, bifore a felow,
and a frend; and of thefte, in the place where ynne thou dwellist; of the treuthe and testament of God; of sittyng at the mete in looues, and of the blemyschyng
of ȝifte, and takyng; of stilnesse, bifore hem that greeten; of the biholdyng of a letcherouse womman, and of the turnyng a wey of the cheer of a cosyn.
Turne thou not awey the face fro thi neiȝbore; and be thou war of takyng a wei a part, and not restorynge.
Biholde thou not the womman of an othere man; and enserche thou not her hand maide, nether stonde thou at hir bed.
Be thou war of frendis, of the wordis of vpbreidyng; and whanne thou hast ȝoue, vpbreide thou not.
Double thou not a word of heryng, of the schewyng of an hid word; and thou schalt be verily with out schame, and thou schalt fynde grace in the siȝt of alle men. Be thou not schent for alle these thingis; and take thou not a persoone, that thou do trespas.
Be thou war of the lawe and testament of the hiȝeste, of doom
to iustifie a wickid man; of the word of felowis, and of weigoeris, and of the ȝyuyng
of eritage of frendis; of the euennesse of balaunce, and of weiȝtis, of the getyng of many thingis, and of fewe
thingis; of corrupcioun of biyng, and of marchauntis, and of myche chastising of sones; and of a worste seruaunt, to make the side to bleede.
A seelyng is good on a wickid man.
Where ben many hondis, close thou; and what euer thing thou schalt bitake, noumbre thou, and weie thou; forsothe discryue thou, ether write, ech ȝifte, and takyng.
Absteine thou fro the techyng of an vnwitti man, and fool, and of eldere men that ben demed of ȝonge men; and thou schalt be lernd in alle thingis, and thou schalt be comendable in the siȝt of alle men.
An hid douȝter of a fadir is wakynge and bisynesse of hym; sche schal take awei sleep; lest perauenture sche be maad auowtresse in hir ȝong wexynge age, and lest sche dwellynge with the hosebonde,
be maad hateful; lest ony tyme sche be defoulid in hir virginytee, and be foundun with child in the kepyng of hir fadir; leste perauenture sche dwellynge with the hosebonde, do trespasse, ether certis be maad bareyn.
Ordeyne thou kepyng on a letcherouse douȝter, lest ony tyme sche make thee to come in to schenschipe to enemyes, of bacbityng in the citee, and of castyng out of the puple; and sche make thee aschamed in the multitude of puple.
Nyle thou take heed to ech man in the fairnesse; and nyle thou dwelle in the myddis of wymmen.
For whi a mouȝte cometh forth of clothis, and the wickidnesse of a man cometh forth of a womman.
For whi the wickidnesse of a man is betere than a womman doynge wel, and a womman schendyng in to schenschipe.
Therfor be thou myndeful of the werkis of the Lord; and Y schal telle the werkis of the Lord, whiche Y siȝ, in the wordis of the Lord.
The sunne liȝtnynge bihelde by alle thingis; and the werk therof is ful of the glorie of the Lord.
Whether the Lord made not hooli men to telle out alle hise merueilis, whiche the Lord almyȝti stidfast in his glorie schal conferme?
He schal enserche the depthe, and the herte of men; and he schal thenke in the felnesse of hem.
For the Lord knew al kunnyng, and bihelde in to the signe of the world; tellynge tho thingis that ben passid, and tho thingis that schulen come; schewynge the steppis of hid thingis.
And no thouȝt passith hym, and no word hidith it silf fro hym.
He made fair the grete werkis of his wisdom, which is bifore the world, and til in to the world; nether ony thing is
encreessid, nether is decreessid, and he hath no nede to the counsel of ony.
Alle hise werkis ben ful desirable, and to biholde, as a sparcle which is.
Alle these thingis lyuen, and dwellen in to the world; and alle thingis obeien to hym in al nede.
Alle thingis ben double, oon aȝens oon; and he made not ony thing to faile. He schal conferme the goodis of ech; and who schal be fillid, seynge his glorie?
The firmament of hiȝnesse is the fairnesse therof; the fairnesse of heuene in the siȝt of glorie.
The sunne in biholdyng, tellynge in goyng out, is a woundurful vessel, the werk of hiȝ God.
In the tyme of myddai it brenneth the erthe; and who schal mow suffre in the siȝt of his heete? Kepynge a furneis in the werkis
of heete; the sunne brennynge hillis in thre maneris, sendynge out beemys of fier, and schynynge aȝen with hise beemys, blyndith iȝen.
The Lord is greet, that made it; and in the wordis of hym it hastide iourney.
And the moone in alle men in his tyme is shewing of tyme, and a signe of the world.
A signe of the feeste dai is takun of the moone; the liȝt which is maad litil in the ende.
The monethe is encreessynge bi the name therof, wondirfuli in to the ending.
A vessel of castels in hiȝ thingis, schynynge gloriousli in the firmament of heuene.
The fairnesse of heuene is the glorie of sterris; the Lord an hiȝ liȝtneth the world.
In the wordis of the hooli tho schulen stonde at the doom; and tho schulen not faile in her wakyngis.
Se thou the bouwe, and blesse thou hym that made it; it is ful fair in his schynyng.
It ȝede aboute heuene in the cumpas of his glorie; the hondis of hiȝ God openyden it.
Bi his comaundement he hastide the snow; and he hastith to sende out the leiȝtyngis of his dom.
Therfor tresouris weren opened, and clowdis fledden out as been.
In his greetnesse he settide clowdis; and stoonys of hail weren brokun.
Hillis schulen be moued in his siȝt; and the south wynd schal blowe in his wille.
The vois of his thundur schal beete the erthe; the tempest of the north, and the gaderyng togidere of wynd.
And as a brid puttynge doun to sitte sprengith snow, and the comyng doun of that snow is as a locust drenchynge doun.
The iȝe schal wondre on the fairnesse of whitnesse therof; and an herte dredith on the reyn therof.
He schal schede out frost as salt on the erthe; and while the wynd blowith, it schal be maad as coppis of a brere.
The coold northun wynd blew, and cristal of watir frees togidre; it restith, on al the gedering togidere of watris, and it clothith it silf with watris, as with an haburioun.
And it schal deuoure hillis, and it schal brenne the desert; and it schal quenche grene thing as fier.
The medicyn of alle thingis is in the haasting of a cloude; a deewe, meetynge the heete comynge of brennyng, schal make it low.
The wynd was stille in the word of God; bi his thouȝt he made peesible the depthe of watris; and the Lord Jhesu plauntide it.
Thei that seilen in the see, tellen out the perels therof; and we heeringe with oure eeris schulen wondre.
There ben ful cleer werkis, and wonderful, dyuerse kindis of beestis, and of alle litle beestis, and the creature of wondurful fischis.
The ende of weie is confermyd for it; and alle thingis ben maad in the word of hym.
We seien many thingis, and we faylen in wordis; forsothe he is the endyng of wordis.
To what thing schulen we be myȝti, that han glorie in alle thingis? for he is al myȝti aboue alle hise werkis.
The Lord is ferdful, and ful greet; and his power is wondurful.
Glorifie ȝe the Lord as myche as euere ȝe moun, ȝit he schal be myȝtiere; and his grete doynge is wondurful.
Ȝe blessynge the Lord, enhaunse hym as myche as ȝe moun; for he is more than al preisyng.
Ȝe enhaunsynge hym schulen be fillid with vertu; trauele ȝe not, for ȝe schulen not take perfitli.
Who siȝ hym, and schal telle out? and who schal magnefie hym, as he is fro the bigynnyng?
Many thingis gretter than these ben hid fro vs; for we han seyn fewe thingis of hise werkis.
Forsothe the Lord made alle thingis; and he ȝaf wisdom to men doynge feithfuli.
Preise we gloriouse men, and oure fadris in her generacioun.
The Lord made myche glorie bi his greet doyng, fro the world.
Grete men in vertu weren lordis in her poweris, and riche in her prudence; tellynge in profetis the dignete of profetis,
and comaundynge in present puple, and tellynge hoolieste wordis to puplis, bi the vertu of prudence.
Sekynge maneres of musik in her childhod, and tellynge songis of scripturis.
Riche men in vertu, hauynge the studie of fairnesse, makynge pees in her housis.
Alle these men gaten glorie in the generaciouns of her folk; and ben had in preysyngis in her daies.
Thei that weren borun of hem, leften a name to telle the preisyngis of hem.
And summe ben, of whiche is no mynde; thei perischiden as thei that weren not, and thei weren borun as not borun; and her sones perischiden with hem.
But also tho men of mercy ben, whose pitees failiden
not; and good eritage dwellide contynueli with the seed of hem.
And the seed of her sones sones stood in testament,
and the eritage of her sones dwellith for hem, til in to with outen ende; the seed of hem, and the glorie of hem, schal not be forsakun.
The bodies of hem ben biried in pees; and the name of hem schal lyue in to generaciouns and generaciouns.
Puplis tellen the wisdom of hem; and the chirche tellith the preysyng of hem.
Enok pleside God, and was translatid in to paradis, that he ȝyue wisdom to folkis.
Noe was foundun parfit and iust, and he was maad recouncelynge in the tyme of wrathfulnesse.
Therfor residue seed was left to erthe, whanne the greet flood was maad.
Testamentis of the world weren set anentis hym, lest al fleisch myȝte be doon awei bi the greet flood.
Abraham was the greet fadir of the multitude of folkis; and noon was foundun lijk hym in glorie, which kepte the lawe of hiȝ God, and was in the testament with hym.
He made a testament to stonde in his fleisch; and he was foundun feithful in temptacioun.
Therfor God with an ooth ȝaf to hym glorie in his folk; God made hym to encreesse, as an heep
of erthe, and to enhaunse his seed as sterris, and to enherite hem fro the see til to the see, and fro the flood til to the endis of erthe.
And to Isaac God dide in the same maner, for Abraham, his fadir.
The Lord ȝaf to hym the blessing of alle folkis; and confermyde his testament on the heed of Jacob.
He knew hym in hise blessyngis, and ȝaf eritage to hym; and departide to hym a part in twelue lynagis.
And he kepte to hym men of merci, fyndynge grace in the siȝt of eche man.
Moises was loued of God and of men; whose mynde is in blessyng.
He made him lijk in the glorie of seyntis, and he magnefiede hym in the drede of enemyes; and in his wordis he made peesible the wondris aȝens kynde.
He glorifiede hym in the siȝt of kyngis, and he comaundide to hym bifore his puple, and schewide his glorie to hym.
In the feith and myldenesse of hym God made hym hooli; and chees him of alle men.
For he herde hym, and his vois; and ledde in hym in a cloude.
And ȝaf to hym an herte to comaundementis, and to the lawe of lijf, and of techyng; to teche Jacob a testament, and Israel hise domes.
He made hiȝ Aaron, his brother, and lijk hym of the lynage of Leuy.
He ordeynede to hym euerlastynge testament, and ȝaf to hym the preesthod of the folk. And he
made hym blissful in glorie, and girte hym with a girdil of riȝtfulnesse; and clothide hym with a stoole of glorie, and crownede hym in the ournementis of vertu.
He settide on hym sandalies, and breeches, and a clooth on the schuldur, and girte hym aboute with ful many small goldun
bellis in cumpas; to ȝyue soun in his goyng, to make soun herd in the temple, in to mynde to the sones of his folk.
God ȝaf to hym an hooli stoole, a wouun werk, with gold, and iacynct, and purpur, the werk of a wijs man, maad riche with
doom and treuthe; the werk of a crafti man, in writhun reed threed, with preciouse iemmes grauun in the byndyng of gold, and grauun bi the werk of a crafti man of stoonys, in to mynde, bi the noumbre of the lynagis of Israel.
A goldun coroun on his mytre, set forth with the signe of hoolynesse, the glorie of onour, and the werk of vertu, ourned to desijr of iȝen.
Siche thingis so faire weren not bifore hym, til to the eest.
Noon alien was clothid ther ynne, but oneli hise sones, and hise sones sones aloone, bi al tyme.
Hise sacrifices weren endid ech dai bi fyer.
Moises fillide hise hondis, and anoyntide hym with hooli oile.
It was maad to hym in to euerlastynge testament, and to his seed as the daies of heuene, to vse presthod, and to haue preisyng, and to glorifie his puple in his name.
God chees hym of ech lyuynge man, to offre sacrifice to God, encense, and good odour, in to mynde, for to plese for his puple.
And he ȝaf to hym power in hise comaundementis, and in the testamentis of domes, to teche Jacob witnessyngis, and in his lawe to ȝyue liȝt to Israel.
For aliens stooden aȝens hym, and men that weren with Datan and Abiron, and the congregacioun of Chore, in wrathfulnesse cumpassiden hym for enuye, in desert.
The Lord siȝ, and it pleside not hym; and thei weren wastid in the feersnesse of wrathfulnesse.
He made to hem wondris aȝens kynde, and in the flawme of fier he wastide hem.
And he encreesside glorie to Aaron, and ȝaf eritage to hym; and he departide to Aaron the firste thingis of fruytis of the erthe.
He made redi his breed in the firste thingis, in to fulnesse; for whi and thei shulen ete the sacrifices of the Lord, whiche he ȝaf to hym, and to his seed.
But in the lond of his folk he schal not haue eritage, and no part is to hym among the folk; for whi God is the part and eritage of hym.
Fynees, the sone of Eleazarus, was the thridde in glorie, in suynge hym in the drede of
God, and to stonde in the reuerence of folk; in the goodnesse and gladnesse of his soule he pleside God of Israel.
Therfor God ordeynede to hym the testament of pees, and made hym prince of hooli men, and of his folk; that the dignete of presthod be to hym and to his seed, with outen ende.
And the testament of Dauid, the sone of Jesse, of the lynage of Juda, was eritage to hym, and to his seed; that he schulde ȝyue wisdom in to oure herte, to deme his folk in riȝtfulnesse, lest her goodis schulen be don awei; and he made the glorie of hem to be euerlastinge, in the folk of hem.
Jhesus Naue, the successour of Moises in profetis, was strong in batel, that was greet bi his name.
The gretteste in to the helthe of chosun men of God, to ouercome enemyes risynge aȝens hem, that he schulde gete the erytage of Israel.
Which glorie he gat in reysynge his hondis, and in castynge scharpe arowis aȝens citees.
Who bifore hym aȝenstood so? for whi the Lord hym silf smoot the enemyes.
Whether the sunne was not lettid in the wrathfulnesse of hym, and o dai was maad as tweyne?
He clepide to help the hiȝeste God, myȝti in ouercomynge enemyes on ech side; and God, greet and hooli, herde hym, in stoonys of hail of ful greet vertu.
He made asauȝt aȝens the folk enemy, and in the comynge doun he loste the aduersaries;
that hethene men knowe the myȝt of hym, for it is not esy to fiȝte aȝens the Lord; and he suede myȝti men at the bak.
And in the daies of Moises he and Caleph, the sone of Jephone, diden merci; to stonde aȝens the enemye, and to forbede the folk fro synnes, and to refreyne the grutchyng of malice.
And thei tweyne weren stidfast, and weren delyuered fro perel, of the noumbre of sixe hundrid thousynde foot men, to brynge hem in to the eritage, in to the lond that flowith mylk and hony.
And the Lord ȝaf strengthe to thilke Caleph, and til in to elde vertu dwellide perfitli to hym; that he stiede in to the hiȝ place of the lond, and his seed gat eritage.
And alle the children of Israel sien, that it is good to obeie to hooli God.
And alle iugis bi her name, the herte of whiche was not corrupt, weren strong in batel, which weren not turned awei fro
the Lord; that the mynde of hem be in blessyng, and her boonys apperen fro her
place; and her name dwellith with outen ende, for the glorie of hooli men dwellith at the sones of hem.
Samuel, the profete of the Lord, that was louyd of his Lord God, made newe the empire, and anoyntide prynces in his folk.
In the lawe of the Lord he demyde the congregacioun, and he siȝ the Lord of Jacob, and in his feith he was preued a profete.
And he was knowun feithful in hise wordis, for he siȝ the Lord of liȝt.
And he clepide in to help the Lord almyȝti, in ouercomynge enemyes stondynge aboute on ech side, in the offrynge of a man vndefoulid.
And the Lord thundride fro heuene, and in greet soun he made his vois herd.
And he al to-brak the princes of men of Tyre, and alle the duykis of Filisteis.
And bifore the tyme of ende of his lijf, and of the world, he ȝaf witnessyng in the siȝt of the Lord, and of Crist; he took not of ony man richessis, ȝhe, til to schoon; and no man accuside hym.
And after this he slepte, and he made knowun to the kyng, and he schewide to hym the ende of his lijf; and he enhaunside his vois fro the erthe in profesie, to do awei the wickidnesse of the folc.
Aftir these thingis Nathan, the profete, roos, in the daies of Dauid.
And as ynnere fatnesse departide fro the fleisch, so Dauid fro the sones of Israel.
He pleiede with liouns, as with lambren; he dide in lijk maner with beris, as with lambren of scheep.
Whether in his ȝongthe he killide not a giaunt, and took awei schenschip fro the folk?
In reisynge the hond in a stoon of a slynge, he castide doun the ful
out ioiyng of Golias, where he clepide to help the Lord almyȝti; and he ȝaf in his riȝt hond to do awei a stronge man in batel, and to enhaunse the horn of his folk.
So he glorifiede hym in ten thousynde, and he preiside hym in the blessyngis of the Lord, in offrynge to hym the coroun of glorie.
For he al to-brak enemyes on ech side, and drow out bi the roote Filisteis contrarie, til in to this dai; he al to-brak the horn of hem, til in to with outen ende.
Dauid in ech werk ȝaf knouleching to hooli God, and hiȝ in the word of glorie.
Of al his herte he heriede God, and he louyde the Lord that made hym, and ȝaf to hym power aȝens enemyes.
And he made syngeris to stonde aȝens the auter; and he made swete motetis in the soun of hem.
And he ȝaf fairnesse in halewyngis, and he ournede tymes til to the endyng of lijf; that thei schulden preise the hooli name of the Lord, and make large eerli the hoolynesse of God.
Crist purgide the synnes of hym, and enhaunside his horn with outen ende; and he ȝaf to hym the testament of kyngis, and the seete of glorie in Israel.
Aftir hym roos a witti sone; and for hym he castide doun al the power of enemyes.
Salomon regnede in the daies of pees, to whom God made suget alle enemyes, that he schulde make an hous in the name of God, and make redi hoolynesse with outen ende, as he was lerned in his ȝongthe.
And he was fillid with wisdom as a flood is fillid; and his soule vnhilide the erthe.
And thou, Salomon, fillidist derk figuratif spechis in licnessis; and thi name was pupplischid to ilis afer, and thou were louyde in thi pees.
Londis wondriden in songis, and in prouerbis, and in licnessis, and interpretyngis, ether exposiciouns;
and in the name of the Lord, to whom the surname is God of Israel.
Thou gaderidist togidere gold as latoun, and thou fillidist siluer as leed.
And thou bouwidist thi thies to wymmen; thou haddist power in thi bodi.
Thou hast ȝoue a wem in thi glorie, and madist vnhooli thi seed, to brynge in wrathfulnesse to thi children,
and thi foli in othere men; that thou schuldist make the rewme departid in to tweyne, and of Effrem to comaunde an hard comaundement.
But God schal not forsake his merci, and schal not distrie, nether do awei hise werkis, nether he schal leese fro generacioun the sones sones of his chosun kyng Dauid; and he schal not distrie the seed of hym that loueth the Lord.
Forsothe God ȝaf remenaunt to Jacob, and to Dauid of that generacioun.
And Salomon hadde an ende with hise fadris.
And he lefte aftir hym of his
seed Roboam, the foli of the folk, and made lesse fro prudence; which Roboam turnede awei the folk bi his councel.
And Jeroboam, the sone of Nabath, that made Israel to do synne, and ȝaf to Effraym weie to do synne; and ful many synnes
of hem weren plenteuouse, for thei turneden hem awei greetli fro her lond.
And the lynage of Effraym souȝte al wickidnessis, til defence cam to hem; and delyuerede hem fro alle synnes.
And Elie, the profete, roos as fier; for whi his word brente as a brond.
Which brouȝte yn hungur on hem, and thei suynge hym weren maad fewe for enuye; for thei myȝten not suffre the comaundementis of the Lord.
Bi the word of the Lord he held togidere heuene, and castide doun fro it fier to the erthe.
So Elie was alargid in his merueils; and who may haue glorie in lijk maner with thee,
which tokist a wei a deed man fro hellis, fro the eritage of deth, in the word of the Lord God?
Which castidist doun kyngis to deth, and hast broke togidere liȝtli the power of hem, and gloriouse men fro her bed.
Which herdist dom in Syna, and in Oreb domes of defence.
Which anoyntist kyngis to penaunce, and makist prophetis successouris aftir thee.
Which were reseyued in a whirlwynde of fier, in a chare of horsis of fier.
Which art writun in the domes of tymes, to plese the wrathfulnesse of the Lord, to recounsele the herte of the fadir to the sone, and to restore the lynagis of Jacob.
Thei ben blessid, that siȝen thee, and weren maad feir in thi
frenschipe; for whi we lyuen oneli in lijf, but after deth oure name schal not be siche.
Elie, that was hilid in a whirlewynd; and his spirit was fillid in Elisee. Elisee in hise daies dredde not the prince,
and no man ouercam hym bi power; nether ony word ouercam hym, and his deed bodi profesiede.
In his lijf he dide wondris aȝens kynde; and in deth he wrouȝte merueilis.
In alle these thingis the puple dide not penaunce, and ȝeden not awei fro her synnes, til whanne thei weren cast awei fro her lond, and weren scatered in to ech lond.
And a ful fewe folk was left, and a prince in the hous of Dauid.
Summe of hem diden that, that pleside God; but othere diden many synnes.
Ezechie maad strong his citee, and brouȝte watir in to the myddis therof; and diggide a rooche with irun, and bildide a pit to watir.
In hise daies Senacherib stiede, and sente Rapsaces; and he reiside his hond aȝens hem, and he reiside his hond aȝens Syon, and was maad proud in his power.
Thanne the hertis and hondis of hem weren moued; and thei hadden sorewe as wymmen trauelynge of child.
And thei clepiden to help the merciful Lord, and thei spredden abrood the hondis, and reisiden to heuene; and the hooli Lord God herde soone the vois of hem.
He hadde not mynde on her synnes, nether ȝaf hem to her enemyes; but he purgide hem in the hond of Isaie, the hooli profete.
The aungel of the Lord castide doun the castels of Assiriens, and al to-brak hem.
For whi Ezechie dide that that pleside the Lord, and ȝede strongli in the weie of Dauith, his fadir; which weie Isaie, the grete profete, and feithful in the siȝt of God, comaundide to hym.
In the daies of hym the sunne ȝede aȝen abak; and God encreesside lijf to the kyng.
With greet spirit Ysaie siȝ the laste thingis; and he coumfortide the moreneris in Sion, in to with outen ende.
He schewide thingis to comynge, and hid thingis, bifore that tho camen.
The mynde of Josie maad in the makyng of odour, is the werk of a pyment makere.
In ech mouth his mynde schal be maad swete as hony, and as musik in the feeste of wyn.
He was dressid of God in the penaunce of folk; and he took awei the abhomynaciouns of wickidnesse.
And the herte of hym gouernede to the Lord; and in the daies of synnes he strengthide pitee.
Outakun Dauid, Ezechie and Josie, alle kyngis diden synne.
For whi the kyngis of Juda leften the lawe of myȝti God, and dispisiden the drede of God.
For thei ȝauen her rewme to othere men, and her glorie to an alien folk.
Thei brenten the chosun citee of hoolynesse; and thei maden the weies therof forsakun in the hond of Jeremye.
For thei tretiden yuel hym, which from the wombe of the modir was halewid a profete, to turne vpsedoun, and to leese, and efte to bilde, and make newe.
Ezechiel, that siȝ the siȝt of glorie, which the Lord schewide to hym in the chare of cherubyn.
For he made mynde of enemyes in reyn, to do wel to hem, that schewiden riȝtful weies.
And the boonys of twelue profetis apperen fro her place; and thei strengthiden Jacob, and aȝenbouȝten hem in the feith of her vertu.
Hou schulen we alarge Zorobabel? for whi and he was a signe in the riȝt hond
of God to Israel; and Jhesu, the sone of Josedech? whiche in her daies bildiden an hous, and enhaunsiden the hooli temple to the Lord, maad redi in to euerlastynge glorie.
And Neemye in the mynde of myche tyme, that reiside to vs the wallis, that weren cast doun, and made the ȝatis and lockis to stonde; which Neemye reiside oure housis.
No man borun in erthe was such as Enok; for whi and he was resseyued fro the erthe.
And Joseph, that was borun a man, the prince of britheren, the stidfastnesse of folk, the gouernour of britheren, the stablischyng
of puple; and his boonys weren visitid, and profesieden after deth.
Seth and Sem, these gaten glorie anentis men, and ouer ech man in the generacioun of Adam.
Symount, the sone of Onyas, was a greet preest, which in his lijf vndursettide the hous, and in hise daies strengthide the temple.
Also the hiȝnesse of the temple was bildide of hym, the double bildyng, and hiȝ wallis of the temple.
In the daies of hym the pittis of watris camen forth; and as the see tho weren fillid aboue mesure.
Which Symount helide his folk, and delyuerede it fro perdicioun.
Which was myȝti to alarge the citee; which gat glorie in the conuersacioun of folk; and alargide the entryng of the hous, and of the large cumpas aboute.
As the dai sterre in the myddis of a cloude, and as a ful moone
schyneth in hise daies; and as the sunne schynynge, so he schynede in the temple

in fier; as a sad vessel of gold, ourned
with ech preciouse stoon; as an olyue tree spryngynge forth, and a cipresse tree reisynge it silf an hiȝ; while he took the stoole of glorie, and was clothid in the perfeccioun of vertu.

Forsothe in takynge partis of the hoond of prestis, and he stood bisidis the auter. The coroun of britheren, as a plauntyng of cedre in the hil Liban, was aboute

He schedde out in the foundement of the auter, the odour of God to the hiȝ prince.
Thanne the sones of Aaron crieden lowde; thei sowneden in trumpis betun out with hameris, and maden a grete vois herd in to mynde bifore God.
Thanne al the puple hastiden togidere, and fellen doun on the face on the erthe, for to worschipe her Lord God, and to ȝyue preyers to almyȝti God an hiȝ.
And men syngynge in her voices alargiden; and a soun ful of swetnesse was maad in the greet hous.
And the puple preiede the hiȝ Lord in preier, til that the onour of the Lord was doon perfitli, and thei parformeden her ȝifte.
Thanne Symount cam doun, and reiside hise hondis in to al the congregacioun of the sones of Israel, to ȝyue glorie to God bi hise lippis, and to haue glorie in the name of hym.
And he reherside his preier, willynge to schewe the vertu of God.
And he preyede more the Lord of alle, that made grete thingis in ech lond; which encreesside oure daies fro the wombe of oure modir, and dide with vs bi his mercy.
Ȝyue he gladnesse of herte to vs, and that pees be maad in Israel bi euerlastynge
daies; that Israel bileue, that Goddis merci is with vs, that he delyuere hem in her dayes.
Mi soule hatith twei folkis; but the thridde is not a folk, whom Y hate.
Thei that sitten in the hil of Seir, and the Filisteis, and the fonned puple, that dwellith in Sichemys.
Jhesus, the sone of Sirach, a man of Jerusalem, wroot in this book the techyng of wisdom, and of kunnyng; and he renulide wisdom of his herte.
He is blessid, that dwellith in these goodis; he that settith tho in his herte, schal euere be wijs.
For if he doith these thingis, he schal be miȝti to alle thingis; for whi the liȝt of God is the step of hym.
Lord kyng, Y schal knouleche to thee; and Y schal togidere herie thee, my sauyour.
Y schal knouleche to thi name, for thou art maad an helpere and defendere
to me; and thou hast delyuered my bodi fro perdicioun, fro the snare of a wickid tunge, and fro the lippis of hem that worchen a leesyng; and in the siȝt of hem that stonden nyȝ thou art maad an helpere to me.
And thou hast delyuered me, bi the multitude of merci of thi name, fro roreris maad redi to mete;
fro the hondis of hem that souȝten my soule, and fro many tribulaciouns that
cumpassiden me; fro ouerleiyng of flawme that cumpasside me, and in the myddis of
fier Y was not brent; fro the depthe of the wombe of helle, and fro a tunge defoulyd, and fro a word of leesyng; fro a wickid kyng, and fro a tunge vniust.
Til to the deth my soule schal preise
thee, Lord; and my lijf was neiȝynge in helle bynethe.
Thei cumpassiden me on ech side, and noon was that helpide; Y was biholdynge to the help of men, and noon was.
Lord, Y hadde mynde on thi merci, and on thi worchyng togidere, that
ben fro the world; for thou delyuerst hem that abiden thee, and thou delyuerst hem fro the hond of hethene men.
Thou enhaunsidist my dwellyng on erthe; and Y bisouȝte for deth fletynge doun.
Y clepyde to help the Lord, fadir of my Lord, that he forsake not me in the dai of my tribulacioun, and forsake not me with outen help, in the tyme of hem that ben proude.
Y schal preise thi name contynueli, and Y schal herie it togidere in knoulechyng; and my preier is herd.
And thou hast delyuered me fro perdicioun, and thou hast delyuered me fro the wickid tyme.
Therfor Y schal knouleche, and Y schal seie heriyng to thee; and Y schal blesse the name of the Lord.
Whanne ȝit Y was ȝongere, bifore that Y erride, Y souȝte wisdom opynli in my preier.
Bifore the tyme of eelde Y axide for it, and til in to the laste thingis Y schal enquere it; and it schal flour as a grape ripe bifore othere.
Myn herte was glad ther ynne, my foot ȝede a riȝtful weye; fro my ȝongthe Y souȝte it.
Y bowide doun a litil myn eere, and Y took it.
Y foonde myche wisdom in my silf, and Y profitide myche ther ynne.
Y schal ȝyue glorie to hym, that ȝyueth wisdom to me.
For whi Y took councel to do it; Y loued feruentli good, and Y schal not be schent.
My soule wrastlide togidere ther ynne; and Y was confermyd in doynge it.
Y stretchide forth myn hondis an hiȝ; and my soule schynede in the wisdom of hym, and he liȝtnyde myn vnkunnyngis.
Y dresside my soule to it; and Y foond it in knowyng.
Y hadde pesibli fro the bigynnyng an herte with tho; for this thing Y schal not be forsakun.
My soule was disturblid in sekynge it; therfor Y schal haue pesibli a good possessioun.
For whi the Lord ȝaf to me a tunge my meede; and in it Y schal preise hym.
Ȝe vntauȝt men, neiȝe to me; and gadere ȝe ȝou in to the hous of techyng.
What tarien ȝe ȝit? and what seien ȝe in these thingis? ȝoure soules thristen greetli.
Y openyde my mouth, and Y spak, Bie ȝe wisdom to ȝou with
out siluer, and make ȝoure necke suget to the ȝok therof, and ȝoure soule resseyue techyng; for whi it is in the nexte to fynde it.
Se ȝe with ȝoure iȝen, that Y trauelide a litil, and Y foond myche reste to me.
Take ȝe techyng in myche noumbre of siluere, and welde ȝe plenteuouse gold ther ynne.
Ȝoure soule be glad in the merci of hym; and ȝe schulen not be schent in the preysing of hym.
Worche ȝe ȝoure werk bifore the tyme; and he schal ȝyue to ȝou ȝoure meede in his tyme.
The visioun, ether profesie, of Ysaie, the sone of Amos, which he siȝ on Juda and Jerusalem, in the daies of Osie, of Joathan, of Achas, and of Ezechie, kyngis of Juda.
Ȝe heuenes, here, and thou erthe, perseyue with eeris, for the Lord spak. Y haue nurschid and Y haue enhaunsid sones; sotheli thei han dispisid me.
An oxe knew his lord, and an asse knew the cratche of his lord; but Israel knewe not me, and my puple vndurstood not.
Wo to the synful folk, to the puple heuy in wickidnesse, to the weiward seed, to the cursid sones; thei han forsake the Lord, thei han blasfemyd the hooli of Israel, thei ben aliened bacward.
On what thing schal Y smyte ȝou more, that encreessen trespassyng? Ech heed is sijk, and ech herte is morenynge.
Fro the sole of the foot til to the nol, helthe is not ther ynne; wounde, and wannesse, and betyng bolnynge is not boundun aboute, nether curid bi medicyn, nether nurschid with oile.
Ȝoure lond is forsakun, ȝoure citees ben brent bi fier; aliens deuouren ȝoure cuntrei bifore ȝou, and it schal be disolat as in the distriyng of enemyes.
And the douȝtir of Sion, that is, Jerusalem, schal be forsakun as a schadewynge place in a vyner, and as an hulke in a place where gourdis wexen, and as a citee which is wastid.
If the Lord of oostis hadde not left seed to vs, we hadden be as Sodom, and we hadden be lijk as Gomorre.
Ȝe princes of men of Sodom, here the word of the Lord; and ȝe puple of Gommorre, perseyue with eeris the lawe of ȝoure God.
Wherto offren ȝe to me the multitude of ȝoure sacrifices? seith the Lord. Y am ful; Y wolde not the brent sacrifices of wetheris, and the ynnere fatnesse of fatte beestis, and the blood of calues, and of lambren, and of buckis of geet.
Whanne ȝe camen bifore my siȝt, who axide of ȝoure hondis these thingis, that ȝe schulden go in myn hallys?
Offre ȝe no more sacrifice in veyn; encense is abhomynacioun to me; Y schal not suffre neomenye, and sabat, and othere feestis.
Ȝoure cumpenyes ben wickid; my soule hatith ȝoure calendis and ȝoure solempnytees; tho ben maad diseseful to me, Y trauelide suffrynge.
And whanne ȝe stretchen forth ȝoure hondis, Y schal turne awei myn iȝen fro ȝou; and whanne ȝe multiplien preyer, Y schal not here; for whi ȝoure hondis ben ful of blood.
Be ȝe waischun, be ȝe clene; do ȝe awei the yuel of ȝoure thouȝtis fro myn iȝen; ceesse ȝe to do weiwardli, lerne ȝe to do wel.
Seke ȝe doom, helpe ȝe hym that is oppressid, deme ȝe to the fadirles and modirles child, defende ȝe a widewe.
And come ȝe, and repreue ȝe me, seith the Lord. Thouȝ ȝoure synnes ben as blood reed, tho schulen be maad whijt as snow; and thouȝ tho ben reed as vermylioun, tho schulen be whijt as wolle.
If ȝe wolen, and heren me, ȝe schulen ete the goodis of erthe.
That if ȝe nylen, and ȝe terren me to wrathfulnesse, swerd schal deuoure ȝou; for whi the mouth of the Lord spak.
Hou is the feithful citee ful of dom maad an hoore? riȝtfulnesse dwellide ther ynne; but now menquelleris dwellen ther ynne.
Thi siluer is turned in to dros, ether filthe; thi wyn is medlid with watir.
Thi princes ben vnfeithful, the felowis of theuys; alle louen ȝiftis, suen meedis; thei demen not to a fadirles child, and the cause of a widewe entrith not to hem.
For this thing, seith the Lord God of oostis, the stronge of Israel, Alas! Y schal be coumfortid on myn enemyes, and Y schal be vengid on myn enemyes.
And Y schal turne myn hond to thee, and Y schal sethe out thi filthe to the cleene, and Y schal do awei al thi tyn.
And Y schal restore thi iuges, as thei weren bifor to, and thi counselours, as in elde tyme. Aftir these thingis thou schalt be clepid the citee of the riȝtful, a feithful citee.
Sion schal be aȝen bouȝt in dom, and thei schulen bringe it aȝen
in to riȝtfulnesse; and God schal al tobreke cursid men and synneris togidere, and thei that forsoken the Lord, schulen be wastid.
For thei schulen be aschamed of idols, to whiche thei maden sacrifice; and ȝe shulen be aschamid on the orcherdis, whiche ȝe chesiden.
Whanne ȝe schulen be as an ook, whanne the leeues fallen doun, and as an orcherd with out watir.
And ȝoure strengthe schal be as a deed sparcle of bonys, ether of herdis of flex, and ȝoure werk schal be as a quyk sparcle; and euer either schal be brent togidere, and noon schal be that schal quenche.
The word which Ysaie, the sone of Amos, siȝ on Juda and Jerusalem.
And in the laste daies the hil of the hous of the Lord schal be maad redi in the cop of hillis, and schal be reisid aboue litle hillis. And alle hethene men schulen flowe to
hym; and many puplis schulen go, and schulen seie, Come ȝe, stie we to the hil of the Lord, and to the hous of God of Jacob; and he schal teche vs hise weies, and we schulen go in the pathis of hym. For whi the lawe schal go out of Syon, and the word of the Lord fro Jerusalem.
And he schal deme hethene men, and he schal repreue many puplis; and thei schulen welle togidere her swerdes in to scharris, and her speris in to sikelis, ether sithes; folk schal no more reise swerd aȝens folk, and thei schulen no more be exercisid to batel.
Come ȝe, the hous of Jacob, and go we in the liȝt of the Lord.
Forsothe thou hast cast awei thi puple, the hous of Jacob, for thei ben fillid as sum tyme bifore; and thei hadden false dyuynouris bi the chiteryng of briddis, as Filisteis, and thei cleuyden to alien children.
The lond is fillid with siluer and gold, and noon ende is of the tresouris therof; and the lond therof is fillid with horsis, and the foure horsid cartis therof ben vnnoumbrable.
And the lond therof is fillid with ydols, and thei worschipiden the werk of her hondis, which her fyngris
maden; and a man bowide hymsilf, and a man of ful age was maad low. Therfor forȝyue thou not to hem.
Entre thou, puple of Juda, in to a stoon, be thou hid in a diche in erthe, fro the face of the drede of the Lord, and fro the glorie of his mageste.
The iȝen of an hiȝ man ben maad low, and the hiȝnesse of men schal be bowid doun; forsothe the Lord aloone schal be enhaunsid in that dai.
For the dai of the Lord of oostis schal be on ech proud man and hiȝ, and on ech boostere,
and he schal be maad low; and on alle the cedres of the Liban hiȝe and reisid,
and on alle the ookis of Baisan, and on alle hiȝ munteyns, and on alle litle hillis,
that ben reisid; and on ech hiȝ tour, and
on ech strong wal; and on alle schippis of Tharsis, and on al thing which is fair in siȝt.
And al the hiȝnesse of men schal be bowid doun, and the hiȝnesse of men schal be maad low; and the Lord aloone
schal be reisid in that dai, and idols schulen be brokun togidere outirli.
And thei schulen entre in to dennes of stoonys, and in to the swolewis of erthe, fro the face of the inward drede of the Lord, and fro the glorie of his maieste, whanne he schal ryse to smyte the lond.
In that dai a man schal caste awei the idols of his siluer, and the symylacris of his gold, whiche he hadde maad to hym silf, for to worschipe moldewarpis and backis, ether rere myis.
And he schal entre in to chynnis, ethir crasyngis, of stoonys, and in to the caues of hard roochis, fro the face of the inward drede of the Lord, and fro the glorie of his mageste, whanne he schal ryse to smyte the lond.
Therfor ceesse ȝe fro a man, whos spirit is in hise nose thirlis, for he is arettid hiȝ.
For lo! the lordli gouernour, the Lord of oostis, schal take awei fro Jerusalem and fro Juda a myȝti man, and strong, and al the strengthe of breed, and al the
strengthe of watir; a strong man, and a man a werriour, and a domesman, and a profete, and a false dyuynour in auteris,
and an elde man, a prince ouer fifti men, and a worschipful man in cheer, and a counselour, and a wijs man of principal crafti men, and a prudent man of mystik, ethir goostli, speche.
And Y schal ȝyue children the princes of hem, and men of wymmens condiciouns schulen be lordis of hem.
And the puple schal falle doun, a man to a man, ech man to his neiȝbore; a child schal make noyse aȝens an eld man, and an vnnoble man aȝens a noble man.
For a man schal take his brother, the meneal of his fadir, and schal seie, A clooth is to thee, be thou oure prince; forsothe this fallyng be vndur thin hond.
And he schal answere in that dai, and seie, Y am no leche, and nether breed, nether cloth is in myn hous; nyle ȝe make me prince of the puple.
For whi Jerusalem felle doun, and Juda felle doun togidere; for the tunge of hem, and the fyndingis of hem weren aȝens the Lord, for to terre to wraththe the iȝen of his mageste.
The knowyng of her cheer schal answere to hem; and thei prechiden her synne, as Sodom dide, and hidden not. Wo to the soule of hem, for whi yuels ben ȝoldun to hem.
Seie ȝe to the iust man, that it schal be to hym wel; for he schal ete the fruyt of hise fyndyngis.
Wo to the wickid man in to yuel; for whi the ȝeldyng of hise hondis schal be maad to hym.
The wrongful axeris of my puple robbiden it, and wymmen weren lordis therof. Mi puple, thei that seien thee blessid, disseyuen thee, and distrien the weie of thi steppis.
The Lord stondith for to deme, and the Lord stondith for
to deme puplis; the Lord schal come to doom, with the eldere men of his puple, and with hise princes; for ȝe han wastid my vyner, and the raueyn of a pore man is in ȝoure hous.
Whi al to-breken ȝe my puple, and grynden togidere the faces of pore men? seith the Lord God of oostis.
And the Lord God seide, For that that the douȝtris of Syon weren reisid, and ȝeden with a necke stretchid forth, and ȝeden bi signes of iȝen, and flappiden with hondis, and ȝeden, and with her feet
ȝeden in wel araied goyng, the Lord schal make ballyd the nol of the douȝtris of Sion, and the Lord schal make nakid the heer of hem.

Also thi faireste men schulen falle bi swerd, and thi stronge men schulen falle in batel.

In that dai the buriownyng of the Lord schal be in greet worschip and glorie; and the fruyt of erthe schal be hiȝ, and ful out ioye schal be to hem that schulen be sauyd of Israel.
And it schal be, ech that is left in Sion, and is resydue in Jerusalem, schal be clepid hooli; ech
that is writun in lijf in Jerusalem; if the Lord waischith awei the filthis of the douȝtris of Sion, and waischith the blood of Jerusalem fro the myddis therof, in the spirit of doom, and in the spirit of heete.
And the Lord made on ech place of the hille of Sion, and where he was clepid to help, a cloude bi dai, and smoke, and briȝtnesse of fier flawmynge in the niȝt; for whi hilyng schal be aboue al glorie.
And a tabernacle schal be in to a schadewynge place of the dai, fro heete, and in to sikirnesse and in to hidyng, fro whirlewynd and fro reyn.
I schal synge for my derlyng the song of myn vnclis sone, of his vyner. A vyner was maad to my derlyng, in the horne in the sone of oile.
And he heggide it, and chees stoonys therof, and plauntide a chosun vyner; and he bildide a tour in the myddis therof, and rerede a presse ther ynne; and he abood, that it schulde bere grapis, and it bare wielde grapis.
Now therfor, ȝe dwelleris of Jerusalem, and ȝe men of Juda, deme bitwixe me and my viner.
What is it that Y ouȝt to do more to my vyner, and Y dide not to it? whether that Y abood, that it schulde bere grapis, and it bare wielde grapis?
And now Y schal schewe to ȝou, what Y schal do to my vyner. Y schal take awei the hegge therof, and it schal be in to rauyschyng; Y schal caste doun the wal therof, and it schal be in to defoulyng;
and Y schal sette it desert, ether forsakun. It schal not be kit, and it schal not be diggid, and breris and thornes schulen growe vp on it; and Y schal comaunde to cloudis, that tho reyne not reyn on it.
Forsothe the vyner of the Lord of oostis is the hous of Israel, and the men of Juda ben the delitable buriownyng of hym. Y abood, that it schal make doom, and lo! wickidnesse; and that it schulde do riȝtfulnesse, and lo! cry.
Wo to ȝou that ioynen hows to hous, and couplen feeld to feeld, til to the ende of place. Whether ȝe aloone schulen dwelle in the myddis of the lond?
These thingis ben in the eeris of me, the Lord of oostis; if many housis ben not forsakun, grete housis and faire, with outen dwellere, bileue ȝe not to me.
For whi ten acris of vynes schulen make a potel, and thretti buschels of seed schulen make thre buschels.
Wo to ȝou that risen togidere eerli to sue drunkennesse, and to drinke til to euentid, that ȝe brenne with wyn.
Harpe, and giterne, and tympan, and pipe, and wyn ben in ȝoure feestis; and ȝe biholden not the werk of the Lord, nether ȝe biholden the werkis of hise hondis.
Therfor my puple is led prisoner, for it hadde not kunnyng; and the noble men therof perischiden in hungur, and the multitude therof was drye in thirst.
Therfor helle alargide his soule, and openyde his mouth with outen ony ende; and strong men therof, and the puple therof, and the hiȝ men, and gloriouse men therof, schulen go doun to it.
And a man schal be bowid doun, and a man of age schal be maad low; and the iȝen of hiȝ men schulen be pressid doun.
And the Lord of oostis schal be enhaunsid in doom, and hooli God schal be halewid in riȝtfulnesse.
And lambren schulen be fed bi her ordre, and comelyngis schulen ete desert places turned in to plentee.
Wo to ȝou that drawen wickydnesse in the cordis of vanyte, and drawen synne as the boond of a wayn;
and ȝe seien, The werk of hym haaste, and come soone, that we se; and the counsel of the hooli of Israel neiȝ, and come, and we schulen knowe it.
Wo to ȝou that seien yuel good, and good yuel; and putten derknessis liȝt, and liȝt derknessis; and putten bittir thing in to swete, and swete thing in to bittir.
Wo to ȝou that ben wise men in ȝoure iȝen, and ben prudent bifor ȝou silf.
Wo to ȝou that ben myȝti to drynke wyn, and ben
stronge to meddle drunkenesse; and ȝe iustifien a wickid man for ȝiftis, and ȝe taken awei the riȝtfulnesse of a iust man fro hym.
For this thing, as the tunge of fier deuourith stobil, and the heete of flawme brenneth, so the roote of hem schal be as a deed sparcle, and the seed of hem schal stie as dust; for thei castiden awei the lawe of the Lord of oostis, and blasfemyden the speche of the hooli of Israel.
Therfor the strong veniaunce of the Lord was wrooth aȝens his puple, and he stretchide forth his hond on it, and smoot it; and hillis weren disturblid, and the deed bodies of hem weren maad as a toord in the myddis of stretis. In alle these thingis the stronge vengeaunce of him was not turned awei, but ȝit his hond was stretchid forth.
And he schal reise a signe among naciouns afer, and he schal hisse to hym fro the endis of erthe; and lo! he schal haaste, and schal come swiftli.
Noon is failynge nethir trauelynge in that oost; he schal not nappe, nether slepe, nether the girdil of his reynes schal be vndo, nether the lace of his scho schal be brokun.
Hise arowis ben scharpe, and alle hise bowis ben bent; the houys of hise horsis ben as a flynt, and hise wheelis ben as the feersnesse of tempest.
His roryng schal be as of a lioun; he schal rore as the whelpis of liouns; and he schal gnaste, and schal holde prey, and schal biclippe, and noon schal be, that schal delyuere.
And he schal sowne on it in that dai, as doith the soun of the see; we schulen biholde in to the erthe, and lo! derknessis of tribulacioun, and liȝt is maad derk in the derknesse therof.
In the ȝeer in which the kyng Osie was deed, Y siȝ the Lord sittynge on an hiȝ seete, and reisid; and the hous was ful of his mageste, and tho thingis that weren vndur hym, filliden the temple.
Serafyn stoden on it, sixe wyngis weren to oon, and sixe wyngis to the tothir; with twei wyngis thei hiliden the face of hym, and with twei wyngis thei hiliden the feet of hym, and with twei wyngis thei flowen.
And thei crieden the toon to the tother, and seiden, Hooli, hooli, hooli is the Lord God of oostis; al erthe is ful of his glorie.
And the lyntels aboue of the herris were moued togidere of the vois of the criere, and the hous was fillid with smoke.
And Y seide, Wo to me, for Y was stille; for Y am a man defoulid in lippis, and Y dwelle in the myddis of the puple hauynge defoulid lippis, and Y siȝ with myn iȝen the kyng Lord of oostis.
And oon of serafyn flei to me, and a brennynge cole was in his hond, which cole he hadde take with a tonge fro the auter.

And it was don in the daies of Achas, the sone of Joathan, the sone of Osias, kyng of Juda, Rasyn, the kyng of Sirie, and Facee, the sone of Romelie, the kyng of Israel, stieden to Jerusalem, for to fiȝte aȝens it; and thei myȝten not ouercome it.
And thei telden to the hous of Dauid, and seiden, Sirie hath restid on Effraym, and the herte of hym and of his puple was mouyd togidere, as the trees of wodis ben mouyd of the face of the wynd.

For whi bifore that the child kunne repreue yuel, and chese good, the lond, which thou wlatist, schal be forsakun of the face of her twei kyngis.

In the firste tyme the lond of Zabulon and the lond of Neptalym was releessid; and at the laste the weie of the see biȝende Jordan of Galile of hethene men was maad heuy.
The puple that ȝede in derknessis siȝ a greet liȝt; whanne men dwelliden in the cuntre of schadewe of deth, liȝt roos vp to hem.
Thou multipliedist folk, thou magnefiedist not gladnesse; thei schulen be glad bifore thee, as thei that ben glad in heruest, as ouercomeris maken ful out ioie, whanne thei han take a prey, whanne thei departen the spuylis.

herte, Tijl stoonys fellen doun, but we schulen bilde with square stoonys; thei han kit doun sicomoris, but we schulen chaunge cedris.
